nodes.statement: Jesus did 'many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book; but these are written, that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name' (20:30-31) - the evangelist's own statement about the book's selection and aim.

nodes.label: Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias
nodes.statement: After these things Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias (21:1) - a resurrection appearance to the disciples by that lake.
nodes.note: Appearance claim, written and searched honestly; the naming evidence for 'the sea of Tiberias' is entered on claim:jn-06-01-sea-called-tiberias, which this scene reuses (related_to), not on this appearance claim.

nodes.label: Seven disciples were together by the lake: Peter, Thomas, Nathanael of Cana, the sons of Zebedee and two others
nodes.statement: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee and two other disciples were together (21:2); only John names this group after the resurrection.

nodes.label: The disciples fished from the boat through the night and caught nothing
nodes.statement: Peter and the others entered the boat that night and caught nothing (21:3); night fishing was the ordinary working method on the lake (Luke 5:5 'we toiled all night and took nothing').

nodes.label: At the stranger's word they cast the net on the right side and could not draw it for the multitude of fish
nodes.statement: They cast the net at the stranger's word and were not able to draw it for the multitude of fish (21:6) - a miracle claim.
nodes.note: Miracle claim, searched honestly; the evidence entered attests the fishing practice and the lake's fishery, never the catch.

nodes.label: The beloved disciple recognized the risen Jesus and Peter threw himself into the sea
nodes.statement: The disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter 'It is the Lord!'; Peter wrapped his coat around himself and threw himself into the sea (21:7).
nodes.note: John's detail alone; the P66/Sinaiticus first-hand variant of this verse assimilates Luke 5:5's wording (see the passage variant).

nodes.label: The boat was about two hundred cubits from land
nodes.statement: The other disciples came in the little boat, for they were not far from land but about two hundred cubits away (about 90-105 m on the common cubit), dragging the net full of fish (21:8).

nodes.label: A charcoal fire (anthrakia) with fish laid on it and bread on the shore
nodes.statement: On the land they saw a fire of coals (anthrakia) with fish laid on it, and bread (21:9) - a shore breakfast cooked over a charcoal fire.
nodes.note: The same rare word anthrakia as John 18:18's courtyard fire (related_to); both occurrences are John's.

nodes.label: The net held 153 large fish and was not torn
nodes.statement: Peter drew the net to land, full of great fish, one hundred and fifty-three; and for so many the net was not torn (21:11) - the exact count is John's detail alone.

nodes.label: The risen Jesus served the disciples bread and fish on the shore
nodes.statement: Jesus said 'Come and eat breakfast', took the bread and gave it to them, and the fish likewise (21:12-13) - the risen Jesus eating with the disciples.
nodes.note: Appearance claim, written and searched honestly. Luke 24:42-43 knows a different appearance meal (broiled fish in Jerusalem); the fish-eating motif is shared, the scenes are not the same event.

nodes.label: This was the third time Jesus was revealed to the disciples after he had risen
nodes.statement: This is now the third time that Jesus was revealed to his disciples after he had risen from the dead (21:14) - John counts the appearances of John 20 plus this scene.
nodes.note: Appearance claim; John's own counting (20:19-23 evening, 20:26-29 with Thomas, 21:1 by the lake). The Synoptics count differently; no external evidence.

nodes.label: The threefold question 'do you love me' and commission 'feed my sheep' to Peter
nodes.statement: Jesus asked Simon Peter three times 'do you love me', Peter answered three times, and Jesus commissioned him 'Feed my lambs... Tend my sheep... Feed my sheep' (21:15-17).
nodes.note: John's private rehabilitation scene after the denials (18:17, 18:25-27); no external evidence.

nodes.label: Jesus predicted that when Peter is old another will gird him and carry him where he does not wish - signifying the death by which he would glorify God
nodes.statement: 'When you were young you girded yourself... when you are old you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and carry you where you do not wish' - 'this he said, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God' (21:18-19).
nodes.note: The verse never says 'crucifixion'; the martyrdom reading is tradition. 1 Clement (c. 96) is the earliest witness that Peter died a martyr's death; the Roman crucifixion setting and the upside-down detail are later and disputed (see the claim's documented_by).

nodes.label: The saying circulated among the brothers that the beloved disciple would not die, and John corrects it
nodes.statement: Peter asked about the beloved disciple; Jesus answered 'If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you?'; the saying went out among the brothers that this disciple would not die, and the evangelist corrects it (21:20-23).
nodes.note: A report of early Christian rumor corrected in the text itself - John's detail alone, no external evidence.

nodes.label: The beloved disciple testifies to these things and wrote them, and 'we know his witness is true'
nodes.statement: 'This is the disciple who testifies about these things and wrote these things; we know that his witness is true' (21:24) - the Gospel's own claim that the beloved disciple was its eyewitness author.
nodes.note: Modern scholarship is divided: most scholars read 21:24 as claiming the beloved disciple authored the Gospel, others as a later group endorsing his testimony (fetched Gospel of John article); the identification of the beloved disciple with John son of Zebedee rests on reception (Irenaeus, Papias), graded D here.

nodes.label: The world itself could not hold the books of everything Jesus did
nodes.statement: 'There are also many other things which Jesus did, which if they would all be written, I suppose that even the world itself would not have room for the books that would be written' (21:25) - the Gospel's final word on its own selection.
nodes.note: The twin of 20:30-31 (related_to); a statement about the book's selection, not an event.

nodes.label: Luke wrote his ordered account for a man called Theophilus, addressed as 'most excellent'.
nodes.statement: Luke wrote his ordered account for a man called Theophilus, addressed as 'most excellent'.

nodes.label: Priests served in the Temple in rotation through twenty-four named divisions, each serving one week.
nodes.statement: Priests served in the Temple in rotation through twenty-four named divisions, each serving one week.

nodes.label: Elizabeth, Zechariah's wife, was descended from Aaron (a priestly family).
nodes.statement: Elizabeth, Zechariah's wife, was descended from Aaron (a priestly family).

nodes.label: Zechariah was a priest of the division (course) of Abijah.
nodes.statement: Zechariah was a priest of the division (course) of Abijah.

nodes.label: In the daily Temple service the priest to burn incense was chosen by lot, and he entered the sanctuary to burn it.
nodes.statement: In the daily Temple service the priest to burn incense was chosen by lot, and he entered the sanctuary to burn it.

nodes.label: The multitude of the people prayed outside the sanctuary at the hour of incense.
nodes.statement: The multitude of the people prayed outside the sanctuary at the hour of incense.

nodes.label: An angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.
nodes.statement: An angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.

nodes.label: The angel announced that the barren, aged Elizabeth would bear a son to be named John.
nodes.statement: The angel announced that the barren, aged Elizabeth would bear a son to be named John.

nodes.label: John was to drink no wine nor strong drink, an abstinence like a nazirite vow.
nodes.statement: John was to drink no wine nor strong drink, an abstinence like a nazirite vow.

nodes.label: The angel identified himself as Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God.
nodes.statement: The angel identified himself as Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God.

nodes.label: Zechariah was left unable to speak until the day these things happened.
nodes.statement: Zechariah was left unable to speak until the day these things happened.

nodes.label: Elizabeth, barren and advanced in years, conceived and hid herself five months.
nodes.statement: Elizabeth, barren and advanced in years, conceived and hid herself five months.

nodes.label: In Elizabeth's sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent to Nazareth, a city of Galilee, to the virgin Mary.
nodes.statement: In Elizabeth's sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent to Nazareth, a city of Galilee, to the virgin Mary.

nodes.label: Mary was pledged in marriage to Joseph, of the house of David.
nodes.statement: Mary was pledged in marriage to Joseph, of the house of David.

nodes.label: Mary was told she would conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear a son who will be called the Son of God.
nodes.statement: Mary was told she would conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear a son who will be called the Son of God.

nodes.label: Mary's son was predicted to receive the throne of his father David and to reign over the house of Jacob.
nodes.statement: Mary's son was predicted to receive the throne of his father David and to reign over the house of Jacob.

nodes.label: Jews of this period expected a king from David's line who would reign forever.
nodes.statement: Jews of this period expected a king from David's line who would reign forever.

nodes.label: Mary visited Elizabeth in the hill country and stayed with her about three months.
nodes.statement: Mary visited Elizabeth in the hill country and stayed with her about three months.

nodes.label: Mary went into the hill country to a city of Judah, to Zechariah's and Elizabeth's house.
nodes.statement: Mary went into the hill country to a city of Judah, to Zechariah's and Elizabeth's house.

nodes.label: At Mary's greeting the baby leaped in Elizabeth's womb and Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, blessed Mary and her child.
nodes.statement: At Mary's greeting the baby leaped in Elizabeth's womb and Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, blessed Mary and her child.

nodes.label: Elizabeth gave birth to a son, and her neighbors and relatives rejoiced with her.
nodes.statement: Elizabeth gave birth to a son, and her neighbors and relatives rejoiced with her.

nodes.label: On the eighth day the neighbours came to circumcise the child, as the custom required.
nodes.statement: On the eighth day the neighbours came to circumcise the child, as the custom required.

nodes.label: Zechariah asked for a writing tablet and wrote, 'His name is John.'
nodes.statement: Zechariah asked for a writing tablet and wrote, 'His name is John.'

nodes.label: The child John grew and lived in the deserts until the day of his public appearance to Israel.
nodes.statement: The child John grew and lived in the deserts until the day of his public appearance to Israel.
Caesar Augustus issued a decree that the inhabited world be enrolled (registered).
nodes.label: Augustus decreed an enrollment of the world

nodes.statement: The enrollment was made while Quirinius was governor of Syria, at the time of Jesus's birth (Luke 1:5 places the annunciation in the days of Herod, king of Judea).
nodes.label: Enrollment dated to Quirinius's governorship at the birth

nodes.statement: Quirinius was governor (hegemon) of Syria.
nodes.label: Quirinius governor of Syria

nodes.statement: The enrollment required everyone to go to his own city to be registered.
nodes.label: Everyone enrolled in his own city

nodes.statement: Joseph went up from Nazareth in Galilee to Bethlehem in Judea, David's city, because he was of the house and family of David, to enroll with Mary, who was pregnant.
nodes.label: Joseph went from Nazareth to Bethlehem for the enrollment

nodes.statement: The newborn was wrapped in bands of cloth and laid in a feeding trough (phatne) because there was no room for them in the lodging (kataluma).
nodes.label: No room in the kataluma; the child laid in a manger

nodes.statement: Shepherds were staying in the fields near Bethlehem, keeping watch by night over their flock.
nodes.label: Shepherds keeping watch by night

nodes.statement: Jesus was circumcised on the eighth day after his birth, as the law required.
nodes.label: Circumcision on the eighth day

nodes.statement: After the days of purification the parents brought Jesus to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord and offered a sacrifice of a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
nodes.label: Purification sacrifice of two turtledoves or pigeons

nodes.statement: Simeon, a righteous and devout man in Jerusalem who was looking for the consolation of Israel, received the infant Jesus in his arms in the temple and blessed him.
nodes.label: Simeon received the child in the temple

nodes.statement: Anna, a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, an aged widow who worshiped in the temple night and day, gave thanks and spoke of Jesus to those looking for redemption in Jerusalem.
nodes.label: Anna the prophetess spoke of the child

nodes.statement: When they had accomplished all things required by the law of the Lord, the family returned to Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.
nodes.label: The family returned to Nazareth after the purification

nodes.statement: Jesus's parents went up to Jerusalem every year for the feast of the Passover, and Jesus went with them at the age of twelve.
nodes.label: Annual Passover pilgrimage to Jerusalem

nodes.statement: After three days Jesus was found in the temple courts sitting among the teachers (didaskaloi), listening to them and asking them questions.
nodes.label: Jesus among the teachers in the temple
Herod Antipas was tetrarch of Galilee in the fifteenth year of Tiberius
nodes.statement: Herod (Antipas) was tetrarch of Galilee at the time Luke dates: the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar.

nodes.label: Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene
nodes.statement: Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene (the region of Abila, northwest of Damascus) at the time Luke dates; whether he is the Lysanias executed by Antony in 36 BCE, a younger tetrarch of the reduced Abilene, or the inscription's Tiberian-era tetrarch is debated.

nodes.label: Herod Philip was tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis in the fifteenth year of Tiberius
nodes.statement: Philip, Antipas's brother, was tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis at the time Luke dates; Josephus lists his territories as Gaulanitis, Trachonitis, Paneas, Batanea, Auranitis and part of the House of Zenodorus, without naming Ituraea.

nodes.label: Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea in the fifteenth year of Tiberius
nodes.statement: Pontius Pilate held the governorship (prefecture) of Judea at the time Luke dates: the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar.

nodes.label: John's ministry began in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar
nodes.statement: John's public appearance is dated to the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar - AD 28/29 counting from Tiberius's accession on Augustus's death in AD 14, or AD 26/27 on William Ramsay's counting from Tiberius's co-princeps association in AD 12.

nodes.label: Annas shared the high-priesthood formula with Caiaphas
nodes.statement: Luke names the high priesthood of 'Annas and Caiaphas' jointly; Annas (Ananus son of Seth) had been high priest AD 6-15 and remained the dominant figure of the priestly house while Caiaphas, his son-in-law's appointee line, held the office, though a joint high priesthood was not permitted under Jewish law.

nodes.label: Caiaphas was high priest in the fifteenth year of Tiberius
nodes.statement: Joseph Caiaphas held the high priesthood at the time Luke dates: the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar.

nodes.label: Luke applies Isaiah 40:3-5 to John, quoting the fuller text through 'all flesh shall see God's salvation'
nodes.statement: Luke introduces John's preaching with Isaiah 40:3-5 from 'the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet', quoting the fuller passage whose closing ('All flesh will see God's salvation') Matthew's quotation of Isaiah 40:3 does not carry.

nodes.label: John warned the crowds coming for baptism to flee the wrath to come and produce fruits worthy of repentance
nodes.statement: John said to the multitudes who went out to be baptized by him: 'You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance.'

nodes.label: John warned against relying on descent from Abraham: God can raise up children to Abraham from stones
nodes.statement: John told the crowds not to say 'We have Abraham for our father', for God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones.

nodes.label: John told the crowds that he who has two coats or food should share with those who have none
nodes.statement: To the multitudes asking what they must do, John answered: 'He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.'

nodes.label: Tax collectors came to John's baptism and were told to collect no more than what was appointed
nodes.statement: Tax collectors came to be baptized and asked John what to do; he told them, 'Collect no more than that which is appointed to you' - presupposing tax collectors with fixed assessments in the Jordan region.

nodes.label: Soldiers asked John what to do and were told not to extort by violence and to be content with their wages
nodes.statement: Soldiers asked John what they must do; he told them to extort no one by violence, accuse no one wrongfully, and be content with their wages - presupposing soldiers serving in the region.

nodes.label: The people were in expectation and wondered whether John might be the Christ
nodes.statement: As the people were in expectation and all reasoned in their hearts about John, whether perhaps he was the Christ, John answered them all that one mightier than he was coming.

nodes.label: John preached that the mightier one would baptize with the Holy Spirit and with fire
nodes.statement: John answered the people that he baptized with water, but the mightier one whose sandal strap he was not worthy to loosen would baptize them in the Holy Spirit and fire.

nodes.label: John described the coming one with a winnowing fan: wheat gathered into the barn, chaff burned with unquenchable fire
nodes.statement: John's image of the coming judge: 'whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor, and will gather the wheat into his barn; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.'

nodes.label: Luke's genealogy traces Jesus (as was supposed, through Joseph) from Heli back through David's son Nathan to Adam and God
nodes.statement: Luke's genealogy runs Joseph - Heli ... Nathan - David ... Abraham - ... - Adam - God: through Nathan, not Solomon; the names from David to Jesus differ entirely from Matthew's list; Luke reaches back to Adam, Matthew only to Abraham.

nodes.label: Jesus was about thirty years old when he began his work
nodes.statement: Jesus himself, when he began (to teach), was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph.

nodes.label: The devil: 'command this stone to become bread'
nodes.statement: The devil challenged Jesus, 'If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.'

nodes.label: Jesus quotes Deuteronomy 8:3 against the first temptation
nodes.statement: Jesus answered the first temptation by quoting Deuteronomy 8:3: 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.'

nodes.label: Jesus quotes Deuteronomy 6:13 against worshipping Satan
nodes.statement: Jesus answered the temptation to worship the devil by quoting Deuteronomy 6:13: 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.'

nodes.label: Jesus quotes Deuteronomy 6:16 at the temple pinnacle
nodes.statement: Jesus answered the temple-pinnacle challenge by quoting Deuteronomy 6:16: 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God.'

nodes.label: Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit
nodes.statement: After the temptation Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and news about him spread through the surrounding area.

nodes.label: Sabbath synagogue custom: standing up to read
nodes.statement: In Nazareth, where he had been brought up, Jesus entered the synagogue on the Sabbath 'as was his custom' and stood up to read.

nodes.label: A scroll of Isaiah was handed to Jesus and unrolled
nodes.statement: The book (scroll) of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Jesus in the Nazareth synagogue; he unrolled it and found the place he wanted.

nodes.label: Jesus reads Isaiah 61:1-2 in the Nazareth synagogue
nodes.statement: Luke records Jesus reading Isaiah 61:1-2, with 'recovering of sight to the blind' inserted and the reading stopping before 'the day of vengeance' (61:2b).

nodes.label: Rolling up the scroll, returning it to the attendant, sitting
nodes.statement: Jesus closed (rolled up) the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down, while the whole synagogue looked at him.

nodes.label: The Nazarenes ask 'Isn't this Joseph's son?'
nodes.statement: The Nazareth congregation testified about him and asked, 'Isn't this Joseph's son?'

nodes.label: Famine with the sky shut 'three years and six months'
nodes.statement: Jesus described a great famine over all the land in the days of Elijah, 'when the sky was shut up three years and six months'.

nodes.label: Elijah sent to the widow of Zarephath in the land of Sidon
nodes.statement: Jesus said Elijah was sent to none of the widows of Israel except to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.

nodes.label: Of many lepers in Israel only Naaman the Syrian was cleansed
nodes.statement: Jesus said there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet none was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.

nodes.label: The Nazareth crowd led Jesus to the brow of the hill to throw him off
nodes.statement: The Nazareth synagogue crowd, filled with wrath, rose up, threw Jesus out of the city and led him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, intending to throw him off the cliff.

nodes.label: Demons cry 'You are the Christ, the Son of God' at the evening healings
nodes.statement: At the sunset healings in Capernaum demons came out of many, crying 'You are the Christ, the Son of God', and Jesus rebuked them and did not allow them to speak.

nodes.label: Sent to preach the good news of God's Kingdom to other cities
nodes.statement: Jesus said, 'I must preach the good news of God's Kingdom to the other cities also, for this reason I have been sent.'

nodes.label: After a night of fishing without catch, Simon let down the nets at Jesus' word and they enclosed a great multitude of fish, so that the net was breaking (a miracle claim).
nodes.statement: After a night of fishing without catch, Simon let down the nets at Jesus' word and they enclosed a great multitude of fish, so that the net was breaking (a miracle claim).

nodes.label: Jesus said to Simon: 'Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching people alive.'
nodes.statement: Jesus said to Simon: 'Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching people alive.'

nodes.label: Simon had fishing partners (koinonoi) in the other boat, James and John the sons of Zebedee, who came to help fill both boats.
nodes.statement: Simon had fishing partners (koinonoi) in the other boat, James and John the sons of Zebedee, who came to help fill both boats.

nodes.label: The multitude pressed on Jesus to hear the word of God, and he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.
nodes.statement: The multitude pressed on Jesus to hear the word of God, and he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.

nodes.label: They brought their boats to land, left everything and followed Jesus.
nodes.statement: They brought their boats to land, left everything and followed Jesus.

nodes.label: Jesus saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, called him to follow, and Levi left everything, rose up and followed him.
nodes.statement: Jesus saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, called him to follow, and Levi left everything, rose up and followed him.

nodes.label: Jesus answered the critics with a physician comparison: the healthy need no physician, and he had not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.
nodes.statement: Jesus answered the critics with a physician comparison: the healthy need no physician, and he had not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.

nodes.label: Paralytic lowered through the roof tiles
nodes.statement: Not finding a way through the crowd, the paralytic's carriers went up to the housetop and let him down through the tiles (keramoi) with his cot into the middle before Jesus.

nodes.label: The paralytic rose up before them, took up what he had been lying on and went to his house glorifying God, and all who saw were amazed and glorified God.
nodes.statement: The paralytic rose up before them, took up what he had been lying on and went to his house glorifying God, and all who saw were amazed and glorified God.

nodes.label: Jesus entered one of the boats, which was Simon's, put out a little from the land, and taught the multitudes from the boat.
nodes.statement: Jesus entered one of the boats, which was Simon's, put out a little from the land, and taught the multitudes from the boat.

nodes.label: Pharisees and teachers of the law had come from every village of Galilee, Judea and Jerusalem and were sitting by while he taught.
nodes.statement: Pharisees and teachers of the law had come from every village of Galilee, Judea and Jerusalem and were sitting by while he taught.

nodes.label: Fishermen had gone out of two boats standing by the lake and were washing their nets.
nodes.statement: Fishermen had gone out of two boats standing by the lake and were washing their nets.

nodes.label: Jesus said: 'Blessed are you when men hate, exclude, mock and cast out your name as evil for the Son of Man's sake; rejoice, for your reward is great in heaven, for their fathers did the same to the prophets.'
nodes.statement: Jesus said: 'Blessed are you when men hate, exclude, mock and cast out your name as evil for the Son of Man's sake; rejoice, for your reward is great in heaven, for their fathers did the same to the prophets.'

nodes.label: Jesus said: 'Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled; blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.'
nodes.statement: Jesus said: 'Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled; blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.'

nodes.label: Jesus said to his disciples: 'Blessed are you who are poor, for God's Kingdom is yours.'
nodes.statement: Jesus said to his disciples: 'Blessed are you who are poor, for God's Kingdom is yours.'

nodes.label: Jesus asked: 'Can the blind guide the blind? Will they not both fall into a pit?' A disciple is not above his teacher, but when fully trained will be like his teacher.
nodes.statement: Jesus asked: 'Can the blind guide the blind? Will they not both fall into a pit?' A disciple is not above his teacher, but when fully trained will be like his teacher.

nodes.label: Sermon on a level place, crowds from Judea and Tyre-Sidon
nodes.statement: Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place, with a crowd of his disciples and a great number of people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon.

nodes.label: Jesus said to them: 'The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.'
nodes.statement: Jesus said to them: 'The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.'

nodes.label: Jesus taught: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
nodes.statement: Jesus taught: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.

nodes.label: The multitude sought to touch him, for power came out of him and healed them all; those troubled by unclean spirits came and were healed.
nodes.statement: The multitude sought to touch him, for power came out of him and healed them all; those troubled by unclean spirits came and were healed.

nodes.label: Jesus asked the scribes and Pharisees: 'Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?'
nodes.statement: Jesus asked the scribes and Pharisees: 'Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?'

nodes.label: The Twelve named, with Judas son of James
nodes.statement: The Twelve are named: Simon (whom he named Peter), Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon called the Zealot, Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, whom he named apostles.

nodes.label: Jesus spoke woes against the rich, the full, those who laugh, and those of whom all men speak well - Luke's counterpart to the blessings, with no Matthean parallel.
nodes.statement: Jesus spoke woes against the rich, the full, those who laugh, and those of whom all men speak well - Luke's counterpart to the blessings, with no Matthean parallel.

nodes.label: The centurion sent Jewish elders to ask Jesus to come
nodes.statement: The centurion sent elders of the Jews to Jesus, asking him to come and save his servant, and the elders pleaded earnestly: 'He is worthy... he loves our nation'.

nodes.label: The centurion built the Capernaum synagogue
nodes.statement: The elders told Jesus that the centurion 'loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us' - a Roman centurion credited with building the synagogue of Capernaum.

nodes.label: The centurion's servant was found well
nodes.statement: The messengers returned to the house and found the sick servant well - the healing Luke reports at a distance, through those sent.

nodes.label: A city called Nain
nodes.statement: Soon afterwards Jesus went to a city called Nain, with his disciples and a great multitude - a village of Lower Galilee near Endor, south of Mount Tabor.

nodes.label: The dead carried out of the town in a funeral procession
nodes.statement: The dead was carried out of the city gate in a procession, with many townspeople accompanying - public funeral processions with mourners were the custom.

nodes.label: A widow's only son had died at Nain
nodes.statement: A dead man, the only son of his mother, and she a widow, was being carried out of Nain's gate, and many people of the city were with her - a woman left without support.

nodes.label: Jesus raised the widow's son at Nain
nodes.statement: Jesus came near, touched the coffin so the bearers stood still, and said 'Young man, I tell you, arise'; the dead man sat up, began to speak, and Jesus gave him to his mother.
nodes.note: A resurrection miracle; external attestation is not expected and was searched for honestly (see matrix).

nodes.label: The crowd acclaimed 'a great prophet has arisen among us'
nodes.statement: Fear took hold of all, and they glorified God, saying 'A great prophet has arisen among us' and 'God has visited his people' - first-century prophetic expectation voiced in Galilee.

nodes.label: In that hour Jesus cured many
nodes.statement: In that hour Jesus cured many of diseases and plagues and evil spirits, and to many who were blind he gave sight - Luke's summary immediately before the answer sent to John.

nodes.label: The people baptized; Pharisees and lawyers refused
nodes.statement: When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they declared God just, having been baptized with John's baptism; but the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God, not being baptized by him.

nodes.label: A Pharisee named Simon hosted Jesus at dinner
nodes.statement: One of the Pharisees (named Simon in verse 40) invited Jesus to eat with him; Jesus entered the Pharisee's house and reclined at table.

nodes.label: A sinful woman brought an alabaster jar of ointment
nodes.statement: A woman of the city who was a sinner, learning that Jesus reclined in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster jar of ointment.

nodes.label: The woman wet, wiped, kissed and anointed Jesus's feet
nodes.statement: Standing behind at his feet weeping, she wet his feet with her tears, wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet and anointed them with the ointment.

nodes.label: Two debtors owing 500 and 50 denarii
nodes.statement: In the parable a lender had two debtors: one owed five hundred denarii, the other fifty - sums in the standard silver day-wage coin (about 20 months' and 2 months' wages).
nodes.note: A parable: evidence attests the coin and the wage scale it presupposes, never that the parable was told.

nodes.label: The omitted courtesies: foot-water, kiss, head-oil
nodes.statement: Jesus listed the courtesies Simon omitted: no water for his feet, no kiss of greeting, no anointing of his head with oil - guest courtesies of the period.

nodes.label: Women healed by Jesus travelled with the Twelve and provided for them
nodes.statement: Certain women healed of evil spirits and infirmities - Mary called Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna and many others - accompanied Jesus and the Twelve and served them from their possessions.

nodes.label: Mary Magdalene delivered of seven demons
nodes.statement: Mary, called Magdalene, had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, from whom seven demons had gone out.

nodes.label: Chuza was Herod's steward (epitropos)
nodes.statement: Chuza, Joanna's husband, held the office of steward (epitropos) of Herod Antipas - manager of the tetrarch's household and estates.

nodes.label: Joanna the wife of Chuza among the women
nodes.statement: Joanna, the wife of Chuza, was one of the women who followed Jesus and provided for the group.
nodes.note: Luke names her only here and at Luke 24:10.

nodes.label: Isaiah 6:9-10 quoted on seeing and not perceiving
nodes.statement: Jesus quotes Isaiah 6:9-10 ('seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand') to explain why he speaks to outsiders in parables.
nodes.note: Matthew cites the same passage at 13:14-15; the Gospels are not independent evidence for each other.

nodes.label: Hearers of the word called mother and brothers
nodes.statement: Jesus answered that his mother and his brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it.

nodes.label: The exorcism set in the country of the Gadarenes, opposite Galilee
nodes.statement: Luke 8:26 sets the event in the country of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galilee.
nodes.note: Manuscripts read Gerasenes (P75, B, D), Gergesenes (Sinaiticus and others) or Gadarenes (A, W, Byz; the WEB); Matthew 8:28 reads Gergesenes/Gadarenes and Mark 5:1 Gadarenes/Gerasenes; the site is disputed (Gadara, Gerasa, Hippos, Kursi).

nodes.label: The healed Gerasene sent home to proclaim in his city
nodes.statement: The delivered man begged to go with Jesus; Jesus sent him home with the charge 'Return to your house, and declare what great things God has done for you', and he proclaimed it throughout the whole city.
nodes.note: Mark 5:19-20 sends him through the Decapolis; Luke keeps him in his city. Related difference, not evidence.

nodes.label: Jairus's only daughter, about twelve, dying
nodes.statement: Jairus had an only daughter, about twelve years of age, who was dying; as Jesus went, the crowds pressed on him.
nodes.note: Mark 5:23 says the girl was at the point of death; Mark 5:42 says she was twelve.

nodes.label: Peter, John, James and the parents inside the house
nodes.statement: At the house Jesus allowed no one to enter except Peter, John and James, and the child's father and mother.
nodes.note: Mark 5:37 names only Peter, James and John following in; Luke admits the parents too and orders John before James.

nodes.label: Household and neighbours weeping and mourning over the girl
nodes.statement: All were weeping and mourning the girl; Jesus said she was not dead but sleeping, and they ridiculed him, knowing that she was dead.
nodes.note: Matthew 9:23 adds the flute players of professional mourning; Luke mentions only the weeping crowd.

nodes.label: Herod the tetrarch was perplexed by the range of identifications
nodes.statement: Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done and was very perplexed, because some said John had risen from the dead, some that Elijah had appeared, and others that one of the old prophets had risen again.
nodes.note: Matthew 14:1-2 has Herod tell his servants that Jesus is John risen; Luke adds his perplexity and the wider range.

nodes.label: Herod sought to see Jesus
nodes.statement: Herod said 'John I beheaded, but who is this about whom I hear such things?' and sought to see him.

nodes.label: The withdrawal was to a deserted place belonging to Bethsaida
nodes.statement: The apostles returned and reported; Jesus took them and withdrew apart to a desert region of a city called Bethsaida.
nodes.note: Luke alone locates the feeding near Bethsaida; Matthew 14:13 says only 'a deserted place'.

nodes.label: The crowd seated in groups of about fifty
nodes.statement: Jesus told the disciples to make the crowd sit down in groups (symposia) of about fifty each.
nodes.note: Mark 6:39-40 has groups by hundreds and by fifties on the green grass; Luke keeps only fifties and no grass.

nodes.label: 'Who do the multitudes say that I am?' asked while praying alone
nodes.statement: As Jesus was praying alone with the disciples, he asked them who the multitudes said he was.
nodes.note: Luke omits Matthew and Mark's location (Caesarea Philippi / villages of Caesarea Philippi).

nodes.label: The identifications: John, Elijah, one of the old prophets
nodes.statement: The disciples answered: John the Baptizer, others Elijah, and others that one of the old prophets is risen again.
nodes.note: Matthew 16:14 adds Jeremiah; Mark 8:28 has 'one of the prophets'.

nodes.label: Peter: 'The Christ of God'
nodes.statement: Peter answered that Jesus is 'The Christ of God', and Jesus warned them to tell this to no one.
nodes.note: Matthew 16:16 has 'the Christ, the Son of the living God'; Mark 8:29 'the Christ'.

nodes.label: Moses and Elijah spoke of his departure at Jerusalem
nodes.statement: Moses and Elijah, appearing in glory, spoke of his departure (exodos), which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
nodes.note: Luke alone gives the content of the conversation.

nodes.label: Jesus set his face to go to Jerusalem
nodes.statement: When the days drew near for him to be taken up, Jesus set his face (esterixen to prosopon) to go to Jerusalem and sent messengers ahead.
nodes.note: Itinerary claim; the turning point of Luke's travel narrative.

nodes.label: A Samaritan village refused to receive him
nodes.statement: Messengers entered a village of the Samaritans to prepare for him, but the village did not receive him, because his face was set toward Jerusalem.
nodes.note: Samaritan hostility to Galilean pilgrims bound for Jerusalem is the historical setting; Josephus records a village on that route killing Galilean pilgrims under Cumanus.

nodes.label: James and John ask to call down fire; Jesus rebukes them
nodes.statement: James and John asked to command fire from the sky to destroy the village, as Elijah did; Jesus turned and rebuked them.
nodes.note: The Elijah allusion points to 2 Kings 1 (fire from heaven on the captains of fifty); the 'as Elijah did' clause itself is a textual variant.

nodes.label: Hand to the plow and looking back
nodes.statement: 'No one, having put his hand to the plow and looking back, is fit for the Kingdom of God' - the image of ox-drawn plowing, in which looking back crooks the furrow.
nodes.note: Parallel to Elijah's call of Elisha (1 Kings 19:19-21, plowing with twelve yoke), but the saying itself is Luke-only here.

nodes.label: The mission of the seventy (-two)
nodes.statement: Jesus appointed seventy (-two) others and sent them out two by two ahead of him into every city and place where he was about to come.
nodes.note: The number varies between 70 and 72 in the manuscripts; Luke is the only gospel naming them (Wikipedia, Seventy disciples).

nodes.label: Travelers on the road exchanged formal greetings, so that 'greet no on
nodes.statement: Travelers on the road exchanged formal greetings, so that 'greet no one on the way' meant bypassing a customary social ritual.

nodes.label: A household was greeted with the words 'Peace be to this house', echoi
nodes.statement: A household was greeted with the words 'Peace be to this house', echoing the Hebrew shalom greeting.

nodes.label: Laborers received wages, and the saying 'the laborer is worthy of his
nodes.statement: Laborers received wages, and the saying 'the laborer is worthy of his wages' stated a fair-payment principle; the missionaries were to stay in one house, eating and drinking what was set before them.

nodes.label: The seventy were commissioned to heal the sick in each city and to tel
nodes.statement: The seventy were commissioned to heal the sick in each city and to tell it that God's Kingdom had come near to it.

nodes.label: Rejecting the messengers was counted as rejecting him who sent them -
nodes.statement: Rejecting the messengers was counted as rejecting him who sent them - the agent treated as the sender himself.

nodes.label: The seventy returned with joy, reporting that even the demons were sub
nodes.statement: The seventy returned with joy, reporting that even the demons were subject to them in his name.

nodes.label: Jesus told the returning seventy, 'I saw Satan having fallen like ligh
nodes.statement: Jesus told the returning seventy, 'I saw Satan having fallen like lightning from heaven.'

nodes.label: Venomous serpents and scorpions were real dangers in the region, so 't
nodes.statement: Venomous serpents and scorpions were real dangers in the region, so 'tread on serpents and scorpions' named familiar hazards.
nodes.note: Matthew 10:16 names serpents only; Luke adds scorpions.

nodes.label: Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and thanked the Father, Lord of heav
nodes.statement: Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and thanked the Father, Lord of heaven and earth, for hiding these things from the wise and understanding and revealing them to little children, saying that all things had been delivered to him by the Father.

nodes.label: Jesus told the disciples privately that their eyes were blessed for se
nodes.statement: Jesus told the disciples privately that their eyes were blessed for seeing what many prophets and kings desired to see and did not see.

nodes.label: A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers
nodes.statement: A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers, who stripped him, beat him and left him half dead.

nodes.label: Contact with a dead body made a person unclean, so a priest or Levite
nodes.statement: Contact with a dead body made a person unclean, so a priest or Levite avoided touching a body that might be dead.

nodes.label: A priest and then a Levite came down that road, saw the wounded man an
nodes.statement: A priest and then a Levite came down that road, saw the wounded man and passed by on the other side.

nodes.label: Oil and wine were poured on wounds as a treatment, and wounds were bou
nodes.statement: Oil and wine were poured on wounds as a treatment, and wounds were bound up.

nodes.label: There was an inn (pandocheion) with an innkeeper on the Jerusalem-Jeri
nodes.statement: There was an inn (pandocheion) with an innkeeper on the Jerusalem-Jericho road where a wounded man could be left for care.

nodes.label: The Samaritan paid two denarii to the innkeeper in advance for the man
nodes.statement: The Samaritan paid two denarii to the innkeeper in advance for the man's care, promising to repay any excess - two denarii being about two days' wages.
nodes.note: A different sum from Matthew 20:2's one denarius for a day's work; see the related_to edge.

nodes.label: Martha received Jesus in a village
nodes.statement: Jesus entered a certain village where a woman named Martha received him into her house.
nodes.note: Luke does not name the village; John 11:1 later places Martha and Mary in Bethany - an inference, not Luke's statement.

nodes.label: Martha's sister Mary sat at Jesus's feet and heard his word
nodes.statement: Martha's sister Mary sat at Jesus's feet and heard his word.
nodes.note: Luke names her only 'Mary'; the identification with Mary of Bethany rests on John 11:1.

nodes.label: John taught his disciples to pray, and one of Jesus's disciples asked
nodes.statement: John taught his disciples to pray, and one of Jesus's disciples asked him to teach them to pray as John had.

nodes.label: A guest arriving from a journey had to be set food even at midnight, a
nodes.statement: A guest arriving from a journey had to be set food even at midnight, and loaves were borrowed from a neighbor when the household had none.

nodes.label: Households shut their doors at night, so that knocking at a shut door
nodes.statement: Households shut their doors at night, so that knocking at a shut door and asking until it was opened was a familiar scene.

nodes.label: Jesus cast out a demon that made a man mute, and when it had gone out
nodes.statement: Jesus cast out a demon that made a man mute, and when it had gone out the mute man spoke.

nodes.label: Others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven
nodes.statement: Others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.

nodes.label: Jesus argued that every kingdom or house divided against itself falls:
nodes.statement: Jesus argued that every kingdom or house divided against itself falls: if Satan is divided against himself, his kingdom cannot stand.

nodes.label: Jesus said that if he cast out demons by the finger of God, then God's
nodes.statement: Jesus said that if he cast out demons by the finger of God, then God's Kingdom had come upon them.
nodes.note: Matthew 12:28 has 'by the Spirit of God' and 'kingdom of heaven'; Luke has 'by the finger of God' and 'kingdom of God'.

nodes.label: The strong man, fully armed, guards his dwelling until someone stronge
nodes.statement: The strong man, fully armed, guards his dwelling until someone stronger attacks, overcomes him and divides his plunder.

nodes.label: Whoever is not with him is against him, and whoever does not gather wi
nodes.statement: Whoever is not with him is against him, and whoever does not gather with him scatters.

nodes.label: A woman in the crowd blessed the womb that bore him and the breasts th
nodes.statement: A woman in the crowd blessed the womb that bore him and the breasts that nursed him; Jesus answered that those who hear the word of God and keep it are blessed.

nodes.label: As Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so would the Son of Man be to
nodes.statement: As Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so would the Son of Man be to this generation.

nodes.label: A Pharisee marveled that Jesus reclined at table without first washing
nodes.statement: A Pharisee marveled that Jesus reclined at table without first washing (baptizesthai) before dinner - an expected purification before the meal.

nodes.label: The Pharisees tithed mint and rue and every garden herb, while bypassi
nodes.statement: The Pharisees tithed mint and rue and every garden herb, while bypassing justice and the love of God.

nodes.label: Unmarked hidden graves defiled those who walked over them without know
nodes.statement: Unmarked hidden graves defiled those who walked over them without knowing it.

nodes.label: The lawyers loaded men with burdens hard to carry while themselves not
nodes.statement: The lawyers loaded men with burdens hard to carry while themselves not touching the load with one finger - multiplying legal restrictions.

nodes.label: The blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah
nodes.statement: The wisdom of God said 'I will send them prophets and apostles', and the blood of all the prophets shed from the foundation of the world, from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary, would be required of this generation.
nodes.note: Luke names no father for Zechariah and says 'between the altar and the sanctuary'; Matthew 23:35 names Zechariah son of Barachiah and says 'between the sanctuary and the altar'.

nodes.label: The lawyers took away the key of knowledge: they did not enter themsel
nodes.statement: The lawyers took away the key of knowledge: they did not enter themselves and hindered those who were entering.

nodes.label: Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy
nodes.statement: Jesus warned his disciples first of all: 'Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy' - Luke defines the leaven as hypocrisy.

nodes.label: Five sparrows sold for two assaria
nodes.statement: Five sparrows were sold for two assaria coins - small birds sold cheap in the market for the lowest bronze coinage.
nodes.note: Matthew's parallel saying (10:29) prices two sparrows for one assarion; Luke's ratio is different but the same cheap market custom.

nodes.label: A brother asked Jesus to divide the inheritance
nodes.statement: A man in the crowd asked Jesus, 'Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me', and Jesus refused to be a judge or arbitrator (krites, meristes) over the property - family inheritance divisions could be brought to a respected teacher for arbitration.

nodes.label: The steward set over a great household
nodes.statement: A great household had a steward (oikonomos) whom the lord set over his servants to give them their portion of food at the right time; an unfaithful steward beat the menservants and maidservants, ate, drank and got drunk.

nodes.label: Reading the weather: west cloud = rain, south wind = heat
nodes.statement: Jesus told the crowds: when you see a cloud rising from the west you say a shower is coming, and when the south wind blows you say there will be scorching heat - Judeans read the rain-bearing clouds from the western sea and the hot desert wind from the south.

nodes.label: The very last lepton
nodes.statement: Luke's debtor will not leave the prison 'until you have paid the very last penny' - Greek lepton, the smallest Judean bronze coin.
nodes.note: Matthew's parallel saying (5:26) names a kodrantes (quadrans), which two lepta together equal (Mark 12:42).

nodes.label: Pilate killed Galileans as they offered sacrifices
nodes.statement: Some present told Jesus that Pontius Pilate had killed Galileans while they were offering sacrifices, mingling their blood with that of their sacrifices.
nodes.note: The specific event is otherwise unrecorded. Josephus documents Pilate's lethal violence in Jerusalem (the Corban-aqueduct beating, War 2.175-177) and against the Samaritans at Gerizim (Ant. 18.85-87) but never names this event; the graph records it as a gap.

nodes.label: Siloam, a water source at southern Jerusalem
nodes.statement: Siloam was a place at the southern end of Jerusalem in the first century, named for its water (the pool and fountain of Siloam), where 'the men who dwell in Jerusalem' lived near.

nodes.label: The tower in Siloam fell and killed eighteen
nodes.statement: A tower in Siloam fell and killed eighteen people, whom Jesus compared with 'all the men who dwell in Jerusalem'.
nodes.note: The tower is not otherwise recorded. Identification is disputed: Weill (1920) proposed a tower flanking the wall by the Pool of Siloam; Szanton (2023) showed both towers were Hellenistic in origin and rebuilt in the first century; a circular foundation c. 6 m across is believed by some to be the tower's ruins.

nodes.label: A fruitless fig tree is dug around and manured
nodes.statement: In the parable a fig tree planted in a vineyard bore no fruit for three years; the vine-dresser asked to dig around it and fertilize (throw manure about) it before cutting it down - figs were cultivated in vineyards, and digging and manuring were the cultivator's remedies.

nodes.label: The bent woman straightened on the Sabbath
nodes.statement: A woman bent over and unable to straighten herself for eighteen years was healed when Jesus called her, laid his hands on her, and she stood up straight and glorified God.
nodes.note: Miracle claim written neutrally and searched honestly; recorded as none-found, as in Matthew and Mark for comparable healings.

nodes.label: The ruler of the synagogue
nodes.statement: The ruler of the synagogue (archisynagogos), indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, spoke to the crowd: there are six days for work, come and be healed on those days.

nodes.label: Untying ox or donkey to water on the Sabbath
nodes.statement: Jesus answered: does not each of you untie his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead it away to water? - Sabbath care for animals, including watering, was ordinary practice.
nodes.note: Matthew's parallel argument (12:11) uses lifting a sheep from a pit; Luke's example is untying and watering.

nodes.label: The mustard seed sown in a garden
nodes.statement: The kingdom is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and put in his own garden, where it grew into a large tree and the birds of the sky lodged in its branches.
nodes.note: Matthew's parallel says the man sowed the seed in his field (13:31); Luke says he put it in his own garden.

nodes.label: The narrow door into the Kingdom
nodes.statement: Jesus said: 'Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in, and will not be able' - the image of a narrow entry that many seek and cannot pass once the master has shut it.
nodes.note: Matthew's parallel (7:13-14) has the narrow gate and the broad road; Luke's image is the door of a house whose master shuts.

nodes.label: 'Go and tell that fox' - Herod's threat
nodes.statement: Some Pharisees warned Jesus, 'Get out, for Herod wants to kill you'; Jesus sent back the reply, 'Go and tell that fox: I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.'
nodes.note: The Herod is Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee. The threat and the exchange are not otherwise recorded; Antipas had already beheaded John the Baptist.

nodes.statement: One of the rulers of the Pharisees hosted Jesus for a meal in his house on a Sabbath, and those present were watching him.
nodes.label: A Sabbath meal in a ruler of the Pharisees' house

nodes.statement: At the Sabbath meal a man who had dropsy stood in front of Jesus, and Jesus took him, healed him, and let him go.
nodes.label: The man with dropsy healed on the Sabbath

nodes.statement: Dropsy (fluid retention) was a recognized, serious illness in the ancient Mediterranean world, known to the Hippocratic corpus centuries before Luke.
nodes.label: Dropsy a recognized ancient illness
Sabbath rescue: a son or an ox out of a well
nodes.statement: Jesus argued that a man would immediately pull his son or his ox out of a well on the Sabbath day - Sabbath rescue of a child or animal was accepted practice (Luke's example; Matthew 12:11 has one sheep out of a pit).
Guests invited to a marriage feast chose the best seats for themselves; banquet seating was ranked, with a best seat that could be reassigned and a lowest place to which a guest could be moved up.
nodes.label: Choosing the best seats at a feast

nodes.statement: A host giving a dinner or supper was urged to invite the poor, the maimed, the lame and the blind, who do not have the resources to repay him.
nodes.label: Inviting the poor who cannot repay
A man's great supper; servant sent to call the invited
nodes.statement: A certain man who made a great supper sent his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, 'Come, for everything is ready now' (Luke's host is a man, not Matthew's king giving a marriage feast for his son).
Invited guests excused themselves from a great supper: one had bought a field and must see it, one had bought five yoke of oxen and must try them, one had married a wife.
nodes.label: Invited guests making excuses

nodes.statement: When the invited guests refused, the master of the house sent his servant into the streets and lanes of the city to bring in the poor, maimed, blind and lame, and then out into the highways and hedges, compelling them to come in.
nodes.label: Bringing in the poor from streets and lanes

nodes.statement: Building a tower was a major expense: a man intending one would first sit down and count the cost, and a man who laid a foundation and could not finish was mocked by all who saw it.
nodes.label: Counting the cost of building a tower

nodes.statement: A king going to encounter another king in war would first sit down and consider whether ten thousand could meet twenty thousand, and if not, send an envoy while the other was far off to ask for conditions of peace.
nodes.label: A king deliberating before a war he might lose

nodes.statement: A woman searching her house for a lost coin would light a lamp and sweep the house until she found it.
nodes.label: Lighting a lamp and sweeping the house

nodes.statement: A woman could keep a savings of ten drachma coins and lose one of them; the drachma was a silver coin in circulation into the Roman period, roughly a day's wage.
nodes.label: A woman's savings of ten drachmas

nodes.statement: A father could divide his living (property) between his two sons while still alive, at the younger son's request for his share.
nodes.label: Dividing the living between two sons

nodes.statement: A citizen of a far country could hire a destitute man and send him into his fields to feed pigs; pig-keeping was practiced in the Gentile lands around Judea.
nodes.label: Hired out to feed pigs in a far country

nodes.statement: Carob pods (keratia) served as pig fodder, and a starving hired man might long to fill his belly with them.
nodes.label: Carob pods as pig fodder

nodes.statement: The best robe, a ring for the hand and shoes for the feet were given to a returning son to mark his restoration and honor in the household.
nodes.label: The best robe, the ring and the shoes

nodes.statement: A fattened calf was kept in the household and killed for a day of celebration.
nodes.label: The fattened calf for a celebration

nodes.statement: A household celebration at the return of a son was marked with music and dancing.
nodes.label: Music and dancing at the celebration
The estate manager (oikonomos) accountable to his lord
nodes.statement: A rich man's estate had a manager (oikonomos) who administered the property for his lord and could be accused of wasting it and dismissed.

nodes.label: Debts recorded in written bills, reducible
nodes.statement: A debtor owed his lord a sum recorded in a written bill (grammata) which he held, and the bill could be rewritten for a lesser sum.

nodes.label: The batos (bath) as a measure of oil
nodes.statement: The batos, the Hebrew bath of about 22 liters, was a liquid measure in which oil was stored and traded.

nodes.label: The kor as a measure of wheat
nodes.statement: The kor was a large dry measure in which wheat was counted and traded; its exact volume is disputed (Josephus compares it to Attic medimni).

nodes.label: Pharisees, lovers of money, scoffed
nodes.statement: Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all this and scoffed at him.

nodes.label: The law and the prophets until John
nodes.statement: The law and the prophets were until John; from John's time the good news of the kingdom of God is preached.

nodes.label: Clothed in purple and fine linen
nodes.statement: The rich man was clothed in purple and fine linen: murex-dyed purple and fine linen were the costliest garments of the period.

nodes.label: Lazarus the beggar at the gate
nodes.statement: A beggar named Lazarus was laid at the rich man's gate, full of sores.

nodes.label: Abraham's bosom and Hades divided by a gulf
nodes.statement: In first-century Jewish belief the righteous dead were carried by angels to Abraham's bosom, while the wicked were tormented in Hades, with a great gulf fixed between them.

nodes.label: Forgive a repentant brother seven times in a day
nodes.statement: If a brother sins against you and repents, forgive him - even seven times in a day.

nodes.label: The sycamore tree (Ficus sycomorus) in Palestine
nodes.statement: The sycamore (sykomorea, Ficus sycomorus) was a tree known in first-century Palestine.

nodes.label: A slave plows, shepherds, and serves supper first
nodes.statement: A slave plowed the field or kept sheep and, coming in from the field, prepared and served his master's meal before he ate himself.

nodes.label: The border route between Samaria and Galilee to Jerusalem
nodes.statement: On the way to Jerusalem he passed along the borders of Samaria and Galilee - the road Galileans took going up to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Ten leprous men met him, standing at a distance
nodes.statement: As he entered a village, ten leprous men met him and stood at a distance, raising their voices for mercy.

nodes.label: The ten were cleansed as they went
nodes.statement: As the ten lepers went to the priests, they were cleansed.

nodes.label: Cleansed lepers show themselves to the priests
nodes.statement: A cleansed leper was to show himself to the priest, the examination and cleansing prescribed in Leviticus 14.

nodes.label: The thankful one was a Samaritan, a stranger
nodes.statement: The one who turned back to glorify God at Jesus' feet was a Samaritan - a stranger to Judeans.

nodes.label: The days of Noah: the flood remembered as judgment
nodes.statement: In the days of Noah people ate, drank and married until the day Noah entered the ark and the flood came and destroyed them all - remembered as a sudden divine judgment.

nodes.label: The days of Lot: fire from heaven on Sodom
nodes.statement: In the days of Lot they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted and built; on the day Lot went out from Sodom, fire and sulfur rained from the sky and destroyed them all.

nodes.label: A widow pleaded repeatedly before a city judge
nodes.statement: In the parable's setting, a widow could bring a case against an adversary before a judge in a city, and could keep coming to him until he granted justice. The judge is a parable character; evidence attests the institution of city courts, not that the parable was told.

nodes.label: The Pharisee fasts twice a week
nodes.statement: The Pharisee in the parable says 'I fast twice a week'. Evidence attests the custom of twice-weekly voluntary fasting in that period, not that the parable was told.

nodes.label: The Pharisee tithes all that he gets
nodes.statement: The Pharisee in the parable says 'I give tithes of all that I get' - tithing beyond the strictly required (crops grown in the land) to all income. Evidence attests the tithing custom, not that the parable was told.

nodes.label: A certain ruler, very rich, asked about eternal life and went away sad
nodes.statement: A certain ruler (archon) asked Jesus what he should do to inherit eternal life, claimed to have kept the commandments from his youth, and went away sad, for he was very rich.

nodes.label: Many times more in this time, eternal life in the age to come
nodes.statement: Everyone who leaves house or family for the Kingdom of God will receive many times more in this time, and eternal life in the age to come (Luke's 'many times more'; Matthew 19:29 says 'a hundred times').

nodes.label: The third passion prediction: delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, spat on, scourged, killed, rising the third day
nodes.statement: Jesus said (18:31-33) that the Son of Man would be delivered up to the Gentiles, mocked, treated shamefully and spit on, scourged and killed, and rise the third day. The saying is recorded neutrally; evidence can bear only on the events said to come, not on the saying.

nodes.label: A blind beggar at Jericho cries 'Son of David' and receives his sight
nodes.statement: As Jesus drew near Jericho, a certain blind beggar sat by the road, cried out 'Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me', and at Jesus's word received his sight and followed, glorifying God. The healing itself is a miracle claim; external evidence can bear only on the setting.

nodes.label: Jericho's balsam was a prized revenue crop
nodes.statement: The plain of Jericho produced balsam prized as the region's most precious crop, farmed as a revenue source (under Cleopatra and Herod, and later imperial property). This is the economic background the verse's 'he was rich' points to at Jericho, not a fact the verse states.

nodes.label: Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector (architelones), rich, at Jericho; Jesus lodged at his house
nodes.statement: Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector (architelones, over other tax collectors) and rich, was in Jericho; Jesus told him 'today I must stay at your house', stayed, and the crowd murmured that he had gone in to lodge with a sinner.

nodes.label: Zacchaeus climbed a sycamore-fig tree at Jericho
nodes.statement: Zacchaeus ran ahead and climbed into a sycamore-fig tree (sykomorea) at Jericho to see Jesus, who was to pass that way.

nodes.label: Restitution: half of goods to the poor, fourfold to the defrauded
nodes.statement: Zacchaeus declared that he gives half of his goods to the poor and restores fourfold anything wrongfully exacted - fourfold being the restitution scale of 2 Samuel 12:6 (and the law's fivefold ox/fourfold sheep of Exodus 22:1).

nodes.label: A nobleman went to a far country to receive a kingdom; his citizens sent an embassy against him
nodes.statement: In the parable, a nobleman travelled to a far country to receive a kingdom and return, gave his servants minas to trade, and his citizens sent an envoy after him saying 'We don't want this man to reign over us'; on return he rewarded the servants and had his enemies killed before him. Evidence attests the events the parable appears to assume (Archelaus's journey to Rome and the Jewish embassy against him), not that the parable was told.

nodes.label: The mina, a money sum of about 100 drachmae
nodes.statement: The nobleman gave each of ten servants one mina (Greek mna) to conduct business until his return; the mina is a weight/money sum, in the Greek system equal to 100 drachmae.

nodes.label: A colt tied, never ridden; its owners question the untying
nodes.statement: Two disciples sent into the opposite village found a colt tied, on which no man had ever sat; as they untied it its owners (despotai) asked why they were untying it, and they answered 'The Lord needs it'.

nodes.label: Cloaks on the colt and cloaks spread on the road
nodes.statement: They threw their cloaks on the colt and set Jesus on them, and as he went they spread their cloaks on the road (no branches are cut in Luke).

nodes.label: Acclamation at the descent of the Mount of Olives: 'Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord'
nodes.statement: At the descent of the Mount of Olives the whole multitude of disciples acclaimed 'Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!' (Psalm 118:26 with 'King').

nodes.label: He wept over Jerusalem and said enemies would throw up a barricade, encircle and level it
nodes.statement: Jesus wept over the city and said that the days would come when enemies would throw up a barricade (charax) against it, surround and hem it in on every side, and dash it and its children within it to the ground, not leaving one stone on another. The saying is recorded neutrally; evidence attests the siege of 70 CE it describes, not the saying.

nodes.label: He taught daily in the Temple; the leaders plotted but feared the people
nodes.statement: He was teaching daily in the Temple; the chief priests, the scribes and the leading men of the people sought to destroy him, but could not find what to do, for all the people hung on his words.

nodes.label: Spies pretending to be righteous were sent to deliver Jesus to the governor's authority
nodes.statement: Spies who pretended to be righteous were sent to trap Jesus in his words, so as to hand him over to the authority and power of the governor - presupposing that such a matter belonged to the Roman governor's jurisdiction.

nodes.label: In this age people marry; those worthy of the resurrection neither marry nor die, being like the angels
nodes.statement: The children of this age marry and are given in marriage, but those counted worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor die any more, being like the angels.

nodes.label: The Temple of Jesus' day was adorned with beautiful stones
nodes.statement: The Temple of Jesus' day was adorned with beautiful stones - some spoke of how it was decorated with them.

nodes.label: The Temple was adorned with consecrated (votive) gifts
nodes.statement: The Temple of Jesus' day was decorated with consecrated gifts (anathemata) - votive offerings dedicated to God.

nodes.label: Terrors and great signs from heaven appeared in the period
nodes.statement: Terrors and great signs from heaven appeared in the period alongside the wars, earthquakes, famines and plagues - predicted in the discourse.

nodes.label: Jerusalem was surrounded by armies and its desolation was at hand
nodes.statement: Jerusalem was surrounded by armies, and its desolation was at hand - predicted in the discourse.

nodes.label: Jerusalem's inhabitants fell by the sword and survivors were led captive into all the nations
nodes.statement: Jerusalem's inhabitants fell by the edge of the sword, and survivors were led captive into all the nations - predicted in the discourse.

nodes.label: Jerusalem was trampled down by the Gentiles
nodes.statement: After its capture Jerusalem was trampled down by the Gentiles - predicted in the discourse.

nodes.label: The teaching warns against hearts weighed down with carousing, drunkenness and anxieties
nodes.statement: The teaching warns that hearts can be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness and the anxieties of life, and that the day will come like a snare on all who dwell on the face of the earth - predicted in the discourse.

nodes.label: Every day he taught in the temple; every night he lodged on the Mount of Olives
nodes.statement: Every day Jesus was teaching in the temple, and every night he lodged on the mountain called Olivet; the people came early in the morning to hear him in the temple.

nodes.label: Satan entered Judas before he went to the chief priests
nodes.statement: Luke alone reports that 'Satan entered into Judas, who was also called Iscariot, who was counted with the twelve' before the betrayal bargain.

nodes.label: Judas conferred with the chief priests and captains and agreed on money
nodes.statement: Judas talked with the chief priests and captains about delivering Jesus; they were glad and agreed to give him money, and he sought an opportunity away from the crowd. Luke gives no number of pieces.

nodes.label: A cup was taken, blessed and shared before the bread
nodes.statement: Luke alone has Jesus receive a cup, give thanks and say 'Take this, and share it among yourselves' before the bread of 22:19 - a first cup before the meal.

nodes.label: Bread was broken and a cup taken after supper
nodes.statement: Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it ('This is my body which is given for you'), and 'likewise he took the cup after supper' - a cup that follows the meal.

nodes.label: A dispute arose at the Passover table about who was greatest
nodes.statement: A contention arose among the disciples 'which of them was considered to be greatest', and Jesus contrasted the kings who lord it over others with 'I am among you as one who serves'.

nodes.label: Kings with authority were called 'benefactors'
nodes.statement: Jesus said 'those who have authority over them are called benefactors' (euergetai) - the Hellenistic royal epithet Euergetes.

nodes.label: The rooster will not crow today until Peter has denied three times
nodes.statement: Jesus told Peter 'the rooster will by no means crow today until you deny that you know me three times' - in Luke the crow follows the denials, and 22:61 recites the prediction as 'before the rooster crows'.

nodes.label: The disciples produced two swords
nodes.statement: Jesus told the disciples to buy a sword if they had none; they said 'Lord, behold, here are two swords', and he said 'That is enough'.

nodes.label: Going to the Mount of Olives was Jesus's custom
nodes.statement: Jesus came out and went 'as his custom was' to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples followed him.

nodes.label: An angel from heaven appeared, strengthening Jesus
nodes.statement: Luke alone reports 'An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him' during the agony - a passage textually disputed (see the passage variants).

nodes.label: Jesus's sweat became like great drops of blood
nodes.statement: Luke alone reports 'Being in agony he prayed more earnestly. His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down on the ground' - part of the disputed 22:43-44 passage.

nodes.label: Jesus touched the servant's ear and healed him
nodes.statement: Luke alone reports that Jesus said 'Let me at least do this', touched the high priest's servant's ear and healed him after it was cut off.

nodes.label: The chief priests, captains of the temple and elders came against Jesus
nodes.statement: The chief priests, captains of the temple, and elders came against Jesus in Gethsemane.

nodes.label: The assembly of elders, chief priests and scribes met as soon as it was day
nodes.statement: Luke alone reports a morning session: 'As soon as it was day, the assembly of the elders of the people were gathered together, both chief priests and scribes, and they led him away into their council'.

nodes.label: The Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God
nodes.statement: Jesus said 'From now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God' - enthroned Son-of-Man language without Matthew's 'coming on the clouds of the sky'.

nodes.label: The charges before Pilate: perverting the nation, forbidding tribute to Caesar
nodes.statement: The chief priests accused Jesus before Pilate of perverting the nation, forbidding the payment of tribute to Caesar, and claiming to be Christ, a king.
nodes.note: Luke's charge list is unique: Matthew 27:11 and Mark 15:2 record only the 'King of the Jews' charge.

nodes.label: Pilate declares Jesus innocent three times
nodes.statement: Pilate told the chief priests and the crowd that he found no basis for a capital charge against Jesus, and that Herod found nothing worthy of death either.
nodes.note: Luke states the innocence verdict three times (23:4, 14-15, 22); Matthew instead has Pilate's wife's dream and the hand-washing (27:19, 24).

nodes.label: Galilee was under Herod Antipas's jurisdiction
nodes.statement: When Pilate heard that Jesus was a Galilean, Galilee was under Herod Antipas's jurisdiction, so the case fell outside Pilate's own province.
nodes.note: Luke alone reports the jurisdictional reasoning; Josephus assigns Perea and Galilee to Antipas as tetrarch.

nodes.label: Pilate sent Jesus to Herod Antipas, who was in Jerusalem
nodes.statement: Pilate sent Jesus to Herod Antipas, who was in Jerusalem during those days.
nodes.note: Luke only. Antipas's presence in Jerusalem fits the Passover pilgrimage season.

nodes.label: Herod and his soldiers mocked Jesus and dressed him in splendid clothing
nodes.statement: Herod with his soldiers treated Jesus with contempt and mocked him; dressing him in splendid clothing, they sent him back to Pilate.
nodes.note: The mockery is by Herod and his soldiers (Luke only); in Matthew 27:27-31 and Mark 15:16-20 it is Pilate's soldiers, and Mark's robe is purple.

nodes.label: Herod and Pilate became friends that day
nodes.statement: Herod and Pilate, previously at enmity with each other, became friends with each other that very day.
nodes.note: Luke only. The Pontius Pilate article reports that Daniel Schwartz takes both the difficult relationship and its mending as potentially historical.

nodes.label: Pilate proposed to chastise Jesus and release him
nodes.statement: Pilate proposed to chastise (paideusas) Jesus and then release him, as a compromise short of crucifixion.
nodes.note: In Matthew 27:26 and Mark 15:15 the scourging is actually carried out before the release/crucifixion; Luke frames chastisement as Pilate's repeated proposal.

nodes.label: The lamenting women of Jerusalem followed him
nodes.statement: A great multitude of the people followed Jesus, including women of Jerusalem who mourned and lamented him, and he turned and addressed them.
nodes.note: Luke alone gives the lamenting women and the address to the 'daughters of Jerusalem' (23:27-31).

nodes.label: Days are coming: blessed are the barren, the mountains fall on us
nodes.statement: Jesus warned the women that days were coming when they would say 'blessed are the barren' and call on the mountains to fall and the hills to cover them, closing with the green-tree proverb.
nodes.note: Verse 30 echoes Hosea 10:8. A prediction: evidence can attest the destruction of 70 CE that the warning points to, not that it was predicted.

nodes.label: 'Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing'
nodes.statement: Jesus said, 'Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.'
nodes.note: Textually uncertain: the sentence is omitted in P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus and other early witnesses, and is included in the majority text (see the variants on passage:lk-23-34).

nodes.label: The soldiers mocked him and offered sour wine
nodes.statement: The soldiers came to Jesus and mocked him, offering him vinegar and saying, 'If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself.'
nodes.note: Luke: soldiers offer sour wine during the mockery; Matthew 27:48 and Mark 15:36 have sour wine on a sponge raised on a reed at the moment of the death cry.

nodes.label: The inscription in Greek, Latin and Hebrew letters
nodes.statement: An inscription was written over him in letters of Greek, Latin and Hebrew: 'THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.'
nodes.note: The trilingual detail is the Byzantine reading; the Alexandrian text reads only 'There was also an inscription above him' (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 23:38). The WEB follows the Byzantine text here.

nodes.label: The two criminals: one blasphemed, one asked to be remembered
nodes.statement: One criminal insulted Jesus; the other rebuked him, confessed his own guilt, said Jesus had done nothing wrong, and asked, 'Jesus, remember me when you come into your Kingdom'; Jesus answered, 'today you will be with me in Paradise'.
nodes.note: Matthew 27:44 and Mark 15:32 have both criminals reviling Jesus; Luke alone splits them and records the exchange. Luke 23:42 Alexandrian reads 'Jesus, remember me'; Byzantine 'Remember me, Lord'.

nodes.label: The sun's light failed
nodes.statement: The sun's light failed (Luke's distinctive wording, tou heliou eklipontos in the Alexandrian text; the Byzantine text and WEB read 'the sun was darkened').
