nodes.note: Luke's verb ekleipo is the word for eclipse and invited eclipse readings of the darkness (Thallus, Phlegon); see the complicates edge from the eclipse-impossible observation.

nodes.label: 'Father, into your hands I commit my spirit'
nodes.statement: Jesus cried with a loud voice, 'Father, into your hands I commit my spirit', and died.
nodes.note: The final cry differs: Matthew 27:46 and Mark 15:34 quote Psalm 22:1 ('My God, my God, why have you forsaken me'); Luke quotes Psalm 31:5.

nodes.label: The centurion: 'Certainly this was a righteous man'
nodes.statement: When the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God and said, 'Certainly this was a righteous man.'
nodes.note: Matthew 27:54 and Mark 15:39 record the centurion saying 'truly this was the Son of God'; Luke records 'righteous/innocent'.

nodes.label: Joseph of Arimathea had not consented to their counsel
nodes.statement: Joseph, a member of the council from the Jewish city of Arimathea, was a good and righteous man who had not consented to their counsel and deed, and was waiting for God's Kingdom.
nodes.note: Luke alone: the non-consent to the council's deed and the waiting for the Kingdom; Mark 15:43 makes him a prominent bouleutes.

nodes.label: The women prepared spices and rested on the Sabbath
nodes.statement: The women returned from the tomb and prepared spices and ointments, and on the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.
nodes.note: Mark 16:1 has the women buy spices after the Sabbath; Luke has them prepare spices before it and rest on the Sabbath itself.

nodes.label: The women brought burial spices they had prepared to the tomb at early dawn on the first day of the week
nodes.statement: On the first day of the week, at early dawn, the women came to the tomb bringing the spices which they had prepared (24:1).

nodes.label: Two men in dazzling clothing appeared to the women at the tomb
nodes.statement: While the women were perplexed at the empty tomb, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing and asked why they seek the living among the dead (24:4-5).

nodes.label: The women reported the empty tomb to the eleven and were not believed
nodes.statement: The women returned from the tomb and told all these things to the eleven and to all the rest, but the words seemed to them nonsense and they did not believe them (24:9-11).

nodes.label: The women at the tomb were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James
nodes.statement: The women were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, with the other women with them, who told these things to the apostles (24:10).

nodes.label: Peter ran to the tomb and saw the linen strips lying by themselves
nodes.statement: Peter got up, ran to the tomb, stooped and looked in, saw the strips of linen (othonia) lying by themselves, and went home wondering (24:12); the verse is omitted by Codex Bezae and the Old Latin tradition.

nodes.label: Emmaus was a village sixty stadia from Jerusalem
nodes.statement: Two of them were going that very day to a village named Emmaus, which was sixty stadia (about 11 km) from Jerusalem (24:13); some manuscripts (א original hand, K*, Θ, Π, 079) read 'a hundred sixty stadia' instead, and the village's identification is disputed.

nodes.label: The risen Jesus walked unrecognized with the two to Emmaus and was recognized in the breaking of bread
nodes.statement: While the two talked, Jesus himself came near and went with them unrecognized; at table in Emmaus he took the bread, blessed, broke it and gave it to them, their eyes were opened, they recognized him, and he vanished out of their sight (24:15-31).

nodes.label: One of the two on the Emmaus road was named Cleopas
nodes.statement: One of the two disciples walking to Emmaus answered Jesus and was named Cleopas (24:18); his companion is unnamed.

nodes.label: The two returned to Jerusalem and were told the Lord had appeared to Simon
nodes.statement: The two rose that very hour, returned to Jerusalem, found the eleven gathered with those with them, and were told 'The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon' (24:33-34).

nodes.label: The risen Jesus appeared to the gathered disciples in Jerusalem, showed his hands and feet and ate broiled fish
nodes.statement: While they spoke, Jesus himself stood among them in Jerusalem; he invited them to touch him, 'for a spirit doesn't have flesh and bones', showed his hands and feet, and ate a piece of broiled fish (and honeycomb in Byzantine witnesses) before them (24:36-43).

nodes.label: Jesus told the disciples to wait in Jerusalem until clothed with power from on high
nodes.statement: Jesus told the disciples: 'I send out the promise of my Father on you. But wait in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high' (24:49).

nodes.label: Jesus led the disciples out as far as Bethany and was carried up into heaven
nodes.statement: Jesus led them out as far as Bethany, lifted up his hands and blessed them, and while blessing them withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven (24:50-51); 'and was carried up into heaven' is omitted by the Sinaiticus original hand and the Western witnesses.

nodes.label: The disciples returned to Jerusalem and were continually in the temple blessing God
nodes.statement: They worshiped him, returned to Jerusalem with great joy, and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God (24:52-53).
Mark attributed a combined quotation - Malachi 3:1 ('Behold, I send my messenger before your face') and Isaiah 40:3 ('the voice of one crying in the wilderness') - to Isaiah the prophet.
nodes.label: Mark 1:2-3 combined quotation under Isaiah's name

nodes.statement: John preached that one mightier than he was coming, whose sandal's thong he was not worthy to stoop down and loosen.
nodes.label: John unworthy to loosen the sandal's thong

nodes.statement: Jesus was in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan; he was with the wild animals, and angels served him.
nodes.label: Forty days tempted by Satan, with the wild animals

nodes.statement: On a Sabbath Jesus taught in the synagogue at Capernaum, and the congregation was astonished, for he taught as one having authority and not as the scribes.
nodes.label: Sabbath teaching in the Capernaum synagogue

nodes.statement: In the Capernaum synagogue Jesus rebuked an unclean spirit, and it came out of a man, amazing the congregation.
nodes.label: Exorcism of an unclean spirit in the Capernaum synagogue

nodes.statement: Unable to come near Jesus for the crowd, the paralytic's carriers dug through the roof where he was and lowered the mat the paralytic lay on.
nodes.label: Roof dug open and the paralytic lowered

nodes.statement: Levi the son of Alphaeus sat at the tax office (telonion) and was called by Jesus to follow him.
nodes.label: Levi son of Alphaeus at the tax office

nodes.statement: David ate the showbread, which is lawful for priests alone, 'in the days of Abiathar the high priest'.
nodes.label: The showbread episode 'in the days of Abiathar the high priest'
The Pharisees conspired with the Herodians
nodes.statement: The Pharisees went out and immediately conspired with the Herodians against Jesus, how they might destroy him.

nodes.label: Crowds from Idumaea, Tyre and Sidon
nodes.statement: A great multitude followed Jesus from Galilee, Judea, Jerusalem, Idumaea, beyond the Jordan, and those from around Tyre and Sidon.

nodes.label: A small boat kept near Jesus
nodes.statement: Because of the crowd Jesus told his disciples that a small boat should stay near him, so that they would not press on him; he had healed many, and the sick pressed on him to touch him.

nodes.label: Unclean spirits cry "Son of God"
nodes.statement: Unclean spirits, whenever they saw Jesus, fell down before him and cried "You are the Son of God!", and he sternly warned them not to make him known.

nodes.label: Boanerges, "sons of thunder"
nodes.statement: Jesus gave James and John the name Boanerges, which means "Sons of Thunder" - an Aramaic name whose etymology is disputed.

nodes.label: The crowd gathered so they could not eat bread
nodes.statement: Jesus came into a house and the multitude came together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.

nodes.label: His friends went to seize him, "He is insane"
nodes.statement: When his friends (his family) heard it, they went out to seize Jesus, for they said "He is insane".

nodes.label: Scribes from Jerusalem: "He has Beelzebul"
nodes.statement: Scribes who came down from Jerusalem said "He has Beelzebul" and "By the prince of the demons he casts out the demons".

nodes.label: Parables hide the mystery; Isaiah 6 quoted
nodes.statement: To those outside everything is told in parables, 'that seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest perhaps they should turn again, and their sins should be forgiven them' (Isaiah 6:9-10).

nodes.label: The seed grows by itself: blade, ear, full grain, sickle
nodes.statement: Seed sown on the earth springs up and grows without the farmer's knowing how - first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear - and when the fruit is ripe he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.

nodes.label: Other small boats on the crossing
nodes.statement: Other small boats were also with Jesus in the boat on the crossing of the sea.

nodes.label: Asleep in the stern on a cushion
nodes.statement: Jesus was in the stern of the boat, asleep on a cushion.

nodes.label: "Peace! Be still!" - the wind ceased
nodes.statement: Jesus awoke, rebuked the wind and said to the sea 'Peace! Be still!', and the wind ceased and there was a great calm.

nodes.label: Mark 5:1 sets the exorcism in the country of the Gadarenes
nodes.statement: Mark 5:1 sets the event in the country of the Gadarenes (Gerasenes in the oldest manuscripts), on the far side of the Sea of Galilee.

nodes.label: One man with an unclean spirit came from the tombs
nodes.statement: A man with an unclean spirit came out of the tombs to meet Jesus - one man, where Matthew tells of two demoniacs.

nodes.label: The demoniac could not be bound and cut himself with stones
nodes.statement: Nobody could bind the demoniac any more, not even with chains; night and day among the tombs and in the mountains he cried out and cut himself with stones.

nodes.label: The man named the demons 'Legion, for we are many'
nodes.statement: Asked his name, the man answered 'My name is Legion, for we are many' - the Greek transliterates Latin legio, a Roman military unit.

nodes.label: About two thousand pigs rushed into the sea and were drowned
nodes.statement: The unclean spirits entered a herd of about two thousand pigs feeding on the mountainside, which rushed down the steep bank into the sea and were drowned.

nodes.label: The healed man proclaimed in the Decapolis
nodes.statement: The healed man went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone marveled.

nodes.label: Jairus, one of the rulers of the synagogue, begged for his dying daughter
nodes.statement: Jairus, one of the rulers (archisynagogoi) of the synagogue, fell at Jesus's feet and begged him to come and lay his hands on his little daughter, who was at the point of death.

nodes.label: The woman had spent all she had on many physicians and grew worse
nodes.statement: The woman with the twelve-year flow of blood had suffered much under many physicians, had spent all she had, and grew worse rather than better.

nodes.label: Only Peter, James and John followed into the house
nodes.statement: Jesus allowed no one to follow him into the synagogue ruler's house except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.

nodes.label: 'Talitha cumi' - Aramaic words to the girl
nodes.statement: Taking the girl by the hand, Jesus said 'Talitha cumi', which Mark translates 'Little girl, I tell you, get up' - a transliterated Aramaic phrase.

nodes.label: The girl was twelve years old and rose and walked
nodes.statement: The girl rose up and walked immediately, for she was twelve years old.

nodes.label: The Nazarenes called Jesus himself 'the carpenter', the son of Mary
nodes.statement: The Nazarenes asked 'Isn't this the carpenter (tekton), the son of Mary?' - calling Jesus himself the building craftsman, not, as in Matthew, the carpenter's son.

nodes.label: In Nazareth he could do no mighty work because of their unbelief
nodes.statement: In Nazareth he could do no mighty work, except laying his hands on a few sick people; and he marveled because of their unbelief.

nodes.label: He sent the twelve out two by two with authority over unclean spirits
nodes.statement: Jesus called the twelve and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over the unclean spirits.

nodes.label: For the journey: a staff, sandals and one tunic permitted
nodes.statement: He commanded them to take nothing for the journey except a staff only - no bread, no wallet, no money in the purse - but to wear sandals and not put on two tunics.

nodes.label: The twelve anointed many sick people with oil
nodes.statement: The twelve went out, preached that people should repent, cast out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.

nodes.label: Mark calls Herod 'king' when Jesus's fame reaches him
nodes.statement: Mark 6:14 calls Herod 'king' ('King Herod heard this') - the ruler Mark names king is Antipas, whom Matthew and Josephus call tetrarch.

nodes.label: Herod feared John as a righteous and holy man and heard him gladly
nodes.statement: Herod feared John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, kept him safe, heard him gladly, and did many things (at his word).

nodes.label: Herod swore to give the girl up to half of his kingdom
nodes.statement: Herod swore to the dancing girl: 'Whatever you shall ask of me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom.'

nodes.label: Herod sent a speculatore, a soldier of his guard, to behead John
nodes.statement: The king sent out a speculatore (σπεκουλάτωρ, a soldier of his guard), who beheaded John in the prison.

nodes.label: 'Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii of bread?'
nodes.statement: The disciples answered: 'Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread, and give them something to eat?'

nodes.label: The crowd sat down on the green grass
nodes.statement: Jesus commanded the crowd to sit down in groups on the green grass - a seasonal detail Mark alone records.

nodes.label: They sat in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties
nodes.statement: The crowd sat down in ranks (prisiai, garden beds), by hundreds and by fifties.

nodes.label: He sent the disciples ahead by boat toward Bethsaida
nodes.statement: He made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he sent the crowd away.

nodes.label: The sick were carried on mats and laid in the marketplaces
nodes.statement: People ran through the whole region carrying the sick on mats, and laid them in the marketplaces of villages, cities and countryside, begging to touch the fringe of his garment.

nodes.label: Vessel washings of the purity tradition
nodes.statement: Besides hand-washing before eating and bathing after the marketplace, the tradition required washings (immersions) of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels and couches (couches per some manuscripts).

nodes.label: Mark's comment: all foods thus declared clean
nodes.statement: Mark's parenthetical comment: because what enters goes into the stomach and out, Jesus 'thus purifying all foods' - all foods are declared clean.

nodes.label: A Greek, a Syrophoenician by race, begged for her daughter
nodes.statement: A Greek woman, a Syrophoenician by race, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, came and fell at Jesus' feet and begged him to cast the demon out of her daughter.

nodes.label: The Syrophoenician's daughter healed at a distance
nodes.statement: Jesus told the woman the demon had gone out of her daughter, and she found the child lying on the bed, healed, when she went home. (Miracle claim, recorded honestly; the setting evidence never attests the miracle.)

nodes.label: From Tyre and Sidon through the Decapolis to the sea of Galilee
nodes.statement: Departing the borders of Tyre and Sidon, Jesus came to the sea of Galilee through the middle of the region of the Decapolis.

nodes.label: A deaf man with a speech impediment brought to Jesus
nodes.statement: In the Decapolis region people brought Jesus one who was deaf and had an impediment in his speech, and begged him to lay his hand on him.

nodes.label: Fingers in ears, spittle touched to the tongue
nodes.statement: Jesus used physical healing gestures: he took the man aside, put his fingers into his ears, spat, and touched his tongue.

nodes.label: 'Ephphatha': an Aramaic word Mark preserves with translation
nodes.statement: Jesus addressed the deaf man with the word 'Ephphatha' - an Aramaic word, which Mark preserves and translates 'Be opened'.

nodes.label: The deaf man's ears opened and speech restored
nodes.statement: Immediately the man's ears were opened, the impediment of his tongue was released, and he spoke clearly. (Miracle claim, recorded honestly; the setting evidence never attests the miracle.)

nodes.label: About four thousand ate
nodes.statement: Those who had eaten were about four thousand; then he sent them away.

nodes.label: He came into the region of Dalmanutha
nodes.statement: He entered into the boat with his disciples and came into the region (parts) of Dalmanutha, an otherwise unattested place name.

nodes.label: The Pharisees sought a sign from heaven
nodes.statement: The Pharisees came out and began to question Jesus, seeking from him a sign from heaven, and testing him.

nodes.label: 'No sign will be given to this generation'
nodes.statement: Sighing deeply in his spirit, Jesus said: 'Why does this generation seek a sign? Most certainly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.'

nodes.label: Only one loaf in the boat
nodes.statement: The disciples had forgotten to take bread, and they had no more than one loaf in the boat with them.

nodes.label: 'Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod'
nodes.statement: Jesus warned the disciples: 'Take heed: beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod' - Herod here being Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee.

nodes.label: A blind man brought to Jesus at Bethsaida
nodes.statement: He came to Bethsaida, and people brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch him. (Mark only.)

nodes.label: Spittle on the eyes, hands laid on, out of the village
nodes.statement: Jesus took the blind man by the hand out of the village, spat on his eyes, and laid his hands on him, asking if he saw anything.

nodes.label: The Bethsaida blind man restored after a second laying on of hands
nodes.statement: First he saw men like trees walking; after Jesus laid his hands on his eyes again, he looked intently, was restored, and saw everyone clearly. (Miracle claim, recorded honestly; the setting evidence never attests the miracle.)

nodes.label: John the Baptizer, Elijah, or one of the prophets
nodes.statement: People identified Jesus as John the Baptizer, as Elijah, or as one of the prophets.

nodes.label: Peter answered, 'You are the Christ'
nodes.statement: When Jesus asked 'But who do you say that I am?', Peter answered, 'You are the Christ.'

nodes.label: His clothing became glistening white, beyond any launderer's work
nodes.statement: At the transfiguration Jesus's clothing became glistening, exceedingly white, like snow - 'such as no launderer on earth can whiten them'.

nodes.label: A cloud overshadows them and a voice from the cloud speaks
nodes.statement: A cloud came overshadowing them, and a voice out of the cloud said, 'This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.'

nodes.label: Tell no one what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen
nodes.statement: Coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded Peter, James and John to tell no one what things they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
nodes.note: Modern scholarship calls this motif the 'messianic secret' (Wrede); that is a modern theory and stays in notes.md, not in the graph as evidence.

nodes.label: The boy with the mute and deaf spirit
nodes.statement: A father brought his son, possessed from childhood by a mute and deaf spirit that convulsed him, made him foam at the mouth and grind his teeth, and often threw him into fire and water; Jesus rebuked the spirit and it came out.
nodes.note: Mark describes the spirit as mute and deaf and gives the symptoms and their duration from childhood; Matthew 17:15 calls the boy 'moonstruck' (seleniazetai). A difference between Gospels, recorded with related_to.

nodes.label: This kind comes out only by prayer (and fasting)
nodes.statement: 'This kind can come out by nothing, except by prayer and fasting' - deliverance from this kind of spirit was linked to prayer and fasting.
nodes.note: The parallel Matthew 17:21 is 'believed to have been assimilated from Mark' (fetched Wikipedia 'List of omitted Bible verses') and is omitted in Matthew by the original hand of Sinaiticus and by Vaticanus; WEB prints it in both Gospels.

nodes.label: First of all = last of all and servant of all
nodes.statement: 'If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.'

nodes.label: The stranger casting out demons in Jesus's name
nodes.statement: John reported that the disciples had forbidden a man who did not follow them from casting out demons in Jesus's name; Jesus said not to forbid him, for no one doing a mighty work in his name could quickly speak evil of him.

nodes.label: The Isaiah 66:24 refrain on Gehenna
nodes.statement: Mark quotes Isaiah 66:24 three times as a refrain on Gehenna: 'where their worm doesn't die, and the fire is not quenched.'

nodes.label: Everyone salted with fire; every sacrifice seasoned with salt
nodes.statement: 'Everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt' - salt belonged to the sacrificial ritual the saying draws on.

nodes.label: Pharisees test Jesus: is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?
nodes.statement: Pharisees came to Jesus, testing him, and asked whether it is lawful for a man to divorce his wife.
nodes.note: Mark asks the question without Matthew's qualifier 'for any cause' (Matthew 19:3).

nodes.label: Divorce and remarriage as adultery - no exception clause
nodes.statement: 'Whoever divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery against her' - Mark states the rule with no exception clause.
nodes.note: Matthew 19:9 excepts 'for sexual immorality' and adds a clause about the divorced woman's remarriage; a difference between Gospels, recorded with related_to, never evidence.

nodes.label: A woman who divorces her husband
nodes.statement: 'If a woman herself divorces her husband, and marries another, she commits adultery' - Mark's wording presumes a woman could divorce her husband, a case Matthew does not address.
nodes.note: Josephus says Salome's divorce of Costobarus was 'not according to the Jewish laws' (complicates edge), and the fetched Wikipedia 'Women in Judaism' states that in biblical times a wife could not divorce a husband without his consent; the tension is recorded, not smoothed away.

nodes.label: 'Do not defraud' in the commandment list
nodes.statement: Mark's list of commandments includes 'Do not defraud' (me apostereseis), which Matthew's list does not have.

nodes.label: 'Taking up the cross' in the call to the rich man
nodes.statement: Jesus tells the man to come and follow him, 'taking up the cross' - a detail Matthew omits in the parallel (Matthew 19:21).

nodes.label: James and John ask for the seats at right and left
nodes.statement: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, asked Jesus to grant them to sit, one at his right hand and one at his left hand, in his glory.

nodes.label: Great = your servant; first = bondservant of all
nodes.statement: 'Whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant, and whoever of you wants to become first among you shall be bondservant of all.'

nodes.label: Bartimaeus son of Timaeus cries out at Jericho
nodes.statement: At Jericho, Bartimaeus son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, sat by the road and cried out, 'Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me.'

nodes.label: Bartimaeus receives his sight
nodes.statement: Bartimaeus asked, 'Rabboni, that I may see again'; Jesus said, 'Go your way. Your faith has made you well', and immediately he received his sight and followed him on the way.
nodes.note: A healing; searched honestly and found no external evidence - the setting evidence is attached to claim:mk-10-46-47-bartimaeus and claim:mt-20-29-out-of-jericho.

nodes.label: A young donkey on which no one had sat
nodes.statement: The disciples found a young donkey (colt) tied, on which no one had ever sat, and brought it after saying 'The Lord needs him'.

nodes.label: Acclamation of the coming kingdom of David
nodes.statement: The crowd acclaimed 'Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that is coming in the name of the Lord!' at the entry to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Entry-day temple visit, then Bethany
nodes.statement: On the entry day Jesus entered the Temple, looked around at everything, and went out to Bethany with the Twelve because it was already evening; Mark places the cleansing the next day (11:15).

nodes.label: No figs because it was not the season
nodes.statement: The roadside fig tree in leaf had nothing but fig leaves, 'for it was not the season for figs'.

nodes.label: No one allowed to carry a vessel through the Temple
nodes.statement: During the cleansing he would not allow anyone to carry a container (skeuos) through the Temple courts.

nodes.label: Quotation preserving 'for all the nations'
nodes.statement: He taught: 'Is it not written, My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations?' (Isaiah 56:7, with the phrase 'for all the nations' Mark preserves) and 'a den of robbers' (Jeremiah 7:11).

nodes.label: Chief priests and scribes sought to destroy him
nodes.statement: The chief priests and the scribes heard it and sought how they might destroy him, fearing him because all the multitude was astonished at his teaching.

nodes.label: The Shema quoted in full
nodes.statement: Jesus opened his answer with the full Shema, 'Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one' (Deuteronomy 6:4), before the love command (Deuteronomy 6:5).

nodes.label: The scribe agrees; love exceeds sacrifices
nodes.statement: The scribe agreed that loving God with all one's heart, understanding, soul and strength, and one's neighbor as oneself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices; Jesus told him he was not far from the kingdom of God, and no one dared ask him any question after that.

nodes.label: Scribes seek long robes, greetings and best seats
nodes.statement: In his teaching he warned against scribes who like to walk in long robes, receive greetings in the marketplaces, and take the best seats in the synagogues and the best places at feasts.

nodes.label: Scribes who devour widows' houses
nodes.statement: He accused scribes who devour widows' houses and for a pretense make long prayers; they will receive greater condemnation.

nodes.label: The Temple treasury with collection chests
nodes.statement: He sat down opposite the treasury (gazophylakion) and saw the multitude casting money into it - the treasury was a place where worshipers deposited coin.

nodes.label: Two lepta, which make a quadrans
nodes.statement: A poor widow cast in two lepta, which together make a quadrans - the smallest coins in Judean circulation.

nodes.label: The widow gave all she had to live on
nodes.statement: The rich gave out of their abundance, but the widow out of her poverty gave all she had, her whole living.
The Temple complex of Jesus's day was built of great stones and had imposing buildings - the disciple points at 'what kind of stones and what kind of buildings'.
nodes.label: The Temple's great stones and buildings

nodes.statement: Peter, James, John and Andrew asked Jesus privately, as he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the Temple, when the foretold things would happen.
nodes.label: Four disciples asked privately on the Mount of Olives

nodes.statement: The night was divided into watches with named divisions: Mark lists evening, midnight, 'when the rooster crows' and morning - the Roman four-watch night, in which cockcrow was a standard time marker.
nodes.label: The night's named watch divisions (evening, midnight, cockcrow, morning)

nodes.statement: The ointment was pure nard, very costly, worth more than three hundred denarii; the woman broke the alabaster jar and poured it on Jesus's head.
nodes.label: Ointment of pure nard worth more than 300 denarii

nodes.statement: The chief priests, on hearing Judas, were glad and promised to give him money for delivering Jesus - Mark gives no amount.
nodes.label: The chief priests promised Judas money (no amount given)

nodes.statement: On the first day of unleavened bread, 'when they sacrificed the Passover', the Passover lambs were slaughtered in the Temple and eaten that evening in Jerusalem.
nodes.label: The Passover lambs were sacrificed in the Temple

nodes.statement: A man carrying a jar of water would meet the two disciples in the city, and they were to follow him into the house he entered.
nodes.label: A man carrying a jar of water as the sign

nodes.statement: The house had a large upper room, furnished and ready, where the Passover could be eaten reclining.
nodes.label: A large furnished upper room in the house

nodes.statement: Mark 14:27 quotes scripture with 'it is written': 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered' - Zechariah 13:7 without its opening 'O sword'.
nodes.label: Zechariah 13:7 quoted ('I will strike the shepherd')

nodes.statement: Jesus told Peter he would deny him three times 'before the rooster crows twice' - Mark specifies a second cockcrow within the night.
nodes.label: 'Before the rooster crows twice' - the second cockcrow

nodes.statement: Jesus's Gethsemane prayer addressed God as 'Abba, Father' - Mark preserves the Aramaic address alongside its Greek translation.
nodes.label: 'Abba, Father' - the Aramaic address preserved

nodes.statement: A young man wearing only a linen cloth followed Jesus at the arrest; the men seized him, and he left the linen cloth and fled naked.
nodes.label: The young man who fled naked (Mark only)

nodes.statement: At the hearing, witnesses testified that Jesus said: 'I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and in three days I will build another made without hands.'
nodes.label: The 'destroy this temple made with hands' saying reported
Barabbas was bound with insurgents who committed murder
nodes.statement: There was one called Barabbas, bound with his fellow insurgents, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.

nodes.label: The soldiers clothed Jesus in a purple cloak
nodes.statement: The soldiers clothed him with purple (a purple cloak) inside the praetorium, before leading him out to crucify him.

nodes.label: Simon of Cyrene was the father of Alexander and Rufus
nodes.statement: Simon of Cyrene, whom the soldiers compelled to carry the cross, was the father of Alexander and Rufus.

nodes.label: Wine mixed with myrrh offered at Golgotha
nodes.statement: They offered Jesus wine mixed with myrrh to drink at Golgotha, but he did not take it.

nodes.label: The crucifixion at the third hour
nodes.statement: It was the third hour (about nine in the morning, reckoned from sunrise) when they crucified him.

nodes.label: Isaiah 53:12 quoted at the crucifixion: 'He was counted with transgressors'
nodes.statement: At the crucifixion Mark 15:28 quotes the Scripture, 'He was counted with transgressors' (Isaiah 53:12) - a quotation in the text (reworded by reviewer 5 to neutral wording; the verse itself is absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and other witnesses, recorded in the passage variants).

nodes.label: The ninth-hour cry 'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani'
nodes.statement: At the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, 'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?' - 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' (Psalm 22:1 in Aramaic).

nodes.label: The watching women named: Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James the less and Joses, Salome
nodes.statement: Women watched the crucifixion from afar: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome, who had followed and served him in Galilee.

nodes.label: The burial on Preparation Day, the day before the Sabbath
nodes.statement: When evening had come it was the Preparation Day (paraskeue), that is, the day before the Sabbath.

nodes.label: Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent council member (bouleutes)
nodes.statement: Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member (bouleutes) who was also looking for God's Kingdom, boldly went in to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body.

nodes.label: Pilate verified the death with the centurion and granted the body
nodes.statement: Pilate marveled that Jesus was already dead, summoned the centurion, asked him whether he had been dead long, and on learning it granted the body to Joseph.

nodes.label: The women buy spices, find the tomb open, and flee in fear
nodes.statement: After the Sabbath Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Salome bought spices to anoint him; very early on the first day of the week, at sunrise, they found the great stone rolled back and a young man in a white robe inside who told them 'He has risen; he is not here' and to tell his disciples and Peter that he goes before them into Galilee; they fled from the tomb and said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.

nodes.label: Appearances of the risen Jesus (longer ending)
nodes.statement: The risen Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons, then in another form to two of them walking into the country, then to the eleven at table; those who heard did not believe.

nodes.label: The commission and the signs of believers (longer ending)
nodes.statement: The risen Jesus commissioned the eleven to go into all the world and preach the gospel to the whole creation, saying that he who believes and is baptized will be saved, and that signs will accompany believers: casting out demons, speaking new languages, taking up serpents, drinking deadly things unharmed, and healing the sick by the laying on of hands.

nodes.label: The ascension and the preaching everywhere (longer ending)
nodes.statement: The Lord, after speaking to them, was received up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God; and the disciples went out and preached everywhere.

nodes.label: Jesus is called the Christ (Messiah), the son of David and the son of Abraham.
nodes.statement: Jesus is called the Christ (Messiah), the son of David and the son of Abraham.

nodes.label: Abraham became the father of Isaac; Isaac of Jacob; Jacob of Judah and his brothers.
nodes.statement: Abraham became the father of Isaac; Isaac of Jacob; Jacob of Judah and his brothers.

nodes.label: Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar; Perez of Hezron; Hezron of Ram.
nodes.statement: Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar; Perez of Hezron; Hezron of Ram.

nodes.label: Ram became the father of Amminadab; Amminadab of Nahshon; Nahshon of Salmon.
nodes.statement: Ram became the father of Amminadab; Amminadab of Nahshon; Nahshon of Salmon.

nodes.label: Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab; Boaz of Obed by Ruth; Obed of Jesse.
nodes.statement: Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab; Boaz of Obed by Ruth; Obed of Jesse.

nodes.label: David was king, the founder of the royal line called the 'house of David'.
nodes.statement: David was king, the founder of the royal line called the 'house of David'.

nodes.label: Jesse became the father of King David; David the father of Solomon by her who had been Uriah's wife.
nodes.statement: Jesse became the father of King David; David the father of Solomon by her who had been Uriah's wife.

nodes.label: Solomon was a king in this line.
nodes.statement: Solomon was a king in this line.

nodes.label: Abijah was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Abijah was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Asa was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Asa was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Rehoboam was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Rehoboam was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Solomon became the father of Rehoboam; Rehoboam of Abijah; Abijah of Asa.
nodes.statement: Solomon became the father of Rehoboam; Rehoboam of Abijah; Abijah of Asa.

nodes.label: Asa became the father of Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat of Joram; Joram of Uzziah.
nodes.statement: Asa became the father of Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat of Joram; Joram of Uzziah.

nodes.label: Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Joram (Jehoram) was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Joram (Jehoram) was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Uzziah (Azariah) was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Uzziah (Azariah) was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Ahaz was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Ahaz was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Hezekiah was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Hezekiah was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Jotham was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Jotham was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Uzziah became the father of Jotham; Jotham of Ahaz; Ahaz of Hezekiah.
nodes.statement: Uzziah became the father of Jotham; Jotham of Ahaz; Ahaz of Hezekiah.

nodes.label: Amon was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Amon was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Hezekiah became the father of Manasseh; Manasseh of Amon; Amon of Josiah.
nodes.statement: Hezekiah became the father of Manasseh; Manasseh of Amon; Amon of Josiah.

nodes.label: Josiah was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Josiah was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Manasseh was king of Judah.
nodes.statement: Manasseh was king of Judah.

nodes.label: Judah underwent an exile to Babylon, beginning with Nebuchadnezzar's capture of Jerusalem in 597 BCE.
nodes.statement: Judah underwent an exile to Babylon, beginning with Nebuchadnezzar's capture of Jerusalem in 597 BCE.

nodes.label: Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) was king of Judah when Babylon took Jerusalem (597 BCE).
nodes.statement: Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) was king of Judah when Babylon took Jerusalem (597 BCE).

nodes.label: Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the exile to Babylon.
nodes.statement: Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the exile to Babylon.

nodes.label: After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah became the father of Shealtiel; Shealtiel of Zerubbabel.
nodes.statement: After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah became the father of Shealtiel; Shealtiel of Zerubbabel.

nodes.label: After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah's line continued in Judah through Shealtiel and Zerubbabel.
nodes.statement: After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah's line continued in Judah through Shealtiel and Zerubbabel.

nodes.label: Zerubbabel became the father of Abiud; Abiud of Eliakim; Eliakim of Azor.
nodes.statement: Zerubbabel became the father of Abiud; Abiud of Eliakim; Eliakim of Azor.

nodes.label: Azor became the father of Zadok; Zadok of Achim; Achim of Eliud.
nodes.statement: Azor became the father of Zadok; Zadok of Achim; Achim of Eliud.

nodes.label: Eliud became the father of Eleazar; Eleazar of Matthan; Matthan of Jacob.
nodes.statement: Eliud became the father of Eleazar; Eleazar of Matthan; Matthan of Jacob.

nodes.label: Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
nodes.statement: Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

nodes.label: Matthew presents the genealogy as three blocks of fourteen generations: Abraham to David, David to the exile, exile to the Christ.
nodes.statement: Matthew presents the genealogy as three blocks of fourteen generations: Abraham to David, David to the exile, exile to the Christ.

nodes.label: Mary was found to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit before she and Joseph came together.
nodes.statement: Mary was found to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit before she and Joseph came together.

nodes.label: In Jewish custom, a betrothed woman could be 'put away' - released only by a divorce - by her husband.
nodes.statement: In Jewish custom, a betrothed woman could be 'put away' - released only by a divorce - by her husband.

nodes.label: An angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, telling him to take Mary as his wife and to name the child Jesus.
nodes.statement: An angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, telling him to take Mary as his wife and to name the child Jesus.

nodes.label: Matthew quotes Isaiah 7:14 ('Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall give birth to a son. They shall call his name Immanuel') as spoken by the Lord through the prophet.
nodes.statement: Matthew quotes Isaiah 7:14 ('Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall give birth to a son. They shall call his name Immanuel') as spoken by the Lord through the prophet.

nodes.label: Jesus was born of Mary, and Joseph named him Jesus.
nodes.statement: Jesus was born of Mary, and Joseph named him Jesus.
Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king.
nodes.label: Jesus born in Bethlehem of Judea

nodes.statement: Herod the Great was king over Judea at the time of Jesus' birth.
nodes.label: Herod the Great was king over Judea

nodes.statement: Magi (wise men) from the east came to Jerusalem seeking the newborn king of the Jews.
nodes.label: Magi came from the east to Jerusalem

nodes.statement: The Magi said they saw his star in the east and came to worship the one born king of the Jews.
nodes.label: The Magi saw his star in the east

nodes.statement: Herod gathered the chief priests and scribes of the people to ask where the Christ was to be born.
nodes.label: Herod consulted the chief priests and scribes

nodes.statement: The chief priests cited the prophet Micah, who located the coming ruler in Bethlehem of Judea.
nodes.label: Micah located the ruler in Bethlehem

nodes.statement: The Magi offered the child gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh.
nodes.label: Gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh

nodes.statement: Joseph fled by night with the child and his mother into Egypt and stayed there until Herod's death.
nodes.label: Flight of the family into Egypt

nodes.statement: Matthew applied Hosea 11:1, 'Out of Egypt I called my son,' to Jesus' return from Egypt.
nodes.label: Hosea 11:1 applied to the return from Egypt

nodes.statement: Herod ordered the killing of all the male children in Bethlehem and its surrounding region aged two years and under.
nodes.label: Herod killed the boys of Bethlehem aged two and under

nodes.statement: Herod died after the Magi's visit and before Joseph's return from Egypt.
nodes.label: Herod the Great died

nodes.statement: Archelaus son of Herod was ruling over Judea when Joseph returned from Egypt.
nodes.label: Archelaus ruled Judea after Herod

nodes.statement: Fearing Archelaus in Judea, Joseph settled the family in a city called Nazareth in Galilee.
nodes.label: Joseph settled the family in Nazareth

nodes.statement: John the Baptist appeared, preaching in the wilderness of Judea.
nodes.label: John preached in the wilderness of Judea

nodes.statement: John preached repentance, announcing that the Kingdom of Heaven was at hand.
nodes.label: John's preaching of repentance and the near Kingdom

nodes.statement: Matthew applied Isaiah 40:3, 'the voice of one crying in the wilderness', to John.
nodes.label: Isaiah 40:3 applied to John

nodes.statement: John wore clothing made of camel's hair with a leather belt around his waist.
nodes.label: John's garment of camel's hair and leather belt

nodes.statement: John ate locusts and wild honey.
nodes.label: John's diet of locusts and wild honey

nodes.statement: People from Jerusalem, all Judea and the region around the Jordan went out to John.
nodes.label: Crowds from Jerusalem, Judea and the Jordan went out to John

nodes.statement: John baptized confessing sinners in the Jordan River.
nodes.label: Baptism of confessing crowds in the Jordan

nodes.statement: Pharisees and Sadducees came out to John's baptism.
nodes.label: Pharisees and Sadducees came to John's baptism

nodes.statement: Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.
nodes.label: Jesus came from Galilee to be baptized by John
Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness after his baptism.
nodes.statement: Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness after his baptism.

nodes.label: Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights in the wilderness.
nodes.statement: Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights in the wilderness.

nodes.label: The tempter challenged Jesus to command stones to become bread.
nodes.statement: The tempter challenged Jesus to command stones to become bread.

nodes.label: The devil set Jesus on the pinnacle of the Temple in the holy city (Jerusalem).
nodes.statement: The devil set Jesus on the pinnacle of the Temple in the holy city (Jerusalem).

nodes.label: From an exceedingly high mountain the devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
nodes.statement: From an exceedingly high mountain the devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.

nodes.label: John the Baptist was delivered up (arrested) before Jesus withdrew into Galilee.
nodes.statement: John the Baptist was delivered up (arrested) before Jesus withdrew into Galilee.

nodes.label: Jesus left Nazareth and made Capernaum, by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali, his home.
nodes.statement: Jesus left Nazareth and made Capernaum, by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali, his home.

nodes.label: Matthew quotes Isaiah 9:1-2, on the land of Zebulun and Naphtali, toward the sea, Galilee of the Gentiles.
nodes.statement: Matthew quotes Isaiah 9:1-2, on the land of Zebulun and Naphtali, toward the sea, Galilee of the Gentiles.

nodes.label: Jesus began to preach, 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.'
nodes.statement: Jesus began to preach, 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.'

nodes.label: Simon (Peter) and Andrew, fishermen casting a net into the Sea of Galilee, were called by Jesus to follow him.
nodes.statement: Simon (Peter) and Andrew, fishermen casting a net into the Sea of Galilee, were called by Jesus to follow him.

nodes.label: James the son of Zebedee and John, mending nets in their boat with their father Zebedee, were called by Jesus.
nodes.statement: James the son of Zebedee and John, mending nets in their boat with their father Zebedee, were called by Jesus.

nodes.label: Jesus taught in the synagogues throughout Galilee.
nodes.statement: Jesus taught in the synagogues throughout Galilee.

nodes.label: The report about Jesus went out into all Syria, and the sick were brought to him.
nodes.statement: The report about Jesus went out into all Syria, and the sick were brought to him.

nodes.label: Great crowds followed Jesus from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and beyond the Jordan.
nodes.statement: Great crowds followed Jesus from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and beyond the Jordan.
Jesus went up onto a mountain and taught his disciples who came to him there.
nodes.label: Jesus taught the disciples on a mountain

nodes.statement: Salt was a common household commodity, and salt could lose its flavor and become useless.
nodes.label: Household salt that could lose its flavor

nodes.statement: Cities were located on hills, where they could be seen from afar and could not be hidden.
nodes.label: Cities set on hills

nodes.statement: Households lit rooms with small oil lamps set on a lamp stand.
nodes.label: Oil lamps set on lamp stands

nodes.statement: The law existed as a written Hebrew text in which the smallest letters and strokes were regarded as binding.
nodes.label: The written law and its smallest letters

nodes.statement: The scribes and Pharisees were the recognized religious teachers of the Jews.
nodes.label: Scribes and Pharisees as religious teachers

nodes.statement: The council (Sanhedrin) could put a man on trial before judges in Jerusalem.
nodes.label: The council (Sanhedrin) as a court

nodes.statement: Gehenna, the Valley of Hinnom near Jerusalem, was associated with fire and judgment.
nodes.label: Gehenna, the valley of fire

nodes.statement: Worshippers brought gifts and offerings to the altar at the Temple.
nodes.label: Gifts offered at the Temple altar

nodes.statement: An adversary could hand a debtor over to the officer, and the debtor was imprisoned until he paid the last small coin.
nodes.label: Imprisonment of debtors until payment

nodes.statement: The quadrans was the smallest Roman copper coin in circulation.
nodes.label: The quadrans, the last penny

nodes.statement: Divorce was carried out by giving the wife a written certificate of divorcement.
nodes.label: The written certificate of divorce

nodes.statement: People swore oaths by heaven, by earth, and by Jerusalem, the city of the great King.
nodes.label: Oaths by heaven, earth and Jerusalem

nodes.statement: The law required an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth as retribution for injury.
nodes.label: An eye for an eye in the law

nodes.statement: Ordinary dress consisted of an inner tunic and an outer cloak, and garments could be taken from a man in a lawsuit.
nodes.label: Tunic and cloak as ordinary dress

nodes.statement: Agents of Roman authority could compel a civilian to carry a burden for one mile.
nodes.label: Compelled carriage of burdens (angaria)

nodes.statement: Almsgiving (tzedakah) was a recognized religious duty among Jews, customarily performed publicly.
nodes.label: Almsgiving as a religious duty

nodes.statement: Prayer and almsgiving were performed publicly in synagogues and at street corners, standing.
nodes.label: Public prayer and almsgiving in synagogues and streets

nodes.statement: The word 'hypocrites' (hypokritai) literally meant stage actors, and theatres stood in Roman Galilee (e.g. at Sepphoris).
nodes.label: Hypocrites as stage actors; theatres in Galilee

nodes.statement: Giving in the Temple courts was connected with trumpet imagery: thirteen trumpet-shaped collection chests (shofarot) stood there.
nodes.label: Trumpet-shaped offering chests (shofarot) in the Temple

nodes.statement: Houses had an inner room (tameion, a storage chamber) where one could pray in private.
nodes.label: The inner room (tameion) of a house

nodes.statement: Gentile (pagan) prayers were characterized by much speaking and repetition.
nodes.label: Pagan prayer by much speaking and repetition

nodes.statement: Jesus taught his disciples a model prayer (the Lord's Prayer), fixed enough to be prayed as given.
nodes.label: The Lord's Prayer as a taught form of prayer

nodes.statement: The WEB text of Matthew 6:13 closes the prayer with the doxology 'For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever.'
nodes.label: The doxology at the end of the Lord's Prayer

nodes.statement: Fasting was a recognized religious practice, and some fasters made their fasting visible on their faces.
nodes.label: Fasting and its visible display

nodes.statement: Anointing the head with oil was a normal grooming practice.
nodes.label: Anointing the head with oil as grooming

nodes.statement: Thieves broke into houses by digging through the wall (mudbrick or earthen construction).
nodes.label: Thieves digging through house walls

nodes.statement: Wealth was laid up in goods subject to decay and theft: garments, metal objects and household stores.
nodes.label: Laying up treasure in goods on earth

nodes.statement: Stored garments were consumed by moths and stored metal by rust.
nodes.label: Moth and rust consuming stored goods

nodes.statement: The eye was conceived as the lamp of the body, in keeping with ancient ideas of vision and light.
nodes.label: The eye as the lamp of the body

nodes.statement: Mammon (Aramaic mamona) was a common Aramaic word for wealth and possessions.
nodes.label: Mammon: an Aramaic word for wealth

nodes.statement: Slaves served a household master in the Roman world, and a slave could not serve two masters.
nodes.label: Serving a master: slavery in the Roman world

nodes.statement: Food, drink and clothing were the constant daily concerns of ordinary households.
nodes.label: Daily concern for food, drink and clothing

nodes.statement: Farmers sowed, reaped and gathered produce into barns, while birds of the sky live without sowing, reaping or barns.
nodes.label: Sowing, reaping and barns; birds without farming

nodes.statement: Wild flowers ('lilies of the field') grew in the fields of Galilee.
nodes.label: The lilies of the field

nodes.statement: Solomon was proverbially arrayed in glory and wealth.
nodes.label: Solomon in all his glory

nodes.statement: Households baked in clay ovens fuelled with dried grass and other dried plants.
nodes.label: Clay ovens fuelled with dried plants

nodes.statement: Measure-for-measure reciprocity was a current principle in Jewish teaching.
nodes.label: Measure for measure

nodes.statement: Standardized measures of capacity were used in trade, and jars were marked with the measure they held.
nodes.label: Standard measures in trade

nodes.statement: Building used large wooden beams, and small splinters or chips of wood were a familiar household nuisance.
nodes.label: Wooden beams and splinters (speck and plank)

nodes.statement: Dogs and pigs lived around towns and villages as scavengers and were treated as unclean.
nodes.label: Dogs and pigs as scavengers

nodes.statement: Pearls were counted among the most precious and costly of goods.
nodes.label: Pearls as precious goods

nodes.statement: Bread was the daily staple, baked as round loaves whose shape could be imitated by stones.
nodes.label: Bread as the daily staple

nodes.statement: Fish was a common food in Galilee, and snakes were familiar dangers in the region.
nodes.label: Fish and serpents

nodes.statement: A golden rule in negative form was current in Jewish teaching, as in Hillel's saying and Tobit.
nodes.label: The golden rule in Jewish teaching

nodes.statement: Towns were entered through gates, some of them narrow, and broad roads led away from them.
nodes.label: Narrow gates and broad roads

nodes.statement: Prophets claiming divine commission appeared in Judea in this period.
nodes.label: False prophets as a known phenomenon

nodes.statement: Wolves lived in the region and preyed on sheep and flocks.
nodes.label: Wolves in the region

nodes.statement: Grapes, figs, thorns and thistles were familiar plants of Galilee and Judea.
nodes.label: Grapes, figs, thorns and thistles

nodes.statement: Axes were used to cut down trees, and useless wood was burned as fuel.
nodes.label: Axe and fire for useless trees

nodes.statement: Exorcists cast out demons using names and methods believed to be effective.
nodes.label: Exorcism as a known practice

nodes.statement: Houses were built on foundations of rock or of sand, and the choice of foundation decided their fate in storms.
nodes.label: Building on rock and sand

nodes.statement: Sudden rain floods in dry valleys struck houses and could destroy them.
nodes.label: Flash floods in the wadis

nodes.statement: The scribes were the customary teachers whose authority the crowds knew, and Jesus taught differently.
nodes.label: Scribes as the customary teachers
Great crowds followed Jesus down from the mountain
nodes.statement: When he came down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.

nodes.label: A leper came to Jesus asking to be made clean
nodes.statement: A leper came to Jesus and worshiped him, saying that he could make him clean if he wanted to.

nodes.label: Jesus touched the leper and cleansed him
nodes.statement: Jesus stretched out his hand and touched the leper, and the leprosy was cleansed.

nodes.label: The cleansed leper's offering that Moses commanded
nodes.statement: The cleansed leper was to tell nobody, show himself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony.

nodes.label: A centurion came to Jesus at Capernaum
nodes.statement: When Jesus came into Capernaum, a centurion came to him asking for his paralyzed servant.

nodes.label: The centurion commanded soldiers under authority
nodes.statement: The centurion was a man under authority with soldiers under himself, saying to one 'Go' and he goes, to another 'Come' and he comes.

nodes.label: Reclining at the banquet of the Kingdom with the patriarchs
nodes.statement: Many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven.

nodes.label: Peter's mother-in-law sick with fever in Peter's house
nodes.statement: When Jesus came into Peter's house in Capernaum, he saw his wife's mother lying sick with a fever; he touched her hand, the fever left her, and she got up and served him.

nodes.label: Many possessed with demons brought to Jesus at evening
nodes.statement: When evening came, they brought to him many possessed with demons, and he cast out the spirits with a word and healed all who were sick.

nodes.label: Matthew quotes Isaiah on taking our infirmities
nodes.statement: Matthew quotes Isaiah the prophet: 'He took our infirmities, and bore our diseases.'

nodes.label: Foxes have holes and birds have nests
nodes.statement: Foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.

nodes.label: Burying a father as a duty delaying discipleship
nodes.statement: A disciple asked to go first and bury his father; Jesus said to follow him and leave the dead to bury their own dead.

nodes.label: Jesus and his disciples crossed the sea in a boat
nodes.statement: Jesus got into a boat and his disciples followed him across the sea.

nodes.label: A violent storm suddenly came up on the sea
nodes.statement: A violent storm came up on the sea so suddenly that the boat was covered with the waves.

nodes.label: Crossing to the other side into the Gadarene/Gergesene country
nodes.statement: Jesus came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gergesenes (Gadarenes in most translations; the manuscripts differ).
nodes.note: Manuscripts differ: Gadarenes, Gerasenes or Gergesenes; the location is disputed (Gadara, Gerasa or Kursi).

nodes.label: Demoniacs coming out of the tombs
nodes.statement: Two men possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, so fierce that nobody could pass that way.

nodes.label: A herd of many pigs feeding near the tombs
nodes.statement: A herd of many pigs was feeding far away from them.

nodes.label: The herd of pigs rushed down the cliff into the sea
nodes.statement: The demons entered the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the cliff into the sea and died in the water.

nodes.label: The whole city begged Jesus to depart
nodes.statement: The whole city came out to meet Jesus, and seeing him, they begged him to depart from their borders.

nodes.label: The return crossing to 'his own city' (Capernaum)
nodes.statement: After the Gadarene episode Jesus crossed back by boat and came into his own city, Capernaum (Matt 4:13).

nodes.label: A paralytic lying on a bed was carried to Jesus
nodes.statement: A paralytic lying on a bed (krabattos) was carried to Jesus in Capernaum.

nodes.label: Scribes reasoned that forgiving sins was blasphemy
nodes.statement: Some scribes reasoned within themselves that Jesus' claim to forgive sins was blasphemy.

nodes.label: The Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins
nodes.statement: Jesus declared that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins, and told the paralytic to take up his mat and walk.

nodes.label: Matthew sat at the tax-collection office in Capernaum
nodes.statement: Matthew sat at the tax-collection office (telonion) in Capernaum - a toll or customs point - and was called by Jesus to follow him.

nodes.label: Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners; Pharisees objected
nodes.statement: Many tax collectors and sinners reclined at table with Jesus and his disciples, and Pharisees objected to the teacher eating with them.

nodes.label: 'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice' quoted
nodes.statement: Jesus quoted Hosea 6:6, 'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice', against the objectors.

nodes.label: John's disciples and the Pharisees fasted
nodes.statement: John's disciples and the Pharisees practised fasting while Jesus' disciples did not while the bridegroom is with them.

nodes.label: Unshrunk cloth on an old garment
nodes.statement: No one puts a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or the patch tears away and the hole worsens.

nodes.label: New wine in fresh wineskins
nodes.statement: New wine is put into fresh wineskins, not old ones, or the skins burst and both wine and skins are ruined.

nodes.label: A synagogue ruler came about his dead daughter
nodes.statement: A ruler (of the synagogue, archisynagogos) came and asked Jesus to lay his hand on his daughter, who had just died.

nodes.label: The haemorrhaging woman touched the fringe (tzitzit)
nodes.statement: A woman with a twelve-year haemorrhage came behind Jesus and touched the fringe (tzitzit) of his garment.

nodes.label: Flute players and a wailing crowd at the ruler's house
nodes.statement: At the ruler's house Jesus saw flute players and a crowd in noisy disorder - professional mourners at a death.

nodes.label: Reports of the healings spread through all that land
nodes.statement: The report of the raisings and healings went out and spread through all that land.

nodes.label: Two blind men called Jesus 'Son of David'
nodes.statement: Two blind men followed Jesus calling, 'Have mercy on us, Son of David', and were healed.

nodes.label: A mute demoniac was brought and healed
nodes.statement: A mute man possessed by a demon was brought to Jesus; when the demon was cast out the mute man spoke.

nodes.label: 'By the prince of the demons he casts out demons'
nodes.statement: The Pharisees said that Jesus casts out demons by the prince of the demons (Beelzebul).

nodes.label: Teaching in the synagogues of cities and villages
nodes.statement: Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the good news of the Kingdom.

nodes.label: The crowds like sheep without a shepherd
nodes.statement: Jesus was moved with compassion for the harassed and scattered crowds, like sheep without a shepherd.

nodes.label: The harvest is plentiful; pray for labourers
nodes.statement: Jesus told his disciples the harvest is plentiful but the labourers are few, and to pray the Lord of the harvest to send out labourers.
Jesus chose twelve disciples, gave them authority over unclean spirits and disease, and sent them out.
nodes.label: The Twelve sent out with authority

nodes.statement: The Twelve are named: Simon Peter, Andrew, James and John the sons of Zebedee, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew the tax collector, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot (Cananaean) and Judas Iscariot.
nodes.label: The names of the Twelve

nodes.statement: Matthew, one of the Twelve, was a tax collector.
nodes.label: Matthew the tax collector

nodes.statement: Judas bears the epithet 'Iscariot', whose meaning is disputed (man of Kerioth; a form of sicarius, 'dagger man'; 'the liar').
nodes.label: The epithet 'Iscariot'

nodes.statement: Simon is called 'the Zealot' (Cananaean), matching the Zealot movement ('fourth philosophy') of first-century Judea.
nodes.label: Simon the Zealot and the Zealot movement

nodes.statement: The mission is restricted to Israel: the Twelve are told not to go among the Gentiles or into Samaritan cities.
nodes.label: Mission limited to Israel

nodes.statement: The Samaritans were a distinct people of the land, centred on Shechem and Mount Gerizim, with their own temple.
nodes.label: The Samaritans and their Gerizim temple

nodes.statement: Gold, silver and bronze/copper coinage circulated in Judea and was carried on the person (in the belt).
nodes.label: Coinage in the money belt

nodes.statement: Travelers carried a bag, tunics, sandals and a staff: the standard travel gear of the period.
nodes.label: Travel gear (bag, tunics, sandals, staff)

nodes.statement: Shaking the dust off one's feet when leaving a rejecting house or city, a gesture of testimony against it.
nodes.label: Shaking off the dust

nodes.statement: Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed and remembered in the first century as objects of divine judgment.
nodes.label: Sodom and Gomorrah

nodes.statement: Venomous snakes were familiar dangers in the region ('wise as serpents').
nodes.label: Serpents of the region

nodes.statement: Wolves lived in the region and preyed on sheep, so sending disciples out 'as sheep among wolves' was a real image.
nodes.label: Sheep among wolves

nodes.statement: Disciples would be delivered up to councils (synedria) and flogged: councils and synagogues acted as judicial institutions, and flogging was a court punishment.
nodes.label: Councils, synagogues and flogging

nodes.statement: Believers would be brought before governors and kings: Roman governors ruled provinces such as Judaea.
nodes.label: Governors and kings

nodes.statement: 'Beelzebul' was a current name for the ruler of demons; its etymology is disputed.
nodes.label: Beelzebul

nodes.statement: Two sparrows were sold for one assarion, a small bronze/copper coin of the lowest value.
nodes.label: Two sparrows for an assarion

nodes.statement: The sword (machaira) was a familiar weapon in Judea.
nodes.label: The sword

nodes.statement: Crucifixion was a Roman punishment used in Judaea before 30 CE, so 'take up his cross' pointed to a known death.
nodes.label: Crucifixion in Judaea

nodes.statement: Giving a cup of cold water to drink was an act of hospitality toward those on the road.
nodes.label: A cup of cold water

nodes.statement: After directing the Twelve, Jesus went on to teach and preach in their cities - the towns of Galilee.
nodes.label: Jesus taught and preached in their cities

nodes.statement: John the Baptist was being held in prison when he heard about the works of Christ and sent two of his disciples to Jesus.
nodes.label: John the Baptist in prison

nodes.statement: Jesus's answer to John lists healings: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news preached to them - the language of Isaiah 35:5-6 and 61:1.
nodes.label: The healing list in Jesus's reply

nodes.statement: Jesus asked the crowds what they went out into the wilderness to see: 'A reed shaken by the wind?'
nodes.label: A reed shaken by the wind
nodes.note: A modern suggestion that the reed alludes to the reed emblem on Antipas's coinage could not be sourced from a fetched page this run; only the coin motif itself is entered.

nodes.statement: Those who wear soft clothing are in kings' houses - soft raiment marks royal palaces, not the wilderness prophet.
nodes.label: Soft raiment in kings' houses

nodes.statement: Jesus applied to John the written promise 'Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you' (Malachi 3:1).
nodes.label: The messenger quotation (Malachi 3:1)

nodes.statement: Jesus called John 'Elijah, who is to come', invoking the first-century expectation that Elijah would return before the day of the Lord.
nodes.label: Elijah who is to come

nodes.statement: Children sat in the marketplaces calling to their companions with wedding and funeral games: 'We played the flute for you, and you didn't dance. We mourned for you, and you didn't lament.'
nodes.label: Children in the marketplaces

nodes.statement: Opponents called the Son of Man 'a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners' - the charge formula of Deuteronomy 21:20.
nodes.label: Glutton and drunkard, friend of tax collectors

nodes.statement: Bethsaida was a town of the period near the Sea of Galilee, denounced in the woes for not repenting.
nodes.label: Woe to Bethsaida

nodes.statement: Chorazin was a Galilean town on the Korazim Plateau above the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee, denounced in the woes for not repenting.
nodes.label: Woe to Chorazin

nodes.statement: Tyre and Sidon stood as Phoenician cities of the Roman period, known to Galilean audiences and remembered as objects of judgment.
nodes.label: Tyre and Sidon

nodes.statement: The land of Sodom was remembered as judged by God; its day would be more tolerable than Capernaum's.
nodes.label: The land of Sodom on the day of judgment

nodes.statement: Capernaum, where most of Jesus's mighty works were done, was denounced: 'You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, you will go down to Hades.'
nodes.label: Capernaum exalted to heaven

nodes.statement: Jesus used the yoke - the wooden farm implement and, in rabbinic idiom, a metaphor of discipleship - to describe his teaching: 'my yoke is easy'.
nodes.label: Take my yoke upon you
Plucking grain on the Sabbath
nodes.statement: On a Sabbath Jesus walked through the grain fields and his hungry disciples began to pluck heads of grain and eat.

nodes.label: Plucking grain as unlawful Sabbath work
nodes.statement: The Pharisees held the disciples' plucking of grain on the Sabbath to be work that was not lawful to do.

nodes.label: David ate the showbread
nodes.statement: David, when hungry, entered the house of God and ate the showbread, which was lawful for the priests alone.

nodes.label: Priests' Sabbath service in the temple
nodes.statement: The priests work in the temple on the Sabbath days and are held guiltless of profaning the Sabbath.

nodes.label: Teaching in their synagogue
nodes.statement: Jesus departed and went into a synagogue in Galilee, where he taught.

nodes.label: Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?
nodes.statement: Healing on the Sabbath was a live question of law: 'Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath day?'

nodes.label: The sheep fallen into a pit on the Sabbath
nodes.statement: A man would lift his one sheep out of a pit on the Sabbath day.

nodes.label: The withered hand restored
nodes.statement: A man with a withered hand was healed in the synagogue; he stretched it out and it was restored whole.

nodes.label: The Pharisees' plot to destroy Jesus
nodes.statement: The Pharisees went out and conspired against Jesus, how they might destroy him.

nodes.label: Isaiah 42:1-4 quoted
nodes.statement: Matthew 12:18-21 quotes Isaiah 42:1-4 as what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet.

nodes.label: The blind and mute demoniac healed
nodes.statement: A demon-possessed man who was blind and mute was brought to Jesus and healed, so that he spoke and saw.

nodes.label: Can this be the son of David?
nodes.statement: The crowds asked in amazement whether Jesus could be the son of David, the messianic title.

nodes.label: Beelzebul, prince of the demons
nodes.statement: The Pharisees said Jesus cast out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.

nodes.label: 'By whom do your sons cast them out?'
nodes.statement: Jewish exorcists - 'your sons' - cast out demons in the period.

nodes.label: Brood of vipers
nodes.statement: The invective 'offspring of vipers' was addressed to the Pharisees.

nodes.label: The sign of Jonah the prophet
nodes.statement: No sign would be given to that evil and adulterous generation except the sign of Jonah the prophet.

nodes.label: Nineveh, a great city
nodes.statement: Nineveh, the city of Jonah's preaching, was a great city.

nodes.label: The men of Nineveh repented
nodes.statement: The men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonah.

nodes.label: The queen of the south and Solomon's wisdom
nodes.statement: The queen of the south came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon.

nodes.label: The unclean spirit in waterless places
nodes.statement: An unclean spirit was believed to pass through waterless places seeking rest.

nodes.label: Jesus' brother James
nodes.statement: Jesus had brothers, among them James ('the brother of Jesus, who was called Christ', Josephus, Ant. 20).

nodes.label: His mother and brothers outside
nodes.statement: The mother and brothers of Jesus stood outside, seeking to speak to him.

nodes.label: Teaching from a boat to the crowd on the shore
nodes.statement: Pressed by the crowds, Jesus sat in a boat on the sea and taught the whole crowd standing on the shore

nodes.label: Seed on the path and rocky ground
nodes.statement: In Galilean sowing, some seed fell on the path (eaten by birds) and on rocky ground with too little soil, where it sprang up quickly but withered under the sun for lack of root

nodes.label: Seed choked by thorns
nodes.statement: Seed sown among thorns was choked by the thorns as they grew up

nodes.label: Yields of thirty, sixty and a hundredfold
nodes.statement: Good soil could yield a crop of thirty, sixty or a hundred times what was sown

nodes.label: Isaiah 6:9-10 quoted as fulfilled
nodes.statement: Matthew cites Isaiah 6:9-10 ('By hearing you will hear... and will in no way understand') as fulfilled in the crowds' dull response

nodes.label: Darnel sown among the wheat by an enemy
nodes.statement: An enemy sowed darnel (zizania, Lolium temulentum) among the wheat while people slept, and it appeared only when the crop produced fruit

nodes.label: Darnel gathered first, bundled and burned
nodes.statement: At harvest the darnel was gathered first, bound in bundles and burned, and the wheat gathered into the barn

nodes.label: Mustard seed sown in a field
nodes.statement: A man sowed a mustard seed in his field: mustard was raised by sowing seed in fields, not gardens

nodes.label: Mustard greater than the herbs, a tree for the birds
nodes.statement: The sown mustard grew greater than the herbs and became a tree, so that the birds of the air lodged in its branches

nodes.label: Leaven hidden in three measures of meal
nodes.statement: A woman hid leaven in three measures (sata, three se'ahs) of meal until the whole batch was leavened

nodes.label: Treasure hidden in a field
nodes.statement: Valuables were hidden in the ground of a field, and a man who found treasure hid it again and bought the field

nodes.label: A merchant seeking fine pearls
nodes.statement: A merchant sought fine pearls, and pearls of great price were bought with everything a man had

nodes.label: A dragnet gathering fish of every kind
nodes.statement: A dragnet (seine) cast into the sea gathered fish of every kind and was drawn up on the beach when filled

nodes.label: Good fish into containers, bad thrown away
nodes.statement: Fishermen sat on the beach, put the good fish into containers and threw the bad away

nodes.label: A scribe bringing out treasures new and old
nodes.statement: A scribe made a disciple in the Kingdom of Heaven is like a householder bringing out of his treasure things new and old

nodes.label: Teaching in the Nazareth synagogue
nodes.statement: Jesus taught the Nazareth crowd in their synagogue

nodes.label: His own country was Nazareth
nodes.statement: Jesus's 'own country', where he came and taught, was Nazareth, a village of first-century Galilee

nodes.label: Brothers James, Joses, Simon and Judas
nodes.statement: Jesus's brothers were called James, Joses, Simon and Judas

nodes.label: His mother called Mary
nodes.statement: Jesus's mother was called Mary

nodes.label: The carpenter's son (tekton)
nodes.statement: Jesus was known as 'the carpenter's son' - the son of a tekton, a building craftsman

nodes.label: His sisters with us
nodes.statement: Jesus had sisters who lived among the Nazareth villagers

nodes.label: A prophet without honour in his own country
nodes.statement: A prophet is not without honour except in his own country and in his own house

nodes.label: Herod Antipas held the office of tetrarch
nodes.statement: Herod (Antipas) held the office of tetrarch of Galilee and Perea at the time.

nodes.label: Herod the tetrarch heard the report concerning Jesus
nodes.statement: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report concerning Jesus.

nodes.label: Herod said Jesus was John the Baptizer risen from the dead
nodes.statement: Herod said to his servants that Jesus was John the Baptizer risen from the dead, whose powers worked in him.

nodes.label: John bound in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife
nodes.statement: Herod had laid hold of John, bound him, and put him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife.

nodes.label: John told Herod it was not lawful to have her
nodes.statement: John said to Herod, 'It is not lawful for you to have her.'

nodes.label: Herod feared the multitude who counted John a prophet
nodes.statement: Herod wanted to put John to death but feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.

nodes.label: Herod's birthday kept with a banquet
nodes.statement: Herod's birthday was kept with a banquet at which guests sat at table and a daughter danced before them.

nodes.label: The daughter of Herodias danced before the guests
nodes.statement: The daughter of Herodias danced among the guests at Herod's birthday banquet and pleased Herod.

nodes.label: Herod promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked
nodes.statement: Herod promised with an oath to give the dancing girl whatever she should ask.

nodes.label: The head of John requested and given on a platter
nodes.statement: The girl, prompted by her mother, asked for the head of John the Baptizer on a platter, and the head was brought on a platter.

nodes.label: John beheaded in the prison
nodes.statement: Herod sent and beheaded John in the prison.

nodes.label: John's disciples took the body and buried it
nodes.statement: John's disciples came, took the body and buried it, then went and told Jesus.

nodes.label: Jesus withdrew by boat to a deserted place
nodes.statement: When Jesus heard of John's death he withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place apart, and the crowds followed on foot from the cities.

nodes.label: Five loaves and two fish
nodes.statement: The disciples had only five loaves and two fish with which to feed the crowd in the deserted place.

nodes.label: Twelve baskets (kophinoi) of leftovers taken up
nodes.statement: After the meal the disciples took up twelve baskets (kophinoi) full of broken pieces left over.

nodes.label: About five thousand men ate
nodes.statement: Those who ate were about five thousand men, besides women and children.

nodes.label: The boat distressed by waves in a contrary wind
nodes.statement: The boat was now in the middle of the sea, distressed by the waves, for the wind was contrary.

nodes.label: The fourth watch of the night
nodes.statement: Jesus came to the disciples in the fourth watch of the night, the last of the night's divisions.

nodes.label: Jesus walked on the sea
nodes.statement: Jesus came to the disciples, walking on the sea in the storm.

nodes.label: Peter walked on the water and began to sink
nodes.statement: Peter stepped down from the boat, walked on the water toward Jesus, and beginning to sink cried out to be saved.

nodes.label: They came to the land of Gennesaret
nodes.statement: When they had crossed over, they came to the land (plain) of Gennesaret on the shore of the Sea of Galilee.

nodes.label: The people begged to touch the fringe (kraspedon) of his garment
