nodes.statement: The people of Gennesaret begged to touch the fringe (kraspedon, tzitzit) of Jesus' garment, and as many as touched it were made whole.

nodes.label: Scribes and Pharisees came from Jerusalem to Jesus
nodes.statement: Scribes and Pharisees came from Jerusalem to Jesus

nodes.label: Pharisees ritually wash their hands before eating bread
nodes.statement: Pharisees ritually wash their hands before eating bread

nodes.label: Pharisees keep the 'tradition of the elders': observances handed down from former generations
nodes.statement: Pharisees keep the 'tradition of the elders': observances handed down from former generations

nodes.label: Declaring support to parents 'a gift devoted to God' (korban) voids honoring father or mother
nodes.statement: Declaring support to parents 'a gift devoted to God' (korban) voids honoring father or mother

nodes.label: Jesus applies Isaiah 29:13 ('teaching as doctrine rules made by men') to the Pharisees
nodes.statement: Jesus applies Isaiah 29:13 ('teaching as doctrine rules made by men') to the Pharisees

nodes.label: What enters the mouth does not defile the man; what proceeds out of the mouth does
nodes.statement: What enters the mouth does not defile the man; what proceeds out of the mouth does

nodes.label: Every plant the heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted
nodes.statement: Every plant the heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted

nodes.label: They are blind guides of the blind; if the blind guide the blind, both fall into a pit
nodes.statement: They are blind guides of the blind; if the blind guide the blind, both fall into a pit

nodes.label: Jesus withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon
nodes.statement: Jesus withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon

nodes.label: A Canaanite woman from those borders cried out to Jesus for mercy
nodes.statement: A Canaanite woman from those borders cried out to Jesus for mercy

nodes.label: The Canaanite woman addresses Jesus as 'son of David'
nodes.statement: The Canaanite woman addresses Jesus as 'son of David'

nodes.label: Dogs eat the crumbs falling from their masters' table
nodes.statement: Dogs eat the crumbs falling from their masters' table

nodes.label: Jesus came near the sea of Galilee and went up into the mountain and sat there
nodes.statement: Jesus came near the sea of Galilee and went up into the mountain and sat there

nodes.label: Great multitudes brought the lame, blind, mute and maimed, and he healed them
nodes.statement: Great multitudes brought the lame, blind, mute and maimed, and he healed them

nodes.label: The multitude continued with him three days and had nothing to eat
nodes.statement: The multitude continued with him three days and had nothing to eat

nodes.label: The disciples had seven loaves and a few small fish
nodes.statement: The disciples had seven loaves and a few small fish

nodes.label: Seven baskets (spyrides) full of broken pieces were taken up
nodes.statement: Seven baskets (spyrides) full of broken pieces were taken up

nodes.label: Those who ate were four thousand men, besides women and children
nodes.statement: Those who ate were four thousand men, besides women and children

nodes.label: He came into the borders of Magdala (variant Magadan)
nodes.statement: He came into the borders of Magdala (variant Magadan)

nodes.label: Pharisees and Sadducees as two distinct Jewish parties
nodes.statement: Pharisees and Sadducees were two distinct Jewish parties active in this period.

nodes.label: Pharisees and Sadducees asked for a sign from heaven
nodes.statement: Pharisees and Sadducees came and, testing Jesus, asked him to show them a sign from heaven.

nodes.label: Weather read from the colour of the sky
nodes.statement: Fair weather was read from a red evening sky and foul weather from a red and threatening morning sky ('red sky at night').

nodes.label: The sign of the prophet Jonah
nodes.statement: An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign would be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.

nodes.label: The disciples forgot to take bread
nodes.statement: Crossing to the other side, the disciples had forgotten to take bread.

nodes.label: The leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees
nodes.statement: Jesus warned, 'Beware of the yeast (leaven) of the Pharisees and Sadducees'; the disciples understood leaven as figurative for their teaching.

nodes.label: Recall of the five loaves for the five thousand
nodes.statement: Jesus recalled the five loaves for the five thousand and the baskets taken up (a recall of the ch 14 feeding).

nodes.label: Recall of the seven loaves for the four thousand
nodes.statement: Jesus recalled the seven loaves for the four thousand and the baskets taken up (the ch 15 feeding).

nodes.label: Jesus came into the parts of Caesarea Philippi
nodes.statement: Jesus came into the parts (region) of Caesarea Philippi, the city Philip the Tetrarch refounded at Paneas (Banias) by the springs of the Jordan, with the Pan sanctuary and Herod's temple to Augustus.

nodes.label: 'Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?'
nodes.statement: At Caesarea Philippi Jesus asked his disciples, 'Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?'

nodes.label: Popular identifications: John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah
nodes.statement: Some said John the Baptizer, some Elijah, and others Jeremiah or one of the prophets - redivivus and eschatological-expectation identifications.

nodes.label: Peter's confession at Caesarea Philippi
nodes.statement: Simon Peter answered, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.'

nodes.label: Simon Bar Jonah
nodes.statement: Jesus blessed 'Simon Bar Jonah' - Simon Peter as son of Jonah.

nodes.label: The gates of Hades
nodes.statement: 'The gates of Hades will not prevail against it' - Hades as the abode of the dead.

nodes.label: 'You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly'
nodes.statement: Jesus said, 'You are Peter (Petros), and on this rock (petra) I will build my assembly (ekklesia).'

nodes.label: Binding and loosing
nodes.statement: 'Whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; and whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven' - the rabbinic idiom of binding (forbidding) and loosing (permitting).

nodes.label: The keys of the Kingdom of Heaven
nodes.statement: Jesus gave Simon Peter 'the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven'.

nodes.label: Suffering at Jerusalem from the elders, chief priests and scribes
nodes.statement: Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders, chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.

nodes.label: 'Take up his cross'
nodes.statement: Whoever would come after Jesus must deny himself and take up his cross - crucifixion as a known death in the period.

nodes.label: The Son of Man coming in his Father's glory with his angels
nodes.statement: The Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and render to everyone according to his deeds.

nodes.label: Some standing here will see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom
nodes.statement: Some standing there would in no way taste of death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.

nodes.label: Transfiguration on a high mountain
nodes.statement: After six days Jesus took Peter, James and John up a high mountain and was transfigured before them. The mountain is not named; since the 3rd century tradition has identified it with Mount Tabor, while others argue for a ridge near Caesarea Philippi, usually Mount Hermon.
nodes.note: Disputed identification (grade D for any): Tabor (Origen and later tradition, against the fortress objection) versus Hermon or 'some mountain near Caesarea-Philippi' (Lightfoot; France 1987).

nodes.label: Moses and Elijah appear with Jesus
nodes.statement: Moses and Elijah appeared and talked with Jesus at the transfiguration - the Law and the Prophets with the Son.

nodes.label: Peter's three tents (sukkot)
nodes.statement: Peter proposed making three tents (skênai, booths) - one for Jesus, one for Moses, one for Elijah - the language of the sukkot dwelt in at the Feast of Tabernacles.

nodes.label: Elijah must come first
nodes.statement: The scribes taught that Elijah must come first before the restoration; Jesus answered that Elijah has already come, and the disciples understood that he spoke of John the Baptist (reusing the Elijah-expectation node from ch 11).

nodes.label: The 'moonstruck' (epileptic) boy
nodes.statement: A boy was brought with epilepsy - Greek selêniazetai, 'moonstruck' - the condition Greek medicine called the 'sacred disease' and antiquity linked with the moon.
nodes.note: The moon-seizure association is ancient (a Babylonian sufferer was 'diagnosed as being under the influence of a moon god'); the Wikipedia source documenting it is modern documentation, not evidence.

nodes.label: Faith as a grain of mustard seed
nodes.statement: Jesus likened faith to a grain of mustard seed - proverbially tiny - which could tell 'this mountain' to move; reusing the ch 13 mustard nodes.

nodes.label: The second passion prediction, in Galilee
nodes.statement: While staying in Galilee Jesus predicted that the Son of Man would be delivered into the hands of men, killed, and raised the third day.

nodes.label: The didrachma collectors and the half-shekel Temple tax
nodes.statement: At Capernaum collectors of the didrachma asked whether Jesus paid it - the annual half-shekel Temple tax for the upkeep of the Temple (Exod 30:13).

nodes.label: Kings take toll and poll-tax from strangers
nodes.statement: The kings of the earth take toll (telos) and poll-tax (kênsos) from strangers, not from their own children - the imperial taxation of subject peoples.

nodes.label: The stater in the fish's mouth
nodes.statement: Peter was to find a stater in the mouth of the first fish he hooked - a coin of four drachmae, two didrachmas - paying the tax 'for me and you'.

nodes.label: The disciples asked Jesus who is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven, and he called a little child and…
nodes.statement: The disciples asked Jesus who is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven, and he called a little child and set him in their midst

nodes.label: Entering the Kingdom requires turning and becoming like little children; whoever humbles himself as …
nodes.statement: Entering the Kingdom requires turning and becoming like little children; whoever humbles himself as a little child is the greatest, and whoever receives such a little one receives him

nodes.label: Better for a stumbling-block-setter that a huge millstone (mylos onikos, a donkey-driven millstone) …
nodes.statement: Better for a stumbling-block-setter that a huge millstone (mylos onikos, a donkey-driven millstone) be hung around his neck and he be sunk in the depths of the sea

nodes.label: Cutting off the hand or foot and plucking out the eye rather than being cast into the eternal fire, …
nodes.statement: Cutting off the hand or foot and plucking out the eye rather than being cast into the eternal fire, the Gehenna of fire

nodes.label: The little ones have angels in heaven who always see the face of the Father who is in heaven
nodes.statement: The little ones have angels in heaven who always see the face of the Father who is in heaven

nodes.label: A shepherd leaves ninety-nine sheep on the mountains to seek the one gone astray, and rejoices over …
nodes.statement: A shepherd leaves ninety-nine sheep on the mountains to seek the one gone astray, and rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine

nodes.label: A sinning brother is first confronted alone; if he refuses to listen, before one or two more, that e…
nodes.statement: A sinning brother is first confronted alone; if he refuses to listen, before one or two more, that every word be established at the mouth of two or three witnesses

nodes.label: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly (ekklēsia); if he refuses to hear the assem…
nodes.statement: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly (ekklēsia); if he refuses to hear the assembly also, let him be to you as a Gentile or a tax collector

nodes.label: Whatever the community binds on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever it releases on ea…
nodes.statement: Whatever the community binds on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever it releases on earth will have been released in heaven

nodes.label: If two agree on earth concerning anything they ask, the Father does it; where two or three are gathe…
nodes.statement: If two agree on earth concerning anything they ask, the Father does it; where two or three are gathered in his name, he is in the midst of them

nodes.label: Forgiving the sinning brother not until seven times, but until seventy times seven
nodes.statement: Forgiving the sinning brother not until seven times, but until seventy times seven

nodes.label: A king reconciling accounts with his servants; one servant was brought to him who owed ten thousand …
nodes.statement: A king reconciling accounts with his servants; one servant was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents, a fantastically large sum

nodes.label: Because the servant could not pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, with his wife, his children, a…
nodes.statement: Because the servant could not pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, with his wife, his children, and all that he had, and payment to be made

nodes.label: The fellow servant owed one hundred denarii (about a hundred days' wages)
nodes.statement: The fellow servant owed one hundred denarii (about a hundred days' wages)

nodes.label: The unforgiving servant cast his fellow servant into prison until he should pay back what was due
nodes.statement: The unforgiving servant cast his fellow servant into prison until he should pay back what was due

nodes.label: The angry lord delivered the unforgiving servant to the tormentors until he should pay all that was …
nodes.statement: The angry lord delivered the unforgiving servant to the tormentors until he should pay all that was due

nodes.label: Jesus goes to the region beyond the Jordan
nodes.statement: Jesus left Galilee and came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan (Perea).

nodes.label: Great multitudes followed and he healed them there
nodes.statement: Great multitudes followed Jesus in the region beyond the Jordan, and he healed them there.

nodes.label: Divorce 'for any cause' was a disputed question
nodes.statement: Whether a man may divorce his wife for any cause was a live, disputed question between the Houses of Shammai and Hillel.

nodes.label: Pharisees test Jesus with the divorce question
nodes.statement: Pharisees came, testing Jesus, asking whether it is lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any cause.

nodes.label: Genesis 1:27 quoted for marriage
nodes.statement: Jesus answered from Genesis 1:27: he who made them from the beginning made them male and female.

nodes.label: Genesis 2:24 quoted: one flesh
nodes.statement: Jesus cited Genesis 2:24: a man leaves father and mother, is joined to his wife, and the two become one flesh.

nodes.label: The bill of divorce (get)
nodes.statement: Divorce was carried out by giving the wife a written bill of divorce, which Moses commanded.

nodes.label: Divorce and remarriage as adultery
nodes.statement: Whoever divorces his wife except for sexual immorality and marries another commits adultery; so does he who marries her when she is divorced.

nodes.label: Three kinds of eunuchs
nodes.statement: Jesus names eunuchs born so from the womb, eunuchs made so by men, and eunuchs who made themselves so for the kingdom of heaven.

nodes.label: Children brought for laying on of hands
nodes.statement: Little children were brought to Jesus so that he might lay his hands on them and pray, and the disciples rebuked the bringers.

nodes.label: The rich man asks about eternal life
nodes.statement: A man came and asked Jesus what good thing he should do to have eternal life, and went away sad for he had great possessions.

nodes.label: The commandments listed
nodes.statement: Jesus lists commandments: not murder, not adultery, not steal, not false witness, honor father and mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.

nodes.label: Sell, give to the poor, treasure in heaven
nodes.statement: Jesus tells the man to sell what he has, give to the poor, and so have treasure in heaven, and to come and follow him.

nodes.label: A camel through a needle's eye
nodes.statement: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.

nodes.label: Twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes
nodes.statement: In the regeneration the Son of Man will sit on the throne of his glory, and his followers will sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

nodes.label: A hundredfold for leaving houses and lands
nodes.statement: Everyone who leaves houses, brothers, sisters, father, mother, wife, children or lands for Jesus's sake will receive a hundred times and inherit eternal life.

nodes.label: The first will be last
nodes.statement: Many will be last who are first, and first who are last.

nodes.label: A landowner went out early in the morning to hire labourers for his vineyard.
nodes.statement: A landowner went out early in the morning to hire labourers for his vineyard.

nodes.label: Vineyards with wine presses (Hebrew gath) were part of Judean agriculture.
nodes.statement: Vineyards with wine presses (Hebrew gath) were part of Judean agriculture.

nodes.label: The labourers agreed on a denarius as the wage for a day's work.
nodes.statement: The labourers agreed on a denarius as the wage for a day's work.

nodes.label: The working day was reckoned in twelve hours of daylight, the third, sixth, ninth and eleventh hours being mid-morning, noon, mid-afternoon and late afternoon.
nodes.statement: The working day was reckoned in twelve hours of daylight, the third, sixth, ninth and eleventh hours being mid-morning, noon, mid-afternoon and late afternoon.

nodes.label: Day labourers who had not been hired stood idle in the marketplace (agora) waiting for work.
nodes.statement: Day labourers who had not been hired stood idle in the marketplace (agora) waiting for work.

nodes.label: Labourers' wages were to be paid the same day, beginning when evening came.
nodes.statement: Labourers' wages were to be paid the same day, beginning when evening came.

nodes.label: Jesus went up to Jerusalem with the Twelve for the final journey.
nodes.statement: Jesus went up to Jerusalem with the Twelve for the final journey.

nodes.label: The Son of Man would be delivered to the chief priests and scribes and condemned to death.
nodes.statement: The Son of Man would be delivered to the chief priests and scribes and condemned to death.

nodes.label: He would be handed over to the Gentiles to be mocked, flogged and crucified, and rise on the third day.
nodes.statement: He would be handed over to the Gentiles to be mocked, flogged and crucified, and rise on the third day.

nodes.label: The mother of the sons of Zebedee asked that her two sons sit, one at his right hand and one at his left, in his kingdom.
nodes.statement: The mother of the sons of Zebedee asked that her two sons sit, one at his right hand and one at his left, in his kingdom.

nodes.label: Jesus spoke of the cup he was about to drink as a share in suffering ('the cup' as a figure for one's allotted fate).
nodes.statement: Jesus spoke of the cup he was about to drink as a share in suffering ('the cup' as a figure for one's allotted fate).

nodes.label: The rulers of the Gentiles lord it over their subjects, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
nodes.statement: The rulers of the Gentiles lord it over their subjects, and their great ones exercise authority over them.

nodes.label: The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom (lytron) for many.
nodes.statement: The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom (lytron) for many.

nodes.label: Jesus and the crowd went out from Jericho, the Herodian city on the road up to Jerusalem.
nodes.statement: Jesus and the crowd went out from Jericho, the Herodian city on the road up to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Two blind men sitting by the road outside Jericho cried out to Jesus, 'Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.'
nodes.statement: Two blind men sitting by the road outside Jericho cried out to Jesus, 'Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.'

nodes.label: Jesus approaches Jerusalem via Bethphage and the Mount of Olives
nodes.statement: Jesus approached Jerusalem from Jericho and came to Bethsphage, at the Mount of Olives, and sent two disciples into the village opposite.

nodes.label: Disciples fetch a donkey and its colt
nodes.statement: The disciples found, untied and brought a donkey tied with its colt, saying 'The Lord needs them' if questioned.

nodes.label: The entry quoted with Zechariah 9:9 (donkey and colt)
nodes.statement: The entry is narrated with the words of Zechariah 9:9 (a quotation in the text): 'your King comes to you, humble, and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey'.

nodes.label: Garments laid on the animals as a mount
nodes.statement: Garments were laid on the animals to serve as a riding cushion for the royal entry.

nodes.label: Crowd spreads cloaks and branches on the road
nodes.statement: A great crowd spread clothes and cut branches on the road ahead of him, an honorific welcome of a royal or victorious entrant.

nodes.label: The crowd acclaims 'Hosanna to the son of David' (Psalm 118)
nodes.statement: The crowds acclaimed him with 'Hosanna to the son of David' and 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord', the language of Psalm 118:25-26.

nodes.label: All the city is stirred; the crowd names Jesus of Nazareth a prophet
nodes.statement: His arrival stirred the whole city, and the crowds identified him as 'the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee'.

nodes.label: Jesus drives out sellers and buyers in the Temple courts
nodes.statement: Jesus entered the Temple courts and drove out all who sold and bought there.

nodes.label: Money changers exchanged coin for the half-shekel Temple tax
nodes.statement: Money changers operated in and for the Temple, exchanging pilgrims' currency for the half-shekel Temple tax, which was required to be Tyrian silver.

nodes.label: Doves sold in the Temple for purification offerings
nodes.statement: Doves were sold in the Temple precincts for the offerings of the purifying (women after childbirth, zavim), and their market price was a live public concern.

nodes.label: He overturned the money changers' tables and the dove sellers' seats
nodes.statement: He overturned the money changers' tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.

nodes.label: He quotes Isaiah 56:7 and Jeremiah 7:11
nodes.statement: He justified the action by quoting Isaiah 56:7 ('my house shall be called a house of prayer') against Jeremiah 7:11 ('you have made it a den of robbers').

nodes.label: The blind and lame healed in the Temple
nodes.statement: The blind and the lame came to him in the Temple courts, and he healed them there.

nodes.label: Children cry 'Hosanna'; he answers with Psalm 8:2
nodes.statement: Children cried 'Hosanna to the son of David' in the Temple, and Jesus answered the indignant chief priests with Psalm 8:2, 'out of the mouth of babes... you have perfected praise'.

nodes.label: He lodges at Bethany outside Jerusalem
nodes.statement: He left the city each evening and lodged at Bethany, a village outside Jerusalem, during the final week.

nodes.label: The leafy fig tree has no fruit and withers at his word
nodes.statement: On the morning return he found a roadside fig tree in full leaf but with no fruit, cursed it, and it withered at once.

nodes.label: Chief priests and elders question his authority in the Temple
nodes.statement: While he was teaching in the Temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people confronted him and demanded by what authority he acted.

nodes.label: The leaders fear the crowds because all hold John a prophet
nodes.statement: The leaders dared not call John's baptism merely human, because the crowds all held John to be a prophet and the leaders feared them.

nodes.label: The two sons and the father's vineyard work
nodes.statement: The parable assumes a father's sons owe a day's work in the family vineyard, and that doing the father's will, not the first answer, counts.

nodes.label: Absentee landowner leases the vineyard to tenant farmers
nodes.statement: The parable assumes an absentee landowner who leases his vineyard to tenant farmers (georgoi) and at harvest sends servants to collect his share of the fruit.

nodes.label: Vineyard with hedge, winepress and watchtower (Isaiah 5)
nodes.statement: The parable's vineyard has a hedge, a dug winepress and a built watchtower, the fittings of Isaiah 5's vineyard song.

nodes.label: He quotes Psalm 118:22-23 (the rejected stone)
nodes.statement: He answered with Psalm 118:22-23, the stone the builders rejected made the head of the corner, 'marvelous in our eyes'.

nodes.label: The leaders perceive the parables are against them but fear the crowds
nodes.statement: The chief priests and Pharisees understood that the parables were spoken against them, and would have seized him but feared the multitudes, who held him to be a prophet.

nodes.label: The king's marriage feast and its invited guests
nodes.statement: A king made a marriage feast for his son and sent out his servants to call those who were invited.

nodes.label: The king's armies burned their city
nodes.statement: In the parable, the king sent his armies, destroyed the murderers and burned their city.

nodes.label: The wedding garment required of the guest
nodes.statement: A guest at the marriage feast without wedding clothing was challenged, bound and cast out.

nodes.label: The Pharisees and the Herodians together
nodes.statement: The Pharisees sent their disciples, along with the Herodians, to entrap Jesus in his talk.

nodes.label: The tribute question
nodes.statement: Whether it was lawful to pay taxes to Caesar was a live question in Judea.

nodes.label: The denarius brought to Jesus
nodes.statement: They brought Jesus a denarius when he asked to see the tax money.

nodes.label: Caesar's image and inscription on the coin
nodes.statement: The coin bore Caesar's image and inscription, and Jesus said to give to Caesar the things that are Caesar's.

nodes.label: The Sadducees deny the resurrection
nodes.statement: The Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to Jesus with a question.

nodes.label: Levirate marriage
nodes.statement: Moses commanded that if a man dies having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.

nodes.label: Exodus 3:6 quoted
nodes.statement: Jesus quoted 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' (Exodus 3:6) about the resurrection of the dead.

nodes.label: The Shema's love command as the greatest commandment
nodes.statement: The first and great commandment is 'You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind' (Deut 6:5).

nodes.label: The Christ as the son of David
nodes.statement: The Christ was expected to be the son of David.

nodes.label: Psalm 110:1 quoted
nodes.statement: Jesus quoted Psalm 110:1, 'The Lord said to my Lord, sit on my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.'

nodes.label: The scribes and Pharisees sit on Moses' seat
nodes.statement: The scribes and the Pharisees sat on Moses' seat - a recognized seat or office of teaching authority in the synagogue setting.

nodes.label: They enlarge the fringes of their garments
nodes.statement: The scribes and Pharisees wear fringes (tzitzit) on their garments and enlarge them to be seen by men.

nodes.label: They make their phylacteries broad
nodes.statement: The scribes and Pharisees wear phylacteries (tefillin) and make them broad to be seen by men.

nodes.label: Places of honor at feasts and best seats in the synagogues
nodes.statement: The scribes and Pharisees love the place of honor at feasts, the best seats in the synagogues, and the salutations in the marketplaces.

nodes.label: They love to be called 'Rabbi'
nodes.statement: The scribes and Pharisees love to be called 'Rabbi, Rabbi' by men; Jesus tells his disciples not to be called Rabbi, for one is their teacher.

nodes.label: They travel sea and land to make one proselyte
nodes.statement: The scribes and Pharisees travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one they make him twice as much a son of Gehenna as themselves.

nodes.label: A hierarchy of oaths by the temple, its gold, the altar and heaven
nodes.statement: The blind guides teach that whoever swears by the temple it is nothing, but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is obligated - likewise the altar and its gift; Jesus ranks the temple, the altar and heaven above gold, gift and throne.

nodes.label: They tithe mint, dill and cumin
nodes.statement: The scribes and Pharisees tithe mint, dill and cumin, while leaving undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy and faith.

nodes.label: They clean the outside of the cup and platter
nodes.statement: The scribes and Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and of the platter while the inside is full of extortion and unrighteousness; Jesus says first clean the inside, that the outside may become clean also.

nodes.label: Whitewashed tombs, beautiful outside, full of bones
nodes.statement: The scribes and Pharisees are like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful but inwardly are full of dead men's bones and all uncleanness.

nodes.label: They build and decorate the tombs of the prophets and righteous
nodes.statement: The scribes and Pharisees build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the tombs of the righteous, saying they would not have shared in their fathers' bloodshed.

nodes.label: Zechariah son of Barachiah killed between the sanctuary and the altar
nodes.statement: Zechariah son of Barachiah was killed between the sanctuary and the altar - the martyrdom that closes the list from righteous Abel.

nodes.label: Jerusalem kills the prophets; the house is left desolate
nodes.statement: Jesus laments that Jerusalem kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, and says 'Behold, your house is left to you desolate' (a prediction in the text; the Temple was destroyed in 70 CE).

nodes.label: They will not see him till they say 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord'
nodes.statement: Jesus says they will not see him from now on until they say 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord' - the acclamation of Psalm 118:26.

nodes.label: The Temple buildings were thrown down, so that not one stone was left on another
nodes.statement: The Temple buildings were thrown down, so that not one stone was left on another - predicted in the discourse (24:2); the Temple buildings were destroyed and razed in 70 CE. The claim is scoped to the Temple buildings: the platform's retaining walls survive.

nodes.label: Men claiming to be the messiah or a prophet ('I am the Christ'; false christs and false prophets) arose and led followers astray in Judea
nodes.statement: Men claiming to be the messiah or a prophet ('I am the Christ'; false christs and false prophets) arose and led followers astray in Judea - predicted in 24:5, 11, 23-26.

nodes.label: Wars and rumors of wars, famines, plagues and earthquakes in various places afflicted the period
nodes.statement: Wars and rumors of wars, famines, plagues and earthquakes in various places afflicted the period - predicted in 24:6-7.

nodes.label: The disciples were delivered up to oppression and killed, hated by all the nations for Jesus' name's sake
nodes.statement: The disciples were delivered up to oppression and killed, hated by all the nations for Jesus' name's sake - predicted in 24:9.

nodes.label: The abomination of desolation, spoken of through Daniel the prophet, stood in the holy place
nodes.statement: The abomination of desolation, spoken of through Daniel the prophet, stood in the holy place - predicted in 24:15 (the desolating sacrilege set up in the Temple).

nodes.label: When the desolation appeared, those in Judea fled to the mountains
nodes.statement: When the desolation appeared, those in Judea fled to the mountains - predicted as a command in 24:16-20.

nodes.label: Signs appeared in the heavens
nodes.statement: Signs appeared in the heavens - the sun darkened, the moon without light, stars falling - and the sign of the Son of Man was seen coming on the clouds of the sky - predicted in 24:29-30.

nodes.label: The fig tree's branch becoming tender and producing leaves is the sign that summer is near
nodes.statement: The fig tree's branch becoming tender and producing leaves is the sign that summer is near - a custom of reading the seasons from the fig tree, taught as a parable in 24:32-33.

nodes.label: Two women ground grain at a hand-mill, one taken and one left
nodes.statement: Two women ground grain at a hand-mill, one taken and one left - the domestic grinding custom named in 24:41.

nodes.label: A householder who knew in what watch of the night the thief was coming would have watched
nodes.statement: A householder who knew in what watch of the night the thief was coming would have watched - the night-watch custom named in 24:43.

nodes.label: Bridesmaids go out with lamps to meet the bridegroom
nodes.statement: The parable assumes bridesmaids (virgins) carrying lamps as they go out to meet the bridegroom; the custom is attested, never that the parable was told.

nodes.label: Lamps burning oil carried in vessels
nodes.statement: The lamps burn oil, and the oil is carried in vessels alongside the lamps; the foolish took no oil with them.

nodes.label: The bridegroom arrives at night and the party goes out to meet him
nodes.statement: The bridegroom arrives at midnight and the wedding party goes out to meet him in procession.

nodes.label: Oil could be bought from sellers
nodes.statement: Oil was a retail commodity that could be bought from sellers, as the parable's 'go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves' assumes.

nodes.label: The talent as a large sum of money entrusted to servants
nodes.statement: The talent is a unit of money: a master entrusts five, two and one talent to his servants - five talents was a very large sum.

nodes.label: Hiding money by burying it in the ground
nodes.statement: The servant hid his lord's money by digging in the earth and burying it - burying sums of money in the ground as safekeeping.

nodes.label: Depositing money with bankers to earn interest
nodes.statement: Money could be deposited with bankers (trapezitai, 'table-keepers'), who used it and returned it with interest.

nodes.label: The Son of Man sits on the throne of his glory
nodes.statement: The Son of Man comes in his glory with the holy angels and sits on the throne of his glory to judge the nations - a scene with pre-Christian Jewish parallels.

nodes.label: A shepherd separates sheep from goats in a mixed flock
nodes.statement: The simile assumes a shepherd who herds sheep and goats together and separates them, setting the sheep on his right and the goats on the left.

nodes.label: The six acts of mercy: food, drink, shelter, clothing, sick, prisoners
nodes.statement: The judgment scene names feeding the hungry, giving drink to the thirsty, taking in the stranger, clothing the naked, and visiting the sick and the imprisoned. The moral criterion of the scene itself (who is counted righteous) is a human-judgment matter, not claimed here.

nodes.label: Prisons and imprisonment under Herodian and Roman rule
nodes.statement: Prisons existed, and people were held prisoner, under Herodian and Roman rule in Judea in the first century.

nodes.label: Caiaphas was high priest when the leaders gathered
nodes.statement: The leaders gathered in the court of the high priest 'who was called Caiaphas': Joseph Caiaphas held the high priesthood at the time of the feast.

nodes.label: The chief priests and elders plotted to seize and kill Jesus
nodes.statement: The chief priests, scribes and elders took counsel together that they might take Jesus by deceit and kill him.

nodes.label: They avoided arresting Jesus during the feast for fear of a riot
nodes.statement: They said 'not during the feast, lest a riot occur among the people': the authorities feared the Passover crowds.

nodes.label: Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper
nodes.statement: Jesus stayed in Bethany, at the house of Simon the leper, in the final week.

nodes.label: A woman poured very expensive ointment from an alabaster jar on his head
nodes.statement: A woman poured very expensive ointment from an alabaster jar on the head of the reclining Jesus - costly perfumed oil in a stone flask.

nodes.label: Judas was promised and paid thirty pieces of silver
nodes.statement: Judas asked 'what are you willing to give me?', and the chief priests weighed out thirty pieces of silver to him for delivering Jesus.

nodes.label: The disciples prepared the Passover on the first day of unleavened bread
nodes.statement: On the first day of unleavened bread the disciples prepared the Passover meal in Jerusalem, in a house Jesus designated.

nodes.label: Jesus reclined at table with the twelve in the evening
nodes.statement: When evening had come, Jesus was reclining at table (the Passover meal posture) with the twelve disciples.

nodes.label: They sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives
nodes.statement: When they had sung a hymn (the Passover Hallel) they went out to the Mount of Olives.

nodes.label: Before the cock crows Peter will deny Jesus three times
nodes.statement: Jesus told Peter he would deny him three times that night before the rooster crows - cockcrow used as a time marker of the night.

nodes.label: Jesus came with his disciples to a place called Gethsemane
nodes.statement: Jesus came with his disciples to a place (chorion, an estate) called Gethsemane across the Kidron, and prayed there.

nodes.label: Judas came with a great crowd armed with swords and clubs
nodes.statement: Judas came with a great crowd carrying swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests and elders of the people, to seize Jesus.

nodes.label: A companion drew his sword and cut off the ear of the high priest’s servant
nodes.statement: One of those with Jesus drew his sword (a short Roman-era blade) and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.

nodes.label: Twelve legions of angels - the legion as a large Roman unit
nodes.statement: Jesus said his Father could send more than twelve legions of angels; the legion was the Roman army’s largest unit, numbering thousands of men.

nodes.label: Jesus sat daily teaching in the temple
nodes.statement: Jesus said he sat daily in the temple teaching, and was not arrested there - public teaching in the temple courts during the festival week.

nodes.label: Jesus was led to Caiaphas where the scribes and elders gathered
nodes.statement: Those who seized Jesus led him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered for the hearing.

nodes.label: Peter followed into the courtyard of the high priest’s house
nodes.statement: Peter followed at a distance into the court (courtyard) of the high priest’s house and sat with the officers to see the end.

nodes.label: The whole council sought testimony to put Jesus to death
nodes.statement: The chief priests, the elders and the whole council (the Sanhedrin) sought testimony against Jesus to put him to death.

nodes.label: The Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky
nodes.statement: Jesus said they would see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of the sky - Danielic and Enochic Son-of-Man language.

nodes.label: The high priest tore his clothing at the alleged blasphemy
nodes.statement: The high priest tore his clothing and said "He has spoken blasphemy", and the council declared him worthy of death.

nodes.label: Peter’s Galilean accent gave him away
nodes.statement: Bystanders said to Peter "your speech makes you known" - his Galilean accent identified him as one of Jesus’ Galilean followers.

nodes.label: Jesus was bound and delivered up to Pontius Pilate, the governor
nodes.statement: Jesus was bound and delivered up to Pontius Pilate, the governor, by the chief priests and elders.

nodes.label: Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea when Jesus was delivered up and judged
nodes.statement: Pontius Pilate held the governor's office over Judea when Jesus was delivered up and judged by him.

nodes.label: Judas returned the thirty pieces of silver, threw them into the sanctuary and hanged himself
nodes.statement: Judas, remorseful, brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests, threw them into the sanctuary, and went away and hanged himself.

nodes.label: The priests bought the potter's field as a burial ground for strangers, called the Field of Blood
nodes.statement: The chief priests took the silver, bought the potter's field to bury strangers in, and the field was called the Field of Blood.

nodes.label: It was not lawful to put the price of blood into the temple treasury (korbanas)
nodes.statement: The chief priests held it not lawful to put the price of blood into the temple treasury (korbanas).

nodes.label: Jesus stood before the governor, was accused by the chief priests and answered nothing
nodes.statement: Jesus stood before the governor, was accused by the chief priests and elders, and gave no answer, not even one word.

nodes.label: At the feast the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner whom the crowd desired
nodes.statement: At the feast (Passover) the governor was accustomed to release to the multitude one prisoner whom they desired.

nodes.label: Barabbas, a notable prisoner, was released and Jesus was handed over to be crucified
nodes.statement: At the governor's offer of a Passover release, the crowd chose Barabbas, a notable prisoner, and Jesus was handed over to be crucified.

nodes.label: Pilate's wife sent him word about her dream concerning the righteous man
nodes.statement: While Pilate sat on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying she had suffered much in a dream because of the righteous man.

nodes.label: Pilate washed his hands before the crowd and declared himself innocent of Jesus' blood
nodes.statement: Pilate took water and washed his hands before the multitude, declaring himself innocent of the blood of the righteous man; the people answered, 'His blood be on us and on our children.'

nodes.label: Jesus was crucified by order of Pontius Pilate
nodes.statement: Jesus was crucified at the order of Pontius Pilate (27:26-35), at Golgotha outside Jerusalem.

nodes.label: A condemned man was flogged (scourged) by Roman soldiers before being handed over for crucifixion
nodes.statement: Jesus was flogged (scourged) by the governor's soldiers before being handed over to be crucified - the Roman scourging custom of 27:26.

nodes.label: The governor had a headquarters (praetorium) in Jerusalem
nodes.statement: The governor had a headquarters (praetorium) in Jerusalem.

nodes.label: The governor's soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the cohort
nodes.statement: The governor's soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole garrison (cohort) against him.

nodes.label: The soldiers stripped Jesus, dressed him in a scarlet robe with a reed, and mocked him as king
nodes.statement: The governor's soldiers stripped Jesus, put a scarlet robe on him, put a reed in his right hand, knelt, and mocked him, 'Hail, King of the Jews!', spat on him and struck his head.

nodes.label: A crown plaited from thorns was woven and put on his head
nodes.statement: The soldiers braided a crown out of thorns and put it on his head (27:29).

nodes.label: The soldiers compelled Simon of Cyrene to carry the cross
nodes.statement: Coming out, the soldiers found Simon of Cyrene and compelled him to carry the cross of Jesus (27:32).

nodes.label: The crucifixion took place at Golgotha, 'the place of a skull', outside the city
nodes.statement: They came to a place called Golgotha, 'the place of a skull', where he was crucified - outside the walls of Jerusalem of that time.

nodes.label: The condemned was offered sour wine mixed with gall before execution
nodes.statement: They gave Jesus sour wine mixed with gall to drink; he tasted it and would not drink (27:34).

nodes.label: The executioners divided the condemned man's clothing among themselves by casting lots
nodes.statement: When they had crucified him, the soldiers divided his clothing among them by casting lots (27:35).

nodes.label: A written placard stating the charge was set up over the crucified man's head
nodes.statement: They set up over his head the written accusation against him: 'THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS' (27:37).

nodes.label: Darkness covered the land from the sixth hour until the ninth hour
nodes.statement: From the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour (27:45).

nodes.label: A soldier gave the crucified man sour wine (vinegar) on a sponge raised on a reed
nodes.statement: One of the bystanders ran, filled a sponge with vinegar (sour wine), put it on a reed and gave him drink (27:48).

nodes.label: The earth quaked and the rocks were split at the time of the crucifixion
nodes.statement: The earth quaked and the rocks were split (27:51); the centurion and his men saw the earthquake (27:54).

nodes.label: The veil of the Jerusalem temple was torn in two from top to bottom
nodes.statement: The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom (27:51).

nodes.label: Tombs were opened and many bodies of sleeping saints were raised and appeared to many
nodes.statement: The tombs were opened; many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised, came out of the tombs after his resurrection, entered the holy city and appeared to many (27:52-53).

nodes.label: Women who had followed Jesus from Galilee, among them Mary Magdalene, watched the crucifixion and sat opposite the tomb
nodes.statement: Many women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and served him watched from afar, among them Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Joses; Mary Magdalene and the other Mary sat opposite the tomb.

nodes.label: Joseph of Arimathea, a rich disciple, asked Pilate for the body of Jesus and received it
nodes.statement: Joseph of Arimathea, a rich man and disciple of Jesus, came in the evening, went to Pilate, asked for the body, and Pilate commanded it to be given up (27:57-58).

nodes.label: The body was wrapped in linen and laid in a new rock-cut tomb closed with a great rolled stone
nodes.statement: Joseph wrapped the body in clean linen and laid it in his own new tomb cut in the rock, and rolled a great stone against the door of the tomb (27:59-60).

nodes.label: The chief priests and Pharisees posted a guard and sealed the stone of the tomb
nodes.statement: On the day after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered to Pilate, asked for the tomb to be secured until the third day; Pilate gave them a guard, and they sealed the stone and set the guard (27:62-66).

nodes.label: The week was reckoned from the Sabbath in Judea
nodes.statement: In Judea the week ran to the Sabbath, the day of rest; the day after the Sabbath was the first day of the week, and the visit of 28:1 is dated 'after the Sabbath'.

nodes.label: Mary Magdalene came from Magdala
nodes.statement: Mary Magdalene ('the Magdalene') is named by her town, Magdala; the attribution rests on the Gospel epithet and later tradition ('It is believed to be the birthplace of Mary Magdalene' per the fetched Magdala article), while excavation confirms the first-century town itself.

nodes.label: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to the tomb on the first day of the week
nodes.statement: After the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb (28:1).

nodes.label: An angel of the Lord descended and rolled away the stone
nodes.statement: An angel of the Lord descended from the sky, rolled away the stone from the door and sat on it; the guards shook and became like dead men (28:2-4).

nodes.label: The tomb was sealed with a large stone rolled across the entrance
nodes.statement: The tomb's entrance was closed by a great stone that was rolled away from the door (28:2). Tension recorded: a documented rolling-stone tomb attests the practice in 1st-century Jerusalem, but the fetched Rock-cut tombs article reports simple tombs closed 'with a rectangular blocking stone or mudbrick', so a round rolling stone is not shown to be the norm; the Kloner rarity survey could not be verified on a fetched page (see notes).

nodes.label: A great earthquake occurred at the tomb
nodes.statement: There was a great earthquake as the angel descended (28:2).

nodes.label: Jesus rose from the dead and the tomb was found empty
nodes.statement: The angel tells the women, 'He is not here, for he has risen' (28:5-6), and sends them to tell the disciples (28:7).

nodes.label: Jesus appeared to the women and to the eleven in Galilee
nodes.statement: Jesus met the women as they ran to the disciples (28:9) and the eleven saw him on the Galilean mountain (28:17).

nodes.label: The guards reported to the chief priests and were bribed
nodes.statement: Some of the guards reported to the chief priests, who gave a large sum of silver and promised to persuade the governor (28:11-14); the story presupposes that a sleeping sentry faced punishment.

nodes.label: The stolen-body report was spread among the Jews
nodes.statement: The chief priests had the guards say the disciples stole the body by night while they slept, and 'this saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today' (28:15).

nodes.label: The eleven went to the mountain in Galilee Jesus appointed
nodes.statement: The eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them (28:16); the specific mountain is unidentified (gap).

nodes.label: The movement was commissioned to all the nations and spread beyond Judea
nodes.statement: 'Go and make disciples of all nations' (28:19); within a few decades the movement had spread from Judaea to Rome.

nodes.label: Baptism into the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit
nodes.statement: Jesus commissions baptizing 'in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit' (28:19); early Christian witnesses know the threefold formula but are reception, never attestation.

nodes.label: Acts 1:1
nodes.text: The first book I wrote, Theophilus, concerned all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,

nodes.label: Acts 1:2
nodes.text: until the day in which he was received up, after he had given commandment through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen.

nodes.label: Acts 1:3
nodes.text: To these he also showed himself alive after he suffered, by many proofs, appearing to them over a period of forty days, and speaking about God’s Kingdom.

nodes.label: Acts 1:4
nodes.text: Being assembled together with them, he commanded them, “Don’t depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which you heard from me.

nodes.label: Acts 1:5
nodes.text: For John indeed baptized in water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit not many days from now.”

variants.reading: ἐν πνεύματι βαπτισθήσεσθε ἁγίῳ ('with [the] Spirit will be baptised Holy')
variants.note: Sinaiticus* and B, with 81, 915 and Didymus (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles, Acts 1:5).

nodes.label: Acts 1:6
nodes.text: Therefore when they had come together, they asked him, “Lord, are you now restoring the kingdom to Israel?”

nodes.label: Acts 1:7
nodes.text: He said to them, “It isn’t for you to know times or seasons which the Father has set within his own authority.

nodes.label: Acts 1:8
nodes.text: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”

nodes.label: Acts 1:9
nodes.text: When he had said these things, as they were looking, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.

nodes.label: Acts 1:10
nodes.text: While they were looking steadfastly into the sky as he went, behold, two men stood by them in white clothing,

nodes.label: Acts 1:11
nodes.text: who also said, “You men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into the sky? This Jesus, who was received up from you into the sky, will come back in the same way as you saw him going into the sky.”

nodes.label: Acts 1:12
nodes.text: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day’s journey away.

nodes.label: Acts 1:13
nodes.text: When they had come in, they went up into the upper room, where they were staying; that is Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas the son of James.

nodes.label: Acts 1:14
nodes.text: All these with one accord continued steadfastly in prayer and supplication, along with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brothers.

nodes.label: Acts 1:15
nodes.text: In these days, Peter stood up in the middle of the disciples (and the number of names was about one hundred twenty), and said,

variants.reading: ἀδελφῶν ('of the brothers')
variants.note: Sinaiticus, A, B, C*, 33 vid and others; the reading is 'of the brothers' (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles, Acts 1:15).

nodes.label: Acts 1:16
nodes.text: “Brothers, it was necessary that this Scripture should be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke before by the mouth of David concerning Judas, who was guide to those who took Jesus.

nodes.label: Acts 1:17
nodes.text: For he was counted with us, and received his portion in this ministry.

nodes.label: Acts 1:18
nodes.text: Now this man obtained a field with the reward for his wickedness, and falling headlong, his body burst open, and all his intestines gushed out.

variants.reading: πρηνὴς γενόμενος ('headlong having fallen/become')
variants.note: Sinaiticus, A, B, C, D, E, Psi, 049 and the vast majority (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles, Acts 1:18).

nodes.label: Acts 1:19
nodes.text: It became known to everyone who lived in Jerusalem that in their language that field was called ‘Akeldama,’ that is, ‘The field of blood.’

nodes.label: Acts 1:20
nodes.text: For it is written in the book of Psalms, ‘Let his habitation be made desolate. Let no one dwell therein;’ and, ‘Let another take his office.’

nodes.label: Acts 1:21
nodes.text: “Of the men therefore who have accompanied us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,

nodes.label: Acts 1:22
nodes.text: beginning from the baptism of John, to the day that he was received up from us, of these one must become a witness with us of his resurrection.”

nodes.label: Acts 1:23
nodes.text: They put forward two, Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also called Justus, and Matthias.

nodes.label: Acts 1:24

nodes.label: Acts 1:25
nodes.text: to take part in this ministry and apostleship from which Judas fell away, that he might go to his own place.”

nodes.label: Acts 1:26

nodes.text: Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and people from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia,

nodes.label: Acts 2:11
nodes.text: Cretans and Arabians: we hear them speaking in our languages the mighty works of God!”

nodes.label: Acts 2:12
nodes.text: They were all amazed, and were perplexed, saying to one another, “What does this mean?”

nodes.label: Acts 2:13

variants.note: Codex Bezae D* reads 'ten apostles' against the majority's 'the eleven' (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles, Acts 2:14); no manuscript node for Bezae exists in this graph.

nodes.label: Acts 2:15
nodes.text: For these aren’t drunken, as you suppose, seeing it is only the third hour of the day.

nodes.label: Acts 2:17
nodes.text: ‘It will be in the last days, says God, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your young men will see visions. Your old men will dream dreams.

nodes.label: Acts 2:19
nodes.text: I will show wonders in the sky above, and signs on the earth beneath; blood, and fire, and billows of smoke.

nodes.label: Acts 2:21

nodes.label: Acts 2:22
nodes.text: “Men of Israel, hear these words! Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved by God to you by mighty works and wonders and signs which God did by him among you, even as you yourselves know,

nodes.label: Acts 2:24
nodes.text: whom God raised up, having freed him from the agony of death, because it was not possible that he should be held by it.

nodes.label: Acts 2:25
nodes.text: For David says concerning him, ‘I saw the Lord always before my face, For he is on my right hand, that I should not be moved.

nodes.label: Acts 2:26
nodes.text: Therefore my heart was glad, and my tongue rejoiced. Moreover my flesh also will dwell in hope;

nodes.label: Acts 2:27
nodes.text: because you will not leave my soul in Hades, neither will you allow your Holy One to see decay.

nodes.label: Acts 2:28
nodes.text: You made known to me the ways of life. You will make me full of gladness with your presence.’

nodes.label: Acts 2:29
nodes.text: “Brothers, I may tell you freely of the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.

nodes.label: Acts 2:30
nodes.text: Therefore, being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him that of the fruit of his body, according to the flesh, he would raise up the Christ to sit on his throne,

nodes.label: Acts 2:31
nodes.text: he foreseeing this spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, that his soul wasn’t left in Hades, and his flesh didn’t see decay.

nodes.text: This Jesus God raised up, to which we all are witnesses.

nodes.label: Acts 2:33
nodes.text: Being therefore exalted by the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he has poured out this, which you now see and hear.

nodes.label: Acts 2:34
nodes.text: For David didn’t ascend into the heavens, but he says himself, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit by my right hand,

nodes.label: Acts 2:35
nodes.text: until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”’

nodes.label: Acts 2:36
nodes.text: “Let all the house of Israel therefore know certainly that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified.”

nodes.label: Acts 2:37
nodes.text: Now when they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?”

nodes.label: Acts 2:38

nodes.text: For the promise is to you, and to your children, and to all who are far off, even as many as the Lord our God will call to himself.”

nodes.label: Acts 2:42

nodes.label: Acts 3:1

nodes.text:

nodes.text: However, the Most High doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says,

nodes.label: Acts 7:49
nodes.text: ‘heaven is my throne, and the earth a footstool for my feet. What kind of house will you build me?’ says the Lord. ‘Or what is the place of my rest?

nodes.label: Acts 7:50
nodes.text: Didn’t my hand make all these things?’

nodes.label: Acts 7:51
nodes.text: “You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit! As your fathers did, so you do.

nodes.label: Acts 7:52
nodes.text: Which of the prophets didn’t your fathers persecute? They killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you have now become betrayers and murderers.

nodes.label: Acts 7:53
nodes.text: You received the law as it was ordained by angels, and didn’t keep it!”

nodes.label: Acts 7:54
nodes.text: Now when they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed at him with their teeth.

nodes.label: Acts 7:55
nodes.text: But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, looked up steadfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God,

nodes.label: Acts 7:56
nodes.text: and said, “Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!”

nodes.label: Acts 7:57
nodes.text: But they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and rushed at him with one accord.

nodes.label: Acts 7:58
nodes.text: They threw him out of the city, and stoned him. The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.

nodes.label: Acts 7:59
nodes.text: They stoned Stephen as he called out, saying, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!”

nodes.label: Acts 7:60
nodes.text: He kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, “Lord, don’t hold this sin against them!” When he had said this, he fell asleep.

nodes.label: Acts 8:1
nodes.text: Saul was consenting to his death. A great persecution arose against the assembly which was in Jerusalem in that day. They were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles.

nodes.label: Acts 8:2
nodes.text: Devout men buried Stephen, and lamented greatly over him.

nodes.label: Acts 8:3
nodes.text: But Saul ravaged the assembly, entering into every house, and dragged both men and women off to prison.

nodes.label: Acts 8:4
nodes.text: Therefore those who were scattered abroad went around preaching the word.

nodes.label: Acts 8:5
nodes.text: Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and proclaimed to them the Christ.

nodes.label: Acts 8:6
nodes.text: The multitudes listened with one accord to the things that were spoken by Philip, when they heard and saw the signs which he did.

nodes.label: Acts 8:7
nodes.text: For unclean spirits came out of many of those who had them. They came out, crying with a loud voice. Many who had been paralyzed and lame were healed.

nodes.label: Acts 8:8
nodes.text: There was great joy in that city.

nodes.label: Acts 8:9
nodes.text: But there was a certain man, Simon by name, who used to practice sorcery in the city, and amazed the people of Samaria, making himself out to be some great one,

nodes.label: Acts 8:10
nodes.text: to whom they all listened, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is that great power of God.”

nodes.label: Acts 8:11
nodes.text: They listened to him, because for a long time he had amazed them with his sorceries.

nodes.label: Acts 8:12
nodes.text: But when they believed Philip preaching good news concerning God’s Kingdom and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

nodes.label: Acts 8:13
nodes.text: Simon himself also believed. Being baptized, he continued with Philip. Seeing signs and great miracles occurring, he was amazed.

nodes.label: Acts 8:14
nodes.text: Now when the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them,

nodes.label: Acts 8:15
nodes.text: who, when they had come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit;

nodes.label: Acts 8:16
nodes.text: for as yet he had fallen on none of them. They had only been baptized in the name of Christ Jesus.

nodes.label: Acts 8:17
nodes.text: Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.

nodes.label: Acts 8:18
nodes.text: Now when Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money,

nodes.label: Acts 8:19
nodes.text: saying, “Give me also this power, that whomever I lay my hands on may receive the Holy Spirit.”

nodes.label: Acts 8:20
nodes.text: But Peter said to him, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money!

nodes.label: Acts 8:21
nodes.text: You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart isn’t right before God.

nodes.label: Acts 8:22
nodes.text: Repent therefore of this, your wickedness, and ask God if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you.

nodes.label: Acts 8:23
nodes.text: For I see that you are in the poison of bitterness and in the bondage of iniquity.”

nodes.label: Acts 8:24
nodes.text: Simon answered, “Pray for me to the Lord, that none of the things which you have spoken happen to me.”

nodes.label: Acts 8:25
nodes.text: They therefore, when they had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the Good News to many villages of the Samaritans.

nodes.label: Acts 8:26
nodes.text: But an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, “Arise, and go toward the south to the way that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza. This is a desert.”

variants.reading: kata mesembrian read as 'at noon' rather than 'toward the south'
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Acts 8' article: the Greek may mean 'towards the south' or 'at noon'; a marginal note in the Revised Version, the text of the Jerusalem Bible and the Ethiopic text state 'at noon'. No manuscript node of this graph carries the reading.

nodes.label: Acts 8:27
nodes.text: He arose and went; and behold, there was a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure, who had come to Jerusalem to worship.

nodes.label: Acts 8:28
nodes.text: He was returning and sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.

nodes.label: Acts 8:29
nodes.text: The Spirit said to Philip, “Go near, and join yourself to this chariot.”

nodes.label: Acts 8:30
nodes.text: Philip ran to him, and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said, “Do you understand what you are reading?”

nodes.label: Acts 8:31
nodes.text: He said, “How can I, unless someone explains it to me?” He begged Philip to come up and sit with him.

nodes.label: Acts 8:32
nodes.text:
Now the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this,
“He was led as a sheep to the slaughter.
As a lamb before his shearer is silent,
so he doesn’t open his mouth.

nodes.label: Acts 8:33
nodes.text:
In his humiliation, his judgment was taken away.
Who will declare His generation?
For his life is taken from the earth.”

nodes.label: Acts 8:34
nodes.text: The eunuch answered Philip, “Who is the prophet talking about? About himself, or about someone else?”

nodes.label: Acts 8:35
nodes.text: Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, preached to him about Jesus.

nodes.label: Acts 8:36
nodes.text: As they went on the way, they came to some water, and the eunuch said, “Behold, here is water. What is keeping me from being baptized?”

variants.reading: KJV: 'And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.' Verse omitted in most modern versions
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' article: 'verse omitted by P45, P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C, P, Psi, 049...' — Sinaiticus and Vaticanus both omit it; the omission carries UBS confidence A; cited by Irenaeus (c. 180) and present in the Old Latin and Vulgate. No preserves edge from either codex is written for this verse.

nodes.label: Acts 8:38
nodes.text: He commanded the chariot to stand still, and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.

nodes.label: Acts 8:39
nodes.text: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and the eunuch didn’t see him any more, for he went on his way rejoicing.

variants.reading: 'the Holy Spirit fell on the eunuch, and an angel of the Lord caught up Philip'
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' article lists this reading for A, 36a, 94, 103, 307, 322, 323, 385, 453, 467, 945, 1739, it, vg, syr-h; none of these witnesses is a manuscript node of this graph.

nodes.label: Acts 8:40
nodes.text: But Philip was found at Azotus. Passing through, he preached the Good News to all the cities, until he came to Caesarea.

nodes.label: Acts 9:1
nodes.text: But Saul, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest,

nodes.label: Acts 9:2
nodes.text: and asked for letters from him to the synagogues of Damascus, that if he found any who were of the Way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Acts 9:3
nodes.text: As he traveled, he got close to Damascus, and suddenly a light from the sky shone around him.

nodes.label: Acts 9:4
nodes.text:
He fell on the earth, and heard a voice saying to him,
“Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?”

nodes.label: Acts 9:5
nodes.text:
He said, “Who are you, Lord?”
The Lord said,
“I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

nodes.label: Acts 9:6
nodes.text:
But
rise up, and enter into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”

nodes.label: Acts 9:7
nodes.text: The men who traveled with him stood speechless, hearing the sound, but seeing no one.

nodes.label: Acts 9:8
nodes.text: Saul arose from the ground, and when his eyes were opened, he saw no one. They led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.

nodes.label: Acts 9:9
nodes.text: He was without sight for three days, and neither ate nor drank.

nodes.label: Acts 9:10
nodes.text:
Now there was a certain disciple at Damascus named Ananias. The Lord said to him in a vision,
“Ananias!”
He said, “Behold, it’s me, Lord.”

nodes.label: Acts 9:11
Acts 9:12
nodes.text: and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias coming in, and laying his hands on him, that he might receive his sight.”

nodes.label: Acts 9:13
nodes.text: But Ananias answered, “Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he did to your saints at Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Acts 9:14
nodes.text: Here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on your name.”

nodes.label: Acts 9:15
nodes.text:
But the Lord said to him,
“Go your way, for he is my chosen vessel to bear my name before the nations and kings, and the children of Israel.

nodes.label: Acts 9:16
nodes.text: For I will show him how many things he must suffer for my name’s sake.”

nodes.label: Acts 9:17
nodes.text: Ananias departed, and entered into the house. Laying his hands on him, he said, “Brother Saul, the Lord, who appeared to you on the road by which you came, has sent me, that you may receive your sight, and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

nodes.label: Acts 9:18
nodes.text: Immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he received his sight. He arose and was baptized.

nodes.label: Acts 9:19
nodes.text: He took food and was strengthened. Saul stayed several days with the disciples who were at Damascus.

nodes.label: Acts 9:20
nodes.text: Immediately in the synagogues he proclaimed the Christ, that he is the Son of God.

nodes.label: Acts 9:21
nodes.text: All who heard him were amazed, and said, “Isn’t this he who in Jerusalem made havoc of those who called on this name? And he had come here intending to bring them bound before the chief priests!”

nodes.label: Acts 9:22
nodes.text: But Saul increased more in strength, and confounded the Jews who lived at Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.

nodes.label: Acts 9:23
nodes.text: When many days were fulfilled, the Jews conspired together to kill him,

nodes.label: Acts 9:24
nodes.text: but their plot became known to Saul. They watched the gates both day and night that they might kill him,

nodes.label: Acts 9:25
nodes.text: but his disciples took him by night, and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.

nodes.label: Acts 9:26
nodes.text: When Saul had come to Jerusalem, he tried to join himself to the disciples; but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

nodes.label: Acts 9:27
nodes.text: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared to them how he had seen the Lord on the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.

nodes.label: Acts 9:28
nodes.text: He was with them entering into Jerusalem,

nodes.label: Acts 9:29
nodes.text: preaching boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus. He spoke and disputed against the Hellenists, but they were seeking to kill him.

nodes.label: Acts 9:30
nodes.text: When the brothers knew it, they brought him down to Caesarea, and sent him off to Tarsus.

nodes.label: Acts 9:31
nodes.text: So the assemblies throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, and were built up. They were multiplied, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit.

nodes.label: Acts 9:32
nodes.text: As Peter went throughout all those parts, he came down also to the saints who lived at Lydda.

nodes.label: Acts 9:33
nodes.text: There he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had been bedridden for eight years, because he was paralyzed.

nodes.label: Acts 9:34
nodes.text: Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed!” Immediately he arose.

nodes.label: Acts 9:35
nodes.text: All who lived at Lydda and in Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.

nodes.label: Acts 9:36
nodes.text: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which when translated, means Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and acts of mercy which she did.

nodes.label: Acts 9:37
nodes.text: In those days, she became sick, and died. When they had washed her, they laid her in an upper room.

nodes.label: Acts 9:38
nodes.text: As Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, imploring him not to delay in coming to them.

nodes.label: Acts 9:39
nodes.text: Peter got up and went with them. When he had come, they brought him into the upper room. All the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas had made while she was with them.

nodes.label: Acts 9:40
nodes.text: Peter sent them all out, and knelt down and prayed. Turning to the body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.

nodes.label: Acts 9:41
nodes.text: He gave her his hand, and raised her up. Calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.

nodes.label: Acts 9:42
nodes.text: And it became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.

nodes.label: Acts 9:43
nodes.text: He stayed many days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.

nodes.label: Acts 10:1
nodes.text: Now there was a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment,

nodes.label: Acts 10:2
nodes.text: a devout man, and one who feared God with all his house, who gave gifts for the needy generously to the people, and always prayed to God.

nodes.label: Acts 10:3
nodes.text: At about the ninth hour of the day, he clearly saw in a vision an angel of God coming to him, and saying to him, “Cornelius!”

nodes.label: Acts 10:4
nodes.text:
He, fastening his eyes on him, and being frightened, said, “What is it, Lord?”
He said to him, “Your prayers and your gifts to the needy have gone up for a memorial before God.

nodes.label: Acts 10:5
nodes.text: Now send men to Joppa, and get Simon, who is also called Peter.

nodes.label: Acts 10:6
nodes.text: He lodges with a tanner named Simon, whose house is by the seaside.

nodes.label: Acts 10:7
nodes.text: When the angel who spoke to him had departed, Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier of those who waited on him continually.

nodes.label: Acts 10:8
nodes.text: Having explained everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.

nodes.label: Acts 10:9
nodes.text: Now on the next day as they were on their journey, and got close to the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray at about noon.

nodes.label: Acts 10:10
nodes.text: He became hungry and desired to eat, but while they were preparing, he fell into a trance.

nodes.label: Acts 10:11
nodes.text: He saw heaven opened and a certain container descending to him, like a great sheet let down by four corners on the earth,

nodes.label: Acts 10:12
nodes.text: in which were all kinds of four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, reptiles, and birds of the sky.

nodes.label: Acts 10:13
nodes.text:
A voice came to him,
“Rise, Peter, kill and eat!”

variants.reading: Πέτρε (Peter) omitted: 'Rise, kill and eat!'
variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 45, Some notable readings: 'Acts 10:13 Πέτρε (Peter): Omit.: 𝔓45 gig Clement Ambrose'. The WEB prints 'Rise, Peter, kill and eat!'.

nodes.label: Acts 10:14
nodes.text: But Peter said, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten anything that is common or unclean.”

nodes.label: Acts 10:15
nodes.text:
A voice came to him again the second time,
“What God has cleansed, you must not call unclean.”

nodes.label: Acts 10:16
nodes.text: This was done three times, and immediately the vessel was received up into heaven.

variants.reading: εὐθὺς (immediately) omitted
variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 45, Some notable readings: 'Acts 10:16 εὐθὺς (immediately): Omit.: 𝔓45 36 453 1175 2818 it d syr p sa mss bo ms'.

nodes.label: Acts 10:17
nodes.text: Now while Peter was very perplexed in himself what the vision which he had seen might mean, behold, the men who were sent by Cornelius, having made inquiry for Simon’s house, stood before the gate,

nodes.label: Acts 10:18
nodes.text: and called and asked whether Simon, who was also called Peter, was lodging there.

nodes.label: Acts 10:19
nodes.text:
While Peter was pondering the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three
 men seek you.

nodes.label: Acts 10:20
nodes.text: But arise, get down, and go with them, doubting nothing; for I have sent them.”

nodes.label: Acts 10:21
nodes.text: Peter went down to the men, and said, “Behold, I am he whom you seek. Why have you come?”

nodes.label: Acts 10:22
nodes.text: They said, “Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and one who fears God, and well spoken of by all the nation of the Jews, was directed by a holy angel to invite you to his house, and to listen to what you say.”

nodes.label: Acts 10:23
nodes.text: So he called them in and provided a place to stay. On the next day Peter arose and went out with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa accompanied him.

nodes.label: Acts 10:24
nodes.text: On the next day they entered into Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and his near friends.

nodes.label: Acts 10:25
nodes.text: When Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell down at his feet, and worshiped him.

nodes.label: Acts 10:26
nodes.text: But Peter raised him up, saying, “Stand up! I myself am also a man.”

nodes.label: Acts 10:27
nodes.text: As he talked with him, he went in and found many gathered together.

nodes.label: Acts 10:28
nodes.text: He said to them, “You yourselves know how it is an unlawful thing for a man who is a Jew to join himself or come to one of another nation, but God has shown me that I shouldn’t call any man unholy or unclean.

nodes.label: Acts 10:29
nodes.text: Therefore also I came without complaint when I was sent for. I ask therefore, why did you send for me?”

nodes.label: Acts 10:30
nodes.text: Cornelius said, “Four days ago, I was fasting until this hour, and at the ninth hour, I prayed in my house, and behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing,

nodes.label: Acts 10:31
nodes.text: and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer is heard, and your gifts to the needy are remembered in the sight of God.

nodes.label: Acts 10:32
