nodes.text: Send therefore to Joppa, and summon Simon, who is also called Peter. He lodges in the house of a tanner named Simon, by the seaside. When he comes, he will speak to you.’

nodes.label: Acts 10:33
nodes.text: Therefore I sent to you at once, and it was good of you to come. Now therefore we are all here present in the sight of God to hear all things that have been commanded you by God.”

variants.reading: κυρίου (Lord) where the WEB reads 'commanded you by God'
variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 45, Some notable readings: 'Acts 10:33 κυρίου (Lord): 𝔓45 (vid) א A B C E Ψ 81* ...', against θεου (God): 𝔓74 D Byz syr p sa mae bo ms. The WEB keeps 'God'.

nodes.label: Acts 10:34
nodes.text: Peter opened his mouth and said, “Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism;

nodes.label: Acts 10:35
nodes.text: but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.

nodes.label: Acts 10:36
nodes.text: The word which he sent to the children of Israel, preaching good news of peace by Jesus Christ—he is Lord of all—

nodes.label: Acts 10:37
nodes.text: you yourselves know what happened, which was proclaimed throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;

nodes.label: Acts 10:38
nodes.text: even Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.

nodes.label: Acts 10:39
nodes.text: We are witnesses of everything he did both in the country of the Jews, and in Jerusalem; whom they also killed, hanging him on a tree.

nodes.label: Acts 10:40
nodes.text: God raised him up the third day, and gave him to be revealed,

nodes.label: Acts 10:41
nodes.text: not to all the people, but to witnesses who were chosen before by God, to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.

nodes.label: Acts 10:42
nodes.text: He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that this is he who is appointed by God as the Judge of the living and the dead.

nodes.label: Acts 10:43
nodes.text: All the prophets testify about him, that through his name everyone who believes in him will receive remission of sins.”

nodes.label: Acts 10:44
nodes.text: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all those who heard the word.

nodes.label: Acts 10:45
nodes.text: They of the circumcision who believed were amazed, as many as came with Peter, because the gift of the Holy Spirit was also poured out on the Gentiles.

nodes.label: Acts 10:46
nodes.text:
For they heard them speaking in other languages and magnifying God.
Then Peter answered,

nodes.label: Acts 10:47
nodes.text: “Can anyone forbid these people from being baptized with water? They have received the Holy Spirit just like us.”

nodes.label: Acts 10:48
nodes.text: He commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay some days.

nodes.label: Acts 11:1
nodes.text: Now the apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.

nodes.label: Acts 11:2
nodes.text: When Peter had come up to Jerusalem, those who were of the circumcision contended with him,

nodes.label: Acts 11:3
nodes.text: saying, “You went in to uncircumcised men, and ate with them!”

nodes.label: Acts 11:4
nodes.text: But Peter began, and explained to them in order, saying,

nodes.label: Acts 11:5
nodes.text: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain container descending, like it was a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners. It came as far as me.

nodes.label: Acts 11:6
nodes.text: When I had looked intently at it, I considered, and saw the four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky.

nodes.label: Acts 11:7
nodes.text:
I also heard a voice saying to me,
‘Rise, Peter, kill and eat!’

nodes.label: Acts 11:8
nodes.text: But I said, ‘Not so, Lord, for nothing unholy or unclean has ever entered into my mouth.’

nodes.label: Acts 11:9
nodes.text:
But a voice answered me the second time out of heaven,
‘What God has cleansed, don’t you call unclean.’

nodes.label: Acts 11:10
nodes.text: This was done three times, and all were drawn up again into heaven.

nodes.label: Acts 11:11
nodes.text: Behold, immediately three men stood before the house where I was, having been sent from Caesarea to me.

nodes.label: Acts 11:12
nodes.text: The Spirit told me to go with them, without discriminating. These six brothers also accompanied me, and we entered into the man’s house.

variants.reading: μηδὲν διακρίναντα (making no distinction) omitted
variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 45, Some notable readings: 'Acts 11:12 μηδὲν διακρίναντα (making no distinction): Omit.: 𝔓45 D it l p* syr h'. The WEB prints 'without discriminating'.

nodes.label: Acts 11:13
nodes.text: He told us how he had seen the angel standing in his house, and saying to him, ‘Send to Joppa, and get Simon, who is called Peter,

nodes.label: Acts 11:14
nodes.text: who will speak to you words by which you will be saved, you and all your house.’

nodes.label: Acts 11:15
nodes.text: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, even as on us at the beginning.

nodes.label: Acts 11:16
nodes.text:
I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said,
‘John indeed baptized in water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit.’

nodes.label: Acts 11:17
nodes.text: If then God gave to them the same gift as us, when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I could withstand God?”

nodes.label: Acts 11:18
nodes.text: When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, “Then God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life!”

nodes.label: Acts 11:19
nodes.text: They therefore who were scattered abroad by the oppression that arose about Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except to Jews only.

nodes.label: Acts 11:20
nodes.text: But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they had come to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists, preaching the Lord Jesus.

nodes.label: Acts 11:21
nodes.text: The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.

nodes.label: Acts 11:22
nodes.text: The report concerning them came to the ears of the assembly which was in Jerusalem. They sent out Barnabas to go as far as Antioch,

nodes.label: Acts 11:23
nodes.text: who, when he had come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad. He exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they should remain near to the Lord.

nodes.label: Acts 11:24
nodes.text: For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith, and many people were added to the Lord.

nodes.label: Acts 11:25
nodes.text: Barnabas went out to Tarsus to look for Saul.

nodes.label: Acts 11:26
nodes.text: When he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they were gathered together with the assembly, and taught many people. The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.

nodes.label: Acts 11:27
nodes.text: Now in these days, prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

nodes.label: Acts 11:28
nodes.text: One of them named Agabus stood up, and indicated by the Spirit that there should be a great famine all over the world, which also happened in the days of Claudius.

nodes.label: Acts 11:29
nodes.text: As any of the disciples had plenty, each determined to send relief to the brothers who lived in Judea;

nodes.label: Acts 11:30
nodes.text: which they also did, sending it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.

nodes.label: Acts 12:1
nodes.text: Now about that time, King Herod stretched out his hands to oppress some of the assembly.

nodes.label: Acts 12:2
nodes.text: He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.

nodes.label: Acts 12:3
nodes.text: When he saw that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. This was during the days of unleavened bread.

nodes.label: Acts 12:4
nodes.text: When he had arrested him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four squads of four soldiers each to guard him, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover.

nodes.label: Acts 12:5
nodes.text: Peter therefore was kept in the prison, but constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him.

nodes.label: Acts 12:6
nodes.text: The same night when Herod was about to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains. Guards in front of the door kept the prison.

nodes.label: Acts 12:7
nodes.text: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side, and woke him up, saying, “Stand up quickly!” His chains fell off from his hands.

nodes.label: Acts 12:8
nodes.text: The angel said to him, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” He did so. He said to him, “Put on your cloak, and follow me.”

nodes.label: Acts 12:9
nodes.text: And he went out and followed him. He didn’t know that what was being done by the angel was real, but thought he saw a vision.

nodes.label: Acts 12:10
nodes.text: When they were past the first and the second guard, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened to them by itself. They went out, and went down one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.

nodes.label: Acts 12:11
nodes.text: When Peter had come to himself, he said, “Now I truly know that the Lord has sent out his angel and delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from everything the Jewish people were expecting.”

nodes.label: Acts 12:12
nodes.text: Thinking about that, he came to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where many were gathered together and were praying.

nodes.label: Acts 12:13
nodes.text: When Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a maid named Rhoda came to answer.

nodes.label: Acts 12:14
nodes.text: When she recognized Peter’s voice, she didn’t open the gate for joy, but ran in, and reported that Peter was standing in front of the gate.

nodes.label: Acts 12:15
nodes.text: They said to her, “You are crazy!” But she insisted that it was so. They said, “It is his angel.”

nodes.label: Acts 12:16
nodes.text: But Peter continued knocking. When they had opened, they saw him, and were amazed.

nodes.label: Acts 12:17
nodes.text: But he, beckoning to them with his hand to be silent, declared to them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. He said, “Tell these things to James, and to the brothers.” Then he departed, and went to another place.

nodes.label: Acts 12:18
nodes.text: Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers about what had become of Peter.

nodes.label: Acts 12:19
nodes.text: When Herod had sought for him, and didn’t find him, he examined the guards, and commanded that they should be put to death. He went down from Judea to Caesarea, and stayed there.

nodes.label: Acts 12:20
nodes.text: Now Herod was very angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came with one accord to him, and, having made Blastus, the king’s personal aide, their friend, they asked for peace, because their country depended on the king’s country for food.

nodes.label: Acts 12:21
nodes.text: On an appointed day, Herod dressed himself in royal clothing, sat on the throne, and gave a speech to them.

nodes.label: Acts 12:22
nodes.text: The people shouted, “The voice of a god, and not of a man!”

nodes.label: Acts 12:23
nodes.text: Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he didn’t give God the glory, and he was eaten by worms and died.

nodes.label: Acts 12:24
nodes.text: But the word of God grew and multiplied.

nodes.label: Acts 12:25
nodes.text: Barnabas and Saul returned to Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their service, also taking with them John who was called Mark.

variants.reading: εις Ιερουσαλημ ('to Jerusalem', the WEB wording)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' lists Acts 12:25 εις Ιερουσαλημ ('to Jerusalem') for א, B, H, L, P, 049, 056, 0142 and others - the reading both graph codices carry. Against it, εξ Ιερουσαλημ ('from Jerusalem') is listed for P74, A, 33, 69, 630, 2127, and απο Ιερουσαλημ ('from Jerusalem') for D, Ψ, 181, 436, 614, 2412 and lectionaries. The WEB prints the 'to Jerusalem' wording; 'from Jerusalem' would mean the pair set out from Jerusalem for Antioch instead.

nodes.label: Acts 13:1
nodes.text: Now in the assembly that was at Antioch there were some prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

nodes.label: Acts 13:2
nodes.text: As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”

nodes.label: Acts 13:3
nodes.text: Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.

nodes.label: Acts 13:4
nodes.text: So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia. From there they sailed to Cyprus.

nodes.label: Acts 13:5
nodes.text: When they were at Salamis, they proclaimed God’s word in the Jewish synagogues. They had also John as their attendant.

nodes.label: Acts 13:6
nodes.text: When they had gone through the island to Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar Jesus,

nodes.label: Acts 13:7
nodes.text: who was with the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding. This man summoned Barnabas and Saul, and sought to hear the word of God.

nodes.label: Acts 13:8
nodes.text: But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

nodes.label: Acts 13:9
nodes.text: But Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fastened his eyes on him,

nodes.label: Acts 13:10
nodes.text: and said, “Full of all deceit and all cunning, you son of the devil, you enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?

nodes.label: Acts 13:11
nodes.text:
Now, behold, the hand of the Lord is on you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a season!”
Immediately a mist and darkness fell on him. He went around seeking someone to lead him by the hand.

nodes.label: Acts 13:12
nodes.text: Then the proconsul, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.

nodes.label: Acts 13:13
nodes.text: Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos, and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Acts 13:14
nodes.text: But they, passing on from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia. They went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and sat down.

nodes.label: Acts 13:15
nodes.text: After the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, “Brothers, if you have any word of exhortation for the people, speak.”

nodes.label: Acts 13:16
nodes.text: Paul stood up, and beckoning with his hand said, “Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen.

nodes.label: Acts 13:17
nodes.text: The God of this people chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they stayed as aliens in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm, he led them out of it.

nodes.label: Acts 13:18
nodes.text: For a period of about forty years he put up with them in the wilderness.

nodes.label: Acts 13:19
nodes.text: When he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave them their land for an inheritance, for about four hundred fifty years.

nodes.label: Acts 13:20
nodes.text: After these things he gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.

nodes.label: Acts 13:21
nodes.text: Afterward they asked for a king, and God gave to them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.

nodes.label: Acts 13:22
nodes.text: When he had removed him, he raised up David to be their king, to whom he also testified, ‘I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who will do all my will.’

nodes.label: Acts 13:23
nodes.text: From this man’s offspring, God has brought salvation to Israel according to his promise,

nodes.label: Acts 13:24
nodes.text: before his coming, when John had first preached the baptism of repentance to Israel.

nodes.label: Acts 13:25
nodes.text: As John was fulfilling his course, he said, ‘What do you suppose that I am? I am not he. But behold, one comes after me, the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.’

nodes.label: Acts 13:26
nodes.text: Brothers, children of the stock of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, the word of this salvation is sent out to you.

nodes.label: Acts 13:27
nodes.text: For those who dwell in Jerusalem, and their rulers, because they didn’t know him, nor the voices of the prophets which are read every Sabbath, fulfilled them by condemning him.

nodes.label: Acts 13:28
nodes.text: Though they found no cause for death, they still asked Pilate to have him killed.

nodes.label: Acts 13:29
nodes.text: When they had fulfilled all things that were written about him, they took him down from the tree, and laid him in a tomb.

nodes.label: Acts 13:30
nodes.text: But God raised him from the dead,

nodes.label: Acts 13:31
nodes.text: and he was seen for many days by those who came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are his witnesses to the people.

nodes.label: Acts 13:32
nodes.text: We bring you good news of the promise made to the fathers,

nodes.label: Acts 13:33
nodes.text:
that God has fulfilled the same to us, their children, in that he raised up Jesus. As it is also written in the second psalm,
‘You are my Son.
Today I have become your father.’

variants.reading: εν τω πρωτω ψαλμω γεγραπται ('it is written in the FIRST Psalm') and εν τοις ψαλμοις γεγραπται ('it is written in Psalms')
variants.note: Fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles', Acts 13:33: the WEB order εν τω ψαλμω γεγραπται τω δευτερω is read by P75, א, A, B, C, Psi, 33...; D* reads 'first Psalm' and P45 'in Psalms'. Sinaiticus and Vaticanus carry the WEB reading (not the variant).

nodes.label: Acts 13:34
nodes.text: “Concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he has spoken thus: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.’

nodes.label: Acts 13:35
nodes.text: Therefore he says also in another psalm, ‘You will not allow your Holy One to see decay.’

nodes.label: Acts 13:36
nodes.text: For David, after he had in his own generation served the counsel of God, fell asleep, and was laid with his fathers, and saw decay.

nodes.label: Acts 13:37
nodes.text: But he whom God raised up saw no decay.

nodes.label: Acts 13:38
nodes.text: Be it known to you therefore, brothers, that through this man is proclaimed to you remission of sins,

nodes.label: Acts 13:39
nodes.text: and by him everyone who believes is justified from all things, from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.

nodes.label: Acts 13:40
nodes.text: Beware therefore, lest that come on you which is spoken in the prophets:

nodes.label: Acts 13:41
Acts 13:42
nodes.text: So when the Jews went out of the synagogue, the Gentiles begged that these words might be preached to them the next Sabbath.

nodes.label: Acts 13:43
nodes.text: Now when the synagogue broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas; who, speaking to them, urged them to continue in the grace of God.

nodes.label: Acts 13:44
nodes.text: The next Sabbath, almost the whole city was gathered together to hear the word of God.

nodes.label: Acts 13:45
nodes.text: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with jealousy, and contradicted the things which were spoken by Paul, and blasphemed.

nodes.label: Acts 13:46
nodes.text: Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly, and said, “It was necessary that God’s word should be spoken to you first. Since indeed you thrust it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.

nodes.label: Acts 13:47
nodes.text:
For so has the Lord commanded us, saying,
‘I have set you as a light for the Gentiles,
that you should bring salvation to the uttermost parts of the earth.’”

nodes.label: Acts 13:48
nodes.text: As the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of God. As many as were appointed to eternal life believed.

nodes.label: Acts 13:49
nodes.text: The Lord’s word was spread abroad throughout all the region.

nodes.label: Acts 13:50
nodes.text: But the Jews stirred up the devout and prominent women and the chief men of the city, and stirred up a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and threw them out of their borders.

nodes.label: Acts 13:51
nodes.text: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came to Iconium.

nodes.label: Acts 13:52
nodes.text: The disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

nodes.label: Acts 14:1
nodes.text: In Iconium, they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks believed.

nodes.label: Acts 14:2
nodes.text: But the disbelieving Jews stirred up and embittered the souls of the Gentiles against the brothers.

nodes.label: Acts 14:3
nodes.text: Therefore they stayed there a long time, speaking boldly in the Lord, who testified to the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands.

nodes.label: Acts 14:4
nodes.text: But the multitude of the city was divided. Part sided with the Jews, and part with the apostles.

nodes.label: Acts 14:5
nodes.text: When some of both the Gentiles and the Jews, with their rulers, made a violent attempt to mistreat and stone them,

nodes.label: Acts 14:6
nodes.text: they became aware of it, and fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, Derbe, and the surrounding region.

nodes.label: Acts 14:7
nodes.text: There they preached the Good News.

nodes.label: Acts 14:8
nodes.text: At Lystra a certain man sat, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked.

nodes.label: Acts 14:9
nodes.text: He was listening to Paul speaking, who, fastening eyes on him, and seeing that he had faith to be made whole,

nodes.label: Acts 14:10
nodes.text: said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” He leaped up and walked.

nodes.label: Acts 14:11
nodes.text: When the multitude saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice, saying in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!”

nodes.label: Acts 14:12
nodes.text: They called Barnabas “Jupiter”, and Paul “Mercury”, because he was the chief speaker.

nodes.label: Acts 14:13
nodes.text: The priest of Jupiter, whose temple was in front of their city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates, and would have made a sacrifice along with the multitudes.

nodes.label: Acts 14:14
nodes.text: But when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of it, they tore their clothes, and sprang into the multitude, crying out,

nodes.label: Acts 14:15
nodes.text: “Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them;

nodes.label: Acts 14:16
nodes.text: who in the generations gone by allowed all the nations to walk in their own ways.

nodes.label: Acts 14:17
nodes.text: Yet he didn’t leave himself without witness, in that he did good and gave you rains from the sky and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.”

nodes.label: Acts 14:18
nodes.text: Even saying these things, they hardly stopped the multitudes from making a sacrifice to them.

nodes.label: Acts 14:19
nodes.text: But some Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there, and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul, and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.

nodes.label: Acts 14:20
nodes.text: But as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city. On the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.

nodes.label: Acts 14:21
nodes.text: When they had preached the Good News to that city, and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,

nodes.label: Acts 14:22
nodes.text: confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.

nodes.label: Acts 14:23
nodes.text: When they had appointed elders for them in every assembly, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they had believed.

nodes.label: Acts 14:24
nodes.text: They passed through Pisidia, and came to Pamphylia.

nodes.label: Acts 14:25
nodes.text: When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

nodes.label: Acts 14:26
nodes.text: From there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.

nodes.label: Acts 14:27
nodes.text: When they had arrived, and had gathered the assembly together, they reported all the things that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith to the nations.

nodes.label: Acts 14:28
nodes.text: They stayed there with the disciples for a long time.

nodes.label: Acts 15:1
nodes.text: Some men came down from Judea and taught the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised after the custom of Moses, you can’t be saved.”

nodes.label: Acts 15:2
nodes.text: Therefore when Paul and Barnabas had no small discord and discussion with them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas, and some others of them, to go up to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders about this question.

nodes.label: Acts 15:3
nodes.text: They, being sent on their way by the assembly, passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles. They caused great joy to all the brothers.

nodes.label: Acts 15:4
nodes.text: When they had come to Jerusalem, they were received by the assembly and the apostles and the elders, and they reported all things that God had done with them.

nodes.label: Acts 15:5
nodes.text: But some of the sect of the Pharisees who believed rose up, saying, “It is necessary to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.”

nodes.label: Acts 15:6
nodes.text: The apostles and the elders were gathered together to see about this matter.

nodes.label: Acts 15:7
nodes.text: When there had been much discussion, Peter rose up and said to them, “Brothers, you know that a good while ago God made a choice among you, that by my mouth the nations should hear the word of the Good News, and believe.

nodes.label: Acts 15:8
nodes.text: God, who knows the heart, testified about them, giving them the Holy Spirit, just like he did to us.

nodes.label: Acts 15:9
nodes.text: He made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.

nodes.label: Acts 15:10
nodes.text: Now therefore why do you tempt God, that you should put a yoke on the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?

nodes.label: Acts 15:11
nodes.text:
But we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus,
 just as they are.”

nodes.label: Acts 15:12
nodes.text: All the multitude kept silence, and they listened to Barnabas and Paul reporting what signs and wonders God had done among the nations through them.

nodes.label: Acts 15:13
nodes.text: After they were silent, James answered, “Brothers, listen to me.

nodes.label: Acts 15:14
nodes.text: Simeon has reported how God first visited the nations, to take out of them a people for his name.

nodes.label: Acts 15:15
nodes.text: This agrees with the words of the prophets. As it is written,

nodes.label: Acts 15:16
nodes.text:
‘After these things I will return.
I will again build the tabernacle of David, which has fallen.
I will again build its ruins.
I will set it up,

nodes.label: Acts 15:17
Acts 15:18
nodes.text: All of God’s works are known to him from eternity.’

nodes.label: Acts 15:19
nodes.text: “Therefore my judgment is that we don’t trouble those from among the Gentiles who turn to God,

nodes.label: Acts 15:20
nodes.text: but that we write to them that they abstain from the pollution of idols, from sexual immorality, from what is strangled, and from blood.

variants.reading: τῆς πορνείας ('from sexual immorality') omitted
variants.note: Fetched Wikipedia 'Papyrus 45', Some notable readings: "Acts 15:20 τῆς πορνείας (from sexual immorality): Omit.: P45 Incl.: Majority of manuscripts." The WEB prints the majority four-item text; P45 (which carries this verse) omits 'from sexual immorality'.

nodes.label: Acts 15:21
nodes.text: For Moses from generations of old has in every city those who preach him, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath.”

nodes.label: Acts 15:22
nodes.text: Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole assembly, to choose men out of their company, and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, chief men among the brothers.

nodes.label: Acts 15:23
nodes.text:
They wrote these things by their hand:
“The apostles, the elders, and the brothers, to the brothers who are of the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: greetings.

variants.reading: expanded openings after 'by their hand': 'this letter containing this precept' (C, ar, c, gig, w, geo) or D's 'an epistle by their hand containing these things'
variants.note: Fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles': Acts 15:23 γραψαντης δια χειρος αυτων – P45, P74, א*, A, B (the short reading the WEB follows); אc, E, (33), Byz and C, D, Ψ and others add expansions naming the letter.

nodes.label: Acts 15:24
nodes.text: Because we have heard that some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, saying, ‘You must be circumcised and keep the law,’ to whom we gave no commandment;

variants.reading: ψυχας υμων ('unsettling your souls') without the saying 'You must be circumcised and keep the law'
variants.note: Fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles': Acts 15:24 ψυχας υμων – P33, P45, P74, א, A, B, D, 33, 81, 629; the longer 'ψυχας υμων λεγοντες περιτεμνεσθαι και τηρειν τον νομον' is C, E, P, Ψ, 049, 056, 0142 and others. The WEB follows the longer reading; P45 (which carries this verse) supports the shorter.

nodes.label: Acts 15:25
nodes.text: it seemed good to us, having come to one accord, to choose out men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,

nodes.label: Acts 15:26
nodes.text: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

nodes.label: Acts 15:27
nodes.text: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who themselves will also tell you the same things by word of mouth.

nodes.label: Acts 15:28
nodes.text: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit, and to us, to lay no greater burden on you than these necessary things:

nodes.label: Acts 15:29
nodes.text: that you abstain from things sacrificed to idols, from blood, from things strangled, and from sexual immorality, from which if you keep yourselves, it will be well with you. Farewell.”

variants.reading: Western text: three-item decree omitting 'things strangled', plus the added negative Golden Rule ('and whatever things ye would not have done to yourselves, do not do to another')
variants.note: Fetched Wikipedia 'Council of Jerusalem': 'The Western version of Acts ... adds the negative form of the Golden Rule'; its Metzger discussion explains the two forms of the threefold (Western) decree against the fourfold decree most scholars regard as original. Codex Bezae (D), the chief Western witness, is not a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is empty.

nodes.label: Acts 15:30
nodes.text: So, when they were sent off, they came to Antioch. Having gathered the multitude together, they delivered the letter.

nodes.label: Acts 15:31
nodes.text: When they had read it, they rejoiced over the encouragement.

nodes.label: Acts 15:32
nodes.text: Judas and Silas, also being prophets themselves, encouraged the brothers with many words, and strengthened them.

nodes.label: Acts 15:33
nodes.text: After they had spent some time there, they were sent back with greetings from the brothers to the apostles.

nodes.label: Acts 15:35
nodes.text: But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.

nodes.label: Acts 15:36
nodes.text: After some days Paul said to Barnabas, “Let’s return now and visit our brothers in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”

nodes.label: Acts 15:37
nodes.text: Barnabas planned to take John, who was called Mark, with them also.

nodes.label: Acts 15:38
nodes.text: But Paul didn’t think that it was a good idea to take with them someone who had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia, and didn’t go with them to do the work.

nodes.label: Acts 15:39
nodes.text: Then the contention grew so sharp that they separated from each other. Barnabas took Mark with him, and sailed away to Cyprus,

nodes.label: Acts 15:40
nodes.text: but Paul chose Silas, and went out, being commended by the brothers to the grace of God.

variants.reading: κυρίου ('commended ... to the grace of the Lord') instead of θεου ('the grace of God')
variants.note: Fetched Wikipedia 'Papyrus 45', Some notable readings: 'Acts 15:40 κυρίου (Lord): P74 א A B D 33 81 it d vg st sa / θεου (God): P45 C E Ψ 1739 Byz gig it w vg cl syr bo'. The WEB follows θεου, which P45 carries; none of the κυρίου manuscripts is a graph node.

nodes.label: Acts 15:41
nodes.text: He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the assemblies.

nodes.label: Acts 16:1
nodes.text: He came to Derbe and Lystra: and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess who believed; but his father was a Greek.

nodes.label: Acts 16:2
nodes.text: The brothers who were at Lystra and Iconium gave a good testimony about him.

nodes.label: Acts 16:3
nodes.text: Paul wanted to have him go out with him, and he took and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those parts; for they all knew that his father was a Greek.

nodes.label: Acts 16:4
nodes.text: As they went on their way through the cities, they delivered the decrees to them to keep which had been ordained by the apostles and elders who were at Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Acts 16:5
nodes.text: So the assemblies were strengthened in the faith, and increased in number daily.

nodes.label: Acts 16:6
nodes.text: When they had gone through the region of Phrygia and Galatia, they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia.

nodes.label: Acts 16:7
nodes.text: When they had come opposite Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit didn’t allow them.

nodes.label: Acts 16:8
nodes.text: Passing by Mysia, they came down to Troas.

nodes.label: Acts 16:9
nodes.text: A vision appeared to Paul in the night. There was a man of Macedonia standing, begging him, and saying, “Come over into Macedonia and help us.”

nodes.label: Acts 16:10
nodes.text: When he had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go out to Macedonia, concluding that the Lord had called us to preach the Good News to them.

nodes.label: Acts 16:11
nodes.text: Setting sail therefore from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the day following to Neapolis;

nodes.label: Acts 16:12
nodes.text: and from there to Philippi, which is a city of Macedonia, the foremost of the district, a Roman colony. We were staying some days in this city.

nodes.label: Acts 16:13
nodes.text: On the Sabbath day we went outside of the city by a riverside, where we supposed there was a place of prayer, and we sat down, and spoke to the women who had come together.

nodes.label: Acts 16:14
nodes.text: A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, one who worshiped God, heard us; whose heart the Lord opened to listen to the things which were spoken by Paul.

nodes.label: Acts 16:15
nodes.text: When she and her household were baptized, she begged us, saying, “If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and stay.” So she persuaded us.

nodes.label: Acts 16:16
nodes.text: As we were going to prayer, a certain girl having a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much gain by fortune telling.

nodes.label: Acts 16:17
nodes.text: Following Paul and us, she cried out, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to us a way of salvation!”

nodes.label: Acts 16:18
nodes.text:
She was doing this for many days.
But Paul, becoming greatly annoyed, turned and said to the spirit, “I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her!” It came out that very hour.

nodes.label: Acts 16:19
nodes.text: But when her masters saw that the hope of their gain was gone, they seized Paul and Silas, and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers.

nodes.label: Acts 16:20
nodes.text: When they had brought them to the magistrates, they said, “These men, being Jews, are agitating our city,

nodes.label: Acts 16:21
nodes.text: and advocate customs which it is not lawful for us to accept or to observe, being Romans.”

nodes.label: Acts 16:22
nodes.text: The multitude rose up together against them, and the magistrates tore their clothes from them, and commanded them to be beaten with rods.

nodes.label: Acts 16:23
nodes.text: When they had laid many stripes on them, they threw them into prison, charging the jailer to keep them safely,

nodes.label: Acts 16:24
nodes.text: who, having received such a command, threw them into the inner prison, and secured their feet in the stocks.

nodes.label: Acts 16:25
nodes.text: But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.

nodes.label: Acts 16:26
nodes.text: Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened, and everyone’s bonds were loosened.

nodes.label: Acts 16:27
nodes.text: The jailer, being roused out of sleep and seeing the prison doors open, drew his sword and was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.

nodes.label: Acts 16:28
nodes.text: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, “Don’t harm yourself, for we are all here!”

nodes.label: Acts 16:29
nodes.text: He called for lights, sprang in, fell down trembling before Paul and Silas,

nodes.label: Acts 16:30
nodes.text: brought them out, and said, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”

nodes.label: Acts 16:31
nodes.text: They said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.”

nodes.label: Acts 16:32
nodes.text: They spoke the word of the Lord to him, and to all who were in his house.

variants.reading: the word of God (theou) at Acts 16:32
variants.note: Sinaiticus's original hand and B (with pc) read theou (God); P45, P74, a corrected Sinaiticus, A, C, (D), E, Psi, 33, 1739 and the Byzantine text read kyriou (Lord), as printed in the WEB (fetched Wikipedia, Papyrus 45).

nodes.label: Acts 16:33
nodes.text: He took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes, and was immediately baptized, he and all his household.

nodes.label: Acts 16:34
nodes.text: He brought them up into his house, and set food before them, and rejoiced greatly, with all his household, having believed in God.

nodes.label: Acts 16:35
nodes.text: But when it was day, the magistrates sent the sergeants, saying, “Let those men go.”

nodes.label: Acts 16:36
nodes.text: The jailer reported these words to Paul, saying, “The magistrates have sent to let you go; now therefore come out, and go in peace.”

nodes.label: Acts 16:37
nodes.text: But Paul said to them, “They have beaten us publicly, without a trial, men who are Romans, and have cast us into prison! Do they now release us secretly? No, most certainly, but let them come themselves and bring us out!”

nodes.label: Acts 16:38
nodes.text: The sergeants reported these words to the magistrates, and they were afraid when they heard that they were Romans,

nodes.label: Acts 16:39
nodes.text: and they came and begged them. When they had brought them out, they asked them to depart from the city.

nodes.label: Acts 16:40
nodes.text: They went out of the prison, and entered into Lydia’s house. When they had seen the brothers, they encouraged them, and departed.

nodes.label: Acts 17:1
nodes.text: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

nodes.label: Acts 17:2
nodes.text: Paul, as was his custom, went in to them, and for three Sabbath days reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

nodes.label: Acts 17:3
nodes.text: explaining and demonstrating that the Christ had to suffer and rise again from the dead, and saying, “This Jesus, whom I proclaim to you, is the Christ.”

nodes.label: Acts 17:4
nodes.text: Some of them were persuaded, and joined Paul and Silas, of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and not a few of the chief women.

nodes.label: Acts 17:5
nodes.text: But the unpersuaded Jews took along some wicked men from the marketplace, and gathering a crowd, set the city in an uproar. Assaulting the house of Jason, they sought to bring them out to the people.

nodes.label: Acts 17:6
nodes.text: When they didn’t find them, they dragged Jason and certain brothers before the rulers of the city, crying, “These who have turned the world upside down have come here also,

nodes.label: Acts 17:7
nodes.text: whom Jason has received. These all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus!”

nodes.label: Acts 17:8
nodes.text: The multitude and the rulers of the city were troubled when they heard these things.

nodes.label: Acts 17:9
nodes.text: When they had taken security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.

nodes.label: Acts 17:10
nodes.text: The brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Beroea. When they arrived, they went into the Jewish synagogue.

nodes.label: Acts 17:11
nodes.text: Now these were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, examining the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.

nodes.label: Acts 17:12
nodes.text: Many of them therefore believed; also of the prominent Greek women, and not a few men.

nodes.label: Acts 17:13
nodes.text: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was proclaimed by Paul at Beroea also, they came there likewise, agitating the multitudes.

nodes.label: Acts 17:14
nodes.text: Then the brothers immediately sent out Paul to go as far as to the sea, and Silas and Timothy still stayed there.

nodes.label: Acts 17:15
nodes.text: But those who escorted Paul brought him as far as Athens. Receiving a commandment to Silas and Timothy that they should come to him very quickly, they departed.

nodes.label: Acts 17:16
nodes.text: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he saw the city full of idols.

nodes.label: Acts 17:17
nodes.text: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace every day with those who met him.

variants.reading: from one (Greek ex henos), without 'blood'
variants.note: Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' lists Acts 17:26 'ex henos' in P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, 33, 81, 181, 629, 630, 1739, vg, cop sa, bo; 'ex henos aimatos' in D, E, P, 049, 056, 0142, 88, 104, 326, 330, 436, 451, 614, 945, 1241, 1505, 1877, 2127, 2412, 2492, 2495, Byz, Lect; 'ex henos stomatos' in Psi, l 603.

nodes.label: Acts 17:18
nodes.text: Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also were conversing with him. Some said, “What does this babbler want to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign deities,” because he preached Jesus and the resurrection.

nodes.label: Acts 17:19
nodes.text: They took hold of him, and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, “May we know what this new teaching is, which is spoken by you?

nodes.label: Acts 17:20
nodes.text: For you bring certain strange things to our ears. We want to know therefore what these things mean.”

nodes.label: Acts 17:21
nodes.text: Now all the Athenians and the strangers living there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell or to hear some new thing.

nodes.label: Acts 17:22
nodes.text: Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus, and said, “You men of Athens, I perceive that you are very religious in all things.

nodes.label: Acts 17:23
nodes.text: For as I passed along, and observed the objects of your worship, I found also an altar with this inscription: ‘TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.’ What therefore you worship in ignorance, this I announce to you.

nodes.label: Acts 17:24
nodes.text: The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands,

nodes.label: Acts 17:25
nodes.text: neither is he served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath, and all things.

nodes.label: Acts 17:26
nodes.text: He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons, and the boundaries of their dwellings,

nodes.label: Acts 17:27
nodes.text: that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.

nodes.label: Acts 17:28
nodes.text: ‘For in him we live, and move, and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘For we are also his offspring.’

nodes.label: Acts 17:29
nodes.text: Being then the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Divine Nature is like gold, or silver, or stone, engraved by art and design of man.

nodes.label: Acts 17:30
nodes.text: The times of ignorance therefore God overlooked. But now he commands that all people everywhere should repent,

nodes.label: Acts 17:31
nodes.text: because he has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by the man whom he has ordained; of which he has given assurance to all men, in that he has raised him from the dead.”

nodes.label: Acts 17:32
nodes.text: Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked; but others said, “We want to hear you again concerning this.”

nodes.label: Acts 17:33
nodes.text: Thus Paul went out from among them.

nodes.label: Acts 17:34
nodes.text: But certain men joined with him, and believed, among whom also was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

nodes.label: Acts 18:1
nodes.text: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth.

nodes.label: Acts 18:2
nodes.text: He found a certain Jew named Aquila, a man of Pontus by race, who had recently come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome. He came to them,

nodes.label: Acts 18:3
nodes.text: and because he practiced the same trade, he lived with them and worked, for by trade they were tent makers.

nodes.label: Acts 18:4
nodes.text: He reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath, and persuaded Jews and Greeks.

nodes.label: Acts 18:5
nodes.text: But when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was compelled by the Spirit, testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.

nodes.label: Acts 18:6
nodes.text: When they opposed him and blasphemed, he shook out his clothing and said to them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am clean. From now on, I will go to the Gentiles!”

nodes.label: Acts 18:7
nodes.text: He departed there, and went into the house of a certain man named Justus, one who worshiped God, whose house was next door to the synagogue.

nodes.label: Acts 18:8
nodes.text: Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his house. Many of the Corinthians, when they heard, believed and were baptized.

nodes.label: Acts 18:9
nodes.text:
The Lord said to Paul in the night by a vision,
“Don’t be afraid, but speak and don’t be silent;

nodes.label: Acts 18:10
nodes.text: for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many people in this city.”

nodes.label: Acts 18:11
nodes.text: He lived there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

nodes.label: Acts 18:12
nodes.text: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat,

nodes.label: Acts 18:13
nodes.text: saying, “This man persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.”

nodes.label: Acts 18:14
nodes.text: But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If indeed it were a matter of wrong or of wicked crime, you Jews, it would be reasonable that I should bear with you;

nodes.label: Acts 18:15
nodes.text: but if they are questions about words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves. For I don’t want to be a judge of these matters.”

nodes.label: Acts 18:16
nodes.text: So he drove them from the judgment seat.

nodes.label: Acts 18:17
nodes.text: Then all the Greeks laid hold on Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. Gallio didn’t care about any of these things.

nodes.label: Acts 18:18
nodes.text:
Paul, having stayed after this many more days, took his leave of the brothers,
 and sailed from there for Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.

nodes.label: Acts 18:19
nodes.text: He came to Ephesus, and he left them there; but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.

nodes.label: Acts 18:20
nodes.text: When they asked him to stay with them a longer time, he declined;

nodes.label: Acts 18:21
nodes.text: but taking his leave of them, he said, “I must by all means keep this coming feast in Jerusalem, but I will return again to you if God wills.” Then he set sail from Ephesus.

nodes.label: Acts 18:22
nodes.text: When he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the assembly, and went down to Antioch.

nodes.label: Acts 18:23
nodes.text: Having spent some time there, he departed, and went through the region of Galatia, and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples.

nodes.label: Acts 18:24
nodes.text: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus. He was mighty in the Scriptures.

nodes.label: Acts 18:25
nodes.text: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, although he knew only the baptism of John.

nodes.label: Acts 18:26
nodes.text: He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside, and explained to him the way of God more accurately.

variants.reading: την οδον ('the way') instead of την οδον του θεου ('the way of God')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' lists for Acts 18:26: την οδον - D d gig; την οδον του θεου - P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, 33, 88 and others; την οδον του κυριου - E 1505 2495 l598; τον λογον του κυριου - 945 1739; την του θεου οδον - P Psi 049 0142 and the Byzantine text. The WEB follows the Alexandrian reading, carried by codex-sinaiticus and codex-vaticanus; the variant reading itself is carried by no manuscript node of this graph.

nodes.label: Acts 18:27
nodes.text: When he had determined to pass over into Achaia, the brothers encouraged him, and wrote to the disciples to receive him. When he had come, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace;

nodes.label: Acts 18:28
nodes.text: for he powerfully refuted the Jews, publicly showing by the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.

nodes.label: Acts 19:1
nodes.text: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper country, came to Ephesus, and found certain disciples.

nodes.label: Acts 19:2
nodes.text: He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They said to him, “No, we haven’t even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”

nodes.label: Acts 19:3
nodes.text: He said, “Into what then were you baptized?” They said, “Into John’s baptism.”

nodes.label: Acts 19:4
nodes.text: Paul said, “John indeed baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the one who would come after him, that is, in Jesus.”

nodes.label: Acts 19:5
nodes.text: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

nodes.label: Acts 19:6
nodes.text: When Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they spoke with other languages and prophesied.

nodes.label: Acts 19:7
nodes.text: They were about twelve men in all.

nodes.label: Acts 19:8
nodes.text: He entered into the synagogue, and spoke boldly for a period of three months, reasoning and persuading about the things concerning God’s Kingdom.

nodes.label: Acts 19:9
nodes.text: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.

nodes.label: Acts 19:10
nodes.text: This continued for two years, so that all those who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.

nodes.label: Acts 19:11
nodes.text: God worked special miracles by the hands of Paul,

nodes.label: Acts 19:12
nodes.text: so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were carried away from his body to the sick, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out.

nodes.label: Acts 19:13
nodes.text: But some of the itinerant Jews, exorcists, took on themselves to invoke over those who had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, “We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches.”

nodes.label: Acts 19:14
nodes.text: There were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, who did this.

nodes.label: Acts 19:15
nodes.text: The evil spirit answered, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?”

nodes.label: Acts 19:16
nodes.text: The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, overpowered them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.

nodes.label: Acts 19:17
nodes.text: This became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who lived at Ephesus. Fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

nodes.label: Acts 19:18
nodes.text: Many also of those who had believed came, confessing, and declaring their deeds.

nodes.label: Acts 19:19
nodes.text: Many of those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. They counted their price, and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.

nodes.label: Acts 19:20
nodes.text: So the word of the Lord was growing and becoming mighty.

variants.reading: του κυριου ο λογος ('the word of the Lord')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' lists Acts 19:20 του κυριου ο λογος for א, A and B - the reading both graph codices carry. Against it, ο λογος του κυριου is listed for the majority text and η πιστις του κυριου ('the faith of the Lord') for D and syr p 2. The WEB prints the 'word of the Lord' wording.

nodes.label: Acts 19:21
nodes.text: Now after these things had ended, Paul determined in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, “After I have been there, I must also see Rome.”

nodes.label: Acts 19:22
nodes.text: Having sent into Macedonia two of those who served him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.

nodes.label: Acts 19:23
nodes.text: About that time there arose no small stir concerning the Way.

nodes.label: Acts 19:24
nodes.text: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought no little business to the craftsmen,

nodes.label: Acts 19:25
nodes.text: whom he gathered together, with the workmen of like occupation, and said, “Sirs, you know that by this business we have our wealth.

nodes.label: Acts 19:26
nodes.text: You see and hear, that not at Ephesus alone, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away many people, saying that they are no gods, that are made with hands.

nodes.label: Acts 19:27
nodes.text: Not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing, and her majesty destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worships.”

nodes.label: Acts 19:28
nodes.text: When they heard this they were filled with anger, and cried out, saying, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

nodes.label: Acts 19:29
nodes.text: The whole city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel.

nodes.label: Acts 19:30
nodes.text: When Paul wanted to enter in to the people, the disciples didn’t allow him.

nodes.label: Acts 19:31
nodes.text: Certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent to him and begged him not to venture into the theater.

nodes.label: Acts 19:32
nodes.text: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another, for the assembly was in confusion. Most of them didn’t know why they had come together.

nodes.label: Acts 19:33
nodes.text: They brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. Alexander beckoned with his hand, and would have made a defense to the people.

nodes.label: Acts 19:34
nodes.text: But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice for a time of about two hours cried out, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

nodes.label: Acts 19:35
nodes.text: When the town clerk had quieted the multitude, he said, “You men of Ephesus, what man is there who doesn’t know that the city of the Ephesians is temple keeper of the great goddess Artemis, and of the image which fell down from Zeus?

nodes.label: Acts 19:36
nodes.text: Seeing then that these things can’t be denied, you ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rash.

nodes.label: Acts 19:37
nodes.text: For you have brought these men here, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of your goddess.

nodes.label: Acts 19:38
nodes.text: If therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a matter against anyone, the courts are open, and there are proconsuls. Let them press charges against one another.

nodes.label: Acts 19:39
nodes.text: But if you seek anything about other matters, it will be settled in the regular assembly.

nodes.label: Acts 19:40
nodes.text: For indeed we are in danger of being accused concerning today’s riot, there being no cause. Concerning it, we wouldn’t be able to give an account of this commotion.”

nodes.label: Acts 19:41
nodes.text: When he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.

nodes.label: Acts 20:1
nodes.text: After the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.

nodes.label: Acts 20:2
nodes.text: When he had gone through those parts, and had encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece.

nodes.label: Acts 20:3
nodes.text: When he had spent three months there, and a plot was made against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.

nodes.label: Acts 20:4
nodes.text: These accompanied him as far as Asia: Sopater of Beroea; Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians; Gaius of Derbe; Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.

nodes.label: Acts 20:5
nodes.text: But these had gone ahead, and were waiting for us at Troas.

nodes.label: Acts 20:6
nodes.text: We sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.

nodes.label: Acts 20:7
nodes.text: On the first day of the week, when the disciples were gathered together to break bread, Paul talked with them, intending to depart on the next day, and continued his speech until midnight.

nodes.label: Acts 20:8
nodes.text: There were many lights in the upper room where we were gathered together.

nodes.label: Acts 20:9
nodes.text: A certain young man named Eutychus sat in the window, weighed down with deep sleep. As Paul spoke still longer, being weighed down by his sleep, he fell down from the third floor, and was taken up dead.

nodes.label: Acts 20:10
nodes.text: Paul went down, and fell upon him, and embracing him said, “Don’t be troubled, for his life is in him.”

nodes.label: Acts 20:11
nodes.text: When he had gone up, and had broken bread, and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even until break of day, he departed.

nodes.label: Acts 20:12
nodes.text: They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.

nodes.label: Acts 20:13
nodes.text: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there; for he had so arranged, intending himself to go by land.

nodes.label: Acts 20:14
nodes.text: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard, and came to Mitylene.

nodes.label: Acts 20:15
nodes.text: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.

variants.reading: omits 'and stayed at Trogyllium' (και μειναντες εν Τρωγυλλιω)
variants.note: The phrase is present in D (Codex Bezae), uncial 049 and the Byzantine majority; the Alexandrian texts omit it (Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles').

nodes.label: Acts 20:16
nodes.text: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.

nodes.label: Acts 20:17
nodes.text: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called to himself the elders of the assembly.

nodes.label: Acts 20:18
nodes.text: When they had come to him, he said to them, “You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you all the time,

nodes.label: Acts 20:19
nodes.text: serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;

nodes.label: Acts 20:20
nodes.text: how I didn’t shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable, teaching you publicly and from house to house,

nodes.label: Acts 20:21
nodes.text: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus.

nodes.label: Acts 20:22
nodes.text: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there;

nodes.label: Acts 20:23
nodes.text: except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me.

nodes.label: Acts 20:24
nodes.text: But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.

nodes.label: Acts 20:25
nodes.text: “Now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about preaching God’s Kingdom, will see my face no more.

nodes.label: Acts 20:26
nodes.text: Therefore I testify to you today that I am clean from the blood of all men,

nodes.label: Acts 20:27
nodes.text: for I didn’t shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.

nodes.label: Acts 20:28
nodes.text: Take heed, therefore, to yourselves, and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of the Lord and God which he purchased with his own blood.

variants.reading: εκκλησιαν του Θεου ('church of God')
variants.note: Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read 'church of God'; P74, A, C*, D, E and the majority read 'church of the Lord' or 'church of the Lord and God' (Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles').

variants.reading: εκκλησιαν του κυριου ('church of the Lord')
variants.note: P74 reads 'church of the Lord'; the WEB's 'assembly of the Lord and God' is the Byzantine reading (Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles').

nodes.label: Acts 20:29
nodes.text: For I know that after my departure, vicious wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

nodes.label: Acts 20:30
nodes.text: Men will arise from among your own selves, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.

nodes.label: Acts 20:31
nodes.text: Therefore watch, remembering that for a period of three years I didn’t cease to admonish everyone night and day with tears.

nodes.label: Acts 20:32
nodes.text: Now, brothers, I entrust you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build up, and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.

nodes.label: Acts 20:33
nodes.text: I coveted no one’s silver, or gold, or clothing.

nodes.label: Acts 20:34
nodes.text: You yourselves know that these hands served my necessities, and those who were with me.

nodes.label: Acts 20:35
nodes.text: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

nodes.label: Acts 20:36
nodes.text: When he had spoken these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.

nodes.label: Acts 20:37
nodes.text: They all wept a lot, and fell on Paul’s neck and kissed him,

nodes.label: Acts 20:38
nodes.text: sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him to the ship.

nodes.label: Acts 21:1
nodes.text: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

variants.reading: Παταρα ('Patara', the WEB wording)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' lists Acts 21:1 Παταρα for א, B and most witnesses - the reading both graph codices carry. Against it, Πατερα is listed for P74, A and C, and Παταρα και Μυρα ('Patara and Myra') for P41 and D. The WEB prints the 'Patara' wording.

nodes.label: Acts 21:2
nodes.text: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard, and set sail.

nodes.label: Acts 21:3
nodes.text: When we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed to Syria, and landed at Tyre, for there the ship was to unload her cargo.

nodes.label: Acts 21:4
nodes.text: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Acts 21:5
nodes.text: When those days were over, we departed and went on our journey. They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city. Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.

nodes.label: Acts 21:6
nodes.text: After saying goodbye to each other, we went on board the ship, and they returned home again.

nodes.label: Acts 21:7
nodes.text: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers, and stayed with them one day.

nodes.label: Acts 21:8
nodes.text:
On the next day, we, who were Paul’s companions, departed, and came to Caesarea.
We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.

nodes.label: Acts 21:9
nodes.text: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.

nodes.label: Acts 21:10
nodes.text: As we stayed there some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

nodes.label: Acts 21:11
nodes.text: Coming to us, and taking Paul’s belt, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, “Thus says the Holy Spirit: ‘So will the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man who owns this belt, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.’”

nodes.label: Acts 21:12
nodes.text: When we heard these things, both we and they of that place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Acts 21:13
nodes.text: Then Paul answered, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”

nodes.label: Acts 21:14
nodes.text: When he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, “The Lord’s will be done.”

nodes.label: Acts 21:15
nodes.text: After these days we took up our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Acts 21:16
nodes.text: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we would stay.

nodes.label: Acts 21:17
nodes.text: When we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.

nodes.label: Acts 21:18
nodes.text: The day following, Paul went in with us to James; and all the elders were present.

nodes.label: Acts 21:19
nodes.text: When he had greeted them, he reported one by one the things which God had worked among the Gentiles through his ministry.

nodes.label: Acts 21:20
nodes.text: They, when they heard it, glorified God. They said to him, “You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.

nodes.label: Acts 21:21
nodes.text: They have been informed about you, that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children neither to walk after the customs.

nodes.label: Acts 21:22
nodes.text: What then? The assembly must certainly meet, for they will hear that you have come.

nodes.label: Acts 21:23
nodes.text: Therefore do what we tell you. We have four men who have taken a vow.

nodes.label: Acts 21:24
nodes.text: Take them, and purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses for them, that they may shave their heads. Then all will know that there is no truth in the things that they have been informed about you, but that you yourself also walk keeping the law.

nodes.label: Acts 21:25
nodes.text: But concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written our decision that they should observe no such thing, except that they should keep themselves from food offered to idols, from blood, from strangled things, and from sexual immorality.”

nodes.label: Acts 21:26
nodes.text: Then Paul took the men, and the next day, purified himself and went with them into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.

nodes.label: Acts 21:27
nodes.text: When the seven days were almost completed, the Jews from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him,

nodes.label: Acts 21:28
nodes.text: crying out, “Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place. Moreover, he also brought Greeks into the temple, and has defiled this holy place!”

nodes.label: Acts 21:29
nodes.text: For they had seen Trophimus, the Ephesian, with him in the city, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

nodes.label: Acts 21:30
nodes.text: All the city was moved, and the people ran together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Immediately the doors were shut.

nodes.label: Acts 21:31
nodes.text: As they were trying to kill him, news came up to the commanding officer of the regiment that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

nodes.label: Acts 21:32
nodes.text: Immediately he took soldiers and centurions, and ran down to them. They, when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, stopped beating Paul.

nodes.label: Acts 21:33
nodes.text: Then the commanding officer came near, arrested him, commanded him to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he was and what he had done.

nodes.label: Acts 21:34
nodes.text: Some shouted one thing, and some another, among the crowd. When he couldn’t find out the truth because of the noise, he commanded him to be brought into the barracks.

nodes.label: Acts 21:35
nodes.text: When he came to the stairs, he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;

nodes.label: Acts 21:36
nodes.text: for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”

nodes.label: Acts 21:37
nodes.text:
As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he asked the commanding officer, “May I speak to you?”
He said, “Do you know Greek?

nodes.label: Acts 21:38
nodes.text: Aren’t you then the Egyptian, who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?”

nodes.label: Acts 21:39
nodes.text: But Paul said, “I am a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.”

nodes.label: Acts 21:40
nodes.text: When he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand to the people. When there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,

nodes.label: Acts 22:1
nodes.text: “Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make to you.”

nodes.label: Acts 22:2
nodes.text: When they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they were even more quiet. He said,

nodes.label: Acts 22:3
nodes.text: “I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict tradition of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as you all are today.

nodes.label: Acts 22:4
nodes.text: I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

nodes.label: Acts 22:5
nodes.text: As also the high priest and all the council of the elders testify, from whom also I received letters to the brothers, and traveled to Damascus to bring them also who were there to Jerusalem in bonds to be punished.

nodes.label: Acts 22:6
nodes.text: As I made my journey, and came close to Damascus, about noon, suddenly a great light shone around me from the sky.

nodes.label: Acts 22:7
nodes.text:
I fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to me,
‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’

nodes.label: Acts 22:8
nodes.text:
I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ He said to me,
‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute.’

nodes.label: Acts 22:9
nodes.text: “Those who were with me indeed saw the light and were afraid, but they didn’t understand the voice of him who spoke to me.

nodes.label: Acts 22:10
nodes.text:
I said, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ The Lord said to me,
‘Arise, and go into Damascus. There you will be told about all things which are appointed for you to do.’

nodes.label: Acts 22:11
nodes.text: When I couldn’t see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.

nodes.label: Acts 22:12
nodes.text: One Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus,

nodes.label: Acts 22:13
nodes.text: came to me, and standing by me said to me, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ In that very hour I looked up at him.

nodes.label: Acts 22:14
nodes.text: He said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.

nodes.label: Acts 22:15
nodes.text: For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.

nodes.label: Acts 22:16
nodes.text: Now why do you wait? Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.’

nodes.label: Acts 22:17
nodes.text: “When I had returned to Jerusalem, and while I prayed in the temple, I fell into a trance,

nodes.label: Acts 22:18
nodes.text:
and saw him saying to me,
‘Hurry and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not receive testimony concerning me from you.’

nodes.label: Acts 22:19
nodes.text: I said, ‘Lord, they themselves know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue those who believed in you.

nodes.label: Acts 22:20
nodes.text: When the blood of Stephen, your witness, was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting to his death, and guarding the cloaks of those who killed him.’

nodes.label: Acts 22:21
nodes.text:
“He said to me,
‘Depart, for I will send you out far from here to the Gentiles.’”

nodes.label: Acts 22:22
nodes.text: They listened to him until he said that; then they lifted up their voice, and said, “Rid the earth of this fellow, for he isn’t fit to live!”

nodes.label: Acts 22:23
nodes.text: As they cried out, and threw off their cloaks, and threw dust into the air,

nodes.label: Acts 22:24
nodes.text: the commanding officer commanded him to be brought into the barracks, ordering him to be examined by scourging, that he might know for what crime they shouted against him like that.

nodes.label: Acts 22:25
nodes.text: When they had tied him up with thongs, Paul asked the centurion who stood by, “Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and not found guilty?”

nodes.label: Acts 22:26
nodes.text: When the centurion heard it, he went to the commanding officer and told him, “Watch what you are about to do, for this man is a Roman!”

nodes.label: Acts 22:27
nodes.text:
The commanding officer came and asked him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?”
He said, “Yes.”

nodes.label: Acts 22:28
nodes.text:
The commanding officer answered, “I bought my citizenship for a great price.”
Paul said, “But I was born a Roman.”

nodes.label: Acts 22:29
nodes.text: Immediately those who were about to examine him departed from him, and the commanding officer also was afraid when he realized that he was a Roman, because he had bound him.

nodes.label: Acts 22:30
nodes.text: But on the next day, desiring to know the truth about why he was accused by the Jews, he freed him from the bonds, and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.

nodes.label: Acts 23:1
nodes.text: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, “Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until today.”

nodes.label: Acts 23:2
nodes.text: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.

nodes.label: Acts 23:3
nodes.text: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?”

nodes.label: Acts 23:4
nodes.text: Those who stood by said, “Do you malign God’s high priest?”

nodes.label: Acts 23:5
nodes.text: Paul said, “I didn’t know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’”

nodes.label: Acts 23:6
nodes.text: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!”

nodes.label: Acts 23:7
nodes.text: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the crowd was divided.

nodes.label: Acts 23:8
nodes.text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.

nodes.label: Acts 23:9
nodes.text: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and contended, saying, “We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let’s not fight against God!”

variants.reading: the closing phrase 'let us not fight against God' (KJV) is absent
