variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'List of omitted Bible verses' (Acts 23:9 (b)): the phrase, which also appears in Acts 5:39, 'does not appear in the earliest and best resources - Papyrus 74, Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Alexandrinus, Codex Vaticanus, Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus (original hand), Codex Laudianus' - it first appears in 9th-century codices. The WEB prints it.

nodes.label: Acts 23:10
nodes.text: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them, and bring him into the barracks.

nodes.label: Acts 23:11
nodes.text:
The following night, the Lord stood by him, and said,
“Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.”

nodes.label: Acts 23:12
nodes.text: When it was day, some of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

nodes.label: Acts 23:13
nodes.text: There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.

nodes.label: Acts 23:14
nodes.text: They came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, “We have bound ourselves under a great curse, to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.

nodes.label: Acts 23:15
nodes.text: Now therefore, you with the council inform the commanding officer that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to judge his case more exactly. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.”

nodes.label: Acts 23:16
nodes.text: But Paul’s sister’s son heard they were lying in wait, and he came and entered into the barracks and told Paul.

nodes.label: Acts 23:17
nodes.text: Paul summoned one of the centurions, and said, “Bring this young man to the commanding officer, for he has something to tell him.”

nodes.label: Acts 23:18
nodes.text: So he took him, and brought him to the commanding officer, and said, “Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you, who has something to tell you.”

nodes.label: Acts 23:19
nodes.text: The commanding officer took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, “What is it that you have to tell me?”

nodes.label: Acts 23:20
nodes.text: He said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.

nodes.label: Acts 23:21
nodes.text: Therefore don’t yield to them, for more than forty men lie in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they have killed him. Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.”

nodes.label: Acts 23:22
nodes.text: So the commanding officer let the young man go, charging him, “Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.”

nodes.label: Acts 23:23
nodes.text: He called to himself two of the centurions, and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen, and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.”

nodes.label: Acts 23:24
nodes.text: He asked them to provide animals, that they might set Paul on one, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.

nodes.label: Acts 23:25
nodes.text: He wrote a letter like this:

nodes.label: Acts 23:26
nodes.text: “Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.

nodes.label: Acts 23:27
nodes.text: “This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be killed by them, when I came with the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.

nodes.label: Acts 23:28
nodes.text: Desiring to know the cause why they accused him, I brought him down to their council.

nodes.label: Acts 23:29
nodes.text: I found him to be accused about questions of their law, but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.

nodes.label: Acts 23:30
nodes.text: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.”

nodes.label: Acts 23:31
nodes.text: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.

nodes.label: Acts 23:32
nodes.text: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.

nodes.label: Acts 23:33
nodes.text: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.

nodes.label: Acts 23:34
nodes.text: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,

nodes.label: Acts 23:35
nodes.text: “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive.” He commanded that he be kept in Herod’s palace.

nodes.label: Acts 24:1
nodes.text: After five days, the high priest, Ananias, came down with certain elders and an orator, one Tertullus. They informed the governor against Paul.

nodes.label: Acts 24:2
nodes.text: When he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Seeing that by you we enjoy much peace, and that prosperity is coming to this nation by your foresight,

nodes.label: Acts 24:3
nodes.text: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.

nodes.label: Acts 24:4
nodes.text: But, that I don’t delay you, I entreat you to bear with us and hear a few words.

nodes.label: Acts 24:5
nodes.text: For we have found this man to be a plague, an instigator of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.

nodes.label: Acts 24:6
nodes.text: He even tried to profane the temple, and we arrested him.

variants.reading: The short text the WEB prints (24:6 'He even tried to profane the temple, and we arrested him.' straight to 24:8 'By examining him yourself...'): the Western addition 24:6b-8a (Lysias rescuing Paul and commanding his accusers to come) is not printed.
variants.note: The runner brief and the book's known-omissions list state 24:6b-8a is absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' records 'Acts 24:6b-8a verse omitted by majority of the mss.'.

variants.reading: 24:6b-8a contained (with textual differences) in E (Codex Bezae), Psi, 056, 0142, 33, 88, 181, 424, 436, 483, 614, 630, 945, 1505, 2412, 2495
variants.note: Per the fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles'. The WEB therefore prints no verse 7 text; this passage node carries no codex preserves edges from Sinaiticus or Vaticanus, only Bezae.

nodes.label: Acts 24:8
nodes.text: By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him.”

nodes.label: Acts 24:9
nodes.text: The Jews also joined in the attack, affirming that these things were so.

nodes.label: Acts 24:10
nodes.text: When the governor had beckoned to him to speak, Paul answered, “Because I know that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense,

nodes.label: Acts 24:11
nodes.text: seeing that you can verify that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Acts 24:12
nodes.text: In the temple they didn’t find me disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd, either in the synagogues, or in the city.

nodes.label: Acts 24:13
nodes.text: Nor can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.

nodes.label: Acts 24:14
nodes.text: But this I confess to you, that after the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets;

nodes.label: Acts 24:15
nodes.text: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

nodes.label: Acts 24:16
nodes.text: Herein I also practice always having a conscience void of offense toward God and men.

nodes.label: Acts 24:17
nodes.text: Now after some years, I came to bring gifts for the needy to my nation, and offerings;

nodes.label: Acts 24:18
nodes.text: amid which certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, not with a mob, nor with turmoil.

nodes.label: Acts 24:19
nodes.text: They ought to have been here before you, and to make accusation, if they had anything against me.

nodes.label: Acts 24:20
nodes.text: Or else let these men themselves say what injustice they found in me when I stood before the council,

variants.reading: ευρον αδικημα ('what injustice they found') - the WEB prints this shorter reading
variants.note: Per the fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles': ευρον αδικημα in P74, א, A, B, 33, 81, 181.

variants.reading: ευρον εν εμοι αδικημα ('what injustice they found in me')
variants.note: Per the same fetched page: C, E, P, Psi, 049, 056, 0142, 88, 104, 326, 330, 436, 451, 614, 629, Byz. No artifact node exists in the graph for these witnesses.

nodes.label: Acts 24:21
nodes.text: unless it is for this one thing that I cried standing among them, ‘Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged before you today!’”

nodes.label: Acts 24:22
nodes.text: But Felix, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way, deferred them, saying, “When Lysias, the commanding officer, comes down, I will decide your case.”

nodes.label: Acts 24:23
nodes.text: He ordered the centurion that Paul should be kept in custody, and should have some privileges, and not to forbid any of his friends to serve him or to visit him.

nodes.label: Acts 24:24
nodes.text: But after some days, Felix came with Drusilla, his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.

nodes.label: Acts 24:25
nodes.text: As he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, and answered, “Go your way for this time, and when it is convenient for me, I will summon you.”

nodes.label: Acts 24:26
nodes.text: Meanwhile, he also hoped that money would be given to him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore also he sent for him more often, and talked with him.

nodes.label: Acts 24:27
nodes.text: But when two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and desiring to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in bonds.

nodes.label: Acts 25:1
nodes.text: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

nodes.label: Acts 25:2
nodes.text: Then the high priest and the principal men of the Jews informed him against Paul, and they begged him,

nodes.label: Acts 25:3
nodes.text: asking a favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem; plotting to kill him on the way.

nodes.label: Acts 25:4
nodes.text: However Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.

nodes.label: Acts 25:5
nodes.text: “Let them therefore”, said he, “that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”

nodes.label: Acts 25:6
nodes.text: When he had stayed among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.

nodes.label: Acts 25:7
nodes.text: When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing against him many and grievous charges which they could not prove,

nodes.label: Acts 25:8
nodes.text: while he said in his defense, “Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.”

nodes.label: Acts 25:9
nodes.text: But Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem, and be judged by me there concerning these things?”

nodes.label: Acts 25:10
nodes.text: But Paul said, “I am standing before Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.

nodes.label: Acts 25:11
nodes.text: For if I have done wrong, and have committed anything worthy of death, I don’t refuse to die; but if none of those things is true that they accuse me of, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!”

nodes.label: Acts 25:12
nodes.text: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.”

nodes.label: Acts 25:13
nodes.text: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea, and greeted Festus.

nodes.label: Acts 25:14
nodes.text: As he stayed there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, “There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;

nodes.label: Acts 25:15
nodes.text: about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, asking for a sentence against him.

nodes.label: Acts 25:16
nodes.text: To whom I answered that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction, before the accused has met the accusers face to face, and has had opportunity to make his defense concerning the matter laid against him.

nodes.label: Acts 25:17
nodes.text: When therefore they had come together here, I didn’t delay, but on the next day sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought.

nodes.label: Acts 25:18
nodes.text: Concerning whom, when the accusers stood up, they brought no charge of such things as I supposed;

nodes.label: Acts 25:19
nodes.text: but had certain questions against him about their own religion, and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

nodes.label: Acts 25:20
nodes.text: Being perplexed how to inquire concerning these things, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.

nodes.label: Acts 25:21
nodes.text: But when Paul had appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor, I commanded him to be kept until I could send him to Caesar.”

nodes.label: Acts 25:22
nodes.text: Agrippa said to Festus, “I also would like to hear the man myself.” “Tomorrow,” he said, “you shall hear him.”

nodes.label: Acts 25:23
nodes.text: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and they had entered into the place of hearing with the commanding officers and the principal men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.

nodes.label: Acts 25:24
nodes.text: Festus said, “King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

nodes.label: Acts 25:25
nodes.text: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor I determined to send him,

nodes.label: Acts 25:26
nodes.text: of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him out before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, that, after examination, I may have something to write.

nodes.label: Acts 25:27
nodes.text: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to also specify the charges against him.”

nodes.label: Acts 26:1
nodes.text: Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.

nodes.label: Acts 26:2
nodes.text: “I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you today concerning all the things that I am accused by the Jews,

nodes.label: Acts 26:3
nodes.text: especially because you are expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews. Therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.

nodes.label: Acts 26:4
nodes.text: “Indeed, all the Jews know my way of life from my youth up, which was from the beginning among my own nation and at Jerusalem;

nodes.label: Acts 26:5
nodes.text: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

nodes.label: Acts 26:6
nodes.text: Now I stand here to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,

nodes.label: Acts 26:7
nodes.text: which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa!

nodes.label: Acts 26:8
nodes.text: Why is it judged incredible with you, if God does raise the dead?

nodes.label: Acts 26:9
nodes.text: “I myself most certainly thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

nodes.label: Acts 26:10
nodes.text: This I also did in Jerusalem. I both shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were put to death I gave my vote against them.

nodes.label: Acts 26:11
nodes.text: Punishing them often in all the synagogues, I tried to make them blaspheme. Being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.

nodes.label: Acts 26:12
nodes.text: “Whereupon as I traveled to Damascus with the authority and commission from the chief priests,

nodes.label: Acts 26:13
nodes.text: at noon, O king, I saw on the way a light from the sky, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who traveled with me.

nodes.label: Acts 26:14
nodes.text: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’

nodes.label: Acts 26:15
nodes.text: “I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ “He said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

nodes.label: Acts 26:16
nodes.text: But arise, and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things which you have seen, and of the things which I will reveal to you;

nodes.label: Acts 26:17
nodes.text: delivering you from the people, and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,

nodes.label: Acts 26:18
nodes.text: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’

nodes.label: Acts 26:19
nodes.text: “Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,

nodes.label: Acts 26:20
nodes.text: but declared first to them of Damascus, at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.

nodes.label: Acts 26:21
nodes.text: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple, and tried to kill me.

nodes.label: Acts 26:22
nodes.text: Having therefore obtained the help that is from God, I stand to this day testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would happen,

nodes.label: Acts 26:23
nodes.text: how the Christ must suffer, and how, by the resurrection of the dead, he would be first to proclaim light both to these people and to the Gentiles.”

nodes.label: Acts 26:24
nodes.text: As he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “Paul, you are crazy! Your great learning is driving you insane!”

nodes.label: Acts 26:25
nodes.text: But he said, “I am not crazy, most excellent Festus, but boldly declare words of truth and reasonableness.

nodes.label: Acts 26:26
nodes.text: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak freely. For I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.

nodes.label: Acts 26:27
nodes.text: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”

nodes.label: Acts 26:28
nodes.text: Agrippa said to Paul, “With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?”

nodes.label: Acts 26:29
nodes.text: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”

nodes.label: Acts 26:30
nodes.text: The king rose up with the governor, and Bernice, and those who sat with them.

nodes.label: Acts 26:31
nodes.text: When they had withdrawn, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.”

nodes.label: Acts 26:32
nodes.text: Agrippa said to Festus, “This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”

nodes.label: Acts 27:1
nodes.text: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.

nodes.label: Acts 27:2
nodes.text: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea; Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

nodes.label: Acts 27:3
nodes.text: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.

nodes.label: Acts 27:4
nodes.text: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

nodes.label: Acts 27:5
nodes.text: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

nodes.label: Acts 27:6
nodes.text: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.

nodes.label: Acts 27:7
nodes.text: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

nodes.label: Acts 27:8
nodes.text: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.

nodes.label: Acts 27:9
nodes.text: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous, because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them,

nodes.label: Acts 27:10
nodes.text: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”

nodes.label: Acts 27:11
nodes.text: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.

nodes.label: Acts 27:12
nodes.text: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking northeast and southeast.

nodes.label: Acts 27:13
nodes.text: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.

nodes.label: Acts 27:14
nodes.text: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.

nodes.label: Acts 27:15
nodes.text: When the ship was caught, and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it, and were driven along.

nodes.label: Acts 27:16
nodes.text: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.

nodes.label: Acts 27:17
nodes.text: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.

nodes.label: Acts 27:18
nodes.text: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.

nodes.label: Acts 27:19
nodes.text: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.

nodes.label: Acts 27:20
nodes.text: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.

nodes.label: Acts 27:21
nodes.text: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them, and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete, and have gotten this injury and loss.

nodes.label: Acts 27:22
nodes.text: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

nodes.label: Acts 27:23
nodes.text: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,

nodes.label: Acts 27:24
nodes.text: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’

nodes.label: Acts 27:25
nodes.text: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.

nodes.label: Acts 27:26
nodes.text: But we must run aground on a certain island.”

nodes.label: Acts 27:27
nodes.text: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.

nodes.label: Acts 27:28
nodes.text: They took soundings, and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.

nodes.label: Acts 27:29
nodes.text: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.

nodes.label: Acts 27:30
nodes.text: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship, and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,

nodes.label: Acts 27:31
nodes.text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”

nodes.label: Acts 27:32
nodes.text: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat, and let it fall off.

nodes.label: Acts 27:33
nodes.text: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.

nodes.label: Acts 27:34
nodes.text: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”

nodes.label: Acts 27:35
nodes.text: When he had said this, and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all, and he broke it, and began to eat.

nodes.label: Acts 27:36
nodes.text: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.

nodes.label: Acts 27:37
nodes.text: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.

nodes.label: Acts 27:38
nodes.text: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.

nodes.label: Acts 27:39
nodes.text: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.

nodes.label: Acts 27:40
nodes.text: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.

nodes.label: Acts 27:41
nodes.text: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.

nodes.label: Acts 27:42
nodes.text: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.

nodes.label: Acts 27:43
nodes.text: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;

nodes.label: Acts 27:44
nodes.text: and the rest should follow, some on planks, and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.

nodes.label: Acts 28:1
nodes.text: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.

nodes.label: Acts 28:2
nodes.text: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire, and received us all, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

nodes.label: Acts 28:3
nodes.text: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

nodes.label: Acts 28:4
nodes.text: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.”

nodes.label: Acts 28:5
nodes.text: However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn’t harmed.

nodes.label: Acts 28:6
nodes.text: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

nodes.label: Acts 28:7
nodes.text: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us, and courteously entertained us for three days.

nodes.label: Acts 28:8
nodes.text: The father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him.

nodes.label: Acts 28:9
nodes.text: Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came, and were cured.

nodes.label: Acts 28:10
nodes.text: They also honored us with many honors, and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.

nodes.label: Acts 28:11
nodes.text: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose sign was “The Twin Brothers.”

nodes.label: Acts 28:12
nodes.text: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

nodes.label: Acts 28:13
nodes.text: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,

nodes.label: Acts 28:14
nodes.text: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.

nodes.label: Acts 28:15
nodes.text: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God, and took courage.

nodes.label: Acts 28:16
nodes.text: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.

nodes.label: Acts 28:17
nodes.text: After three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,

nodes.label: Acts 28:18
nodes.text: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.

nodes.label: Acts 28:19
nodes.text: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation.

nodes.label: Acts 28:20
nodes.text: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.”

nodes.label: Acts 28:21
nodes.text: They said to him, “We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.

nodes.label: Acts 28:22
nodes.text: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”

nodes.label: Acts 28:23
nodes.text: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about God’s Kingdom, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening.

nodes.label: Acts 28:24
nodes.text: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.

nodes.label: Acts 28:25
nodes.text: When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one word, “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah, the prophet, to our fathers,

nodes.label: Acts 28:26
nodes.text:
saying,
‘Go to this people, and say,
in hearing, you will hear,
but will in no way understand.
In seeing, you will see,
but will in no way perceive.

nodes.label: Acts 28:27
nodes.text:
For this people’s heart has grown callous.
Their ears are dull of hearing.
Their eyes they have closed.
Lest they should see with their eyes,
hear with their ears,
understand with their heart,
and would turn again,
and I would heal them.’

nodes.label: Acts 28:28
nodes.text: “Be it known therefore to you, that the salvation of God is sent to the nations, and they will listen.”

nodes.label: Acts 28:29
nodes.text: When he had said these words, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.

variants.reading: verse absent
variants.note: The verse (KJV: 'And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.') is lacking in Papyrus 74, Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Alexandrinus, Codex Vaticanus, Codex Laudianus and other old witnesses, and appears only in later sources such as Codex Porphyrianus (9th century); modern editions omit it (Wikipedia 'List of New Testament verses not included in modern English translations').

nodes.label: Acts 28:30
nodes.text: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house, and received all who were coming to him,

nodes.label: Acts 28:31
nodes.text: preaching God’s Kingdom, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.

nodes.label: John 1:1
nodes.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

nodes.label: John 1:2
nodes.text: The same was in the beginning with God.

nodes.label: John 1:3
nodes.text: All things were made through him. Without him was not anything made that has been made.

nodes.label: John 1:4
nodes.text: In him was life, and the life was the light of men.

nodes.label: John 1:5
nodes.text:
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome
 it.

nodes.label: John 1:6
nodes.text: There came a man, sent from God, whose name was John.

nodes.label: John 1:7
nodes.text: The same came as a witness, that he might testify about the light, that all might believe through him.

nodes.label: John 1:8
nodes.text: He was not the light, but was sent that he might testify about the light.

nodes.label: John 1:9
nodes.text: The true light that enlightens everyone was coming into the world.

nodes.label: John 1:10
nodes.text: He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world didn’t recognize him.

nodes.label: John 1:11
nodes.text: He came to his own, and those who were his own didn’t receive him.

nodes.label: John 1:12
nodes.text: But as many as received him, to them he gave the right to become God’s children, to those who believe in his name:

nodes.label: John 1:13
nodes.text: who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

nodes.label: John 1:14
nodes.text: The Word became flesh, and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the one and only Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.

nodes.label: John 1:15
nodes.text: John testified about him. He cried out, saying, “This was he of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me, for he was before me.’”

nodes.label: John 1:16
nodes.text: From his fullness we all received grace upon grace.

nodes.label: John 1:17
nodes.text: For the law was given through Moses. Grace and truth were realized through Jesus Christ.

nodes.label: John 1:18
nodes.text: No one has seen God at any time. The one and only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him.

variants.reading: ο μονογενης θεος ('the only-begotten God')
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 1:18): ο μονογενης θεος in P75, אc, 33 and copbo, and μονογενης θεος ('God [the] only-begotten') in P66, א* and B - so Sinaiticus and Vaticanus both carry the 'God' reading against the WEB, which follows ο μονογενης υιος ('the only-begotten son', A C K X Δ Θ Π 063 f1,13 28 565 700 892 Byz).

nodes.label: John 1:19
nodes.text: This is John’s testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”

nodes.label: John 1:20
nodes.text: He declared, and didn’t deny, but he declared, “I am not the Christ.”

nodes.label: John 1:21
nodes.text:
They asked him, “What then? Are you Elijah?”
He said, “I am not.”
“Are you the prophet?”
He answered, “No.”

nodes.label: John 1:22
nodes.text: They said therefore to him, “Who are you? Give us an answer to take back to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”

nodes.label: John 1:23
nodes.text: He said, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.”

nodes.label: John 1:24
nodes.text: The ones who had been sent were from the Pharisees.

nodes.label: John 1:25
nodes.text: They asked him, “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?”

nodes.label: John 1:26
nodes.text: John answered them, “I baptize in water, but among you stands one whom you don’t know.

nodes.label: John 1:27
nodes.text: He is the one who comes after me, who is preferred before me, whose sandal strap I’m not worthy to loosen.”

nodes.label: John 1:28
nodes.text: These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

variants.reading: Bethabara (Βεθαβαρά) instead of Bethany
variants.note: Origen preferred 'Bethabara' over 'Bethany' as the location where John was baptizing (Commentary on John VI.40 (24), per Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John); the reading is also attested in the 6th-century Madaba Map and in the Jewish Talmud (Wikipedia, Bethabara). No manuscript node carries it in this graph.

nodes.label: John 1:29
nodes.text: The next day, he saw Jesus coming to him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!

nodes.label: John 1:30
nodes.text: This is he of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who is preferred before me, for he was before me.’

nodes.label: John 1:31
nodes.text: I didn’t know him, but for this reason I came baptizing in water: that he would be revealed to Israel.”

nodes.label: John 1:32
nodes.text: John testified, saying, “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and it remained on him.

nodes.label: John 1:33
nodes.text: I didn’t recognize him, but he who sent me to baptize in water, he said to me, ‘On whomever you will see the Spirit descending, and remaining on him, the same is he who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’

nodes.label: John 1:34
nodes.text: I have seen, and have testified that this is the Son of God.”

variants.reading: ο εκλεκτος ('the Elect One')
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 1:34): ο εκλεκτος in P5, P106 (vid), 187, 218, 228, 1784, Old Latin and Syriac witnesses, Ambrose and Augustine, against the WEB's 'the Son of God'; no manuscript node for these witnesses exists in this graph.

nodes.label: John 1:35
nodes.text: Again, the next day, John was standing with two of his disciples,

nodes.label: John 1:36
nodes.text: and he looked at Jesus as he walked, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!”

nodes.label: John 1:37
nodes.text: The two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.

nodes.label: John 1:38
nodes.text:
Jesus turned, and saw them following, and said to them,
“What are you looking for?”
They said to him, “Rabbi” (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), “where are you staying?”

nodes.label: John 1:39
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Come, and see.”
They came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.

nodes.label: John 1:40
nodes.text: One of the two who heard John, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.

nodes.label: John 1:41
nodes.text: He first found his own brother, Simon, and said to him, “We have found the Messiah!” (which is, being interpreted, Christ).

nodes.label: John 1:42
nodes.text:
He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him, and said,
“You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas” (which is by interpretation, Peter).

nodes.label: John 1:43
nodes.text:
On the next day, he was determined to go out into Galilee, and he found Philip. Jesus said to him,
“Follow me.”

nodes.label: John 1:44
nodes.text: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, of the city of Andrew and Peter.

nodes.label: John 1:45
nodes.text: Philip found Nathanael, and said to him, “We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, wrote: Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”

nodes.label: John 1:46
nodes.text:
Nathanael said to him, “Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?”
Philip said to him, “Come and see.”

nodes.label: John 1:47
nodes.text:
Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and said about him,
“Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no deceit!”

nodes.label: John 1:48
nodes.text:
Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?”
Jesus answered him,
“Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.”

nodes.label: John 1:49
nodes.text: Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are King of Israel!”

nodes.label: John 1:50
nodes.text:
Jesus answered him,
“Because I told you, ‘I saw you underneath the fig tree,’ do you believe? You will see greater things than these!”

nodes.label: John 1:51
nodes.text:
He said to him,
“Most certainly, I tell you all, hereafter you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”

nodes.label: John 2:1
nodes.text: The third day, there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there.

nodes.label: John 2:2
nodes.text: Jesus also was invited, with his disciples, to the marriage.

nodes.label: John 2:3
nodes.text: When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to him, “They have no wine.”

variants.reading: οινον ουκ ειχον οτι συνετελεσθη ο οινος του γαμου, ειτα (they did not have wine because the wine of the wedding reception was finished, then)
variants.note: Sinaiticus original hand (א*), with Old Latin manuscripts and the Syriac hmg; the rest read υστερησαντος οινου (they were running short of wine). Per the fetched Textual variants in the Gospel of John article.

nodes.label: John 2:4
nodes.text: Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does that have to do with you and me? My hour has not yet come.”

nodes.label: John 2:5
nodes.text: His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he says to you, do it.”

nodes.label: John 2:6
nodes.text: Now there were six water pots of stone set there after the Jews’ way of purifying, containing two or three metretes apiece.

nodes.label: John 2:7
nodes.text: Jesus said to them, “Fill the water pots with water.” They filled them up to the brim.

nodes.label: John 2:8
nodes.text: He said to them, “Now draw some out, and take it to the ruler of the feast.” So they took it.

nodes.label: John 2:9
nodes.text: When the ruler of the feast tasted the water now become wine, and didn’t know where it came from (but the servants who had drawn the water knew), the ruler of the feast called the bridegroom,

nodes.label: John 2:10
nodes.text: and said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when the guests have drunk freely, then that which is worse. You have kept the good wine until now!”

nodes.label: John 2:11
nodes.text: This beginning of his signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.

nodes.label: John 2:12
nodes.text: After this, he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, his brothers, and his disciples; and they stayed there a few days.

nodes.label: John 2:13
nodes.text: The Passover of the Jews was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: John 2:14
nodes.text: He found in the temple those who sold oxen, sheep, and doves, and the changers of money sitting.

nodes.label: John 2:15
nodes.text: He made a whip of cords, and threw all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he poured out the changers’ money, and overthrew their tables.

nodes.label: John 2:16
nodes.text:
To those who sold the doves, he said,
“Take these things out of here! Don’t make my Father’s house a marketplace!”

nodes.label: John 2:17
nodes.text: His disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house will eat me up.”

nodes.label: John 2:18
nodes.text: The Jews therefore answered him, “What sign do you show us, seeing that you do these things?”

nodes.label: John 2:19
nodes.text:
Jesus answered them,
“Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”

nodes.label: John 2:20
nodes.text: The Jews therefore said, “It took forty-six years to build this temple! Will you raise it up in three days?”

nodes.label: John 2:21
nodes.text: But he spoke of the temple of his body.

nodes.label: John 2:22
nodes.text: When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he said this, and they believed the Scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.

nodes.label: John 2:23
nodes.text: Now when he was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in his name, observing his signs which he did.

nodes.label: John 2:24
nodes.text: But Jesus didn’t entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone,

nodes.label: John 2:25
nodes.text: and because he didn’t need for anyone to testify concerning man; for he himself knew what was in man.

nodes.label: John 3:1
nodes.text: Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.

nodes.label: John 3:2
nodes.text: The same came to him by night, and said to him, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher come from God, for no one can do these signs that you do, unless God is with him.”

nodes.label: John 3:3
nodes.text: Jesus answered him, “Most certainly, I tell you, unless one is born anew, he can’t see God’s Kingdom.”

nodes.label: John 3:4
nodes.text: Nicodemus said to him, “How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb, and be born?”

nodes.label: John 3:5
nodes.text: Jesus answered, “Most certainly I tell you, unless one is born of water and spirit, he can’t enter into God’s Kingdom.

nodes.label: John 3:6
nodes.text: That which is born of the flesh is flesh. That which is born of the Spirit is spirit.

nodes.label: John 3:7
nodes.text: Don’t marvel that I said to you, ‘You must be born anew.’

nodes.label: John 3:8
nodes.text: The wind blows where it wants to, and you hear its sound, but don’t know where it comes from and where it is going. So is everyone who is born of the Spirit.”

nodes.label: John 3:9
nodes.text: Nicodemus answered him, “How can these things be?”

nodes.label: John 3:10
nodes.text: Jesus answered him, “Are you the teacher of Israel, and don’t understand these things?

nodes.label: John 3:11
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, we speak that which we know, and testify of that which we have seen, and you don’t receive our witness.

nodes.label: John 3:12
nodes.text: If I told you earthly things and you don’t believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?

nodes.label: John 3:13
nodes.text: No one has ascended into heaven, but he who descended out of heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven.

nodes.label: John 3:14
nodes.text: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Man be lifted up,

nodes.label: John 3:15
nodes.text: that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

nodes.label: John 3:16
nodes.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

nodes.label: John 3:17
nodes.text: For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.

nodes.label: John 3:18
nodes.text: He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn’t believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the one and only Son of God.

nodes.label: John 3:19
nodes.text: This is the judgment, that the light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light; for their works were evil.

nodes.label: John 3:20
nodes.text: For everyone who does evil hates the light, and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed.

nodes.label: John 3:21
nodes.text: But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his works may be revealed, that they have been done in God.”

nodes.label: John 3:22
nodes.text: After these things, Jesus came with his disciples into the land of Judea. He stayed there with them, and baptized.

nodes.label: John 3:23
nodes.text: John also was baptizing in Enon near Salim, because there was much water there. They came, and were baptized.

nodes.label: John 3:24
nodes.text: For John was not yet thrown into prison.

nodes.label: John 3:25
nodes.text: There arose therefore a questioning on the part of John’s disciples with some Jews about purification.

nodes.label: John 3:26
nodes.text: They came to John, and said to him, “Rabbi, he who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you have testified, behold, the same baptizes, and everyone is coming to him.”

nodes.label: John 3:27
nodes.text: John answered, “A man can receive nothing, unless it has been given him from heaven.

nodes.label: John 3:28
nodes.text: You yourselves testify that I said, ‘I am not the Christ,’ but, ‘I have been sent before him.’

nodes.label: John 3:29
nodes.text: He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. This, my joy, therefore is made full.

nodes.label: John 3:30
nodes.text: He must increase, but I must decrease.

nodes.label: John 3:31
nodes.text: He who comes from above is above all. He who is from the earth belongs to the earth, and speaks of the earth. He who comes from heaven is above all.

nodes.label: John 3:32
nodes.text: What he has seen and heard, of that he testifies; and no one receives his witness.

nodes.label: John 3:33
nodes.text: He who has received his witness has set his seal to this, that God is true.

nodes.label: John 3:34
nodes.text: For he whom God has sent speaks the words of God; for God gives the Spirit without measure.

nodes.label: John 3:35
nodes.text: The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into his hand.

nodes.label: John 3:36
nodes.text: One who believes in the Son has eternal life, but one who disobeys the Son won’t see life, but the wrath of God remains on him.”

nodes.label: John 4:1
nodes.text: Therefore when the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John

nodes.label: John 4:2
nodes.text: (although Jesus himself didn’t baptize, but his disciples),

nodes.label: John 4:3
nodes.text: he left Judea, and departed into Galilee.

nodes.label: John 4:4
nodes.text: He needed to pass through Samaria.

nodes.label: John 4:5
nodes.text: So he came to a city of Samaria, called Sychar, near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son, Joseph.

nodes.label: John 4:6
nodes.text: Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being tired from his journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.

nodes.label: John 4:7
nodes.text:
A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her,
“Give me a drink.”

nodes.label: John 4:8
nodes.text: For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.

nodes.label: John 4:9
nodes.text: The Samaritan woman therefore said to him, “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)

variants.reading: the clause 'for Jews have no dealings with Samaritans' omitted
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 4:9): ου γαρ συγχρωνται Ιουδαιοι Σαμαριταις ('for Jews have no association with Samaritans') omitted by א* D it a,b,d,e,j cop fay; the original hand of Sinaiticus omits it. Codex Bezae (D) has no node in the graph.

nodes.label: John 4:10
nodes.text:
Jesus answered her,
“If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”

nodes.label: John 4:11
nodes.text: The woman said to him, “Sir, you have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep. So where do you get that living water?

nodes.label: John 4:12
nodes.text: Are you greater than our father, Jacob, who gave us the well, and drank of it himself, as did his children, and his livestock?”

nodes.label: John 4:13
nodes.text:
Jesus answered her,
“Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again,

nodes.label: John 4:14
nodes.text: but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”

nodes.label: John 4:15
nodes.text: The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water, so that I don’t get thirsty, neither come all the way here to draw.”

nodes.label: John 4:16
nodes.text:
Jesus said to her,
“Go, call your husband, and come here.”

nodes.label: John 4:17
nodes.text:
The woman answered, “I have no husband.”
Jesus said to her,
“You said well, ‘I have no husband,’

nodes.label: John 4:18
nodes.text: for you have had five husbands; and he whom you now have is not your husband. This you have said truly.”

nodes.label: John 4:19
nodes.text: The woman said to him, “Sir, I perceive that you are a prophet.

nodes.label: John 4:20
nodes.text: Our fathers worshiped in this mountain, and you Jews say that in Jerusalem is the place where people ought to worship.”

nodes.label: John 4:21
nodes.text:
Jesus said to her,
“Woman, believe me, the hour comes, when neither in this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, will you worship the Father.

nodes.label: John 4:22
nodes.text: You worship that which you don’t know. We worship that which we know; for salvation is from the Jews.

nodes.label: John 4:23
nodes.text: But the hour comes, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father seeks such to be his worshipers.

nodes.label: John 4:24
nodes.text: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”

nodes.label: John 4:25
nodes.text: The woman said to him, “I know that Messiah comes, he who is called Christ. When he has come, he will declare to us all things.”

nodes.label: John 4:26
nodes.text:
Jesus said to her,
“I am he, the one who speaks to you.”

nodes.label: John 4:27
nodes.text: At this, his disciples came. They marveled that he was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, “What are you looking for?” or, “Why do you speak with her?”

nodes.label: John 4:28
nodes.text: So the woman left her water pot, and went away into the city, and said to the people,

nodes.label: John 4:29
nodes.text: “Come, see a man who told me everything that I did. Can this be the Christ?”

nodes.label: John 4:30
nodes.text: They went out of the city, and were coming to him.

nodes.label: John 4:31
nodes.text: In the meanwhile, the disciples urged him, saying, “Rabbi, eat.”

nodes.label: John 4:32
nodes.text:
But he said to them,
“I have food to eat that you don’t know about.”

nodes.label: John 4:33
nodes.text: The disciples therefore said to one another, “Has anyone brought him something to eat?”

nodes.label: John 4:34
nodes.text:
Jesus said to them,
“My food is to do the will of him who sent me, and to accomplish his work.

nodes.label: John 4:35
nodes.text: Don’t you say, ‘There are yet four months until the harvest?’ Behold, I tell you, lift up your eyes, and look at the fields, that they are white for harvest already.

nodes.label: John 4:36
nodes.text: He who reaps receives wages, and gathers fruit to eternal life; that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together.

nodes.label: John 4:37
nodes.text: For in this the saying is true, ‘One sows, and another reaps.’

variants.reading: the whole verse omitted
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 4:37): 'Verse omitted in P75'. The WEB prints the verse, so no preserves edge runs from artifact:papyrus-75 to this passage.

nodes.label: John 4:38
nodes.text: I sent you to reap that for which you haven’t labored. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.”

nodes.label: John 4:39
nodes.text: From that city many of the Samaritans believed in him because of the word of the woman, who testified, “He told me everything that I did.”

nodes.label: John 4:40
nodes.text: So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them. He stayed there two days.

nodes.label: John 4:41
nodes.text: Many more believed because of his word.

nodes.label: John 4:42
nodes.text: They said to the woman, “Now we believe, not because of your speaking; for we have heard for ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world.”

variants.reading: ο χριστος ('the Christ') omitted
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 4:42): 'the Christ' omitted in P66 P75 א B C* W supp 083 vid, present in the Byzantine text the WEB follows ('indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world').

nodes.label: John 4:43
nodes.text: After the two days he went out from there and went into Galilee.

nodes.label: John 4:44
nodes.text: For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own country.

nodes.label: John 4:45
nodes.text: So when he came into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things that he did in Jerusalem at the feast, for they also went to the feast.

nodes.label: John 4:46
nodes.text: Jesus came therefore again to Cana of Galilee, where he made the water into wine. There was a certain nobleman whose son was sick at Capernaum.

variants.reading: ο Ιησους ('Jesus') omitted
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 4:46): 'Jesus' present in A Θ Ψ f1,13 Byz, omitted in P66 P75 א B C* W supp 086 33 1241; a minor variation, recorded for completeness.

nodes.label: John 4:47
nodes.text: When he heard that Jesus had come out of Judea into Galilee, he went to him, and begged him that he would come down and heal his son, for he was at the point of death.

nodes.label: John 4:48
nodes.text:
Jesus therefore said to him,
“Unless you see signs and wonders, you will in no way believe.”

nodes.label: John 4:49
nodes.text: The nobleman said to him, “Sir, come down before my child dies.”

nodes.label: John 4:50
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“Go your way. Your son lives.” The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went his way.

nodes.label: John 4:51
nodes.text: As he was now going down, his servants met him and reported, saying “Your child lives!”

nodes.label: John 4:52
nodes.text: So he inquired of them the hour when he began to get better. They said therefore to him, “Yesterday at the seventh hour, the fever left him.”

nodes.label: John 4:53
nodes.text:
So the father knew that it was at that hour in which Jesus said to him,
“Your son lives.” He believed, as did his whole house.

variants.reading: ο Ιησους ('Jesus') omitted
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 4:53): 'Jesus' omitted in the original hand of א* and N*, present in the remaining witnesses; N (Codex Purpureus) has no node in the graph.

nodes.label: John 4:54
nodes.text: This is again the second sign that Jesus did, having come out of Judea into Galilee.

nodes.label: John 5:1
nodes.text: After these things, there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: John 5:2
nodes.text: Now in Jerusalem by the sheep gate, there is a pool, which is called in Hebrew, “Bethesda”, having five porches.

variants.reading: Βηθζαθα (Bethzatha)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of John' lists βηθζαθα for א (Sinaiticus) and later witnesses (33, b, 1, ff2); the name the WEB prints is Βηθεσδα (Bethesda), the reading of A C Byz f q TR.

variants.reading: Βηθσαιδα (Bethsaida-like spelling)
variants.note: The fetched variants article lists βηθσαιδα for P75, B (Vaticanus), W, 0125 and versional witnesses (aur c vg bo) - a 'Bethsaida'-shaped spelling of the pool's name, not the Galilean town.

variants.reading: Βηδσαιδα
variants.note: The fetched variants article lists βηδσαιδα for P66 and the Sahidic version.

variants.reading: Βηθεσδα (Bethesda) - the WEB reading
variants.note: The article lists βηθεσδα for A C Byz f q TR; those witnesses are not manuscript nodes of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

nodes.label: John 5:3
nodes.text: In these lay a great multitude of those who were sick, blind, lame, or paralyzed, waiting for the moving of the water;

nodes.label: John 5:4
nodes.text: for an angel went down at certain times into the pool, and stirred up the water. Whoever stepped in first after the stirring of the water was healed of whatever disease he had.

variants.reading: the verse is absent (omitted entirely)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of John' records 'John 5:4 Verse omitted by 𝔓66 𝔓75 א B C* D T W supp 0141 33 157 821 2718 it mss vg mss syr c co arm geo'. Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, P66 and P75 therefore get no preserves edge for this verse; the WEB prints the verse (the later Byzantine text, whose witnesses are not manuscript nodes of this graph).

nodes.label: John 5:5
nodes.text: A certain man was there, who had been sick for thirty-eight years.

nodes.label: John 5:6
nodes.text: When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he had been sick for a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to be made well?”

nodes.label: John 5:7
nodes.text: The sick man answered him, “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, but while I’m coming, another steps down before me.”

nodes.label: John 5:8
nodes.text: Jesus said to him, “Arise, take up your mat, and walk.”

nodes.label: John 5:9
nodes.text: Immediately, the man was made well, and took up his mat and walked. Now it was the Sabbath on that day.

nodes.label: John 5:10
nodes.text: So the Jews said to him who was cured, “It is the Sabbath. It is not lawful for you to carry the mat.”

nodes.label: John 5:11
nodes.text: He answered them, “He who made me well, the same said to me, ‘Take up your mat, and walk.’”

nodes.label: John 5:12
nodes.text: Then they asked him, “Who is the man who said to you, ‘Take up your mat, and walk’?”

nodes.label: John 5:13
nodes.text: But he who was healed didn’t know who it was, for Jesus had withdrawn, a crowd being in the place.

nodes.label: John 5:14
nodes.text: Afterward Jesus found him in the temple, and said to him, “Behold, you are made well. Sin no more, so that nothing worse happens to you.”

nodes.label: John 5:15
nodes.text: The man went away, and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.

nodes.label: John 5:16
nodes.text: For this cause the Jews persecuted Jesus, and sought to kill him, because he did these things on the Sabbath.

nodes.label: John 5:17
nodes.text: But Jesus answered them, “My Father is still working, so I am working, too.”

nodes.label: John 5:18
nodes.text: For this cause therefore the Jews sought all the more to kill him, because he not only broke the Sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal with God.

nodes.label: John 5:19
nodes.text: Jesus therefore answered them, “Most certainly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father doing. For whatever things he does, these the Son also does likewise.

nodes.label: John 5:20
nodes.text: For the Father has affection for the Son, and shows him all things that he himself does. He will show him greater works than these, that you may marvel.

nodes.label: John 5:21
nodes.text: For as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, even so the Son also gives life to whom he desires.

nodes.label: John 5:22
nodes.text: For the Father judges no one, but he has given all judgment to the Son,

nodes.label: John 5:23
nodes.text: that all may honor the Son, even as they honor the Father. He who doesn’t honor the Son doesn’t honor the Father who sent him.

nodes.label: John 5:24
nodes.text: “Most certainly I tell you, he who hears my word, and believes him who sent me, has eternal life, and doesn’t come into judgment, but has passed out of death into life.

nodes.label: John 5:25
nodes.text: Most certainly, I tell you, the hour comes, and now is, when the dead will hear the Son of God’s voice; and those who hear will live.

nodes.label: John 5:26
nodes.text: For as the Father has life in himself, even so he gave to the Son also to have life in himself.

nodes.label: John 5:27
nodes.text: He also gave him authority to execute judgment, because he is a son of man.

nodes.label: John 5:28
nodes.text: Don’t marvel at this, for the hour comes, in which all that are in the tombs will hear his voice,

nodes.label: John 5:29
nodes.text: and will come out; those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment.

nodes.label: John 5:30
nodes.text: I can of myself do nothing. As I hear, I judge, and my judgment is righteous; because I don’t seek my own will, but the will of my Father who sent me.

nodes.label: John 5:31
nodes.text: “If I testify about myself, my witness is not valid.

nodes.label: John 5:32
nodes.text: It is another who testifies about me. I know that the testimony which he testifies about me is true.

nodes.label: John 5:33
nodes.text: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.

nodes.label: John 5:34
nodes.text: But the testimony which I receive is not from man. However, I say these things that you may be saved.

nodes.label: John 5:35
nodes.text: He was the burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light.

nodes.label: John 5:36
nodes.text: But the testimony which I have is greater than that of John, for the works which the Father gave me to accomplish, the very works that I do, testify about me, that the Father has sent me.

nodes.label: John 5:37
nodes.text: The Father himself, who sent me, has testified about me. You have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his form.

nodes.label: John 5:38
nodes.text: You don’t have his word living in you; because you don’t believe him whom he sent.

nodes.label: John 5:39
nodes.text: “You search the Scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and these are they which testify about me.

nodes.label: John 5:40
nodes.text: Yet you will not come to me, that you may have life.

nodes.label: John 5:41
nodes.text: I don’t receive glory from men.

nodes.label: John 5:42
nodes.text: But I know you, that you don’t have God’s love in yourselves.

nodes.label: John 5:43
nodes.text: I have come in my Father’s name, and you don’t receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him.

nodes.label: John 5:44
nodes.text: How can you believe, who receive glory from one another, and you don’t seek the glory that comes from the only God?

nodes.label: John 5:45
nodes.text: “Don’t think that I will accuse you to the Father. There is one who accuses you, even Moses, on whom you have set your hope.

nodes.label: John 5:46
nodes.text: For if you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote about me.

nodes.label: John 5:47
nodes.text: But if you don’t believe his writings, how will you believe my words?”

nodes.label: John 6:1
nodes.text: After these things, Jesus went away to the other side of the sea of Galilee, which is also called the Sea of Tiberias.

nodes.label: John 6:2
nodes.text: A great multitude followed him, because they saw his signs which he did on those who were sick.

nodes.label: John 6:3
nodes.text: Jesus went up into the mountain, and he sat there with his disciples.

nodes.label: John 6:4
nodes.text: Now the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was at hand.

nodes.label: John 6:5
nodes.text:
Jesus therefore lifting up his eyes, and seeing that a great multitude was coming to him, said to Philip,
“Where are we to buy bread, that these may eat?”

nodes.label: John 6:6
nodes.text: This he said to test him, for he himself knew what he would do.

nodes.label: John 6:7
nodes.text: Philip answered him, “Two hundred denarii worth of bread is not sufficient for them, that everyone of them may receive a little.”

nodes.label: John 6:8
nodes.text: One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,

nodes.label: John 6:9
nodes.text: “There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?”

nodes.label: John 6:10
nodes.text:
Jesus said,
“Have the people sit down.” Now there was much grass in that place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.

nodes.label: John 6:11
nodes.text: Jesus took the loaves; and having given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to those who were sitting down; likewise also of the fish as much as they desired.

nodes.label: John 6:12
nodes.text:
When they were filled, he said to his disciples,
“Gather up the broken pieces which are left over, that nothing be lost.”

nodes.label: John 6:13
nodes.text: So they gathered them up, and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces from the five barley loaves, which were left over by those who had eaten.

nodes.label: John 6:14
nodes.text: When therefore the people saw the sign which Jesus did, they said, “This is truly the prophet who comes into the world.”

nodes.label: John 6:15
nodes.text: Jesus therefore, perceiving that they were about to come and take him by force, to make him king, withdrew again to the mountain by himself.

nodes.label: John 6:16
nodes.text: When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea,

nodes.label: John 6:17
nodes.text: and they entered into the boat, and were going over the sea to Capernaum. It was now dark, and Jesus had not come to them.

nodes.label: John 6:18
nodes.text: The sea was tossed by a great wind blowing.

nodes.label: John 6:19
nodes.text:
When therefore they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia,
 they saw Jesus walking on the sea, and drawing near to the boat; and they were afraid.

nodes.label: John 6:20
nodes.text:
But he said to them,
“It is I.
Don’t be afraid.”

nodes.label: John 6:21
nodes.text: They were willing therefore to receive him into the boat. Immediately the boat was at the land where they were going.

nodes.label: John 6:22
nodes.text: On the next day, the multitude that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there, except the one in which his disciples had embarked, and that Jesus hadn’t entered with his disciples into the boat, but his disciples had gone away alone.

nodes.label: John 6:23
nodes.text: However boats from Tiberias came near to the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks.

nodes.label: John 6:24
nodes.text: When the multitude therefore saw that Jesus wasn’t there, nor his disciples, they themselves got into the boats, and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.

nodes.label: John 6:25
nodes.text: When they found him on the other side of the sea, they asked him, “Rabbi, when did you come here?”

nodes.label: John 6:26
nodes.text:
Jesus answered them,
“Most certainly I tell you, you seek me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves, and were filled.

nodes.label: John 6:27
nodes.text: Don’t work for the food which perishes, but for the food which remains to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give to you. For God the Father has sealed him.”

nodes.label: John 6:28
nodes.text: They said therefore to him, “What must we do, that we may work the works of God?”

nodes.label: John 6:29
nodes.text:
Jesus answered them,
“This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.”

nodes.label: John 6:30
nodes.text: They said therefore to him, “What then do you do for a sign, that we may see, and believe you? What work do you do?

nodes.label: John 6:31
nodes.text: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness. As it is written, ‘He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.’”

nodes.label: John 6:32
nodes.text:
Jesus therefore said to them,
“Most certainly, I tell you, it wasn’t Moses who gave you the bread out of heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread out of heaven.

nodes.label: John 6:33
nodes.text: For the bread of God is that which comes down out of heaven, and gives life to the world.”

nodes.label: John 6:34
nodes.text: They said therefore to him, “Lord, always give us this bread.”

nodes.label: John 6:35
nodes.text:
Jesus said to them,
“I am the bread of life. He who comes to me will not be hungry, and he who believes in me will never be thirsty.

nodes.label: John 6:36
nodes.text: But I told you that you have seen me, and yet you don’t believe.

nodes.label: John 6:37
nodes.text: All those whom the Father gives me will come to me. He who comes to me I will in no way throw out.

nodes.label: John 6:38
nodes.text: For I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me.

nodes.label: John 6:39
nodes.text: This is the will of my Father who sent me, that of all he has given to me I should lose nothing, but should raise him up at the last day.

nodes.label: John 6:40
nodes.text: This is the will of the one who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son, and believes in him, should have eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.”

nodes.label: John 6:41
nodes.text:
The Jews therefore murmured concerning him, because he said,
“I am the bread which came down out of heaven.”

nodes.label: John 6:42
nodes.text:
They said, “Isn’t this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then does he say,
‘I have come down out of heaven?’”

nodes.label: John 6:43
nodes.text:
Therefore Jesus answered them,
“Don’t murmur among yourselves.

nodes.label: John 6:44
nodes.text: No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him, and I will raise him up in the last day.

nodes.label: John 6:45
nodes.text:
It is written in the prophets, ‘They will all be taught by God.’


Therefore everyone who hears from the Father, and has learned, comes to me.

nodes.label: John 6:46
nodes.text: Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God. He has seen the Father.

nodes.label: John 6:47
nodes.text: Most certainly, I tell you, he who believes in me has eternal life.

nodes.label: John 6:48
nodes.text: I am the bread of life.

nodes.label: John 6:49
nodes.text: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.

nodes.label: John 6:50
nodes.text: This is the bread which comes down out of heaven, that anyone may eat of it and not die.

nodes.label: John 6:51
nodes.text: I am the living bread which came down out of heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. Yes, the bread which I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.”

nodes.label: John 6:52
nodes.text: The Jews therefore contended with one another, saying, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”

nodes.label: John 6:53
nodes.text:
Jesus therefore said to them,
“Most certainly I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you don’t have life in yourselves.

nodes.label: John 6:54
nodes.text: He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.

nodes.label: John 6:55
nodes.text: For my flesh is food indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.

nodes.label: John 6:56
nodes.text: He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood lives in me, and I in him.

nodes.label: John 6:57
nodes.text: As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father; so he who feeds on me, he will also live because of me.

nodes.label: John 6:58
nodes.text: This is the bread which came down out of heaven—not as our fathers ate the manna, and died. He who eats this bread will live forever.”

nodes.label: John 6:59
nodes.text: He said these things in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum.

nodes.label: John 6:60
nodes.text: Therefore many of his disciples, when they heard this, said, “This is a hard saying! Who can listen to it?”

nodes.label: John 6:61
nodes.text:
But Jesus knowing in himself that his disciples murmured at this, said to them,
“Does this cause you to stumble?

nodes.label: John 6:62
nodes.text: Then what if you would see the Son of Man ascending to where he was before?

nodes.label: John 6:63
nodes.text: It is the spirit who gives life. The flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and are life.

nodes.label: John 6:64
nodes.text: But there are some of you who don’t believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who didn’t believe, and who it was who would betray him.

nodes.label: John 6:65
nodes.text:
He said,
“For this cause I have said to you that no one can come to me, unless it is given to him by my Father.”

nodes.label: John 6:66
nodes.text: At this, many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.

nodes.label: John 6:67
nodes.text:
Jesus said therefore to the twelve,
“You don’t also want to go away, do you?”

nodes.label: John 6:68
nodes.text: Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.

nodes.label: John 6:69
nodes.text: We have come to believe and know that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

nodes.label: John 6:70
nodes.text:
Jesus answered them,
“Didn’t I choose you, the twelve, and one of you is a devil?”

nodes.label: John 6:71
nodes.text: Now he spoke of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, for it was he who would betray him, being one of the twelve.

nodes.label: John 7:1
nodes.text: After these things, Jesus was walking in Galilee, for he wouldn’t walk in Judea, because the Jews sought to kill him.
