He said to them,
“Take nothing for your journey—neither staffs, nor wallet, nor bread, nor money; neither have two coats each.

nodes.label: Luke 9:4
nodes.text: Into whatever house you enter, stay there, and depart from there.

nodes.label: Luke 9:5
nodes.text: As many as don’t receive you, when you depart from that city, shake off even the dust from your feet for a testimony against them.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:6
nodes.text: They departed, and went throughout the villages, preaching the Good News, and healing everywhere.

nodes.label: Luke 9:7
nodes.text: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him; and he was very perplexed, because it was said by some that John had risen from the dead,

nodes.label: Luke 9:8
nodes.text: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the old prophets had risen again.

nodes.label: Luke 9:9
nodes.text: Herod said, “John I beheaded, but who is this, about whom I hear such things?” He sought to see him.

nodes.label: Luke 9:10
nodes.text:
The apostles, when they had returned, told him what things they had done.
He took them, and withdrew apart to a desert region of a city called Bethsaida.

nodes.label: Luke 9:11
nodes.text: But the multitudes, perceiving it, followed him. He welcomed them, and spoke to them of God’s Kingdom, and he cured those who needed healing.

nodes.label: Luke 9:12
nodes.text: The day began to wear away; and the twelve came, and said to him, “Send the multitude away, that they may go into the surrounding villages and farms, and lodge, and get food, for we are here in a deserted place.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:13
nodes.text:
But he said to them,
“You give them something to eat.”
They said, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we should go and buy food for all these people.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:14
nodes.text:
For they were about five thousand men.
He said to his disciples,
“Make them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:15
nodes.text: They did so, and made them all sit down.

nodes.label: Luke 9:16
nodes.text: He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to the sky, he blessed them, and broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the multitude.

nodes.label: Luke 9:17
nodes.text: They ate, and were all filled. They gathered up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.

nodes.label: Luke 9:18
nodes.text:
As he was praying alone, the disciples were with him, and he asked them,
“Who do the multitudes say that I am?”

nodes.label: Luke 9:19
nodes.text: They answered, “‘John the Baptizer,’ but others say, ‘Elijah,’ and others, that one of the old prophets is risen again.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:20
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“But who do you say that I am?”
Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:21
nodes.text: But he warned them, and commanded them to tell this to no one,

nodes.label: Luke 9:22
nodes.text:
saying,
“The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:23
nodes.text:
He said to all,
“If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross,
and follow me.

nodes.label: Luke 9:24
nodes.text: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever will lose his life for my sake, the same will save it.

nodes.label: Luke 9:25
nodes.text: For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world, and loses or forfeits his own self?

nodes.label: Luke 9:26
nodes.text: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words, of him will the Son of Man be ashamed, when he comes in his glory, and the glory of the Father, and of the holy angels.

nodes.label: Luke 9:27
nodes.text: But I tell you the truth: There are some of those who stand here, who will in no way taste of death, until they see God’s Kingdom.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:28
nodes.text: About eight days after these sayings, he took with him Peter, John, and James, and went up onto the mountain to pray.

nodes.label: Luke 9:29
nodes.text: As he was praying, the appearance of his face was altered, and his clothing became white and dazzling.

nodes.label: Luke 9:30
nodes.text: Behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,

nodes.label: Luke 9:31
nodes.text: who appeared in glory, and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Luke 9:32
nodes.text: Now Peter and those who were with him were heavy with sleep, but when they were fully awake, they saw his glory, and the two men who stood with him.

nodes.label: Luke 9:33
nodes.text: As they were parting from him, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah,” not knowing what he said.

nodes.label: Luke 9:34
nodes.text: While he said these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud.

nodes.label: Luke 9:35
nodes.text: A voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”

variants.reading: ο εκλελεγμενος ('my Son, my Elect/Chosen One', the WEB's 'beloved' replaced here)
variants.note: Also L, Xi, 892, 1241 and others read 'Elect One'; 'beloved' (αγαπητος) is read by A, C, W, Theta, family 13, Byz and Marcion (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 9:35). The WEB keeps 'beloved'.

nodes.label: Luke 9:36
nodes.text: When the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They were silent, and told no one in those days any of the things which they had seen.

nodes.label: Luke 9:37
nodes.text: On the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a great multitude met him.

nodes.label: Luke 9:38
nodes.text: Behold, a man from the crowd called out, saying, “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only child.

nodes.label: Luke 9:39
nodes.text: Behold, a spirit takes him, he suddenly cries out, and it convulses him so that he foams, and it hardly departs from him, bruising him severely.

nodes.label: Luke 9:40
nodes.text: I begged your disciples to cast it out, and they couldn’t.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:41
nodes.text:
Jesus answered,
“Faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:42
nodes.text: While he was still coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed him violently. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.

nodes.label: Luke 9:43
nodes.text:
They were all astonished at the majesty of God.
But while all were marveling at all the things which Jesus did, he said to his disciples,

nodes.label: Luke 9:44
nodes.text: “Let these words sink into your ears, for the Son of Man will be delivered up into the hands of men.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:45
nodes.text: But they didn’t understand this saying. It was concealed from them, that they should not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.

nodes.label: Luke 9:46
nodes.text: There arose an argument among them about which of them was the greatest.

nodes.label: Luke 9:47
nodes.text: Jesus, perceiving the reasoning of their hearts, took a little child, and set him by his side,

nodes.label: Luke 9:48
nodes.text:
and said to them,
“Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me. Whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For whoever is least among you all, this one will be great.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:49
nodes.text: John answered, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him, because he doesn’t follow with us.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:50
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“Don’t forbid him, for he who is not against us is for us.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:51
nodes.text: It came to pass, when the days were near that he should be taken up, he intently set his face to go to Jerusalem,

nodes.label: Luke 9:52
nodes.text: and sent messengers before his face. They went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, so as to prepare for him.

nodes.label: Luke 9:53
nodes.text: They didn’t receive him, because he was traveling with his face set towards Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Luke 9:54
nodes.text: When his disciples, James and John, saw this, they said, “Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from the sky, and destroy them, just as Elijah did?”

variants.reading: ωσ και Ηλιας εποιησε(ν) ('just as Elijah did') absent
variants.note: Omitted by the Alexandrian witnesses and included by the Byzantine text (Stephanus, Scrivener, RP 2005); the WEB keeps it (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 9:54); no graph manuscript carries the omission as its main reading.

nodes.label: Luke 9:55
nodes.text:
But he turned and rebuked them,
“You don’t know of what kind of spirit you are.

variants.reading: ουκ οιδατε ποιου πνευματος εστε ('you do not know of what kind of spirit you are') absent
variants.note: P45, P75, Sinaiticus, B, C, L, W, X, Delta, Xi, Psi, 28, 33, 565, 892 read only 'he turned and rebuked them'; the sentence is a Western/Byzantine addition (D, Byz lects). The WEB keeps it (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 9:55-56).

nodes.label: Luke 9:56
nodes.text:
For the Son of Man didn’t come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them.”
They went to another village.

nodes.label: Luke 9:57
nodes.text: As they went on the way, a certain man said to him, “I want to follow you wherever you go, Lord.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:58
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:59
nodes.text:
He said to another,
“Follow me!”
But he said, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:60
nodes.text:
But Jesus said to him,
“Leave the dead to bury their own dead, but you go and announce God’s Kingdom.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:61
nodes.text: Another also said, “I want to follow you, Lord, but first allow me to say good-bye to those who are at my house.”

nodes.label: Luke 9:62
nodes.text:
But Jesus said to him,
“No one, having put his hand to the plow, and looking back, is fit for God’s Kingdom.”

nodes.label: Luke 10:1
nodes.text: Now after these things, the Lord also appointed seventy others, and sent them two by two ahead of him into every city and place, where he was about to come.

nodes.label: Luke 10:2
nodes.text: Then he said to them, “The harvest is indeed plentiful, but the laborers are few. Pray therefore to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send out laborers into his harvest.

nodes.label: Luke 10:3
nodes.text: Go your ways. Behold, I send you out as lambs among wolves.

nodes.label: Luke 10:4
nodes.text: Carry no purse, nor wallet, nor sandals. Greet no one on the way.

nodes.label: Luke 10:5
nodes.text: Into whatever house you enter, first say, ‘Peace be to this house.’

nodes.label: Luke 10:6
nodes.text: If a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; but if not, it will return to you.

nodes.label: Luke 10:7
nodes.text: Remain in that same house, eating and drinking the things they give, for the laborer is worthy of his wages. Don’t go from house to house.

nodes.label: Luke 10:8
nodes.text: Into whatever city you enter, and they receive you, eat the things that are set before you.

nodes.label: Luke 10:9
nodes.text: Heal the sick who are therein, and tell them, ‘God’s Kingdom has come near to you.’

nodes.label: Luke 10:10
nodes.text: But into whatever city you enter, and they don’t receive you, go out into its streets and say,

nodes.label: Luke 10:11
nodes.text: ‘Even the dust from your city that clings to us, we wipe off against you. Nevertheless know this, that God’s Kingdom has come near to you.’

nodes.label: Luke 10:12
nodes.text: I tell you, it will be more tolerable in that day for Sodom than for that city.

nodes.label: Luke 10:13
nodes.text: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

nodes.label: Luke 10:14
nodes.text: But it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.

nodes.label: Luke 10:15
nodes.text: You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Hades.

nodes.label: Luke 10:16
nodes.text: Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me. Whoever rejects me rejects him who sent me.”

nodes.label: Luke 10:17
nodes.text: The seventy returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!”

nodes.label: Luke 10:18
nodes.text: He said to them, “I saw Satan having fallen like lightning from heaven.

nodes.label: Luke 10:19
nodes.text: Behold, I give you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will in any way hurt you.

nodes.label: Luke 10:20
nodes.text: Nevertheless, don’t rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”

nodes.label: Luke 10:21
nodes.text: In that same hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit, and said, “I thank you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.”

nodes.label: Luke 10:22
nodes.text: Turning to the disciples, he said, “All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is, except the Father, and who the Father is, except the Son, and he to whomever the Son desires to reveal him.”

nodes.label: Luke 10:23
nodes.text: Turning to the disciples, he said privately, “Blessed are the eyes which see the things that you see,

nodes.label: Luke 10:24
nodes.text: for I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see them, and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear them.”

nodes.label: Luke 10:25
nodes.text: Behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tested him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”

nodes.label: Luke 10:26
nodes.text: He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”

nodes.label: Luke 10:27
nodes.text: He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself.”

nodes.label: Luke 10:28
nodes.text: He said to him, “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”

nodes.label: Luke 10:29
nodes.text: But he, desiring to justify himself, asked Jesus, “Who is my neighbor?”

nodes.label: Luke 10:30
nodes.text: Jesus answered, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead.

nodes.label: Luke 10:31
nodes.text: By chance a certain priest was going down that way. When he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

nodes.label: Luke 10:32
nodes.text: In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place, and saw him, passed by on the other side.

nodes.label: Luke 10:33
nodes.text: But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,

nodes.label: Luke 10:34
nodes.text: came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

nodes.label: Luke 10:35
nodes.text: On the next day, when he departed, he took out two denarii, and gave them to the host, and said to him, ‘Take care of him. Whatever you spend beyond that, I will repay you when I return.’

nodes.label: Luke 10:36
nodes.text: Now which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”

nodes.label: Luke 10:37
nodes.text: He said, “He who showed mercy on him.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”

nodes.label: Luke 10:38
nodes.text: As they went on their way, he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.

nodes.label: Luke 10:39
nodes.text: She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word.

nodes.label: Luke 10:40
nodes.text: But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she came up to him, and said, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me.”

nodes.label: Luke 10:41
nodes.text: Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,

nodes.label: Luke 10:42
nodes.text: but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”

nodes.label: Luke 11:1
nodes.text: When he finished praying in a certain place, one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”

nodes.label: Luke 11:2
nodes.text: He said to them, “When you pray, say, ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. May your Kingdom come. May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.

variants.reading: 'Father' alone in the earliest witnesses; 'Our Father in heaven' is an expansion in some manuscripts
variants.note: Wikipedia, Lord's Prayer: Luke reads 'Father, [Some manuscripts: Our Father in heaven]', and the longer Luke 11:2c-d ('your will be done...') is absent from the earliest witnesses.

nodes.label: Luke 11:3
nodes.text: Give us day by day our daily bread.

nodes.label: Luke 11:4
nodes.text: Forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us.  Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’”

nodes.label: Luke 11:5
nodes.text: He said to them, “Which of you, if you go to a friend at midnight, and tell him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,

nodes.label: Luke 11:6
nodes.text: for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,’

nodes.label: Luke 11:7
nodes.text: and he from within will answer and say, ‘Don’t bother me. The door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed. I can’t get up and give it to you’?

nodes.label: Luke 11:8
nodes.text: I tell you, although he will not rise and give it to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence, he will get up and give him as many as he needs.

nodes.label: Luke 11:9
nodes.text: “I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you.

nodes.label: Luke 11:10
nodes.text: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.

nodes.label: Luke 11:11
nodes.text: “Which of you fathers, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, he won’t give him a snake instead of a fish, will he?

nodes.label: Luke 11:12
nodes.text: Or if he asks for an egg, he won’t give him a scorpion, will he?

nodes.label: Luke 11:13
nodes.text: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?”

nodes.label: Luke 11:14
nodes.text: He was casting out a demon, and it was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke; and the multitudes marveled.

nodes.label: Luke 11:15
nodes.text: But some of them said, “He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”

nodes.label: Luke 11:16
nodes.text: Others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.

nodes.label: Luke 11:17
nodes.text: But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. A house divided against itself falls.

nodes.label: Luke 11:18
nodes.text: If Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebul.

nodes.label: Luke 11:19
nodes.text: But if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore will they be your judges.

nodes.label: Luke 11:20
nodes.text: But if I by God’s finger cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come to you.

nodes.label: Luke 11:21
nodes.text: “When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own dwelling, his goods are safe.

nodes.label: Luke 11:22
nodes.text: But when someone stronger attacks him and overcomes him, he takes from him his whole armor in which he trusted, and divides his plunder.

nodes.label: Luke 11:23
nodes.text: “He that is not with me is against me. He who doesn’t gather with me scatters.

nodes.label: Luke 11:24
nodes.text: The unclean spirit, when he has gone out of the man, passes through dry places, seeking rest, and finding none, he says, ‘I will turn back to my house from which I came out.’

nodes.label: Luke 11:25
nodes.text: When he returns, he finds it swept and put in order.

nodes.label: Luke 11:26
nodes.text: Then he goes, and takes seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first.”

nodes.label: Luke 11:27
nodes.text: It came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice, and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!”

nodes.label: Luke 11:28
nodes.text: But he said, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”

nodes.label: Luke 11:29
nodes.text: When the multitudes were gathering together to him, he began to say, “This is an evil generation. It seeks after a sign. No sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah, the prophet.

nodes.label: Luke 11:30
nodes.text: For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so will also the Son of Man be to this generation.

nodes.label: Luke 11:31
nodes.text: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and will condemn them: for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.

nodes.label: Luke 11:32
nodes.text: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, one greater than Jonah is here.

nodes.label: Luke 11:33
nodes.text: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a stand, that those who come in may see the light.

variants.reading: omit 'nor under a basket'
variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 45: 'Luke 11:33 ... (nor under a basket): Omit.: P45 P75'.

nodes.label: Luke 11:34
nodes.text: The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore when your eye is good, your whole body is also full of light; but when it is evil, your body also is full of darkness.

nodes.label: Luke 11:35
nodes.text: Therefore see whether the light that is in you isn’t darkness.

nodes.label: Luke 11:36
nodes.text: If therefore your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its bright shining gives you light.”

nodes.label: Luke 11:37
nodes.text: Now as he spoke, a certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him. He went in, and sat at the table.

nodes.label: Luke 11:38
nodes.text: When the Pharisee saw it, he marveled that he had not first washed himself before dinner.

nodes.label: Luke 11:39
nodes.text: The Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.

nodes.label: Luke 11:40
nodes.text: You foolish ones, didn’t he who made the outside make the inside also?

nodes.label: Luke 11:41
nodes.text: But give for gifts to the needy those things which are within, and behold, all things will be clean to you.

nodes.label: Luke 11:42
nodes.text: But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, but you bypass justice and God’s love. You ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.

nodes.label: Luke 11:43
nodes.text: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seats in the synagogues, and the greetings in the marketplaces.

nodes.label: Luke 11:44
nodes.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like hidden graves, and the men who walk over them don’t know it.”

variants.reading: omit 'scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites'
variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 45: 'Luke 11:44 ... (scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!): Omit.: P45 P75 aleph B C'.

nodes.label: Luke 11:45
nodes.text: One of the lawyers answered him, “Teacher, in saying this you insult us also.”

nodes.label: Luke 11:46
nodes.text: He said, “Woe to you lawyers also! For you load men with burdens that are difficult to carry, and you yourselves won’t even lift one finger to help carry those burdens.

nodes.label: Luke 11:47
nodes.text: Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.

nodes.label: Luke 11:48
nodes.text: So you testify and consent to the works of your fathers. For they killed them, and you build their tombs.

nodes.label: Luke 11:49
nodes.text: Therefore also the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send to them prophets and apostles; and some of them they will kill and persecute,

nodes.label: Luke 11:50
nodes.text: that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;

nodes.label: Luke 11:51
nodes.text: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary.’ Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.

nodes.label: Luke 11:52
nodes.text: Woe to you lawyers! For you took away the key of knowledge. You didn’t enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in, you hindered.”

nodes.label: Luke 11:53
nodes.text: As he said these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly angry, and to draw many things out of him;

nodes.label: Luke 11:54
nodes.text: lying in wait for him, and seeking to catch him in something he might say, that they might accuse him.

variants.reading: omit 'so they might catch him'
variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 45: 'Luke 11:54 ... (so they might catch him): Omit.: P45 P75 aleph B'.

nodes.label: Luke 12:1
nodes.text:
Meanwhile, when a multitude of many thousands had gathered together, so much so that they trampled on each other, he began to tell his disciples first of all,
“Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

nodes.label: Luke 12:2
nodes.text: But there is nothing covered up, that will not be revealed, nor hidden, that will not be known.

nodes.label: Luke 12:3
nodes.text: Therefore whatever you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light. What you have spoken in the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.

nodes.label: Luke 12:4
nodes.text: “I tell you, my friends, don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.

nodes.label: Luke 12:5
nodes.text:
But I will warn you whom you should fear. Fear him, who after he has killed, has power to cast into Gehenna.
Yes, I tell you, fear him.

nodes.label: Luke 12:6
nodes.text: “Aren’t five sparrows sold for two assaria coins? Not one of them is forgotten by God.

nodes.label: Luke 12:7
nodes.text: But the very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.

nodes.label: Luke 12:8
nodes.text: “I tell you, everyone who confesses me before men, him will the Son of Man also confess before the angels of God;

nodes.label: Luke 12:9
nodes.text: but he who denies me in the presence of men will be denied in the presence of the angels of God.

nodes.label: Luke 12:10
nodes.text: Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but those who blaspheme against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

nodes.label: Luke 12:11
nodes.text: When they bring you before the synagogues, the rulers, and the authorities, don’t be anxious how or what you will answer, or what you will say;

nodes.label: Luke 12:12
nodes.text: for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that same hour what you must say.”

nodes.label: Luke 12:13
nodes.text: One of the multitude said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”

nodes.label: Luke 12:14
nodes.text:
But he said to him,
“Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”

nodes.label: Luke 12:15
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”

nodes.label: Luke 12:16
nodes.text:
He spoke a parable to them, saying,
“The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.

nodes.label: Luke 12:17
nodes.text: He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’

nodes.label: Luke 12:18
nodes.text: He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, and build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.

nodes.label: Luke 12:19
nodes.text: I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, be merry.”’

nodes.label: Luke 12:20
nodes.text: “But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’

nodes.label: Luke 12:21
nodes.text: So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”

nodes.label: Luke 12:22
nodes.text:
He said to his disciples,
“Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life, what you will eat, nor yet for your body, what you will wear.

nodes.label: Luke 12:23
nodes.text: Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing.

nodes.label: Luke 12:24
nodes.text: Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds!

nodes.label: Luke 12:25
nodes.text: Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height?

nodes.label: Luke 12:26
nodes.text: If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?

nodes.label: Luke 12:27
nodes.text: Consider the lilies, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

nodes.label: Luke 12:28
nodes.text: But if this is how God clothes the grass in the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith?

nodes.label: Luke 12:29
nodes.text: Don’t seek what you will eat or what you will drink; neither be anxious.

nodes.label: Luke 12:30
nodes.text: For the nations of the world seek after all of these things, but your Father knows that you need these things.

nodes.label: Luke 12:31
nodes.text: But seek God’s Kingdom, and all these things will be added to you.

nodes.label: Luke 12:32
nodes.text: Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.

nodes.label: Luke 12:33
nodes.text: Sell that which you have, and give gifts to the needy. Make for yourselves purses which don’t grow old, a treasure in the heavens that doesn’t fail, where no thief approaches, neither moth destroys.

nodes.label: Luke 12:34
nodes.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

nodes.label: Luke 12:35
nodes.text: “Let your waist be dressed and your lamps burning.

nodes.label: Luke 12:36
nodes.text: Be like men watching for their lord, when he returns from the marriage feast; that, when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.

nodes.label: Luke 12:37
nodes.text: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord will find watching when he comes. Most certainly I tell you, that he will dress himself, and make them recline, and will come and serve them.

nodes.label: Luke 12:38
nodes.text: They will be blessed if he comes in the second or third watch, and finds them so.

nodes.label: Luke 12:39
nodes.text: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched, and not allowed his house to be broken into.

nodes.label: Luke 12:40
nodes.text: Therefore be ready also, for the Son of Man is coming in an hour that you don’t expect him.”

nodes.label: Luke 12:41
nodes.text: Peter said to him, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”

nodes.label: Luke 12:42
nodes.text:
The Lord said,
“Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord will set over his household, to give them their portion of food at the right times?

nodes.label: Luke 12:43
nodes.text: Blessed is that servant whom his lord will find doing so when he comes.

nodes.label: Luke 12:44
nodes.text: Truly I tell you, that he will set him over all that he has.

nodes.label: Luke 12:45
nodes.text: But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My lord delays his coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken,

nodes.label: Luke 12:46
nodes.text: then the lord of that servant will come in a day when he isn’t expecting him, and in an hour that he doesn’t know, and will cut him in two, and place his portion with the unfaithful.

nodes.label: Luke 12:47
nodes.text: That servant, who knew his lord’s will, and didn’t prepare, nor do what he wanted, will be beaten with many stripes,

nodes.label: Luke 12:48
nodes.text: but he who didn’t know, and did things worthy of stripes, will be beaten with few stripes. To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.

nodes.label: Luke 12:49
nodes.text: “I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.

nodes.label: Luke 12:50
nodes.text: But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!

nodes.label: Luke 12:51
nodes.text: Do you think that I have come to give peace in the earth? I tell you, no, but rather division.

nodes.label: Luke 12:52
nodes.text: For from now on, there will be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.

nodes.label: Luke 12:53
nodes.text: They will be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”

nodes.label: Luke 12:54
nodes.text: He said to the multitudes also, “When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.

nodes.label: Luke 12:55
nodes.text: When a south wind blows, you say, ‘There will be a scorching heat,’ and it happens.

nodes.label: Luke 12:56
nodes.text: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you don’t interpret this time?

nodes.label: Luke 12:57
nodes.text: Why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?

nodes.label: Luke 12:58
nodes.text: For when you are going with your adversary before the magistrate, try diligently on the way to be released from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.

nodes.label: Luke 12:59
nodes.text: I tell you, you will by no means get out of there, until you have paid the very last penny.”

nodes.label: Luke 13:1
nodes.text: Now there were some present at the same time who told him about the Galileans, whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

nodes.label: Luke 13:2
nodes.text:
Jesus answered them,
“Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered such things?

nodes.label: Luke 13:3
nodes.text: I tell you, no, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.

nodes.label: Luke 13:4
nodes.text: Or those eighteen, on whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed them; do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem?

nodes.label: Luke 13:5
nodes.text: I tell you, no, but, unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”

nodes.label: Luke 13:6
nodes.text:
He spoke this parable.
“A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it, and found none.

nodes.label: Luke 13:7
nodes.text: He said to the vine dresser, ‘Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down. Why does it waste the soil?’

nodes.label: Luke 13:8
nodes.text: He answered, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it, and fertilize it.

nodes.label: Luke 13:9
nodes.text: If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”

nodes.label: Luke 13:10
nodes.text: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath day.

nodes.label: Luke 13:11
nodes.text: Behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and she was bent over, and could in no way straighten herself up.

nodes.label: Luke 13:12
nodes.text:
When Jesus saw her, he called her, and said to her,
“Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”

nodes.label: Luke 13:13
nodes.text: He laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight, and glorified God.

nodes.label: Luke 13:14
nodes.text: The ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the multitude, “There are six days in which men ought to work. Therefore come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day!”

nodes.label: Luke 13:15
nodes.text:
Therefore the Lord answered him,
“You hypocrites! Doesn’t each one of you free his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath, and lead him away to water?

nodes.label: Luke 13:16
nodes.text: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”

nodes.label: Luke 13:17
nodes.text: As he said these things, all his adversaries were disappointed, and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.

nodes.label: Luke 13:18
nodes.text:
He said,
“What is God’s Kingdom like? To what shall I compare it?

nodes.label: Luke 13:19
nodes.text: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and put in his own garden. It grew, and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky live in its branches.”

nodes.label: Luke 13:20
nodes.text:
Again he said,
“To what shall I compare God’s Kingdom?

nodes.label: Luke 13:21
nodes.text:
It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures

of flour, until it was all leavened.”

nodes.label: Luke 13:22
nodes.text: He went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and traveling on to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Luke 13:23
nodes.text:
One said to him, “Lord, are they few who are saved?”
He said to them,

nodes.label: Luke 13:24
nodes.text: “Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in, and will not be able.

nodes.label: Luke 13:25
nodes.text: When once the master of the house has risen up, and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside, and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us!’ then he will answer and tell you, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’

nodes.label: Luke 13:26
nodes.text: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’

nodes.label: Luke 13:27
nodes.text: He will say, ‘I tell you, I don’t know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.’

nodes.label: Luke 13:28
nodes.text: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets, in God’s Kingdom, and yourselves being thrown outside.

nodes.label: Luke 13:29
nodes.text: They will come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit down in God’s Kingdom.

nodes.label: Luke 13:30
nodes.text: Behold, there are some who are last who will be first, and there are some who are first who will be last.”

nodes.label: Luke 13:31
nodes.text: On that same day, some Pharisees came, saying to him, “Get out of here, and go away, for Herod wants to kill you.”

nodes.label: Luke 13:32
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.

nodes.label: Luke 13:33
nodes.text: Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it can’t be that a prophet would perish outside of Jerusalem.’

nodes.label: Luke 13:34
nodes.text: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that kills the prophets, and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you refused!

nodes.label: Luke 13:35
nodes.text: Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me, until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”

nodes.label: Luke 14:1
nodes.text: When he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.

nodes.label: Luke 14:2
nodes.text: Behold, a certain man who had dropsy was in front of him.

nodes.label: Luke 14:3
nodes.text:
Jesus, answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying,
“Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”

nodes.label: Luke 14:4
nodes.text:
But they were silent.
He took him, and healed him, and let him go.

nodes.label: Luke 14:5
nodes.text:
He answered them,
“Which of you, if your son
or an ox fell into a well, wouldn’t immediately pull him out on a Sabbath day?”

variants.reading: ὄνος ἢ βοῦς ('a donkey or an ox fell into a well')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke' lists ὄνος ἢ βοῦς ('donkey or ox') for א (Sinaiticus), K, L, X, Π, Ψ, f1, f13, 33, 892, 1071, ℓ547; the WEB prints the reading υἱὸς ἢ βοῦς ('son or ox') of P45, P75 and B (Vaticanus).

variants.reading: πρόβατον ἢ βοῦς ('a sheep or an ox')
variants.note: The fetched variants article lists this reading for Codex Bezae (D); D is not a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

nodes.label: Luke 14:6
nodes.text: They couldn’t answer him regarding these things.

nodes.label: Luke 14:7
nodes.text: He spoke a parable to those who were invited, when he noticed how they chose the best seats, and said to them,

nodes.label: Luke 14:8
nodes.text: “When you are invited by anyone to a marriage feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him,

nodes.label: Luke 14:9
nodes.text: and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.

nodes.label: Luke 14:10
nodes.text: But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.

nodes.label: Luke 14:11
nodes.text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

nodes.label: Luke 14:12
nodes.text:
He also said to the one who had invited him,
“When you make a dinner or a supper, don’t call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor rich neighbors, or perhaps they might also return the favor, and pay you back.

nodes.label: Luke 14:13
nodes.text: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;

nodes.label: Luke 14:14
nodes.text: and you will be blessed, because they don’t have the resources to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”

nodes.label: Luke 14:15
nodes.text: When one of those who sat at the table with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is he who will feast in God’s Kingdom!”

nodes.label: Luke 14:16
nodes.text:
But he said to him,
“A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.

nodes.label: Luke 14:17
nodes.text: He sent out his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, ‘Come, for everything is ready now.’

nodes.label: Luke 14:18
nodes.text:
They all as one began to make excuses.
“The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please have me excused.’

nodes.label: Luke 14:19
nodes.text: “Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try them out. Please have me excused.’

nodes.label: Luke 14:20
nodes.text: “Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I can’t come.’

nodes.label: Luke 14:21
nodes.text: “That servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’

nodes.label: Luke 14:22
nodes.text: “The servant said, ‘Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.’

nodes.label: Luke 14:23
nodes.text: “The lord said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

nodes.label: Luke 14:24
nodes.text: For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper.’”

nodes.label: Luke 14:25
nodes.text: Now great multitudes were going with him. He turned and said to them,

nodes.label: Luke 14:26
nodes.text:
“If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard
his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.

nodes.label: Luke 14:27
nodes.text: Whoever doesn’t bear his own cross, and come after me, can’t be my disciple.

nodes.label: Luke 14:28
nodes.text: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?

nodes.label: Luke 14:29
nodes.text: Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation, and is not able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him,

nodes.label: Luke 14:30
nodes.text: saying, ‘This man began to build, and wasn’t able to finish.’

nodes.label: Luke 14:31
nodes.text: Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?

nodes.label: Luke 14:32
nodes.text: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy, and asks for conditions of peace.

nodes.label: Luke 14:33
nodes.text: So therefore whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.

nodes.label: Luke 14:34
nodes.text: Salt is good, but if the salt becomes flat and tasteless, with what do you season it?

nodes.label: Luke 14:35
nodes.text: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. It is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

nodes.label: Luke 15:1
nodes.text: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.

nodes.label: Luke 15:2
nodes.text: The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”

nodes.label: Luke 15:3
nodes.text: He told them this parable.

nodes.label: Luke 15:4
nodes.text: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep, and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?

nodes.label: Luke 15:5
nodes.text: When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

nodes.label: Luke 15:6
nodes.text: When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’

nodes.label: Luke 15:7
nodes.text: I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.

nodes.label: Luke 15:8
nodes.text:
Or what woman, if she had ten drachma
coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it?

nodes.label: Luke 15:9
nodes.text: When she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost.’

nodes.label: Luke 15:10
nodes.text: Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”

nodes.label: Luke 15:11
nodes.text:
He said,
“A certain man had two sons.

nodes.label: Luke 15:12
nodes.text: The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ He divided his livelihood between them.

nodes.label: Luke 15:13
nodes.text: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.

nodes.label: Luke 15:14
nodes.text: When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.

nodes.label: Luke 15:15
nodes.text: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.

nodes.label: Luke 15:16
nodes.text: He wanted to fill his belly with the husks that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.

nodes.label: Luke 15:17
nodes.text: But when he came to himself he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!

nodes.label: Luke 15:18
nodes.text: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight.

nodes.label: Luke 15:19
nodes.text: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’

nodes.label: Luke 15:20
nodes.text: “He arose, and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

nodes.label: Luke 15:21
nodes.text: The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

variants.reading: ποίησόν με ὡς ἕνα τῶν μισθίων σου ('Make me as one of your hired servants') is absent
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke' records for Luke 15:21 that the clause (present in Westcott and Hort and NA27/UBS4) is 'omitted by Byzantine text-type, and other Alexandrian mss'; no manuscript node of this graph is named, so attested_by is left empty. The WEB prints the clause.

nodes.label: Luke 15:22
nodes.text: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe, and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.

nodes.label: Luke 15:23
nodes.text: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let us eat, and celebrate;

nodes.label: Luke 15:24
nodes.text: for this, my son, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’ They began to celebrate.

nodes.label: Luke 15:25
nodes.text: “Now his elder son was in the field. As he came near to the house, he heard music and dancing.

nodes.label: Luke 15:26
nodes.text: He called one of the servants to him, and asked what was going on.

nodes.label: Luke 15:27
nodes.text: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’

nodes.label: Luke 15:28
nodes.text: But he was angry, and would not go in. Therefore his father came out, and begged him.

nodes.label: Luke 15:29
nodes.text: But he answered his father, ‘Behold, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never gave me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.

nodes.label: Luke 15:30
nodes.text: But when this your son came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’

nodes.label: Luke 15:31
nodes.text: “He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.

nodes.label: Luke 15:32
nodes.text: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’”

nodes.label: Luke 16:1
nodes.text:
He also said to his disciples,
“There was a certain rich man who had a manager. An accusation was made to him that this man was wasting his possessions.

nodes.label: Luke 16:2
nodes.text: He called him, and said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Give an accounting of your management, for you can no longer be manager.’

nodes.label: Luke 16:3
nodes.text: “The manager said within himself, ‘What will I do, seeing that my lord is taking away the management position from me? I don’t have strength to dig. I am ashamed to beg.

nodes.label: Luke 16:4
nodes.text: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from management, they may receive me into their houses.’

nodes.label: Luke 16:5
nodes.text: Calling each one of his lord’s debtors to him, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe to my lord?’

nodes.label: Luke 16:6
nodes.text: He said, ‘A hundred batos of oil.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’

nodes.label: Luke 16:7
nodes.text: Then he said to another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and write eighty.’

nodes.label: Luke 16:8
nodes.text: “His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely, for the children of this world are, in their own generation, wiser than the children of the light.

nodes.label: Luke 16:9
nodes.text: I tell you, make for yourselves friends by means of unrighteous mammon, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the eternal tents.

nodes.label: Luke 16:10
nodes.text: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.

nodes.label: Luke 16:11
nodes.text: If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?

nodes.label: Luke 16:12
nodes.text: If you have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is your own?

nodes.label: Luke 16:13
nodes.text: No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. You aren’t able to serve God and Mammon.”

nodes.label: Luke 16:14
nodes.text: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, also heard all these things, and they scoffed at him.

nodes.label: Luke 16:15
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“You are those who justify yourselves in the sight of men, but God knows your hearts. For that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.

nodes.label: Luke 16:16
nodes.text: The law and the prophets were until John. From that time the Good News of God’s Kingdom is preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.

nodes.label: Luke 16:17
nodes.text: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away, than for one tiny stroke of a pen in the law to fall.

nodes.label: Luke 16:18
nodes.text: Everyone who divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery. He who marries one who is divorced from a husband commits adultery.

nodes.label: Luke 16:19
nodes.text: “Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, living in luxury every day.

variants.reading: ονοματι Ν[ιν]ευης ('with the name N[in]eue')
variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 75: Luke 16:19 'Ανθρωπος δε τις ην πλουσιος, ονοματι Ν[ιν]ευης' (a rich man with the name Nineue) is read by P75, 36, 37 and Sahidic; the unnamed rich man of the WEB and the majority text is the reading without the name. P75 is a manuscript node of this graph.

nodes.label: Luke 16:20
nodes.text: A certain beggar, named Lazarus, was taken to his gate, full of sores,

nodes.label: Luke 16:21
nodes.text: and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Yes, even the dogs came and licked his sores.

nodes.label: Luke 16:22
nodes.text: The beggar died, and he was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died, and was buried.

nodes.label: Luke 16:23
nodes.text: In Hades, he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus at his bosom.

nodes.label: Luke 16:24
nodes.text: He cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue! For I am in anguish in this flame.’

nodes.label: Luke 16:25
nodes.text: “But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that you, in your lifetime, received your good things, and Lazarus, in the same way, bad things. But here he is now comforted, and you are in anguish.

nodes.label: Luke 16:26
nodes.text: Besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that those who want to pass from here to you are not able, and that no one may cross over from there to us.’

nodes.label: Luke 16:27
nodes.text: “He said, ‘I ask you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house;

nodes.label: Luke 16:28
nodes.text: for I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, so they won’t also come into this place of torment.’

nodes.label: Luke 16:29
nodes.text: “But Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.’

nodes.label: Luke 16:30
nodes.text: “He said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’

nodes.label: Luke 16:31
nodes.text: “He said to him, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if one rises from the dead.’”

nodes.label: Luke 17:1
nodes.text:
He said to the disciples,
“It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom they come!

nodes.label: Luke 17:2
nodes.text: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.

nodes.label: Luke 17:3
nodes.text: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him.

nodes.label: Luke 17:4
nodes.text: If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”

nodes.label: Luke 17:5
nodes.text: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”

nodes.label: Luke 17:6
nodes.text:
The Lord said,
“If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted, and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.

nodes.label: Luke 17:7
nodes.text: But who is there among you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say, when he comes in from the field, ‘Come immediately and sit down at the table,’

nodes.label: Luke 17:8
nodes.text: and will not rather tell him, ‘Prepare my supper, clothe yourself properly, and serve me, while I eat and drink. Afterward you shall eat and drink’?

nodes.label: Luke 17:9
nodes.text: Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded? I think not.

nodes.label: Luke 17:10
nodes.text: Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done our duty.’”

nodes.label: Luke 17:11
nodes.text: As he was on his way to Jerusalem, he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.

nodes.label: Luke 17:12
nodes.text: As he entered into a certain village, ten men who were lepers met him, who stood at a distance.

nodes.label: Luke 17:13
nodes.text: They lifted up their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”

nodes.label: Luke 17:14
nodes.text:
When he saw them, he said to them,
“Go and show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed.

nodes.label: Luke 17:15
nodes.text: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.

nodes.label: Luke 17:16
nodes.text: He fell on his face at Jesus’ feet, giving him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.

nodes.label: Luke 17:17
nodes.text:
Jesus answered,
“Weren’t the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?

nodes.label: Luke 17:18
nodes.text: Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this stranger?”

nodes.label: Luke 17:19
nodes.text:
Then he said to him,
“Get up, and go your way. Your faith has healed you.”

nodes.label: Luke 17:20
nodes.text:
Being asked by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answered them,
“God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation;

nodes.label: Luke 17:21
nodes.text: neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”

nodes.label: Luke 17:22
nodes.text:
He said to the disciples,
“The days will come, when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.

nodes.label: Luke 17:23
nodes.text: They will tell you, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘Look, there!’ Don’t go away, nor follow after them,

nodes.label: Luke 17:24
nodes.text: for as the lightning, when it flashes out of the one part under the sky, shines to the other part under the sky; so will the Son of Man be in his day.

nodes.label: Luke 17:25
nodes.text: But first, he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.

nodes.label: Luke 17:26
nodes.text: As it was in the days of Noah, even so will it be also in the days of the Son of Man.

nodes.label: Luke 17:27
nodes.text: They ate, they drank, they married, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ship, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.

nodes.label: Luke 17:28
nodes.text: Likewise, even as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;

nodes.label: Luke 17:29
nodes.text: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from the sky, and destroyed them all.

nodes.label: Luke 17:30
nodes.text: It will be the same way in the day that the Son of Man is revealed.

nodes.label: Luke 17:31
nodes.text: In that day, he who will be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away. Let him who is in the field likewise not turn back.

nodes.label: Luke 17:32
nodes.text: Remember Lot’s wife!

nodes.label: Luke 17:33
nodes.text: Whoever seeks to save his life loses it, but whoever loses his life preserves it.

nodes.label: Luke 17:34
nodes.text: I tell you, in that night there will be two people in one bed. The one will be taken, and the other will be left.

nodes.label: Luke 17:35
nodes.text: There will be two grinding grain together. One will be taken, and the other will be left.”

variants.reading: the whole verse is absent (the KJV text 'Two men shall be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left' is a repetition of Matthew 24:40)
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke: Luke 17:36 is omitted by א (Sinaiticus), A, B (Vaticanus), K, L, W, X, Δ, Θ, Π, Ψ, 063, f1, 28, 33, 565, 892, 1009, 1010, 1079, 1195, 1216, 1242, 1365, the Byzantine text, ℓ184, ℓ950, Coptic, Gothic and Ethiopic; the reading 'two in the field' is carried by D, 1071, 1230, 2174, ℓ185, ℓ1579, it, vg - no manuscript node of this graph among the supporters. The WEB prints the verse; no preserves edges are written because both codices omit it.

nodes.label: Luke 17:37
nodes.text:
They, answering, asked him, “Where, Lord?”
He said to them,
“Where the body is, there will the vultures also be gathered together.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:1
nodes.text: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray, and not give up,

nodes.label: Luke 18:2
nodes.text:
saying,
“There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God, and didn’t respect man.

nodes.label: Luke 18:3
nodes.text: A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’

nodes.label: Luke 18:4
nodes.text: He wouldn’t for a while, but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God, nor respect man,

nodes.label: Luke 18:5
nodes.text: yet because this widow bothers me, I will defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”

nodes.label: Luke 18:6
nodes.text:
The Lord said,
“Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.

nodes.label: Luke 18:7
nodes.text: Won’t God avenge his chosen ones, who are crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with them?

nodes.label: Luke 18:8
nodes.text: I tell you that he will avenge them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”

nodes.label: Luke 18:9
nodes.text: He spoke also this parable to certain people who were convinced of their own righteousness, and who despised all others.

nodes.label: Luke 18:10
nodes.text: “Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.

nodes.label: Luke 18:11
nodes.text: The Pharisee stood and prayed to himself like this: ‘God, I thank you, that I am not like the rest of men, extortionists, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.

nodes.label: Luke 18:12
nodes.text: I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.’

nodes.label: Luke 18:13
nodes.text: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’

nodes.label: Luke 18:14
nodes.text: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:15
nodes.text: They were also bringing their babies to him, that he might touch them. But when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.

nodes.label: Luke 18:16
nodes.text:
Jesus summoned them, saying,
“Allow the little children to come to me, and don’t hinder them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.

nodes.label: Luke 18:17
nodes.text: Most certainly, I tell you, whoever doesn’t receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:18
nodes.text: A certain ruler asked him, saying, “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”

nodes.label: Luke 18:19
nodes.text:
Jesus asked him,
“Why do you call me good? No one is good, except one—God.

nodes.label: Luke 18:20
nodes.text: You know the commandments: ‘Don’t commit adultery,’ ‘Don’t murder,’ ‘Don’t steal,’ ‘Don’t give false testimony,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother.’”

nodes.label: Luke 18:21
nodes.text: He said, “I have observed all these things from my youth up.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:22
nodes.text:
When Jesus heard these things, he said to him,
“You still lack one thing. Sell all that you have, and distribute it to the poor. You will have treasure in heaven. Come, follow me.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:23
nodes.text: But when he heard these things, he became very sad, for he was very rich.

nodes.label: Luke 18:24
nodes.text:
Jesus, seeing that he became very sad, said,
“How hard it is for those who have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!

nodes.label: Luke 18:25
nodes.text: For it is easier for a camel to enter in through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:26
nodes.text: Those who heard it said, “Then who can be saved?”

nodes.label: Luke 18:27
nodes.text:
But he said,
“The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:28
nodes.text: Peter said, “Look, we have left everything, and followed you.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:29
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or wife, or brothers, or parents, or children, for God’s Kingdom’s sake,

nodes.label: Luke 18:30
nodes.text: who will not receive many times more in this time, and in the world to come, eternal life.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:31
nodes.text:
He took the twelve aside, and said to them,
“Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things that are written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be completed.

nodes.label: Luke 18:32
nodes.text: For he will be delivered up to the Gentiles, will be mocked, treated shamefully, and spit on.

nodes.label: Luke 18:33
nodes.text: They will scourge and kill him. On the third day, he will rise again.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:34
nodes.text: They understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them, and they didn’t understand the things that were said.

nodes.label: Luke 18:35
nodes.text: As he came near Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the road, begging.

nodes.label: Luke 18:36
nodes.text: Hearing a multitude going by, he asked what this meant.

nodes.label: Luke 18:37
nodes.text: They told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.

nodes.label: Luke 18:38
nodes.text: He cried out, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”

nodes.label: Luke 18:39
nodes.text: Those who led the way rebuked him, that he should be quiet; but he cried out all the more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”

nodes.label: Luke 18:40
nodes.text: Standing still, Jesus commanded him to be brought to him. When he had come near, he asked him,

nodes.label: Luke 18:41
nodes.text:
“What do you want me to do?”
He said, “Lord, that I may see again.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:42
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“Receive your sight. Your faith has healed you.”

nodes.label: Luke 18:43
nodes.text: Immediately he received his sight, and followed him, glorifying God. All the people, when they saw it, praised God.

nodes.label: Luke 19:1
nodes.text: He entered and was passing through Jericho.

nodes.label: Luke 19:2
nodes.text: There was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.

nodes.label: Luke 19:3
nodes.text: He was trying to see who Jesus was, and couldn’t because of the crowd, because he was short.

nodes.label: Luke 19:4
nodes.text: He ran on ahead, and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was going to pass that way.

nodes.label: Luke 19:5
nodes.text:
When Jesus came to the place, he looked up and saw him, and said to him,
“Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”

nodes.label: Luke 19:6
nodes.text: He hurried, came down, and received him joyfully.

nodes.label: Luke 19:7
nodes.text: When they saw it, they all murmured, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.”

nodes.label: Luke 19:8
nodes.text: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”

nodes.label: Luke 19:9
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.

nodes.label: Luke 19:10
nodes.text: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”

nodes.label: Luke 19:11
nodes.text: As they heard these things, he went on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem, and they supposed that God’s Kingdom would be revealed immediately.

nodes.label: Luke 19:12
nodes.text:
He said therefore,
“A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.

nodes.label: Luke 19:13
nodes.text:
He called ten servants of his, and gave them ten mina coins,

and told them, ‘Conduct business until I come.’

nodes.label: Luke 19:14
nodes.text: But his citizens hated him, and sent an envoy after him, saying, ‘We don’t want this man to reign over us.’

nodes.label: Luke 19:15
nodes.text: “When he had come back again, having received the kingdom, he commanded these servants, to whom he had given the money, to be called to him, that he might know what they had gained by conducting business.

nodes.label: Luke 19:16
nodes.text: The first came before him, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has made ten more minas.’

nodes.label: Luke 19:17
nodes.text: “He said to him, ‘Well done, you good servant! Because you were found faithful with very little, you shall have authority over ten cities.’

nodes.label: Luke 19:18
nodes.text: “The second came, saying, ‘Your mina, Lord, has made five minas.’

nodes.label: Luke 19:19
nodes.text: “So he said to him, ‘And you are to be over five cities.’

nodes.label: Luke 19:20
nodes.text: Another came, saying, ‘Lord, behold, your mina, which I kept laid away in a handkerchief,

nodes.label: Luke 19:21
nodes.text: for I feared you, because you are an exacting man. You take up that which you didn’t lay down, and reap that which you didn’t sow.’

nodes.label: Luke 19:22
nodes.text: “He said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth will I judge you, you wicked servant! You knew that I am an exacting man, taking up that which I didn’t lay down, and reaping that which I didn’t sow.

nodes.label: Luke 19:23
nodes.text: Then why didn’t you deposit my money in the bank, and at my coming, I might have earned interest on it?’

nodes.label: Luke 19:24
nodes.text: He said to those who stood by, ‘Take the mina away from him, and give it to him who has the ten minas.’

nodes.label: Luke 19:25
nodes.text: “They said to him, ‘Lord, he has ten minas!’

nodes.label: Luke 19:26
nodes.text: ‘For I tell you that to everyone who has, will more be given; but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.

nodes.label: Luke 19:27
nodes.text: But bring those enemies of mine who didn’t want me to reign over them here, and kill them before me.’”

nodes.label: Luke 19:28
nodes.text: Having said these things, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Luke 19:29
nodes.text: When he came near to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the mountain that is called Olivet, he sent two of his disciples,

nodes.label: Luke 19:30
nodes.text:
saying,
“Go your way into the village on the other side, in which, as you enter, you will find a colt tied, which no man had ever sat upon. Untie it, and bring it.

nodes.label: Luke 19:31
nodes.text: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say to him: ‘The Lord needs it.’”

nodes.label: Luke 19:32
nodes.text: Those who were sent went away, and found things just as he had told them.

nodes.label: Luke 19:33
nodes.text: As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, “Why are you untying the colt?”

nodes.label: Luke 19:34
nodes.text: They said, “The Lord needs it.”

nodes.label: Luke 19:35
nodes.text: They brought it to Jesus. They threw their cloaks on the colt, and set Jesus on them.

nodes.label: Luke 19:36
nodes.text: As he went, they spread their cloaks on the road.

nodes.label: Luke 19:37
nodes.text: As he was now getting near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which they had seen,

nodes.label: Luke 19:38
nodes.text:
saying, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!
 Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”

nodes.label: Luke 19:39
nodes.text: Some of the Pharisees from the multitude said to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples!”

nodes.label: Luke 19:40
nodes.text:
He answered them,
“I tell you that if these were silent, the stones would cry out.”

nodes.label: Luke 19:41
nodes.text: When he came near, he saw the city and wept over it,

nodes.label: Luke 19:42
nodes.text:
saying,
“If you, even you, had known today the things which belong to your peace! But now, they are hidden from your eyes.

nodes.label: Luke 19:43
nodes.text: For the days will come on you, when your enemies will throw up a barricade against you, surround you, hem you in on every side,

nodes.label: Luke 19:44
nodes.text: and will dash you and your children within you to the ground. They will not leave in you one stone on another, because you didn’t know the time of your visitation.”

nodes.label: Luke 19:45
nodes.text: He entered into the temple, and began to drive out those who bought and sold in it,

nodes.label: Luke 19:46
nodes.text:
saying to them,
“It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’

but you have made it a ‘den of robbers’!”

nodes.label: Luke 19:47
nodes.text: He was teaching daily in the temple, but the chief priests and the scribes and the leading men among the people sought to destroy him.

nodes.label: Luke 19:48
nodes.text: They couldn’t find what they might do, for all the people hung on to every word that he said.

nodes.label: Luke 20:1
nodes.text:
On one of those days, as he was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the Good News, the
priests and scribes came to him with the elders.

variants.reading: chief priests (archiereis)
variants.note: WEB reads 'priests' (hiereis, A W Byz per the fetched Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke); 'chief priests' is the reading of Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, C and D.

variants.reading: one of the days (mias ton hemeron)
variants.note: WEB follows 'one of those days' (mias ton hemeron ekeinon, A C W Byz); the shorter reading is carried by Sinaiticus and Vaticanus per the fetched Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke.

nodes.label: Luke 20:2
nodes.text: They asked him, “Tell us: by what authority do you do these things? Or who is giving you this authority?”

nodes.label: Luke 20:3
nodes.text:
He answered them,
“I also will ask you one question. Tell me:

nodes.label: Luke 20:4
nodes.text: the baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men?”

nodes.label: Luke 20:5
nodes.text: They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why didn’t you believe him?’

nodes.label: Luke 20:6
nodes.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.”

nodes.label: Luke 20:7
nodes.text: They answered that they didn’t know where it was from.

nodes.label: Luke 20:8
nodes.text:
Jesus said to them,
“Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

nodes.label: Luke 20:9
nodes.text:
He began to tell the people this parable.
“A

man planted a vineyard, and rented it out to some farmers, and went into another country for a long time.

nodes.label: Luke 20:10
nodes.text: At the proper season, he sent a servant to the farmers to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the farmers beat him, and sent him away empty.

nodes.label: Luke 20:11
nodes.text: He sent yet another servant, and they also beat him, and treated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.

nodes.label: Luke 20:12
nodes.text: He sent yet a third, and they also wounded him, and threw him out.

nodes.label: Luke 20:13
nodes.text: The lord of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. It may be that seeing him, they will respect him.’

nodes.label: Luke 20:14
nodes.text: “But when the farmers saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.’

nodes.label: Luke 20:15
nodes.text: They threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him. What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do to them?

nodes.label: Luke 20:16
nodes.text:
He will come and destroy these farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.”
When they heard it, they said, “May it never be!”

nodes.label: Luke 20:17
nodes.text:
But he looked at them, and said,
“Then what is this that is written,
‘The stone which the builders rejected,
the same was made the chief cornerstone?’

nodes.label: Luke 20:18
nodes.text:
Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces,

but it will crush whomever it falls on to dust.”

nodes.label: Luke 20:19
nodes.text: The chief priests and the scribes sought to lay hands on him that very hour, but they feared the people—for they knew he had spoken this parable against them.

nodes.label: Luke 20:20
nodes.text: They watched him, and sent out spies, who pretended to be righteous, that they might trap him in something he said, so as to deliver him up to the power and authority of the governor.

nodes.label: Luke 20:21
nodes.text: They asked him, “Teacher, we know that you say and teach what is right, and aren’t partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God.

nodes.label: Luke 20:22
nodes.text: Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”

nodes.label: Luke 20:23
nodes.text:
But he perceived their craftiness, and said to them,
“Why do you test me?

nodes.label: Luke 20:24
nodes.text:
Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it?”

They answered, “Caesar’s.”

nodes.label: Luke 20:25
nodes.text:
