He said to them,
“Then give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”

nodes.label: Luke 20:26
nodes.text: They weren’t able to trap him in his words before the people. They marveled at his answer, and were silent.

nodes.label: Luke 20:27
nodes.text: Some of the Sadducees came to him, those who deny that there is a resurrection.

nodes.label: Luke 20:28
nodes.text: They asked him, “Teacher, Moses wrote to us that if a man’s brother dies having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take the wife, and raise up children for his brother.

nodes.label: Luke 20:29
nodes.text: There were therefore seven brothers. The first took a wife, and died childless.

nodes.label: Luke 20:30
nodes.text: The second took her as wife, and he died childless.

nodes.label: Luke 20:31
nodes.text: The third took her, and likewise the seven all left no children, and died.

nodes.label: Luke 20:32
nodes.text: Afterward the woman also died.

nodes.label: Luke 20:33
nodes.text: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them will she be? For the seven had her as a wife.”

nodes.label: Luke 20:34
nodes.text:
Jesus said to them,
“The children of this age marry, and are given in marriage.

nodes.label: Luke 20:35
nodes.text: But those who are considered worthy to attain to that age and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage.

nodes.label: Luke 20:36
nodes.text: For they can’t die any more, for they are like the angels, and are children of God, being children of the resurrection.

nodes.label: Luke 20:37
nodes.text: But that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, when he called the Lord ‘The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’

nodes.label: Luke 20:38
nodes.text: Now he is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for all are alive to him.”

nodes.label: Luke 20:39
nodes.text: Some of the scribes answered, “Teacher, you speak well.”

nodes.label: Luke 20:40
nodes.text: They didn’t dare to ask him any more questions.

nodes.label: Luke 20:41
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Why do they say that the Christ is David’s son?

nodes.label: Luke 20:42
nodes.text:
David himself says in the book of Psalms,
‘The Lord said to my Lord,
“Sit at my right hand,

nodes.label: Luke 20:43
nodes.text: until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’

nodes.label: Luke 20:44
nodes.text: “David therefore calls him Lord, so how is he his son?”

nodes.label: Luke 20:45
nodes.text: In the hearing of all the people, he said to his disciples,

nodes.label: Luke 20:46
nodes.text: “Beware of those scribes who like to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the marketplaces, the best seats in the synagogues, and the best places at feasts;

nodes.label: Luke 20:47
nodes.text: who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers: these will receive greater condemnation.”

nodes.label: Luke 21:1
nodes.text: He looked up, and saw the rich people who were putting their gifts into the treasury.

nodes.label: Luke 21:2
nodes.text: He saw a certain poor widow casting in two small brass coins.

nodes.label: Luke 21:3
nodes.text:
He said,
“Truly I tell you, this poor widow put in more than all of them,

nodes.label: Luke 21:4
nodes.text: for all these put in gifts for God from their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all that she had to live on.”

nodes.label: Luke 21:5
nodes.text: As some were talking about the temple and how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts, he said,

nodes.label: Luke 21:6
nodes.text: “As for these things which you see, the days will come, in which there will not be left here one stone on another that will not be thrown down.”

nodes.label: Luke 21:7
nodes.text: They asked him, “Teacher, so when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are about to happen?”

nodes.label: Luke 21:8
nodes.text:
He said,
“Watch out that you don’t get led astray, for many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time is at hand.’ Therefore don’t follow them.

nodes.label: Luke 21:9
nodes.text: When you hear of wars and disturbances, don’t be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end won’t come immediately.”

nodes.label: Luke 21:10
nodes.text:
Then he said to them,
“Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.

nodes.label: Luke 21:11
nodes.text: There will be great earthquakes, famines, and plagues in various places. There will be terrors and great signs from heaven.

nodes.label: Luke 21:12
nodes.text: But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and will persecute you, delivering you up to synagogues and prisons, bringing you before kings and governors for my name’s sake.

nodes.label: Luke 21:13
nodes.text: It will turn out as a testimony for you.

nodes.label: Luke 21:14
nodes.text: Settle it therefore in your hearts not to meditate beforehand how to answer,

nodes.label: Luke 21:15
nodes.text: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all your adversaries will not be able to withstand or to contradict.

nodes.label: Luke 21:16
nodes.text: You will be handed over even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. They will cause some of you to be put to death.

nodes.label: Luke 21:17
nodes.text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake.

nodes.label: Luke 21:18
nodes.text: And not a hair of your head will perish.

nodes.label: Luke 21:19
nodes.text: “By your endurance you will win your lives.

nodes.label: Luke 21:20
nodes.text: “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is at hand.

nodes.label: Luke 21:21
nodes.text: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Let those who are in the middle of her depart. Let those who are in the country not enter therein.

nodes.label: Luke 21:22
nodes.text: For these are days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.

nodes.label: Luke 21:23
nodes.text: Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who nurse infants in those days! For there will be great distress in the land, and wrath to this people.

nodes.label: Luke 21:24
nodes.text: They will fall by the edge of the sword, and will be led captive into all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.

nodes.label: Luke 21:25
nodes.text: There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars; and on the earth anxiety of nations, in perplexity for the roaring of the sea and the waves;

nodes.label: Luke 21:26
nodes.text: men fainting for fear, and for expectation of the things which are coming on the world: for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

nodes.label: Luke 21:27
nodes.text: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

nodes.label: Luke 21:28
nodes.text: But when these things begin to happen, look up, and lift up your heads, because your redemption is near.”

nodes.label: Luke 21:29
nodes.text:
He told them a parable.
“See the fig tree, and all the trees.

nodes.label: Luke 21:30
nodes.text: When they are already budding, you see it and know by your own selves that the summer is already near.

nodes.label: Luke 21:31
nodes.text: Even so you also, when you see these things happening, know that God’s Kingdom is near.

nodes.label: Luke 21:32
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all things are accomplished.

nodes.label: Luke 21:33
nodes.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away.

nodes.label: Luke 21:34
nodes.text: “So be careful, or your hearts will be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day will come on you suddenly.

nodes.label: Luke 21:35
nodes.text: For it will come like a snare on all those who dwell on the surface of all the earth.

nodes.label: Luke 21:36
nodes.text: Therefore be watchful all the time, praying that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things that will happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”

nodes.label: Luke 21:37
nodes.text: Every day Jesus was teaching in the temple, and every night he would go out and spend the night on the mountain that is called Olivet.

nodes.label: Luke 21:38
nodes.text: All the people came early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him.

nodes.label: Luke 22:1
nodes.text: Now the feast of unleavened bread, which is called the Passover, was approaching.

nodes.label: Luke 22:2
nodes.text: The chief priests and the scribes sought how they might put him to death, for they feared the people.

nodes.label: Luke 22:3
nodes.text: Satan entered into Judas, who was also called Iscariot, who was counted with the twelve.

nodes.label: Luke 22:4
nodes.text: He went away, and talked with the chief priests and captains about how he might deliver him to them.

nodes.label: Luke 22:5
nodes.text: They were glad, and agreed to give him money.

nodes.label: Luke 22:6
nodes.text: He consented, and sought an opportunity to deliver him to them in the absence of the multitude.

nodes.label: Luke 22:7
nodes.text: The day of unleavened bread came, on which the Passover must be sacrificed.

nodes.label: Luke 22:8
nodes.text:
Jesus sent Peter and John, saying,
“Go and prepare the Passover for us, that we may eat.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:9
nodes.text: They said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare?”

nodes.label: Luke 22:10
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Behold, when you have entered into the city, a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him into the house which he enters.

nodes.label: Luke 22:11
nodes.text: Tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’

nodes.label: Luke 22:12
nodes.text: He will show you a large, furnished upper room. Make preparations there.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:13
nodes.text: They went, found things as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover.

nodes.label: Luke 22:14
nodes.text: When the hour had come, he sat down with the twelve apostles.

nodes.label: Luke 22:15
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer,

nodes.label: Luke 22:16
nodes.text: for I tell you, I will no longer by any means eat of it until it is fulfilled in God’s Kingdom.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:17
nodes.text:
He received a cup, and when he had given thanks, he said,
“Take this, and share it among yourselves,

nodes.label: Luke 22:18
nodes.text: for I tell you, I will not drink at all again from the fruit of the vine, until God’s Kingdom comes.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:19
nodes.text:
He took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke, and gave it to them, saying,
“This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.”

variants.reading: 22:19b-20 omitted (from 'which is given for you' through 'which is shed for you' and the cup after supper)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke' lists the omission of to hyper hymon didomenon ... to hyper hymon ekchynnomenon for Codex Bezae (D), old Latin a, (b, e with a different word order), d, ff2, i, l (syr-cur omits only 'which is shed for you'). The famous 'Western non-interpolation'; none of these witnesses is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is empty.

nodes.label: Luke 22:20
nodes.text:
Likewise, he took the cup after supper, saying,
“This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.

variants.reading: 22:19b-20 omitted (the cup-after-supper words are part of the omitted passage)
variants.note: Same Western non-interpolation as at Luke 22:19 (see that passage): omitted by D and old Latin witnesses a, b, e, d, ff2, i, l per the fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke'; the List of omitted Bible verses also marks Luke 22:20. No manuscript node of this graph is among the witnesses, so attested_by is empty.

nodes.label: Luke 22:21
nodes.text: But behold, the hand of him who betrays me is with me on the table.

nodes.label: Luke 22:22
nodes.text: The Son of Man indeed goes, as it has been determined, but woe to that man through whom he is betrayed!”

nodes.label: Luke 22:23
nodes.text: They began to question among themselves, which of them it was who would do this thing.

nodes.label: Luke 22:24
nodes.text: There arose also a contention among them, which of them was considered to be greatest.

nodes.label: Luke 22:25
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’

nodes.label: Luke 22:26
nodes.text: But not so with you. But one who is the greater among you, let him become as the younger, and one who is governing, as one who serves.

nodes.label: Luke 22:27
nodes.text: For who is greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves? Isn’t it he who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.

nodes.label: Luke 22:28
nodes.text: But you are those who have continued with me in my trials.

nodes.label: Luke 22:29
nodes.text: I confer on you a kingdom, even as my Father conferred on me,

nodes.label: Luke 22:30
nodes.text: that you may eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom. You will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:31
nodes.text:
The Lord said,
“Simon, Simon, behold, Satan asked to have all of you, that he might sift you as wheat,

nodes.label: Luke 22:32
nodes.text: but I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn’t fail. You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:33
nodes.text: He said to him, “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death!”

nodes.label: Luke 22:34
nodes.text:
He said,
“I tell you, Peter, the rooster will by no means crow today until you deny that you know me three times.”

variants.reading: heos tris me aparnese mhe idenai ('until three times you will deny to not know me')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke' (citing the Luke 22:34 Biblehub text analysis) records three readings: Nestle 1904 'until three times me you will deny to not know'; Westcott-Hort 1881 'until three times me you will deny to know'; Byzantine 'before the three times you will deny not to know me'. None of the named witnesses is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is empty.

nodes.label: Luke 22:35
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“When I sent you out without purse, and wallet, and shoes, did you lack anything?”
They said, “Nothing.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:36
nodes.text:
Then he said to them,
“But now, whoever has a purse, let him take it, and likewise a wallet. Whoever has none, let him sell his cloak, and buy a sword.

nodes.label: Luke 22:37
nodes.text:
For I tell you that this which is written must still be fulfilled in me: ‘He was counted with transgressors.’
For that which concerns me has an end.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:38
nodes.text:
They said, “Lord, behold, here are two swords.”
He said to them,
“That is enough.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:39
nodes.text: He came out, and went, as his custom was, to the Mount of Olives. His disciples also followed him.

nodes.label: Luke 22:40
nodes.text:
When he was at the place, he said to them,
“Pray that you don’t enter into temptation.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:41
nodes.text: He was withdrawn from them about a stone’s throw, and he knelt down and prayed,

nodes.label: Luke 22:42
nodes.text:
saying,
“Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:43
nodes.text: An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.

variants.reading: 22:43-44 omitted (the angel and the sweat like drops of blood)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Luke 22:43-44' article lists the manuscripts that exclude the passage: Papyrus 69, Papyrus 75, Codex Sinaiticus (corrector 1), Alexandrinus (A), Vaticanus (B), Petropolitanus Purpureus (N), Nitriensis (R), Borgianus (T), Washingtonianus (W), minuscules 158, 512, 542, 552, 579, 777, 826, 1071*, 1128 and others. It also records that the passage is placed in double brackets in modern editions and that its authenticity has been disputed by scholars since the second half of the 19th century.

variants.reading: 22:43-44 present (the angel and the sweat like drops of blood)
variants.note: The fetched article lists the includers: Codex Sinaiticus in the ORIGINAL HAND (the first corrector omits it), Bezae (D), Laudianus (E), 0171, Family 1, 565, 700, 892, the Byzantine text, the Vetus Latina, the Vulgate, the Syriac versions, the Diatessaron; Family 13 transposes the passage after Matthew 26:39. Only the graph's manuscript nodes are listed in attested_by.

nodes.label: Luke 22:44
nodes.text: Being in agony he prayed more earnestly. His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down on the ground.

variants.reading: 22:43-44 omitted (the angel and the sweat like drops of blood)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Luke 22:43-44' article lists the manuscripts that exclude the passage: Papyrus 69, Papyrus 75, Codex Sinaiticus (corrector 1), Alexandrinus (A), Vaticanus (B), Petropolitanus Purpureus (N), Nitriensis (R), Borgianus (T), Washingtonianus (W), minuscules 158, 512, 542, 552, 579, 777, 826, 1071*, 1128 and others. It also records that the passage is placed in double brackets in modern editions and that its authenticity has been disputed by scholars since the second half of the 19th century.

variants.reading: 22:43-44 present (the angel and the sweat like drops of blood)
variants.note: The fetched article lists the includers: Codex Sinaiticus in the ORIGINAL HAND (the first corrector omits it), Bezae (D), Laudianus (E), 0171, Family 1, 565, 700, 892, the Byzantine text, the Vetus Latina, the Vulgate, the Syriac versions, the Diatessaron; Family 13 transposes the passage after Matthew 26:39. Only the graph's manuscript nodes are listed in attested_by.

nodes.label: Luke 22:45
nodes.text: When he rose up from his prayer, he came to the disciples, and found them sleeping because of grief,

nodes.label: Luke 22:46
nodes.text:
and said to them,
“Why do you sleep? Rise and pray that you may not enter into temptation.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:47
nodes.text: While he was still speaking, behold, a multitude, and he who was called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. He came near to Jesus to kiss him.

nodes.label: Luke 22:48
nodes.text:
But Jesus said to him,
“Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”

nodes.label: Luke 22:49
nodes.text: When those who were around him saw what was about to happen, they said to him, “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?”

nodes.label: Luke 22:50
nodes.text: A certain one of them struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.

nodes.label: Luke 22:51
nodes.text:
But Jesus answered,
“Let me at least do this”—and he touched his ear, and healed him.

nodes.label: Luke 22:52
nodes.text:
Jesus said to the chief priests, captains of the temple, and elders, who had come against him,
“Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?

nodes.label: Luke 22:53
nodes.text: When I was with you in the temple daily, you didn’t stretch out your hands against me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:54
nodes.text: They seized him, and led him away, and brought him into the high priest’s house. But Peter followed from a distance.

nodes.label: Luke 22:55
nodes.text: When they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard, and had sat down together, Peter sat among them.

nodes.label: Luke 22:56
nodes.text: A certain servant girl saw him as he sat in the light, and looking intently at him, said, “This man also was with him.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:57
nodes.text: He denied Jesus, saying, “Woman, I don’t know him.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:58
nodes.text:
After a little while someone else saw him, and said, “You also are one of them!”
But Peter answered, “Man, I am not!”

nodes.label: Luke 22:59
nodes.text: After about one hour passed, another confidently affirmed, saying, “Truly this man also was with him, for he is a Galilean!”

nodes.label: Luke 22:60
nodes.text: But Peter said, “Man, I don’t know what you are talking about!” Immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.

nodes.label: Luke 22:61
nodes.text:
The Lord turned, and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the Lord’s word, how he said to him,
“Before the rooster crows you will deny me three times.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:62
nodes.text: He went out, and wept bitterly.

nodes.label: Luke 22:63
nodes.text: The men who held Jesus mocked him and beat him.

nodes.label: Luke 22:64
nodes.text: Having blindfolded him, they struck him on the face and asked him, “Prophesy! Who is the one who struck you?”

nodes.label: Luke 22:65
nodes.text: They spoke many other things against him, insulting him.

nodes.label: Luke 22:66
nodes.text: As soon as it was day, the assembly of the elders of the people were gathered together, both chief priests and scribes, and they led him away into their council, saying,

nodes.label: Luke 22:67
nodes.text:
“If you are the Christ, tell us.”
But he said to them,
“If I tell you, you won’t believe,

nodes.label: Luke 22:68
nodes.text: and if I ask, you will in no way answer me or let me go.

nodes.label: Luke 22:69
nodes.text: From now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:70
nodes.text:
They all said, “Are you then the Son of God?”
He said to them,
“You say it, because I am.”

nodes.label: Luke 22:71
nodes.text: They said, “Why do we need any more witness? For we ourselves have heard from his own mouth!”

nodes.label: Luke 23:1
nodes.text: The whole company of them rose up and brought him before Pilate.

nodes.label: Luke 23:2
nodes.text: They began to accuse him, saying, “We found this man perverting the nation, forbidding paying taxes to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ, a king.”

nodes.label: Luke 23:3
nodes.text:
Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
He answered him,
“So you say.”

nodes.label: Luke 23:4
nodes.text: Pilate said to the chief priests and the multitudes, “I find no basis for a charge against this man.”

nodes.label: Luke 23:5
nodes.text: But they insisted, saying, “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this place.”

nodes.label: Luke 23:6
nodes.text: But when Pilate heard Galilee mentioned, he asked if the man was a Galilean.

nodes.label: Luke 23:7
nodes.text: When he found out that he was in Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem during those days.

nodes.label: Luke 23:8
nodes.text: Now when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceedingly glad, for he had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had heard many things about him. He hoped to see some miracle done by him.

nodes.label: Luke 23:9
nodes.text: He questioned him with many words, but he gave no answers.

nodes.label: Luke 23:10
nodes.text: The chief priests and the scribes stood, vehemently accusing him.

nodes.label: Luke 23:11
nodes.text: Herod with his soldiers humiliated him and mocked him. Dressing him in luxurious clothing, they sent him back to Pilate.

nodes.label: Luke 23:12
nodes.text: Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that very day, for before that they were enemies with each other.

nodes.label: Luke 23:13
nodes.text: Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,

nodes.label: Luke 23:14
nodes.text: and said to them, “You brought this man to me as one that perverts the people, and behold, having examined him before you, I found no basis for a charge against this man concerning those things of which you accuse him.

nodes.label: Luke 23:15
nodes.text: Neither has Herod, for I sent you to him, and see, nothing worthy of death has been done by him.

nodes.label: Luke 23:16
nodes.text: I will therefore chastise him and release him.”

nodes.label: Luke 23:17
nodes.text: Now he had to release one prisoner to them at the feast.

variants.reading: the whole verse ('Now he had to release one prisoner to them at the feast.') omitted
variants.note: Missing from Papyrus 75, Codex Alexandrinus, Codex Vaticanus and others; present in Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Washingtonianus, Family 1 and Family 13. The verse parallels Matthew 27:15 and Mark 15:6 and is suspected of assimilation into Luke (Wikipedia, List of omitted Bible verses, Luke 23:17).

variants.reading: the verse present
variants.note: Codex Sinaiticus carries Luke 23:17 (Wikipedia, List of omitted Bible verses).

nodes.label: Luke 23:18
nodes.text: But they all cried out together, saying, “Away with this man! Release to us Barabbas!”—

nodes.label: Luke 23:19
nodes.text: one who was thrown into prison for a certain revolt in the city, and for murder.

nodes.label: Luke 23:20
nodes.text: Then Pilate spoke to them again, wanting to release Jesus,

nodes.label: Luke 23:21
nodes.text: but they shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify him!”

nodes.label: Luke 23:22
nodes.text: He said to them the third time, “Why? What evil has this man done? I have found no capital crime in him. I will therefore chastise him and release him.”

nodes.label: Luke 23:23
nodes.text: But they were urgent with loud voices, asking that he might be crucified. Their voices and the voices of the chief priests prevailed.

nodes.label: Luke 23:24
nodes.text: Pilate decreed that what they asked for should be done.

nodes.label: Luke 23:25
nodes.text: He released him who had been thrown into prison for insurrection and murder, for whom they asked, but he delivered Jesus up to their will.

nodes.label: Luke 23:26
nodes.text: When they led him away, they grabbed one Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, and laid on him the cross, to carry it after Jesus.

nodes.label: Luke 23:27
nodes.text: A great multitude of the people followed him, including women who also mourned and lamented him.

nodes.label: Luke 23:28
nodes.text:
But Jesus, turning to them, said,
“Daughters of Jerusalem, don’t weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.

nodes.label: Luke 23:29
nodes.text: For behold, the days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren, the wombs that never bore, and the breasts that never nursed.’

nodes.label: Luke 23:30
nodes.text: Then they will begin to tell the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and tell the hills, ‘Cover us.’

nodes.label: Luke 23:31
nodes.text: For if they do these things in the green tree, what will be done in the dry?”

nodes.label: Luke 23:32
nodes.text: There were also others, two criminals, led with him to be put to death.

nodes.label: Luke 23:33
nodes.text: When they came to the place that is called The Skull, they crucified him there with the criminals, one on the right and the other on the left.

nodes.label: Luke 23:34
nodes.text:
Jesus said,
“Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.”
Dividing his garments among them, they cast lots.

variants.reading: the sentence 'Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.' omitted
variants.note: Omitted in P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, D*, W, Theta and other early witnesses; included in the majority text. Ehrman argues the words were omitted by some scribes because of anti-Judaic sentiment around the second century (Wikipedia, Papyrus 75; Sayings of Jesus on the cross).

nodes.label: Luke 23:35
nodes.text: The people stood watching. The rulers with them also scoffed at him, saying, “He saved others. Let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God, his chosen one!”

nodes.label: Luke 23:36
nodes.text: The soldiers also mocked him, coming to him and offering him vinegar,

nodes.label: Luke 23:37
nodes.text: and saying, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself!”

nodes.label: Luke 23:38
nodes.text: An inscription was also written over him in letters of Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: “THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.”

variants.reading: 'in letters of Greek, Latin, and Hebrew' absent: 'There was also an inscription above him: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.'
variants.note: Alexandrian text-type (Westcott and Hort 1881, NA27/UBS4); the Byzantine text carries the trilingual detail (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 23:38).

nodes.label: Luke 23:39
nodes.text: One of the criminals who was hanged insulted him, saying, “If you are the Christ, save yourself and us!”

variants.reading: 'Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us!' (Alexandrian) against 'If you are the Christ, save yourself and us!' (Byzantine)
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 23:39.

nodes.label: Luke 23:40
nodes.text: But the other answered, and rebuking him said, “Don’t you even fear God, seeing you are under the same condemnation?

nodes.label: Luke 23:41
nodes.text: And we indeed justly, for we receive the due reward for our deeds, but this man has done nothing wrong.”

nodes.label: Luke 23:42
nodes.text: He said to Jesus, “Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.”

variants.reading: 'And he said: Jesus, remember me' (Alexandrian) against 'And he said to Jesus: Remember me, Lord' (Byzantine)
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 23:42.

nodes.label: Luke 23:43
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”

nodes.label: Luke 23:44
nodes.text: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.

nodes.label: Luke 23:45
nodes.text: The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in two.

variants.reading: 'the sun's light failed' (tou heliou eklipontos; Alexandrian) against 'and the sun was darkened' (Byzantine)
variants.note: Alexandrian text-type (Westcott and Hort 1881, NA27/UBS4, Nestle 1904); the Byzantine text reads 'and the sun was darkened', which the WEB follows (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 23:45).

nodes.label: Luke 23:46
nodes.text:
Jesus, crying with a loud voice, said,
“Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!” Having said this, he breathed his last.

nodes.label: Luke 23:47
nodes.text: When the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, “Certainly this was a righteous man.”

nodes.label: Luke 23:48
nodes.text: All the multitudes that came together to see this, when they saw the things that were done, returned home beating their breasts.

nodes.label: Luke 23:49
nodes.text: All his acquaintances, and the women who followed with him from Galilee, stood at a distance, watching these things.

nodes.label: Luke 23:50
nodes.text: Behold, a man named Joseph, who was a member of the council, a good and righteous man

nodes.label: Luke 23:51
nodes.text: (he had not consented to their counsel and deed), from Arimathaea, a city of the Jews, who was also waiting for God’s Kingdom:

nodes.label: Luke 23:52
nodes.text: this man went to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.

nodes.label: Luke 23:53
nodes.text: He took it down, and wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb that was cut in stone, where no one had ever been laid.

nodes.label: Luke 23:54
nodes.text: It was the day of the Preparation, and the Sabbath was drawing near.

nodes.label: Luke 23:55
nodes.text: The women, who had come with him out of Galilee, followed after, and saw the tomb, and how his body was laid.

nodes.label: Luke 23:56
nodes.text: They returned, and prepared spices and ointments. On the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.

nodes.label: Luke 24:1
nodes.text: But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they and some others came to the tomb, bringing the spices which they had prepared.

nodes.label: Luke 24:2
nodes.text: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.

nodes.label: Luke 24:3
nodes.text: They entered in, and didn’t find the Lord Jesus’ body.

variants.reading: τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ('of Jesus', without 'the Lord')
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': 'of the Lord Jesus' is read by P75, א, A, B, C and most witnesses; 'Jesus' by 579, 1071, 1241, syr cur; and τοῦ Ἰησοῦ is omitted entirely by D (Codex Bezae), it a, b, d, e, ff2, l, r1.

nodes.label: Luke 24:4
nodes.text: While they were greatly perplexed about this, behold, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.

nodes.label: Luke 24:5
nodes.text:
Becoming terrified, they bowed their faces down to the earth.
They said to them, “Why do you seek the living among the dead?

nodes.label: Luke 24:6
nodes.text: He isn’t here, but is risen. Remember what he told you when he was still in Galilee,

variants.reading: 'He is not here, but is risen' (οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἀλλ᾽ ἠγέρθη) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': omitted by D (Codex Bezae), it a, b, d, e, ff2, l (Codex Rehdigerianus), r1, arm mss, geo B.

nodes.label: Luke 24:7
nodes.text: saying that the Son of Man must be delivered up into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again?”

nodes.label: Luke 24:8
nodes.text: They remembered his words,

nodes.label: Luke 24:9
nodes.text: returned from the tomb, and told all these things to the eleven, and to all the rest.

variants.reading: 'from the tomb' (ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': omitted by D, it a, b, c, d, e, ff2, l, r1, arm, geo.

nodes.label: Luke 24:10
nodes.text: Now they were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James. The other women with them told these things to the apostles.

nodes.label: Luke 24:11
nodes.text: These words seemed to them to be nonsense, and they didn’t believe them.

nodes.label: Luke 24:12
nodes.text: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. Stooping and looking in, he saw the strips of linen lying by themselves, and he departed to his home, wondering what had happened.

variants.reading: the whole verse (Peter at the tomb) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': verse omitted by D (Codex Bezae), it a, b, d, e, l (Codex Rehdigerianus), r1 — one of the classic 'Western non-interpolations'.

nodes.label: Luke 24:13
nodes.text: Behold, two of them were going that very day to a village named Emmaus, which was sixty stadia from Jerusalem.

variants.reading: ἑκατόν ἑξήκοντα, 'a hundred and sixty stadia' (about 30 km)
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': the hundred-sixty reading is attested by א (Sinaiticus), K*, N vid, Θ, Π, 079, 1079* pc and some lectionaries; the sixty reading of the standard text is carried by P75, A, B, D, E, F, G, H, K2, L, W, X, Δ, Ψ, 063, 070, f1, f13, Byz, Lect and most versions.

nodes.label: Luke 24:14
nodes.text: They talked with each other about all of these things which had happened.

nodes.label: Luke 24:15
nodes.text: While they talked and questioned together, Jesus himself came near, and went with them.

nodes.label: Luke 24:16
nodes.text: But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.

nodes.label: Luke 24:17
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“What are you talking about as you walk, and are sad?”

nodes.label: Luke 24:18
nodes.text: One of them, named Cleopas, answered him, “Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem who doesn’t know the things which have happened there in these days?”

nodes.label: Luke 24:19
Luke 24:20
nodes.text: and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him up to be condemned to death, and crucified him.

nodes.label: Luke 24:21
nodes.text: But we were hoping that it was he who would redeem Israel. Yes, and besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.

nodes.label: Luke 24:22
nodes.text: Also, certain women of our company amazed us, having arrived early at the tomb;

nodes.label: Luke 24:23
nodes.text: and when they didn’t find his body, they came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels, who said that he was alive.

nodes.label: Luke 24:24
nodes.text: Some of us went to the tomb, and found it just like the women had said, but they didn’t see him.”

nodes.label: Luke 24:25
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Foolish men, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!

nodes.label: Luke 24:26
nodes.text: Didn’t the Christ have to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?”

nodes.label: Luke 24:27
nodes.text: Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.

nodes.label: Luke 24:28
nodes.text: They came near to the village, where they were going, and he acted like he would go further.

nodes.label: Luke 24:29
nodes.text:
They urged him, saying, “Stay with us, for it is almost evening, and the day is almost over.”
He went in to stay with them.

nodes.label: Luke 24:30
nodes.text: When he had sat down at the table with them, he took the bread and gave thanks. Breaking it, he gave it to them.

nodes.label: Luke 24:31
nodes.text: Their eyes were opened, and they recognized him, and he vanished out of their sight.

nodes.label: Luke 24:32
nodes.text: They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us, while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”

nodes.label: Luke 24:33
nodes.text: They rose up that very hour, returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,

nodes.label: Luke 24:34
nodes.text: saying, “The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!”

nodes.label: Luke 24:35
nodes.text: They related the things that happened along the way, and how he was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.

nodes.label: Luke 24:36
nodes.text:
As they said these things, Jesus himself stood among them, and said to them,
“Peace be to you.”

variants.reading: 'and said to them: Peace unto you' (καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς εἰρήνη ὑμῖν) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': the phrase is read by mss of the Alexandrian, Caesarean and Byzantine text-types and bracketed by WH 1881 and Nestle 1904; omitted by D, it a, b, d, e, ff2, l, r1 and by Tischendorf's 8th edition. The same page records ὁ Ἰησοῦς ('Jesus') as omitted in the Alexandrian editions but present in Byz.

nodes.label: Luke 24:37
nodes.text: But they were terrified and filled with fear, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.

nodes.label: Luke 24:38
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Why are you troubled? Why do doubts arise in your hearts?

nodes.label: Luke 24:39
nodes.text: See my hands and my feet, that it is truly me. Touch me and see, for a spirit doesn’t have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.”

nodes.label: Luke 24:40
nodes.text: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.

variants.reading: 'and having said thus, he showed to them the hands and the feet' (24:40) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': the verse is bracketed in the Alexandrian editions (WH 1881, Nestle 1904) and omitted by D, it a, b, d, e, ff2, l, r1, syr s, syr cur.

nodes.label: Luke 24:41
nodes.text:
While they still didn’t believe for joy, and wondered, he said to them,
“Do you have anything here to eat?”

nodes.label: Luke 24:42
nodes.text: They gave him a piece of a broiled fish and some honeycomb.

nodes.label: Luke 24:43
nodes.text: He took them, and ate in front of them.

nodes.label: Luke 24:44
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“This is what I told you, while I was still with you, that all things which are written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms, concerning me must be fulfilled.”

nodes.label: Luke 24:45
nodes.text: Then he opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures.

nodes.label: Luke 24:46
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Thus it is written, and thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead the third day,

nodes.label: Luke 24:47
nodes.text: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all the nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Luke 24:48
nodes.text: You are witnesses of these things.

nodes.label: Luke 24:49
nodes.text: Behold, I send out the promise of my Father on you. But wait in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.”

variants.reading: καθίσατε ἐν τῇ πόλει, 'stay in the city' (Alexandrian) against 'stay in the city of Jerusalem' (Byz)
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': Alexandrian text-type (WH 1881, Tischendorf 8th, Nestle 1904) against Byz.

nodes.label: Luke 24:50
nodes.text: He led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them.

variants.reading: ἕως πρὸς Βηθανίαν, 'as far as the vicinity of Bethany' (Alexandrian) for ἔξω ἕως εἰς Βηθανίαν, 'out as far as to Bethany' (Byz)
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': Alexandrian text-type against Byz (Stephanus TR 1550, Scrivener 1894, RP 2005).

nodes.label: Luke 24:51
nodes.text: While he blessed them, he withdrew from them, and was carried up into heaven.

variants.reading: 'and was carried up into heaven' (καὶ ἀνεφέρετο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': omitted by א* (Sinaiticus original hand), D (Codex Bezae), it a, b, d, e, ff2, l; hiatus in r1, syr s, syr cur, geo 1.

nodes.label: Luke 24:52
nodes.text: They worshiped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,

variants.reading: 'worshiping him' (προσκυνήσαντες αὐτόν) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': omitted by D, it a, b, d, e, ff2, l (hiatus in r1), syr s, syr cur, geo 2.

nodes.label: Luke 24:53
nodes.text: and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

variants.reading: αἰνοῦντες τὸν θεόν, 'praising God' (Western text-type) for 'blessing God'
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': εὐλογοῦντες τὸν θεόν ('blessing God') is the Alexandrian reading of WH 1881, NA27/UBS4 and Nestle 1904; αἰνοῦντες ('praising') is the Western text-type. The WEB prints both: 'praising and blessing God'.

nodes.label: Mark 1:1
nodes.text: The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

variants.reading: Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ('of Jesus Christ') - 'Son of God' absent
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ('of Jesus Christ') in א* (Sinaiticus original hand) Θ 28 530 582* and others, against Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ υἱοῦ θεοῦ ('of Jesus Christ son of God') in B D L W (the NA text). Vaticanus includes 'Son of God'; only Sinaiticus's original hand omits it.

nodes.label: Mark 1:2
nodes.text:
As it is written in the prophets,
“Behold, I send my messenger before your face,
who will prepare your way before you:

variants.reading: ἐν τοῖς προφήταις ('in the prophets')
variants.note: The fetched article lists ἐν τοῖς προφήταις ('in the prophets') in A E F G H K P W (Codex Washingtonianus) f13 and the Byzantine text - the Textus Receptus reading. The Alexandrian reading ἐν τῷ Ἠσαἲᾳ τῷ προφήτῃ ('in Isaiah the prophet') is carried by א (Sinaiticus) and B (Vaticanus).

nodes.label: Mark 1:3
nodes.text:
the voice of one crying in the wilderness,
‘Make ready the way of the Lord!
Make his paths straight!’”

nodes.label: Mark 1:4
nodes.text: John came baptizing in the wilderness and preaching the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.

nodes.label: Mark 1:5
nodes.text: All the country of Judea and all those of Jerusalem went out to him. They were baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.

nodes.label: Mark 1:6
nodes.text: John was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.

nodes.label: Mark 1:7
nodes.text: He preached, saying, “After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and loosen.

nodes.label: Mark 1:8
nodes.text: I baptized you in water, but he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”

nodes.label: Mark 1:9
nodes.text: In those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan.

nodes.label: Mark 1:10
nodes.text: Immediately coming up from the water, he saw the heavens parting, and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.

nodes.label: Mark 1:11
nodes.text: A voice came out of the sky, “You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

nodes.label: Mark 1:12
nodes.text: Immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.

nodes.label: Mark 1:13
nodes.text: He was there in the wilderness forty days tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals; and the angels were serving him.

nodes.label: Mark 1:14
nodes.text: Now after John was taken into custody, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Good News of God’s Kingdom,

nodes.label: Mark 1:15
nodes.text:
and saying,
“The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”

nodes.label: Mark 1:16
nodes.text: Passing along by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.

nodes.label: Mark 1:17
nodes.text:
Jesus said to them,
“Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”

nodes.label: Mark 1:18
nodes.text: Immediately they left their nets, and followed him.

nodes.label: Mark 1:19
nodes.text: Going on a little further from there, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother, who were also in the boat mending the nets.

nodes.label: Mark 1:20
nodes.text: Immediately he called them, and they left their father, Zebedee, in the boat with the hired servants, and went after him.

nodes.label: Mark 1:21
nodes.text: They went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.

nodes.label: Mark 1:22
nodes.text: They were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as having authority, and not as the scribes.

nodes.label: Mark 1:23
nodes.text: Immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,

nodes.label: Mark 1:24
nodes.text: saying, “Ha! What do we have to do with you, Jesus, you Nazarene? Have you come to destroy us? I know you who you are: the Holy One of God!”

nodes.label: Mark 1:25
nodes.text:
Jesus rebuked him, saying,
“Be quiet, and come out of him!”

nodes.label: Mark 1:26
nodes.text: The unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying with a loud voice, came out of him.

nodes.label: Mark 1:27
nodes.text: They were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, “What is this? A new teaching? For with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him!”

nodes.label: Mark 1:28
nodes.text: The report of him went out immediately everywhere into all the region of Galilee and its surrounding area.

nodes.label: Mark 1:29
nodes.text: Immediately, when they had come out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.

nodes.label: Mark 1:30
nodes.text: Now Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick with a fever, and immediately they told him about her.

nodes.label: Mark 1:31
nodes.text: He came and took her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she served them.

nodes.label: Mark 1:32
nodes.text: At evening, when the sun had set, they brought to him all who were sick, and those who were possessed by demons.

nodes.label: Mark 1:33
nodes.text: All the city was gathered together at the door.

nodes.label: Mark 1:34
nodes.text: He healed many who were sick with various diseases, and cast out many demons. He didn’t allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.

nodes.label: Mark 1:35
nodes.text: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, he rose up and went out, and departed into a deserted place, and prayed there.

nodes.label: Mark 1:36
nodes.text: Simon and those who were with him followed after him;

nodes.label: Mark 1:37
nodes.text: and they found him, and told him, “Everyone is looking for you.”

nodes.label: Mark 1:38
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Let’s go elsewhere into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because I came out for this reason.”

nodes.label: Mark 1:39
nodes.text: He went into their synagogues throughout all Galilee, preaching and casting out demons.

nodes.label: Mark 1:40
nodes.text: A leper came to him, begging him, kneeling down to him, and saying to him, “If you want to, you can make me clean.”

nodes.label: Mark 1:41
nodes.text:
Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him,
“I want to. Be made clean.”

variants.reading: ὀργισθείς ('irritated; angry')
variants.note: The fetched article lists ὀργισθεις ('irritated; angry') in D (Codex Bezae) ita ff2 r1, against σπλαγχνισθεις ('filled with compassion') in all other manuscripts. None of the D witnesses is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

nodes.label: Mark 1:42
nodes.text: When he had said this, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was made clean.

nodes.label: Mark 1:43
nodes.text: He strictly warned him, and immediately sent him out,

nodes.label: Mark 1:44
nodes.text:
and said to him,
“See you say nothing to anybody, but go show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing the things which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”

nodes.label: Mark 1:45
nodes.text: But he went out, and began to proclaim it much, and to spread about the matter, so that Jesus could no more openly enter into a city, but was outside in desert places: and they came to him from everywhere.

nodes.label: Mark 2:1
nodes.text: When he entered again into Capernaum after some days, it was heard that he was in the house.

nodes.label: Mark 2:2
nodes.text: Immediately many were gathered together, so that there was no more room, not even around the door; and he spoke the word to them.

nodes.label: Mark 2:3
nodes.text: Four people came, carrying a paralytic to him.

nodes.label: Mark 2:4
nodes.text: When they could not come near to him for the crowd, they removed the roof where he was. When they had broken it up, they let down the mat that the paralytic was lying on.

nodes.label: Mark 2:5
nodes.text:
Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic,
“Son, your sins are forgiven you.”

nodes.label: Mark 2:6
nodes.text: But there were some of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,

nodes.label: Mark 2:7
nodes.text: “Why does this man speak blasphemies like that? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”

nodes.label: Mark 2:8
nodes.text:
Immediately Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, said to them,
“Why do you reason these things in your hearts?

nodes.label: Mark 2:9
nodes.text: Which is easier, to tell the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Arise, and take up your bed, and walk?’

nodes.label: Mark 2:10
nodes.text: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—

nodes.label: Mark 2:11
nodes.text: “I tell you, arise, take up your mat, and go to your house.”

nodes.label: Mark 2:12
nodes.text: He arose, and immediately took up the mat, and went out in front of them all; so that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, “We never saw anything like this!”

nodes.label: Mark 2:13
nodes.text: He went out again by the seaside. All the multitude came to him, and he taught them.

nodes.label: Mark 2:14
nodes.text:
As he passed by, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax office, and he said to him,
“Follow me.” And he arose and followed him.

nodes.label: Mark 2:15
nodes.text: He was reclining at the table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they followed him.

nodes.label: Mark 2:16
nodes.text: The scribes and the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, said to his disciples, “Why is it that he eats and drinks with tax collectors and sinners?”

nodes.label: Mark 2:17
nodes.text:
When Jesus heard it, he said to them,
“Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

nodes.label: Mark 2:18
nodes.text: John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, and they came and asked him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples don’t fast?”

nodes.label: Mark 2:19
nodes.text:
Jesus said to them,
“Can the groomsmen fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they can’t fast.

nodes.label: Mark 2:20
nodes.text: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then will they fast in that day.

nodes.label: Mark 2:21
nodes.text: No one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or else the patch shrinks and the new tears away from the old, and a worse hole is made.

nodes.label: Mark 2:22
nodes.text: No one puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and the wine pours out, and the skins will be destroyed; but they put new wine into fresh wineskins.”

nodes.label: Mark 2:23
nodes.text: He was going on the Sabbath day through the grain fields, and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of grain.

nodes.label: Mark 2:24
nodes.text: The Pharisees said to him, “Behold, why do they do that which is not lawful on the Sabbath day?”

nodes.label: Mark 2:25
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Did you never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry—he, and those who were with him?

nodes.label: Mark 2:26
nodes.text: How he entered into God’s house at the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the show bread, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave also to those who were with him?”

variants.reading: ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθαρ τοῦ ἱερέως ('when Abiatar was priest', without 'high')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθαρ τοῦ ἱερέως in Δ (Codex Sangallensis) and itf - neither is a manuscript node of this graph.

variants.reading: the phrase 'when Abiatar was high priest' omitted
variants.note: The fetched article lists 'phrase is omitted by manuscripts D W 1009. 1546' with Old Latin and Old Syriac support; W (Codex Washingtonianus) is a manuscript node of this graph, D (Codex Bezae) is not. The main reading ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθαρ ἀρχιερέως ('when Abiatar was high priest') is carried by א A B K L and the Byzantine text.

nodes.label: Mark 2:27
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.

nodes.label: Mark 2:28
nodes.text: Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”

nodes.label: Mark 3:1
nodes.text: He entered again into the synagogue, and there was a man there who had his hand withered.

nodes.label: Mark 3:2
nodes.text: They watched him, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath day, that they might accuse him.

nodes.label: Mark 3:3
nodes.text: He said to the man who had his hand withered, “Stand up.”

nodes.label: Mark 3:4
nodes.text: He said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath day to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?” But they were silent.

nodes.label: Mark 3:5
nodes.text: When he had looked around at them with anger, being grieved at the hardening of their hearts, he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored as healthy as the other.

nodes.label: Mark 3:6
nodes.text: The Pharisees went out, and immediately conspired with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

nodes.label: Mark 3:7
nodes.text: Jesus withdrew to the sea with his disciples, and a great multitude followed him from Galilee, from Judea,

nodes.label: Mark 3:8
nodes.text: from Jerusalem, from Idumaea, beyond the Jordan, and those from around Tyre and Sidon. A great multitude, hearing what great things he did, came to him.

nodes.label: Mark 3:9
nodes.text: He spoke to his disciples that a little boat should stay near him because of the crowd, so that they wouldn’t press on him.

nodes.label: Mark 3:10
nodes.text: For he had healed many, so that as many as had diseases pressed on him that they might touch him.

nodes.label: Mark 3:11
nodes.text: The unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, “You are the Son of God!”

nodes.label: Mark 3:12
nodes.text: He sternly warned them that they should not make him known.

nodes.label: Mark 3:13
nodes.text: He went up into the mountain, and called to himself those whom he wanted, and they went to him.

nodes.label: Mark 3:14
nodes.text: He appointed twelve, that they might be with him, and that he might send them out to preach,

nodes.label: Mark 3:15
nodes.text: and to have authority to heal sicknesses and to cast out demons:

nodes.label: Mark 3:16
nodes.text: Simon (to whom he gave the name Peter);

nodes.label: Mark 3:17
nodes.text: James the son of Zebedee; and John, the brother of James, (whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder);

nodes.label: Mark 3:18
nodes.text: Andrew; Philip; Bartholomew; Matthew; Thomas; James, the son of Alphaeus; Thaddaeus; Simon the Zealot;

nodes.label: Mark 3:19
nodes.text: and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. Then he came into a house.

nodes.label: Mark 3:20
nodes.text: The multitude came together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.

nodes.label: Mark 3:21
nodes.text: When his friends heard it, they went out to seize him: for they said, “He is insane.”

nodes.label: Mark 3:22
nodes.text: The scribes who came down from Jerusalem said, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the prince of the demons he casts out the demons.”

nodes.label: Mark 3:23
nodes.text: He summoned them, and said to them in parables, “How can Satan cast out Satan?

nodes.label: Mark 3:24
nodes.text: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

nodes.label: Mark 3:25
nodes.text: If a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.

nodes.label: Mark 3:26
nodes.text: If Satan has risen up against himself, and is divided, he can’t stand, but has an end.

nodes.label: Mark 3:27
nodes.text: But no one can enter into the house of the strong man to plunder, unless he first binds the strong man; and then he will plunder his house.

nodes.label: Mark 3:28
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, all sins of the descendants of man will be forgiven, including their blasphemies with which they may blaspheme;

nodes.label: Mark 3:29
nodes.text: but whoever may blaspheme against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is subject to eternal condemnation.”

nodes.label: Mark 3:30
nodes.text: —because they said, “He has an unclean spirit.”

nodes.label: Mark 3:31
nodes.text: His mother and his brothers came, and standing outside, they sent to him, calling him.

nodes.label: Mark 3:32
nodes.text: A multitude was sitting around him, and they told him, “Behold, your mother, your brothers, and your sisters are outside looking for you.”

nodes.label: Mark 3:33
nodes.text: He answered them, “Who are my mother and my brothers?”

nodes.label: Mark 3:34
nodes.text: Looking around at those who sat around him, he said, “Behold, my mother and my brothers!

nodes.label: Mark 3:35
nodes.text: For whoever does the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.”

nodes.label: Mark 4:1
nodes.text: Again he began to teach by the seaside. A great multitude was gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat in the sea, and sat down. All the multitude were on the land by the sea.

nodes.label: Mark 4:2
nodes.text: He taught them many things in parables, and told them in his teaching,

nodes.label: Mark 4:3
nodes.text: “Listen! Behold, the farmer went out to sow,

nodes.label: Mark 4:4
nodes.text: and as he sowed, some seed fell by the road, and the birds came and devoured it.

nodes.label: Mark 4:5
nodes.text: Others fell on the rocky ground, where it had little soil, and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.

nodes.label: Mark 4:6
nodes.text: When the sun had risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.

nodes.label: Mark 4:7
nodes.text: Others fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.

nodes.label: Mark 4:8
nodes.text: Others fell into the good ground, and yielded fruit, growing up and increasing. Some produced thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times as much.”

nodes.label: Mark 4:9
nodes.text: He said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”

nodes.label: Mark 4:10
nodes.text: When he was alone, those who were around him with the twelve asked him about the parables.

nodes.label: Mark 4:11
nodes.text: He said to them, “To you is given the mystery of God’s Kingdom, but to those who are outside, all things are done in parables,

nodes.label: Mark 4:12
nodes.text: that ‘seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest perhaps they should turn again, and their sins should be forgiven them.’”

nodes.label: Mark 4:13
nodes.text: He said to them, “Don’t you understand this parable? How will you understand all of the parables?

nodes.label: Mark 4:14
nodes.text: The farmer sows the word.

nodes.label: Mark 4:15
nodes.text: The ones by the road are the ones where the word is sown; and when they have heard, immediately Satan comes, and takes away the word which has been sown in them.

nodes.label: Mark 4:16
nodes.text: These in the same way are those who are sown on the rocky places, who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with joy.

nodes.label: Mark 4:17
nodes.text: They have no root in themselves, but are short-lived. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they stumble.

nodes.label: Mark 4:18
nodes.text: Others are those who are sown among the thorns. These are those who have heard the word,

nodes.label: Mark 4:19
nodes.text: and the cares of this age, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

variants.reading: omit και αι περι τα λοιπα επιθυμιαι ('and the desire for other things')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' (Mark 4 section) lists the omission for D, (Theta), W (Codex Washingtonianus), f1, 28, (565, 700) and it; only W is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by carries W alone. WEB follows the fuller reading.

nodes.label: Mark 4:20
nodes.text: Those which were sown on the good ground are those who hear the word, and accept it, and bear fruit, some thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times.”

nodes.label: Mark 4:21
nodes.text: He said to them, “Is the lamp brought to be put under a basket or under a bed? Isn’t it put on a stand?

nodes.label: Mark 4:22
nodes.text: For there is nothing hidden, except that it should be made known; neither was anything made secret, but that it should come to light.

nodes.label: Mark 4:23
nodes.text: If any man has ears to hear, let him hear.”

nodes.label: Mark 4:24
nodes.text: He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you, and more will be given to you who hear.

variants.reading: καὶ προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν ('and more will be given to you'), without τοῖς ἀκούουσιν ('to you who hear')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' (Mark 4 section) lists καὶ προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν for א (Sinaiticus), B (Vaticanus), C, L, Delta, 700, 892; the longer τοῖς ἀκούουσιν for A, K, Pi, 0107, Byz; D, W, 565, 3 omit. The WEB's 'and more will be given to you who hear' follows the longer reading.

nodes.label: Mark 4:25
nodes.text: For whoever has, to him will more be given, and he who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.”

nodes.label: Mark 4:26
nodes.text: He said, “God’s Kingdom is as if a man should cast seed on the earth,

nodes.label: Mark 4:27
nodes.text: and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, though he doesn’t know how.

nodes.label: Mark 4:28
nodes.text: For the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.

nodes.label: Mark 4:29
nodes.text: But when the fruit is ripe, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”

nodes.label: Mark 4:30
nodes.text: He said, “How will we liken God’s Kingdom? Or with what parable will we illustrate it?

nodes.label: Mark 4:31
nodes.text: It’s like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth,

nodes.label: Mark 4:32
nodes.text: yet when it is sown, grows up, and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow.”

nodes.label: Mark 4:33
nodes.text: With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.

nodes.label: Mark 4:34
nodes.text: Without a parable he didn’t speak to them; but privately to his own disciples he explained everything.

nodes.label: Mark 4:35
nodes.text: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side.”

nodes.label: Mark 4:36
nodes.text: Leaving the multitude, they took him with them, even as he was, in the boat. Other small boats were also with him.

nodes.label: Mark 4:37
nodes.text: A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filled.

nodes.label: Mark 4:38
nodes.text: He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion, and they woke him up, and told him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”

nodes.label: Mark 4:39
nodes.text: He awoke, and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

nodes.label: Mark 4:40
nodes.text: He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”

nodes.label: Mark 4:41
nodes.text: They were greatly afraid, and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

nodes.label: Mark 5:1
nodes.text: They came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.

variants.reading: the country of the Gerasenes (την χωραν των Γερασηνων)
variants.note: The fetched Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac article gives Mark 5:1 as 'the region of the Gerasenes' and adds 'Other textual variations include "Gadarenes" and "Gergesenes"'; the WEB text reads 'Gadarenes'.

nodes.label: Mark 5:2
nodes.text: When he had come out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met him out of the tombs.

nodes.label: Mark 5:3
nodes.text: He lived in the tombs. Nobody could bind him any more, not even with chains,

nodes.label: Mark 5:4
nodes.text: because he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the fetters broken in pieces. Nobody had the strength to tame him.

nodes.label: Mark 5:5
nodes.text: Always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.

nodes.label: Mark 5:6
nodes.text: When he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him,

nodes.label: Mark 5:7
nodes.text: and crying out with a loud voice, he said, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, don’t torment me.”

nodes.label: Mark 5:8
nodes.text: For he said to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”

nodes.label: Mark 5:9
nodes.text: He asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”

variants.reading: λεγιων ονομα μοι ('Legion is my name to me')
variants.note: Codex Alexandrinus, Washingtonianus, Koridethi, family 1, family 13 and the Byzantine text read λεγεων (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark, Mark 5:9).

nodes.label: Mark 5:10
nodes.text: He begged him much that he would not send them away out of the country.

nodes.label: Mark 5:11
nodes.text: Now on the mountainside there was a great herd of pigs feeding.

nodes.label: Mark 5:12
nodes.text: All the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, that we may enter into them.”

nodes.label: Mark 5:13
nodes.text: At once Jesus gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered into the pigs. The herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they were drowned in the sea.

nodes.label: Mark 5:14
nodes.text: Those who fed them fled, and told it in the city and in the country. The people came to see what it was that had happened.

nodes.label: Mark 5:15
nodes.text: They came to Jesus, and saw him who had been possessed by demons sitting, clothed, and in his right mind, even him who had the legion; and they were afraid.

nodes.label: Mark 5:16
nodes.text: Those who saw it declared to them what happened to him who was possessed by demons, and about the pigs.

nodes.label: Mark 5:17
nodes.text: They began to beg him to depart from their region.

nodes.label: Mark 5:18
nodes.text: As he was entering into the boat, he who had been possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.

nodes.label: Mark 5:19
nodes.text: He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.”

nodes.label: Mark 5:20
nodes.text: He went his way, and began to proclaim in Decapolis how Jesus had done great things for him, and everyone marveled.

nodes.label: Mark 5:21
nodes.text: When Jesus had crossed back over in the boat to the other side, a great multitude was gathered to him; and he was by the sea.

nodes.label: Mark 5:22
nodes.text: Behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name, came; and seeing him, he fell at his feet,

nodes.label: Mark 5:23
nodes.text: and begged him much, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay your hands on her, that she may be made healthy, and live.”

nodes.label: Mark 5:24
nodes.text: He went with him, and a great multitude followed him, and they pressed upon him on all sides.

nodes.label: Mark 5:25
nodes.text: A certain woman, who had an issue of blood for twelve years,

nodes.label: Mark 5:26
nodes.text: and had suffered many things by many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was no better, but rather grew worse,

nodes.label: Mark 5:27
nodes.text: having heard the things concerning Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd, and touched his clothes.

nodes.label: Mark 5:28
nodes.text: For she said, “If I just touch his clothes, I will be made well.”

nodes.label: Mark 5:29
nodes.text: Immediately the flow of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.

nodes.label: Mark 5:30
nodes.text: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself that the power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd, and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”

nodes.label: Mark 5:31
nodes.text: His disciples said to him, “You see the multitude pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”

nodes.label: Mark 5:32
nodes.text: He looked around to see her who had done this thing.

nodes.label: Mark 5:33
nodes.text: But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had been done to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.

nodes.label: Mark 5:34
nodes.text: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”

nodes.label: Mark 5:35
nodes.text: While he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue ruler’s house saying, “Your daughter is dead. Why bother the Teacher any more?”

nodes.label: Mark 5:36
nodes.text: But Jesus, when he heard the message spoken, immediately said to the ruler of the synagogue, “Don’t be afraid, only believe.”

nodes.label: Mark 5:37
nodes.text: He allowed no one to follow him, except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.

nodes.label: Mark 5:38
nodes.text: He came to the synagogue ruler’s house, and he saw an uproar, weeping, and great wailing.

nodes.label: Mark 5:39
nodes.text: When he had entered in, he said to them, “Why do you make an uproar and weep? The child is not dead, but is asleep.”

nodes.label: Mark 5:40
nodes.text: They ridiculed him. But he, having put them all out, took the father of the child, her mother, and those who were with him, and went in where the child was lying.

nodes.label: Mark 5:41
nodes.text: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha cumi!” which means, being interpreted, “Girl, I tell you, get up!”

nodes.label: Mark 5:42
nodes.text: Immediately the girl rose up and walked, for she was twelve years old. They were amazed with great amazement.

nodes.label: Mark 5:43
nodes.text: He strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and commanded that something should be given to her to eat.

nodes.label: Mark 6:1
nodes.text: He went out from there. He came into his own country, and his disciples followed him.

nodes.label: Mark 6:2
nodes.text: When the Sabbath had come, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many hearing him were astonished, saying, “Where did this man get these things?” and, “What is the wisdom that is given to this man, that such mighty works come about by his hands?

nodes.label: Mark 6:3
nodes.text: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary, and brother of James, Joses, Judah, and Simon? Aren’t his sisters here with us?” They were offended at him.

variants.reading: και ο αδελφος Ἰακώβου ('and the brother of James')
variants.note: Codex Bezae and Regius read the same; minuscules 565, 700 and 892c omit και ('the brother of James') (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark, Mark 6:3).

variants.reading: και αδελφος Ἰακώβου ('and brother of James')
variants.note: Also C, Delta, 579, 1241, 1424; the Byzantine text reads και ο αδελφος Ἰακώβου (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark, Mark 6:3).

nodes.label: Mark 6:4
nodes.text: Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”

nodes.label: Mark 6:5
nodes.text: He could do no mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people, and healed them.

nodes.label: Mark 6:6
nodes.text: He marveled because of their unbelief. He went around the villages teaching.

nodes.label: Mark 6:7
nodes.text: He called to himself the twelve, and began to send them out two by two; and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits.

nodes.label: Mark 6:8
nodes.text: He commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, except a staff only: no bread, no wallet, no money in their purse,

nodes.label: Mark 6:9
nodes.text: but to wear sandals, and not put on two tunics.

nodes.label: Mark 6:10
nodes.text: He said to them, “Wherever you enter into a house, stay there until you depart from there.

nodes.label: Mark 6:11
nodes.text: Whoever will not receive you nor hear you, as you depart from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony against them. Assuredly, I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!”

variants.reading: the sentence 'Assuredly, I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!' is absent
variants.note: It does not appear in the majority of important codices, such as Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Vaticanus, Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus, Codex Bezae, Codex Regius, Codex Washingtonianus, Codex Sangallensis, Codex Koridethi, and Latin, Sahidic, and some Syriac and Bohairic manuscripts (Wikipedia, List of omitted Bible verses, Mark 6:11 (b)); the WEB keeps it.

nodes.label: Mark 6:12
nodes.text: They went out and preached that people should repent.

nodes.label: Mark 6:13
nodes.text: They cast out many demons, and anointed many with oil who were sick, and healed them.

nodes.label: Mark 6:14
nodes.text: King Herod heard this, for his name had become known, and he said, “John the Baptizer has risen from the dead, and therefore these powers are at work in him.”

nodes.label: Mark 6:15
nodes.text: But others said, “He is Elijah.” Others said, “He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.”

nodes.label: Mark 6:16
nodes.text: But Herod, when he heard this, said, “This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”

nodes.label: Mark 6:17
nodes.text: For Herod himself had sent out and arrested John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, for he had married her.

nodes.label: Mark 6:18
nodes.text: For John said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”

nodes.label: Mark 6:19
nodes.text: Herodias set herself against him, and desired to kill him, but she couldn’t,

nodes.label: Mark 6:20
nodes.text: for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many things, and he heard him gladly.

nodes.label: Mark 6:21
nodes.text: Then a convenient day came, that Herod on his birthday made a supper for his nobles, the high officers, and the chief men of Galilee.

nodes.label: Mark 6:22
nodes.text: When the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those sitting with him. The king said to the young lady, “Ask me whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”

nodes.label: Mark 6:23
nodes.text: He swore to her, “Whatever you shall ask of me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom.”

nodes.label: Mark 6:24
nodes.text: She went out, and said to her mother, “What shall I ask?” She said, “The head of John the Baptizer.”

nodes.label: Mark 6:25
nodes.text: She came in immediately with haste to the king, and asked, “I want you to give me right now the head of John the Baptizer on a platter.”

nodes.label: Mark 6:26
nodes.text: The king was exceedingly sorry, but for the sake of his oaths, and of his dinner guests, he didn’t wish to refuse her.

nodes.label: Mark 6:27
nodes.text: Immediately the king sent out a soldier of his guard, and commanded to bring John’s head, and he went and beheaded him in the prison,

nodes.label: Mark 6:28
nodes.text: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the young lady; and the young lady gave it to her mother.

nodes.label: Mark 6:29
nodes.text: When his disciples heard this, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.

nodes.label: Mark 6:30
nodes.text: The apostles gathered themselves together to Jesus, and they told him all things, whatever they had done, and whatever they had taught.

nodes.label: Mark 6:31
nodes.text: He said to them, “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.

nodes.label: Mark 6:32
nodes.text: They went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.

nodes.label: Mark 6:33
nodes.text: They saw them going, and many recognized him and ran there on foot from all the cities. They arrived before them and came together to him.

nodes.label: Mark 6:34
nodes.text: Jesus came out, saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things.

nodes.label: Mark 6:35
nodes.text: When it was late in the day, his disciples came to him, and said, “This place is deserted, and it is late in the day.

nodes.label: Mark 6:36
nodes.text: Send them away, that they may go into the surrounding country and villages, and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat.”

nodes.label: Mark 6:37
nodes.text: But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread, and give them something to eat?”

nodes.label: Mark 6:38
nodes.text: He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go see.” When they knew, they said, “Five, and two fish.”
