nodes.label: Mark 6:39
nodes.text: He commanded them that everyone should sit down in groups on the green grass.

nodes.label: Mark 6:40
nodes.text: They sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties.

variants.reading: κατα εκατον και κατα πεντηκοντα ('by hundreds and by fifties') omitted
variants.note: P45, sy vf and sy h(ms) omit; included by Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, D, L, Theta and most manuscripts (Wikipedia, Papyrus 45, Some notable readings, Mark 6:40).

nodes.label: Mark 6:41
nodes.text: He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he blessed and broke the loaves, and he gave to his disciples to set before them, and he divided the two fish among them all.

nodes.label: Mark 6:42
nodes.text: They all ate, and were filled.

nodes.label: Mark 6:43
nodes.text: They took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and also of the fish.

nodes.label: Mark 6:44
nodes.text: Those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.

variants.reading: τους αρτους ('the loaves') omitted
variants.note: P45, Sinaiticus, D, W, Theta, family 1, family 13 and others omit; included by A, B, L, 33 and the Byzantine text (Wikipedia, Papyrus 45, Some notable readings, Mark 6:44).

nodes.label: Mark 6:45
nodes.text: Immediately he made his disciples get into the boat, and to go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he himself sent the multitude away.

variants.reading: εις το περαν ('to the other side') omitted
variants.note: P45, W, family 1, 118, it q and syr s omit; included by the majority of manuscripts (Wikipedia, Papyrus 45, Some notable readings, Mark 6:45).

nodes.label: Mark 6:46
nodes.text: After he had taken leave of them, he went up the mountain to pray.

nodes.label: Mark 6:47
nodes.text: When evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.

nodes.label: Mark 6:48
nodes.text: Seeing them distressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary to them, about the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea, and he would have passed by them,

nodes.label: Mark 6:49
nodes.text: but they, when they saw him walking on the sea, supposed that it was a ghost, and cried out;

nodes.label: Mark 6:50
nodes.text: for they all saw him, and were troubled. But he immediately spoke with them, and said to them, “Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.”

nodes.label: Mark 6:51
nodes.text: He got into the boat with them; and the wind ceased, and they were very amazed among themselves, and marveled;

nodes.label: Mark 6:52
nodes.text: for they hadn’t understood about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.

nodes.label: Mark 6:53
nodes.text: When they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret, and moored to the shore.

nodes.label: Mark 6:54
nodes.text: When they had come out of the boat, immediately the people recognized him,

nodes.label: Mark 6:55
nodes.text: and ran around that whole region, and began to bring those who were sick, on their mats, to where they heard he was.

nodes.label: Mark 6:56
nodes.text: Wherever he entered, into villages, or into cities, or into the country, they laid the sick in the marketplaces, and begged him that they might just touch the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched him were made well.

nodes.label: Mark 7:1
nodes.text: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes gathered together to him, having come from Jerusalem.

nodes.label: Mark 7:2
nodes.text: Now when they saw some of his disciples eating bread with defiled, that is unwashed, hands, they found fault.

nodes.label: Mark 7:3
nodes.text: (For the Pharisees and all the Jews, don’t eat unless they wash their hands and forearms, holding to the tradition of the elders.

variants.reading: πυγμῃ ('with the fist') – A B D K L X Θ Π; πυκνα ('often') – א W vg; omitted – Δ syr-s sa
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists this variant under 'Mark 7:2' (some editions number the verse differently). The WEB reads 'wash their hands and forearms'.

nodes.label: Mark 7:4
nodes.text: They don’t eat when they come from the marketplace unless they bathe themselves, and there are many other things, which they have received to hold to: washings of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and couches.)

variants.reading: 'and couches' (κλινῶν) omitted
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Mark 7' article records that some manuscripts and accordingly some English translations add or omit 'couches', 'couches for meals on which diseased persons (lepers, etc.) may have lain'. The listed witnesses are not manuscript nodes of this graph.

nodes.label: Mark 7:5
nodes.text: The Pharisees and the scribes asked him, “Why don’t your disciples walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with unwashed hands?”

nodes.label: Mark 7:6
nodes.text: He answered them, “Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written, ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

nodes.label: Mark 7:7
nodes.text: But they worship me in vain, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.’

nodes.label: Mark 7:8
nodes.text: “For you set aside the commandment of God, and hold tightly to the tradition of men—the washing of pitchers and cups, and you do many other such things.”

nodes.label: Mark 7:9
nodes.text: He said to them, “Full well do you reject the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.

nodes.label: Mark 7:10
nodes.text: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother;’ and, ‘He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’

nodes.label: Mark 7:11
nodes.text: But you say, ‘If a man tells his father or his mother, “Whatever profit you might have received from me is Corban, that is to say, given to God”;’

nodes.label: Mark 7:12
nodes.text: then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,

nodes.label: Mark 7:13
nodes.text: making void the word of God by your tradition, which you have handed down. You do many things like this.”

nodes.label: Mark 7:14
nodes.text: He called all the multitude to himself, and said to them, “Hear me, all of you, and understand.

nodes.label: Mark 7:15
nodes.text: There is nothing from outside of the man, that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.

nodes.label: Mark 7:16
nodes.text: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!”

variants.reading: the whole verse ('If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!') is omitted
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' records 'verse is omitted by א Β L Δ 28' for Mark 7:16. Sinaiticus and Vaticanus therefore get no preserves edge for this verse.

nodes.label: Mark 7:17
nodes.text: When he had entered into a house away from the multitude, his disciples asked him about the parable.

nodes.label: Mark 7:18
nodes.text: He said to them, “Are you also without understanding? Don’t you perceive that whatever goes into the man from outside can’t defile him,

nodes.label: Mark 7:19
nodes.text: because it doesn’t go into his heart, but into his stomach, then into the latrine, thus purifying all foods?”

nodes.label: Mark 7:20
nodes.text: He said, “That which proceeds out of the man, that defiles the man.

nodes.label: Mark 7:21
nodes.text: For from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts,

nodes.label: Mark 7:22
nodes.text: covetings, wickedness, deceit, lustful desires, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness.

nodes.label: Mark 7:23
nodes.text: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”

nodes.label: Mark 7:24
nodes.text: From there he arose, and went away into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He entered into a house, and didn’t want anyone to know it, but he couldn’t escape notice.

nodes.label: Mark 7:25
nodes.text: For a woman, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell down at his feet.

nodes.label: Mark 7:26
nodes.text: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. She begged him that he would cast the demon out of her daughter.

nodes.label: Mark 7:27
nodes.text: But Jesus said to her, “Let the children be filled first, for it is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”

nodes.label: Mark 7:28
nodes.text: But she answered him, “Yes, Lord. Yet even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”

nodes.label: Mark 7:29
nodes.text: He said to her, “For this saying, go your way. The demon has gone out of your daughter.”

nodes.label: Mark 7:30
nodes.text: She went away to her house, and found the child having been laid on the bed, with the demon gone out.

nodes.label: Mark 7:31
nodes.text: Again he departed from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and came to the sea of Galilee, through the middle of the region of Decapolis.

nodes.label: Mark 7:32
nodes.text: They brought to him one who was deaf and had an impediment in his speech. They begged him to lay his hand on him.

nodes.label: Mark 7:33
nodes.text: He took him aside from the multitude, privately, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spat, and touched his tongue.

nodes.label: Mark 7:34
nodes.text: Looking up to heaven, he sighed, and said to him, “Ephphatha!” that is, “Be opened!”

nodes.label: Mark 7:35
nodes.text: Immediately his ears were opened, and the impediment of his tongue was released, and he spoke clearly.

nodes.label: Mark 7:36
nodes.text: He commanded them that they should tell no one, but the more he commanded them, so much the more widely they proclaimed it.

nodes.label: Mark 7:37
nodes.text: They were astonished beyond measure, saying, “He has done all things well. He makes even the deaf hear, and the mute speak!”

nodes.label: Mark 8:1
nodes.text: In those days, when there was a very great multitude, and they had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples to himself, and said to them,

nodes.label: Mark 8:2
nodes.text: “I have compassion on the multitude, because they have stayed with me now three days, and have nothing to eat.

nodes.label: Mark 8:3
nodes.text: If I send them away fasting to their home, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come a long way.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:4
nodes.text: His disciples answered him, “From where could one satisfy these people with bread here in a deserted place?”

nodes.label: Mark 8:5
nodes.text: He asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:6
nodes.text: He commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground, and he took the seven loaves. Having given thanks, he broke them, and gave them to his disciples to serve, and they served the multitude.

nodes.label: Mark 8:7
nodes.text: They had a few small fish. Having blessed them, he said to serve these also.

nodes.label: Mark 8:8
nodes.text: They ate, and were filled. They took up seven baskets of broken pieces that were left over.

nodes.label: Mark 8:9
nodes.text: Those who had eaten were about four thousand. Then he sent them away.

nodes.label: Mark 8:10
nodes.text: Immediately he entered into the boat with his disciples, and came into the region of Dalmanutha.

variants.reading: the place name varies: τὰ ὄρη Δαλμανουθά (1071), τὸ ὄρος Δαλμανοῦναι (W), τὰ ὅρια Δαλμανουθά (1241), τὸ ὄρος Μαγεδά (28), τὰ ὅρια Μελεγαδά (D gr), τὰ μέρη Μαγδαλά (Θ, f1, f13, ℓ80), τὰ μέρη Μαγεδά (565)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists these readings for Mark 8:10 against τὰ μέρη Δαλμανουθά (א A B C K L X Δ Π ... Byz). None of the variant witnesses is a manuscript node of this graph.

nodes.label: Mark 8:11
nodes.text: The Pharisees came out and began to question him, seeking from him a sign from heaven, and testing him.

nodes.label: Mark 8:12
nodes.text: He sighed deeply in his spirit, and said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Most certainly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:13
nodes.text: He left them, and again entering into the boat, departed to the other side.

nodes.label: Mark 8:14
nodes.text: They forgot to take bread; and they didn’t have more than one loaf in the boat with them.

nodes.label: Mark 8:15
nodes.text: He warned them, saying, “Take heed: beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:16
nodes.text: They reasoned with one another, saying, “It’s because we have no bread.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:17
nodes.text: Jesus, perceiving it, said to them, “Why do you reason that it’s because you have no bread? Don’t you perceive yet, neither understand? Is your heart still hardened?

nodes.label: Mark 8:18
nodes.text: Having eyes, don’t you see? Having ears, don’t you hear? Don’t you remember?

nodes.label: Mark 8:19
nodes.text: When I broke the five loaves among the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They told him, “Twelve.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:20
nodes.text: “When the seven loaves fed the four thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They told him, “Seven.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:21
nodes.text: He asked them, “Don’t you understand yet?”

nodes.label: Mark 8:22
nodes.text: He came to Bethsaida. They brought a blind man to him, and begged him to touch him.

nodes.label: Mark 8:23
nodes.text: He took hold of the blind man by the hand, and brought him out of the village. When he had spat on his eyes, and laid his hands on him, he asked him if he saw anything.

nodes.label: Mark 8:24
nodes.text: He looked up, and said, “I see men; for I see them like trees walking.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:25
nodes.text: Then again he laid his hands on his eyes. He looked intently, and was restored, and saw everyone clearly.

nodes.label: Mark 8:26
nodes.text: He sent him away to his house, saying, “Don’t enter into the village, nor tell anyone in the village.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:27
nodes.text: Jesus went out, with his disciples, into the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, “Who do men say that I am?”

nodes.label: Mark 8:28
nodes.text: They told him, “John the Baptizer, and others say Elijah, but others: one of the prophets.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:29
nodes.text: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:30
nodes.text: He commanded them that they should tell no one about him.

nodes.label: Mark 8:31
nodes.text: He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.

nodes.label: Mark 8:32
nodes.text: He spoke to them openly. Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.

nodes.label: Mark 8:33
nodes.text: But he, turning around, and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, and said, “Get behind me, Satan! For you have in mind not the things of God, but the things of men.”

nodes.label: Mark 8:34
nodes.text: He called the multitude to himself with his disciples, and said to them, “Whoever wants to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

nodes.label: Mark 8:35
nodes.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever will lose his life for my sake and the sake of the Good News will save it.

nodes.label: Mark 8:36
nodes.text: For what does it profit a man, to gain the whole world, and forfeit his life?

nodes.label: Mark 8:37
nodes.text: For what will a man give in exchange for his life?

nodes.label: Mark 8:38
nodes.text: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him, when he comes in his Father’s glory, with the holy angels.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:1
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste death until they see God’s Kingdom come with power.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:2
nodes.text: After six days Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John, and brought them up onto a high mountain privately by themselves, and he was changed into another form in front of them.

nodes.label: Mark 9:3
nodes.text: His clothing became glistening, exceedingly white, like snow, such as no launderer on earth can whiten them.

nodes.label: Mark 9:4
nodes.text: Elijah and Moses appeared to them, and they were talking with Jesus.

nodes.label: Mark 9:5
nodes.text: Peter answered Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:6
nodes.text: For he didn’t know what to say, for they were very afraid.

nodes.label: Mark 9:7
nodes.text: A cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:8
nodes.text: Suddenly looking around, they saw no one with them any more, except Jesus only.

nodes.label: Mark 9:9
nodes.text: As they were coming down from the mountain, he commanded them that they should tell no one what things they had seen, until after the Son of Man had risen from the dead.

nodes.label: Mark 9:10
nodes.text: They kept this saying to themselves, questioning what the “rising from the dead” meant.

nodes.label: Mark 9:11
nodes.text: They asked him, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

nodes.label: Mark 9:12
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Elijah indeed comes first, and restores all things. How is it written about the Son of Man, that he should suffer many things and be despised?

nodes.label: Mark 9:13
nodes.text: But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they have also done to him whatever they wanted to, even as it is written about him.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:14
nodes.text: Coming to the disciples, he saw a great multitude around them, and scribes questioning them.

nodes.label: Mark 9:15
nodes.text: Immediately all the multitude, when they saw him, were greatly amazed, and running to him, greeted him.

nodes.label: Mark 9:16
nodes.text: He asked the scribes, “What are you asking them?”

nodes.label: Mark 9:17
nodes.text: One of the multitude answered, “Teacher, I brought to you my son, who has a mute spirit;

nodes.label: Mark 9:18
nodes.text: and wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth, and grinds his teeth, and wastes away. I asked your disciples to cast it out, and they weren’t able.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:19
nodes.text: He answered him, “Unbelieving generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to me.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:20
nodes.text: They brought him to him, and when he saw him, immediately the spirit convulsed him, and he fell on the ground, wallowing and foaming at the mouth.

nodes.label: Mark 9:21
nodes.text:
He asked his father,
“How long has it been since this has come to him?”
He said, “From childhood.

nodes.label: Mark 9:22
nodes.text: Often it has cast him both into the fire and into the water, to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us, and help us.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:23
nodes.text: Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:24
nodes.text: Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”

nodes.label: Mark 9:25
nodes.text:
When Jesus saw that a multitude came running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to him,
“You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him, and never enter him again!”

nodes.label: Mark 9:26
nodes.text: After crying out and convulsing him greatly, it came out of him. The boy became like one dead; so much that most of them said, “He is dead.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:27
nodes.text: But Jesus took him by the hand, and raised him up; and he arose.

nodes.label: Mark 9:28
nodes.text: When he had come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why couldn’t we cast it out?”

nodes.label: Mark 9:29
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“This kind can come out by nothing, except by prayer and fasting.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:30
nodes.text: They went out from there, and passed through Galilee. He didn’t want anyone to know it.

nodes.label: Mark 9:31
nodes.text:
For he was teaching his disciples, and said to them,
“The Son of Man is being handed over to the hands of men, and they will kill him; and when he is killed, on the third day he will rise again.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:32
nodes.text: But they didn’t understand the saying, and were afraid to ask him.

nodes.label: Mark 9:33
nodes.text:
He came to Capernaum, and when he was in the house he asked them,
“What were you arguing among yourselves on the way?”

nodes.label: Mark 9:34
nodes.text: But they were silent, for they had disputed one with another on the way about who was the greatest.

nodes.label: Mark 9:35
nodes.text:
He sat down, and called the twelve; and he said to them,
“If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:36
nodes.text: He took a little child, and set him in the middle of them. Taking him in his arms, he said to them,

nodes.label: Mark 9:37
nodes.text: “Whoever receives one such little child in my name, receives me, and whoever receives me, doesn’t receive me, but him who sent me.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:38
nodes.text: John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone who doesn’t follow us casting out demons in your name; and we forbade him, because he doesn’t follow us.”

nodes.label: Mark 9:39
nodes.text: But Jesus said, “Don’t forbid him, for there is no one who will do a mighty work in my name, and be able quickly to speak evil of me.

nodes.label: Mark 9:40
nodes.text: For whoever is not against us is on our side.

nodes.label: Mark 9:41
nodes.text: For whoever will give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because you are Christ’s, most certainly I tell you, he will in no way lose his reward.

nodes.label: Mark 9:42
nodes.text: Whoever will cause one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if he were thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around his neck.

nodes.label: Mark 9:43
nodes.text:
If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life maimed, rather than having your two hands to go into Gehenna,

into the unquenchable fire,

nodes.label: Mark 9:44
nodes.text: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’

variants.reading: the verse is absent (the refrain 'where their worm doesn't die, and the fire is not quenched' is not printed)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'List of omitted Bible verses' records Mark 9:44 and 9:46 as 'both lacking in Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Vaticanus, Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus, Codex Regius, Codex Washingtonianus, Family 1, and some manuscripts of the ancient versions'; they duplicate 9:48, which remains. The UBS text assigns the omission a confidence rating of A. WEB prints the verses; no preserves edge from Sinaiticus or Vaticanus is added for them.

nodes.label: Mark 9:45
nodes.text:
If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life lame, rather than having your two feet to be cast into Gehenna,

into the fire that will never be quenched—

nodes.label: Mark 9:46
nodes.text: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’

variants.reading: the verse is absent (the refrain 'where their worm doesn't die, and the fire is not quenched' is not printed)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'List of omitted Bible verses' records Mark 9:44 and 9:46 as 'both lacking in Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Vaticanus, Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus, Codex Regius, Codex Washingtonianus, Family 1, and some manuscripts of the ancient versions'; they duplicate 9:48, which remains. The UBS text assigns the omission a confidence rating of A. WEB prints the verses; no preserves edge from Sinaiticus or Vaticanus is added for them.

nodes.label: Mark 9:47
nodes.text:
If your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out. It is better for you to enter into God’s Kingdom with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna
of fire,

nodes.label: Mark 9:48
nodes.text: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’

nodes.label: Mark 9:49
nodes.text: For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt.

variants.reading: πας γαρ πυρι αλισθησεται ('everyone will be salted with fire'), without the sacrifice clause
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' (its Mark 9 section lists only 9:49) gives πας γαρ πυρι αλισθησεται for (א εν πυρι) B L W Δ f1 f13 28 565 700 ℓ260 syrs sa - Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Washingtonianus are manuscript nodes of this graph. WEB prints the fuller reading 'everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt' (the A K Π reading).

variants.reading: πασα γαρ θυσια αλι αλισθησεται ('every sacrifice shall be salted with salt'), without the fire clause
variants.note: The article lists πασα γαρ θυσια αλι αλισθησεται for D (Codex Bezae) and the Old Latin - neither is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

nodes.label: Mark 9:50
nodes.text: Salt is good, but if the salt has lost its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:1
nodes.text: He arose from there and came into the borders of Judea and beyond the Jordan. Multitudes came together to him again. As he usually did, he was again teaching them.

variants.reading: εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας διὰ τοῦ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου ('into the region of Judea through the beyond-Jordan', Byzantine)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists the Alexandrian reading εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου ('and beyond the Jordan') for the Westcott-Hort, NA27/UBS4, Tischendorf and Nestle texts against διὰ τοῦ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου in the Byzantine text (Stephanus, Scrivener, RP). The named witnesses are printed editions and text-types, not manuscript nodes of this graph, so attested_by is empty. WEB follows the 'and beyond the Jordan' wording.

nodes.label: Mark 10:2
nodes.text: Pharisees came to him testing him, and asked him, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?”

variants.reading: the verse is omitted
variants.note: The fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists the omission of Mark 10:2 by Codex Bezae (D) and Old Latin a, b, d, k, r and the Syriac sinaitic palimpsest - none of these is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty. WEB prints the verse.

nodes.label: Mark 10:3
nodes.text: He answered, “What did Moses command you?”

nodes.label: Mark 10:4
nodes.text: They said, “Moses allowed a certificate of divorce to be written, and to divorce her.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:5
nodes.text:
But Jesus said to them,
“For your hardness of heart, he wrote you this commandment.

nodes.label: Mark 10:6
nodes.text: But from the beginning of the creation, God made them male and female.

nodes.label: Mark 10:7
nodes.text: For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and will join to his wife,

nodes.label: Mark 10:8
nodes.text:
and the two will become one flesh,
so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.

nodes.label: Mark 10:9
nodes.text: What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:10
nodes.text: In the house, his disciples asked him again about the same matter.

nodes.label: Mark 10:11
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Whoever divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery against her.

nodes.label: Mark 10:12
nodes.text: If a woman herself divorces her husband, and marries another, she commits adultery.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:13
nodes.text: They were bringing to him little children, that he should touch them, but the disciples rebuked those who were bringing them.

nodes.label: Mark 10:14
nodes.text:
But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation, and said to them,
“Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.

nodes.label: Mark 10:15
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:16
nodes.text: He took them in his arms, and blessed them, laying his hands on them.

nodes.label: Mark 10:17
nodes.text: As he was going out into the way, one ran to him, knelt before him, and asked him, “Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?”

nodes.label: Mark 10:18
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“Why do you call me good? No one is good except one—God.

nodes.label: Mark 10:19
nodes.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder,’ ‘Do not commit adultery,’ ‘Do not steal,’ ‘Do not give false testimony,’ ‘Do not defraud,’ ‘Honor your father and mother.’”

nodes.label: Mark 10:20
nodes.text: He said to him, “Teacher, I have observed all these things from my youth.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:21
nodes.text:
Jesus looking at him loved him, and said to him,
“One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:22
nodes.text: But his face fell at that saying, and he went away sorrowful, for he was one who had great possessions.

nodes.label: Mark 10:23
nodes.text:
Jesus looked around, and said to his disciples,
“How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!”

nodes.label: Mark 10:24
nodes.text:
The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus answered again,
“Children, how hard is it for those who trust in riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!

nodes.label: Mark 10:25
nodes.text: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:26
nodes.text: They were exceedingly astonished, saying to him, “Then who can be saved?”

nodes.label: Mark 10:27
nodes.text: Jesus, looking at them, said, “With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:28
nodes.text: Peter began to tell him, “Behold, we have left all, and have followed you.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:29
nodes.text:
Jesus said,
“Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or land, for my sake, and for the sake of the Good News,

nodes.label: Mark 10:30
nodes.text: but he will receive one hundred times more now in this time, houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and land, with persecutions; and in the age to come eternal life.

nodes.label: Mark 10:31
nodes.text: But many who are first will be last; and the last first.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:32
nodes.text: They were on the way, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus was going in front of them, and they were amazed; and those who followed were afraid. He again took the twelve, and began to tell them the things that were going to happen to him.

nodes.label: Mark 10:33
nodes.text: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death, and will deliver him to the Gentiles.

nodes.label: Mark 10:34
nodes.text: They will mock him, spit on him, scourge him, and kill him. On the third day he will rise again.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:35
nodes.text: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came near to him, saying, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we will ask.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:36
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“What do you want me to do for you?”

nodes.label: Mark 10:37
nodes.text: They said to him, “Grant to us that we may sit, one at your right hand, and one at your left hand, in your glory.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:38
nodes.text:
But Jesus said to them,
“You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?”

nodes.label: Mark 10:39
Mark 10:40
nodes.text: but to sit at my right hand and at my left hand is not mine to give, but for whom it has been prepared.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:41
nodes.text: When the ten heard it, they began to be indignant towards James and John.

nodes.label: Mark 10:42
nodes.text:
Jesus summoned them, and said to them,
“You know that they who are recognized as rulers over the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.

nodes.label: Mark 10:43
nodes.text: But it shall not be so among you, but whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant.

nodes.label: Mark 10:44
nodes.text: Whoever of you wants to become first among you, shall be bondservant of all.

nodes.label: Mark 10:45
nodes.text: For the Son of Man also came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:46
nodes.text: They came to Jericho. As he went out from Jericho, with his disciples and a great multitude, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting by the road.

nodes.label: Mark 10:47
nodes.text: When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out, and say, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”

variants.reading: Ναζαρηνός ('Nazarene')
variants.note: The fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists Ναζαρηνός in B L W Δ Θ Ψ against Ναζωραιός in א A C, Ναζορηνός in D and Ναζωρινός in 28. Vaticanus and Washingtonianus are manuscript nodes of this graph; Sinaiticus carries Ναζωραιός. WEB reads 'Jesus the Nazarene'.

nodes.label: Mark 10:48
nodes.text: Many rebuked him, that he should be quiet, but he cried out much more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”

nodes.label: Mark 10:49
nodes.text: Jesus stood still, and said, “Call him.” They called the blind man, saying to him, “Cheer up! Get up. He is calling you!”

nodes.label: Mark 10:50
nodes.text: He, casting away his cloak, sprang up, and came to Jesus.

nodes.label: Mark 10:51
nodes.text:
Jesus asked him,
“What do you want me to do for you?”
The blind man said to him, “Rabboni, that I may see again.”

nodes.label: Mark 10:52
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“Go your way. Your faith has made you well.”
 Immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus on the way.

nodes.label: Mark 11:1
nodes.text: When they came near to Jerusalem, to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,

nodes.label: Mark 11:2
nodes.text: and said to them, “Go your way into the village that is opposite you. Immediately as you enter into it, you will find a young donkey tied, on which no one has sat. Untie him, and bring him.

nodes.label: Mark 11:3
nodes.text: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord needs him;’ and immediately he will send him back here.”

nodes.label: Mark 11:4
nodes.text: They went away, and found a young donkey tied at the door outside in the open street, and they untied him.

nodes.label: Mark 11:5
nodes.text: Some of those who stood there asked them, “What are you doing, untying the young donkey?”

nodes.label: Mark 11:6
nodes.text: They said to them just as Jesus had said, and they let them go.

nodes.label: Mark 11:7
nodes.text: They brought the young donkey to Jesus, and threw their garments on it, and Jesus sat on it.

nodes.label: Mark 11:8
nodes.text: Many spread their garments on the way, and others were cutting down branches from the trees, and spreading them on the road.

nodes.label: Mark 11:9
nodes.text: Those who went in front, and those who followed, cried out, “Hosanna!  Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!

nodes.label: Mark 11:10
nodes.text: Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that is coming in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”

nodes.label: Mark 11:11
nodes.text: Jesus entered into the temple in Jerusalem. When he had looked around at everything, it being now evening, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.

nodes.label: Mark 11:12
nodes.text: The next day, when they had come out from Bethany, he was hungry.

nodes.label: Mark 11:13
nodes.text: Seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he came to see if perhaps he might find anything on it. When he came to it, he found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.

nodes.label: Mark 11:14
nodes.text: Jesus told it, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again!”  and his disciples heard it.

nodes.label: Mark 11:15
nodes.text: They came to Jerusalem, and Jesus entered into the temple, and began to throw out those who sold and those who bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables, and the seats of those who sold the doves.

nodes.label: Mark 11:16
nodes.text: He would not allow anyone to carry a container through the temple.

nodes.label: Mark 11:17
nodes.text: He taught, saying to them, “Isn’t it written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations?’ But you have made it a den of robbers!”

nodes.label: Mark 11:18
nodes.text: The chief priests and the scribes heard it, and sought how they might destroy him. For they feared him, because all the multitude was astonished at his teaching.

nodes.label: Mark 11:19
nodes.text: When evening came, he went out of the city.

nodes.label: Mark 11:20
nodes.text: As they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered away from the roots.

nodes.label: Mark 11:21
nodes.text: Peter, remembering, said to him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree which you cursed has withered away.”

nodes.label: Mark 11:22
nodes.text: Jesus answered them, “Have faith in God.

nodes.label: Mark 11:23
nodes.text: For most certainly I tell you, whoever may tell this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ and doesn’t doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says is happening; he shall have whatever he says.

nodes.label: Mark 11:24
nodes.text: Therefore I tell you, all things whatever you pray and ask for, believe that you have received them, and you shall have them.

nodes.label: Mark 11:25
nodes.text: Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone; so that your Father, who is in heaven, may also forgive you your transgressions.

nodes.label: Mark 11:26
nodes.text: But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your transgressions.”

variants.reading: the whole verse omitted
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists Mark 11:26 as 'Verse omitted by א B L W Δ Ψ 565. 700. 892. 1216. k, l, syr s,pal, cop'; included by K X Θ Π 28 and the Byzantine text. Sinaiticus (א), Vaticanus (B) and Washingtonianus (W) are manuscript nodes of this graph.

nodes.label: Mark 11:27
nodes.text: They came again to Jerusalem, and as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders came to him,

nodes.label: Mark 11:28
nodes.text: and they began saying to him, “By what authority do you do these things? Or who gave you this authority to do these things?”

nodes.label: Mark 11:29
nodes.text: Jesus said to them, “I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.

nodes.label: Mark 11:30
nodes.text: The baptism of John—was it from heaven, or from men? Answer me.”

nodes.label: Mark 11:31
nodes.text: They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we should say, ‘From heaven;’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

nodes.label: Mark 11:32
nodes.text: If we should say, ‘From men’”—they feared the people, for all held John to really be a prophet.

nodes.label: Mark 11:33
nodes.text: They answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” Jesus said to them, “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

nodes.label: Mark 12:1
nodes.text:
He began to speak to them in parables.
“A man planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a pit for the wine press, built a tower, rented it out to a farmer, and went into another country.

nodes.label: Mark 12:2
nodes.text: When it was time, he sent a servant to the farmer to get from the farmer his share of the fruit of the vineyard.

nodes.label: Mark 12:3
nodes.text: They took him, beat him, and sent him away empty.

nodes.label: Mark 12:4
nodes.text: Again, he sent another servant to them; and they threw stones at him, wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully treated.

nodes.label: Mark 12:5
nodes.text: Again he sent another; and they killed him; and many others, beating some, and killing some.

nodes.label: Mark 12:6
nodes.text: Therefore still having one, his beloved son, he sent him last to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

nodes.label: Mark 12:7
nodes.text: But those farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’

nodes.label: Mark 12:8
nodes.text: They took him, killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.

nodes.label: Mark 12:9
nodes.text: What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.

nodes.label: Mark 12:10
nodes.text:
Haven’t you even read this Scripture:
‘The stone which the builders rejected,
the same was made the head of the corner.

nodes.label: Mark 12:11
nodes.text:
This was from the Lord,
it is marvelous in our eyes’?”

nodes.label: Mark 12:12
nodes.text: They tried to seize him, but they feared the multitude; for they perceived that he spoke the parable against them. They left him, and went away.

nodes.label: Mark 12:13
nodes.text: They sent some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to him, that they might trap him with words.

nodes.label: Mark 12:14
nodes.text: When they had come, they asked him, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and don’t defer to anyone; for you aren’t partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?

nodes.label: Mark 12:15
nodes.text:
Shall we give, or shall we not give?”
But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them,
“Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.”

nodes.label: Mark 12:16
nodes.text:
They brought it.
He said to them,
“Whose is this image and inscription?”
They said to him, “Caesar’s.”

nodes.label: Mark 12:17
nodes.text:
Jesus answered them,
“Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
They marveled greatly at him.

nodes.label: Mark 12:18
nodes.text: There came to him Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection. They asked him, saying,

nodes.label: Mark 12:19
nodes.text: “Teacher, Moses wrote to us, ‘If a man’s brother dies, and leaves a wife behind him, and leaves no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up offspring for his brother.’

variants.reading: τέκνον ('child', singular)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists τέκνον ('child') for אc2a B L W Δ Θ Ψ f1 579 700 892 and others, against τέκνα ('children') for P45 D f13 28 427 565 and others. The WEB prints 'children' (τέκνα). Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Washingtonianus are manuscript nodes of this graph; P45 is too.

nodes.label: Mark 12:20
nodes.text: There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and dying left no offspring.

nodes.label: Mark 12:21
nodes.text: The second took her, and died, leaving no children behind him. The third likewise;

nodes.label: Mark 12:22
nodes.text: and the seven took her and left no children. Last of all the woman also died.

nodes.label: Mark 12:23
nodes.text: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be of them? For the seven had her as a wife.”

nodes.label: Mark 12:24
nodes.text:
Jesus answered them,
“Isn’t this because you are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God?

nodes.label: Mark 12:25
nodes.text: For when they will rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.

nodes.label: Mark 12:26
nodes.text: But about the dead, that they are raised; haven’t you read in the book of Moses, about the Bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?

nodes.label: Mark 12:27
nodes.text: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are therefore badly mistaken.”

nodes.label: Mark 12:28
nodes.text: One of the scribes came, and heard them questioning together. Knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, “Which commandment is the greatest of all?”

nodes.label: Mark 12:29
nodes.text:
Jesus answered,
“The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one:

nodes.label: Mark 12:30
nodes.text:
you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’
This is the first commandment.

nodes.label: Mark 12:31
nodes.text:
The second is like this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
There is no other commandment greater than these.”

nodes.label: Mark 12:32
nodes.text: The scribe said to him, “Truly, teacher, you have said well that he is one, and there is none other but he,

nodes.label: Mark 12:33
nodes.text: and to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

nodes.label: Mark 12:34
nodes.text:
When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him,
“You are not far from God’s Kingdom.”
No one dared ask him any question after that.

nodes.label: Mark 12:35
nodes.text:
Jesus responded, as he taught in the temple,
“How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?

nodes.label: Mark 12:36
nodes.text:
For David himself said in the Holy Spirit,
‘The Lord said to my Lord,
“Sit at my right hand,
until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’

nodes.label: Mark 12:37
nodes.text:
Therefore David himself calls him Lord, so how can he be his son?”

The common people heard him gladly.

nodes.label: Mark 12:38
nodes.text:
In his teaching he said to them,
“Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and to get greetings in the marketplaces,

nodes.label: Mark 12:39
nodes.text: and the best seats in the synagogues, and the best places at feasts:

nodes.label: Mark 12:40
nodes.text: those who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”

nodes.label: Mark 12:41
nodes.text: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury, and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much.

nodes.label: Mark 12:42
nodes.text: A poor widow came, and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin.

nodes.label: Mark 12:43
nodes.text:
He called his disciples to himself, and said to them,
“Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,

nodes.label: Mark 12:44
nodes.text: for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”

nodes.label: Mark 13:1
nodes.text: As he went out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, see what kind of stones and what kind of buildings!”

nodes.label: Mark 13:2
nodes.text: Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? There will not be left here one stone on another, which will not be thrown down.”

nodes.label: Mark 13:3
nodes.text: As he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him privately,

nodes.label: Mark 13:4
nodes.text: “Tell us, when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are all about to be fulfilled?”

nodes.label: Mark 13:5
nodes.text: Jesus, answering, began to tell them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.

nodes.label: Mark 13:6
nodes.text: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he!’ and will lead many astray.

nodes.label: Mark 13:7
nodes.text: “When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.

nodes.label: Mark 13:8
nodes.text: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places. There will be famines and troubles. These things are the beginning of birth pains.

nodes.label: Mark 13:9
nodes.text: But watch yourselves, for they will deliver you up to councils. You will be beaten in synagogues. You will stand before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them.

nodes.label: Mark 13:10
nodes.text: The Good News must first be preached to all the nations.

nodes.label: Mark 13:11
nodes.text: When they lead you away and deliver you up, don’t be anxious beforehand, or premeditate what you will say, but say whatever will be given you in that hour. For it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.

nodes.label: Mark 13:12
nodes.text: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.

nodes.label: Mark 13:13
nodes.text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end, the same will be saved.

nodes.label: Mark 13:14
nodes.text: But when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not (let the reader understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains,

nodes.label: Mark 13:15
nodes.text: and let him who is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house.

nodes.label: Mark 13:16
nodes.text: Let him who is in the field not return back to take his cloak.

nodes.label: Mark 13:17
nodes.text: But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse babies in those days!

nodes.label: Mark 13:18
nodes.text: Pray that your flight won’t be in the winter.

nodes.label: Mark 13:19
nodes.text: For in those days there will be oppression, such as there has not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never will be.

nodes.label: Mark 13:20
nodes.text: Unless the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones, whom he picked out, he shortened the days.

nodes.label: Mark 13:21
nodes.text: Then if anyone tells you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ don’t believe it.

nodes.label: Mark 13:22
nodes.text: For there will arise false christs and false prophets, and will show signs and wonders, that they may lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.

nodes.label: Mark 13:23
nodes.text: But you watch. “Behold, I have told you all things beforehand.

nodes.label: Mark 13:24
nodes.text: But in those days, after that oppression, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light,

nodes.label: Mark 13:25
nodes.text: the stars will be falling from the sky, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.

nodes.label: Mark 13:26
nodes.text: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.

nodes.label: Mark 13:27
nodes.text: Then he will send out his angels, and will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of the sky.

nodes.label: Mark 13:28
nodes.text: “Now from the fig tree, learn this parable. When the branch has now become tender, and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near;

nodes.label: Mark 13:29
nodes.text: even so you also, when you see these things coming to pass, know that it is near, at the doors.

nodes.label: Mark 13:30
nodes.text: Most certainly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.

nodes.label: Mark 13:31
nodes.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

nodes.label: Mark 13:32
nodes.text: But of that day or that hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.

variants.reading: οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός ('nor the Son') omitted
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists Mark 13:32: οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός - 'All manuscripts except those cited below'; omitted by X (Codex Monacensis), 389, 983, 1273, 1689 and vgms. None of these witnesses is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

nodes.label: Mark 13:33
nodes.text: Watch, keep alert, and pray; for you don’t know when the time is.

nodes.label: Mark 13:34
nodes.text: “It is like a man, traveling to another country, having left his house, and given authority to his servants, and to each one his work, and also commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.

nodes.label: Mark 13:35
nodes.text: Watch therefore, for you don’t know when the lord of the house is coming, whether at evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or in the morning;

nodes.label: Mark 13:36
nodes.text: lest coming suddenly he might find you sleeping.

nodes.label: Mark 13:37
nodes.text: What I tell you, I tell all: Watch.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:1
nodes.text: It was now two days before the feast of the Passover and the unleavened bread, and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might seize him by deception, and kill him.

nodes.label: Mark 14:2
nodes.text: For they said, “Not during the feast, because there might be a riot among the people.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:3
nodes.text: While he was at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at the table, a woman came having an alabaster jar of ointment of pure nard—very costly. She broke the jar, and poured it over his head.

nodes.label: Mark 14:4
nodes.text: But there were some who were indignant among themselves, saying, “Why has this ointment been wasted?

nodes.label: Mark 14:5
nodes.text: For this might have been sold for more than three hundred denarii, and given to the poor.” They grumbled against her.

nodes.label: Mark 14:6
nodes.text: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for me.

nodes.label: Mark 14:7
nodes.text: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want to, you can do them good; but you will not always have me.

nodes.label: Mark 14:8
nodes.text: She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for the burying.

nodes.label: Mark 14:9
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, wherever this Good News may be preached throughout the whole world, that which this woman has done will also be spoken of for a memorial of her.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:10
nodes.text: Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests, that he might deliver him to them.

nodes.label: Mark 14:11
nodes.text: They, when they heard it, were glad, and promised to give him money. He sought how he might conveniently deliver him.

nodes.label: Mark 14:12
nodes.text: On the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, his disciples asked him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare that you may eat the Passover?”

nodes.label: Mark 14:13
nodes.text: He sent two of his disciples, and said to them, “Go into the city, and there you will meet a man carrying a pitcher of water. Follow him,

nodes.label: Mark 14:14
nodes.text: and wherever he enters in, tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’

nodes.label: Mark 14:15
nodes.text: He will himself show you a large upper room furnished and ready. Get ready for us there.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:16
nodes.text: His disciples went out, and came into the city, and found things as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.

nodes.label: Mark 14:17
nodes.text: When it was evening he came with the twelve.

nodes.label: Mark 14:18
nodes.text: As they sat and were eating, Jesus said, “Most certainly I tell you, one of you will betray me—he who eats with me.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:19
nodes.text: They began to be sorrowful, and to ask him one by one, “Surely not I?” And another said, “Surely not I?”

nodes.label: Mark 14:20
nodes.text: He answered them, “It is one of the twelve, he who dips with me in the dish.

nodes.label: Mark 14:21
nodes.text: For the Son of Man goes, even as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:22
nodes.text: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, and when he had blessed, he broke it, and gave to them, and said, “Take, eat. This is my body.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:23
nodes.text: He took the cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave to them. They all drank of it.

nodes.label: Mark 14:24
nodes.text: He said to them, “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.

nodes.label: Mark 14:25
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, I will no more drink of the fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it anew in God’s Kingdom.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:26
nodes.text: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

nodes.label: Mark 14:27
nodes.text: Jesus said to them, “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’

nodes.label: Mark 14:28
nodes.text: However, after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:29
nodes.text: But Peter said to him, “Although all will be offended, yet I will not.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:30
nodes.text: Jesus said to him, “Most certainly I tell you, that you today, even this night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”

variants.reading: πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι ('before the rooster has crowed') - the 'twice' (δίς) omitted
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists Mark 14:30: πρὶν ἢ δὶς ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι ('before that the rooster has crowed twice') for A Byz, against πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι ('before the rooster has crowed') for א (Sinaiticus), C*, aeth, arm and the Western text-type (D cu2 lat.afr-eur).

nodes.label: Mark 14:31
nodes.text: But he spoke all the more, “If I must die with you, I will not deny you.” They all said the same thing.

nodes.label: Mark 14:32
nodes.text: They came to a place which was named Gethsemane. He said to his disciples, “Sit here, while I pray.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:33
nodes.text: He took with him Peter, James, and John, and began to be greatly troubled and distressed.

nodes.label: Mark 14:34
nodes.text: He said to them, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here, and watch.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:35
nodes.text: He went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.

nodes.label: Mark 14:36
nodes.text: He said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible to you. Please remove this cup from me. However, not what I desire, but what you desire.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:37
nodes.text: He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Couldn’t you watch one hour?

nodes.label: Mark 14:38
nodes.text: Watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:39
nodes.text: Again he went away, and prayed, saying the same words.

variants.reading: τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπών ('saying the same words') omitted
variants.note: The fetched article lists Mark 14:39: τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπών ('saying the same words') omitted by D a, b, c, d, ff2, k and (syrcur). None of these witnesses is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

nodes.label: Mark 14:40
nodes.text: Again he returned, and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy, and they didn’t know what to answer him.

nodes.label: Mark 14:41
nodes.text: He came the third time, and said to them, “Sleep on now, and take your rest. It is enough. The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

nodes.label: Mark 14:42
nodes.text: Arise, let us be going. Behold, he who betrays me is at hand.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:43
nodes.text: Immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, came—and with him a multitude with swords and clubs, from the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.

nodes.label: Mark 14:44
nodes.text: Now he who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying, “Whomever I will kiss, that is he. Seize him, and lead him away safely.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:45
nodes.text: When he had come, immediately he came to him, and said, “Rabbi! Rabbi!” and kissed him.

nodes.label: Mark 14:46
nodes.text: They laid their hands on him, and seized him.

nodes.label: Mark 14:47
nodes.text: But a certain one of those who stood by drew his sword, and struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.

nodes.label: Mark 14:48
nodes.text: Jesus answered them, “Have you come out, as against a robber, with swords and clubs to seize me?

nodes.label: Mark 14:49
nodes.text: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me. But this is so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:50
nodes.text: They all left him, and fled.

nodes.label: Mark 14:51
nodes.text: A certain young man followed him, having a linen cloth thrown around himself over his naked body. The young men grabbed him,

nodes.label: Mark 14:52
nodes.text: but he left the linen cloth, and fled from them naked.

nodes.label: Mark 14:53
nodes.text: They led Jesus away to the high priest. All the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes came together with him.

nodes.label: Mark 14:54
nodes.text: Peter had followed him from a distance, until he came into the court of the high priest. He was sitting with the officers, and warming himself in the light of the fire.

nodes.label: Mark 14:55
nodes.text: Now the chief priests and the whole council sought witnesses against Jesus to put him to death, and found none.

nodes.label: Mark 14:56
nodes.text: For many gave false testimony against him, and their testimony didn’t agree with each other.

nodes.label: Mark 14:57
nodes.text: Some stood up, and gave false testimony against him, saying,

nodes.label: Mark 14:58
nodes.text: “We heard him say, ‘I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and in three days I will build another made without hands.’”

nodes.label: Mark 14:59
nodes.text: Even so, their testimony did not agree.

nodes.label: Mark 14:60
nodes.text: The high priest stood up in the middle, and asked Jesus, “Have you no answer? What is it which these testify against you?”

nodes.label: Mark 14:61
nodes.text: But he stayed quiet, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?”

nodes.label: Mark 14:62
nodes.text: Jesus said, “I am. You will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming with the clouds of the sky.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:63
nodes.text: The high priest tore his clothes, and said, “What further need have we of witnesses?

nodes.label: Mark 14:64
nodes.text: You have heard the blasphemy! What do you think?” They all condemned him to be worthy of death.

nodes.label: Mark 14:65
nodes.text: Some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to beat him with fists, and to tell him, “Prophesy!” The officers struck him with the palms of their hands.

nodes.label: Mark 14:66
nodes.text: As Peter was in the courtyard below, one of the maids of the high priest came,

nodes.label: Mark 14:67
nodes.text: and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him, and said, “You were also with the Nazarene, Jesus!”

nodes.label: Mark 14:68
nodes.text: But he denied it, saying, “I neither know, nor understand what you are saying.” He went out on the porch, and the rooster crowed.

variants.reading: καὶ ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν ('and the rooster crowed') omitted
variants.note: The fetched article: καὶ άλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν ('and the rooster crowed') is inserted by the Western and Byzantine text-types after προαύλιον; not found in the Alexandrian text-type (א (Sinaiticus), B (Vaticanus), L, it, 17c, me). The WEB's wording follows the Western/Byzantine reading.

nodes.label: Mark 14:69
nodes.text: The maid saw him, and began again to tell those who stood by, “This is one of them.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:70
nodes.text: But he again denied it. After a little while again those who stood by said to Peter, “You truly are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech shows it.”

nodes.label: Mark 14:71

nodes.label: Matt 1:1
nodes.text: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.

nodes.label: Matt 1:2
nodes.text: Abraham became the father of Isaac. Isaac became the father of Jacob. Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers.

nodes.label: Matt 1:3
nodes.text: Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez became the father of Hezron. Hezron became the father of Ram.

nodes.label: Matt 1:4
nodes.text: Ram became the father of Amminadab. Amminadab became the father of Nahshon. Nahshon became the father of Salmon.

nodes.label: Matt 1:5
nodes.text: Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab. Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth. Obed became the father of Jesse.

nodes.label: Matt 1:6
nodes.text: Jesse became the father of King David. David became the father of Solomon by her who had been Uriah's wife.

nodes.label: Matt 1:7
nodes.text: Solomon became the father of Rehoboam. Rehoboam became the father of Abijah. Abijah became the father of Asa.

nodes.label: Matt 1:8
nodes.text: Asa became the father of Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat became the father of Joram. Joram became the father of Uzziah.

nodes.label: Matt 1:9
nodes.text: Uzziah became the father of Jotham. Jotham became the father of Ahaz. Ahaz became the father of Hezekiah.

nodes.label: Matt 1:10
nodes.text: Hezekiah became the father of Manasseh. Manasseh became the father of Amon. Amon became the father of Josiah.

nodes.label: Matt 1:11
nodes.text: Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the exile to Babylon.

nodes.label: Matt 1:12
nodes.text: After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah became the father of Shealtiel. Shealtiel became the father of Zerubbabel.

nodes.label: Matt 1:13
nodes.text: Zerubbabel became the father of Abiud. Abiud became the father of Eliakim. Eliakim became the father of Azor.

nodes.label: Matt 1:14
nodes.text: Azor became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Achim. Achim became the father of Eliud.

nodes.label: Matt 1:15
nodes.text: Eliud became the father of Eleazar. Eleazar became the father of Matthan. Matthan became the father of Jacob.

nodes.label: Matt 1:16
nodes.text: Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

nodes.label: Matt 1:17
nodes.text: So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; from David to the exile to Babylon fourteen generations; and from the carrying away to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.

nodes.label: Matt 1:18
nodes.text: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this: After his mother, Mary, was engaged to Joseph, before they came together, she was found pregnant by the Holy Spirit.

nodes.label: Matt 1:19
nodes.text: Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, intended to put her away secretly.

nodes.label: Matt 1:20
nodes.text: But when he thought about these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, "Joseph, son of David, don't be afraid to take to yourself Mary, your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.

nodes.label: Matt 1:21
nodes.text: She shall give birth to a son. You shall call his name Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins."

nodes.label: Matt 1:22
nodes.text: Now all this has happened, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,

nodes.label: Matt 1:23
nodes.text: "Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall give birth to a son. They shall call his name Immanuel"; which is, being interpreted, "God with us."

nodes.label: Matt 1:24
nodes.text: Joseph arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took his wife to himself;

nodes.label: Matt 1:25
nodes.text: and didn't know her sexually until she had given birth to her firstborn son. He named him Jesus.
Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, behold, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem, saying,
nodes.label: Matthew 2:1

nodes.text: “Where is he who is born King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east, and have come to worship him.”
nodes.label: Matthew 2:2

nodes.text: When King Herod heard it, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
nodes.label: Matthew 2:3

nodes.text: Gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he asked them where the Christ would be born.
nodes.label: Matthew 2:4

nodes.text: They said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is written through the prophet,
nodes.label: Matthew 2:5

nodes.text: ‘You Bethlehem, land of Judah, are in no way least among the princes of Judah: for out of you shall come a governor, who shall shepherd my people, Israel.’”
nodes.label: Matthew 2:6

nodes.text: Then Herod secretly called the wise men, and learned from them exactly what time the star appeared.
nodes.label: Matthew 2:7

nodes.text: He sent them to Bethlehem, and said, “Go and search diligently for the young child. When you have found him, bring me word, so that I also may come and worship him.”
nodes.label: Matthew 2:8

nodes.text: They, having heard the king, went their way; and behold, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, until it came and stood over where the young child was.
nodes.label: Matthew 2:9

nodes.text: When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
nodes.label: Matthew 2:10

nodes.text: They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
nodes.label: Matthew 2:11

nodes.text: Being warned in a dream that they shouldn’t return to Herod, they went back to their own country another way.
nodes.label: Matthew 2:12

nodes.text: Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.”
nodes.label: Matthew 2:13

nodes.text: He arose and took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt,
nodes.label: Matthew 2:14

nodes.text: and was there until the death of Herod; that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, “Out of Egypt I called my son.”
nodes.label: Matthew 2:15

nodes.text: Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked by the wise men, was exceedingly angry, and sent out, and killed all the male children who were in Bethlehem and in all the surrounding countryside, from two years old and under, according to the exact time which he had learned from the wise men.
nodes.label: Matthew 2:16

nodes.text: Then that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying,
nodes.label: Matthew 2:17

nodes.text: “A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children; she wouldn’t be comforted, because they are no more.”
nodes.label: Matthew 2:18

nodes.text: But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying,
nodes.label: Matthew 2:19

nodes.text: “Arise and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel, for those who sought the young child’s life are dead.”
nodes.label: Matthew 2:20

nodes.text: He arose and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel.
nodes.label: Matthew 2:21

nodes.text: But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in the place of his father, Herod, he was afraid to go there. Being warned in a dream, he withdrew into the region of Galilee,
nodes.label: Matthew 2:22

nodes.text: and came and lived in a city called Nazareth; that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophets: “He will be called a Nazarene.”
nodes.label: Matthew 2:23

nodes.text: In those days, John the Baptizer came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea, saying,
nodes.label: Matthew 3:1

nodes.text: “Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!”
nodes.label: Matthew 3:2

nodes.text: For this is he who was spoken of by Isaiah the prophet, saying, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness, make ready the way of the Lord. Make his paths straight.”
nodes.label: Matthew 3:3

nodes.text: Now John himself wore clothing made of camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
nodes.label: Matthew 3:4

nodes.text: Then people from Jerusalem, all of Judea, and all the region around the Jordan went out to him.
nodes.label: Matthew 3:5

nodes.text: They were baptized by him in the Jordan, confessing their sins.
nodes.label: Matthew 3:6

nodes.text: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming for his baptism, he said to them, “You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
nodes.label: Matthew 3:7

nodes.text: Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance!
nodes.label: Matthew 3:8

nodes.text: Don’t think to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham for our father,’ for I tell you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones.
nodes.label: Matthew 3:9

nodes.text: “Even now the ax lies at the root of the trees. Therefore every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit is cut down, and cast into the fire.
nodes.label: Matthew 3:10

nodes.text: I indeed baptize you in water for repentance, but he who comes after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.
nodes.label: Matthew 3:11

nodes.text: His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor. He will gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn up with unquenchable fire.”
nodes.label: Matthew 3:12

nodes.text: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him.
nodes.label: Matthew 3:13

nodes.text: But John would have hindered him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?”
nodes.label: Matthew 3:14

nodes.text: But Jesus, answering, said to him, “Allow it now, for this is the fitting way for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he allowed him.
nodes.label: Matthew 3:15

nodes.text: Jesus, when he was baptized, went up directly from the water: and behold, the heavens were opened to him. He saw the Spirit of God descending as a dove, and coming on him.
nodes.label: Matthew 3:16

nodes.text: Behold, a voice out of the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
nodes.label: Matthew 3:17
Matt 4:1
nodes.text: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.

nodes.label: Matt 4:2
nodes.text: When he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was hungry afterward.

nodes.label: Matt 4:3
nodes.text: The tempter came and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.”

nodes.label: Matt 4:4
nodes.text: But he answered, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.’”

nodes.label: Matt 4:5
nodes.text: Then the devil took him into the holy city. He set him on the pinnacle of the temple,

nodes.label: Matt 4:6
nodes.text: and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down, for it is written, ‘He will put his angels in charge of you.’ and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, so that you don’t dash your foot against a stone.’”

nodes.label: Matt 4:7
nodes.text: Jesus said to him, “Again, it is written, ‘You shall not test the Lord, your God.’”

nodes.label: Matt 4:8
nodes.text: Again, the devil took him to an exceedingly high mountain, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world, and their glory.

nodes.label: Matt 4:9
nodes.text: He said to him, “I will give you all of these things, if you will fall down and worship me.”

nodes.label: Matt 4:10
nodes.text: Then Jesus said to him, “Get behind me, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.’”

nodes.label: Matt 4:11
nodes.text: Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came and served him.

nodes.label: Matt 4:12
nodes.text: Now when Jesus heard that John was delivered up, he withdrew into Galilee.

nodes.label: Matt 4:13
nodes.text: Leaving Nazareth, he came and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,

nodes.label: Matt 4:14
nodes.text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,

nodes.label: Matt 4:15
nodes.text: “The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,

nodes.label: Matt 4:16
nodes.text: the people who sat in darkness saw a great light, to those who sat in the region and shadow of death, to them light has dawned.”

nodes.label: Matt 4:17
nodes.text: From that time, Jesus began to preach, and to say, “Repent! For the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand.”

nodes.label: Matt 4:18
nodes.text: Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.

nodes.label: Matt 4:19
nodes.text: He said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”

nodes.label: Matt 4:20
nodes.text: They immediately left their nets and followed him.

nodes.label: Matt 4:21
nodes.text: Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets. He called them.

nodes.label: Matt 4:22
nodes.text: They immediately left the boat and their father, and followed him.

nodes.label: Matt 4:23
nodes.text: Jesus went about in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

nodes.label: Matt 4:24
nodes.text: The report about him went out into all Syria. They brought to him all who were sick, afflicted with various diseases and torments, possessed with demons, epileptics, and paralytics; and he healed them.

nodes.label: Matt 4:25
nodes.text: Great multitudes from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and from beyond the Jordan followed him.
Seeing the multitudes, he went up onto the mountain. When he had sat down, his disciples came to him.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:1

nodes.text: He opened his mouth and taught them, saying,
nodes.label: Matthew 5:2

nodes.text:
“Blessed are the poor in spirit,
for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:3

nodes.text:
Blessed are those who mourn,
for they shall be comforted.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:4

nodes.text:
Blessed are the gentle,
for they shall inherit the earth.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:5

nodes.text:
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness,

for they shall be filled.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:6

nodes.text:
Blessed are the merciful,
for they shall obtain mercy.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:7

nodes.text:
Blessed are the pure in heart,
for they shall see God.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:8

nodes.text:
Blessed are the peacemakers,
for they shall be called children of God.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:9

nodes.text:
Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake,

for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:10

nodes.text: “Blessed are you when people reproach you, persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:11
