nodes.text: Rejoice, and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven. For that is how they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:12

nodes.text: “You are the salt of the earth, but if the salt has lost its flavor, with what will it be salted? It is then good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under the feet of men.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:13

nodes.text: You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:14

nodes.text: Neither do you light a lamp, and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:15

nodes.text: Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:16

nodes.text: “Don’t think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn’t come to destroy, but to fulfill.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:17

nodes.text:
For most certainly, I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not even one smallest letter
or one tiny pen stroke
shall in any way pass away from the law, until all things are accomplished.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:18

nodes.text: Whoever, therefore, shall break one of these least commandments, and teach others to do so, shall be called least in the Kingdom of Heaven; but whoever shall do and teach them shall be called great in the Kingdom of Heaven.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:19

nodes.text: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, there is no way you will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:20

nodes.text:
“You have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not murder;’
and ‘Whoever murders will be in danger of the judgment.’
nodes.label: Matthew 5:21

nodes.text:
But I tell you, that everyone who is angry with his brother without a cause


will be in danger of the judgment; and whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca!’

will be in danger of the council; and whoever says, ‘You fool!’ will be in danger of the fire of Gehenna.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:22

nodes.text: “If therefore you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has anything against you,
nodes.label: Matthew 5:23

nodes.text: leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:24

nodes.text: Agree with your adversary quickly, while you are with him on the way; lest perhaps the prosecutor deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be cast into prison.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:25

nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, you shall by no means get out of there, until you have paid the last penny.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:26

nodes.text:
“You have heard that it was said,

‘You shall not commit adultery;’
nodes.label: Matthew 5:27

nodes.text: but I tell you that everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:28

nodes.text: If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:29

nodes.text: If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:30

nodes.text: “It was also said, ‘Whoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorce,’
nodes.label: Matthew 5:31

nodes.text: but I tell you that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of sexual immorality, makes her an adulteress; and whoever marries her when she is put away commits adultery.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:32

nodes.text: “Again you have heard that it was said to them of old time, ‘You shall not make false vows, but shall perform to the Lord your vows,’
nodes.label: Matthew 5:33

nodes.text: but I tell you, don’t swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;
nodes.label: Matthew 5:34

nodes.text: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:35

nodes.text: Neither shall you swear by your head, for you can’t make one hair white or black.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:36

nodes.text: But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:37

nodes.text: “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’
nodes.label: Matthew 5:38

nodes.text: But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:39

nodes.text: If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:40

nodes.text: Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:41

nodes.text: Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:42

nodes.text:
“You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor

and hate your enemy.’
nodes.label: Matthew 5:43

nodes.text: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
nodes.label: Matthew 5:44

nodes.text: that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:45

nodes.text: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
nodes.label: Matthew 5:46

nodes.text:
If you only greet your friends, what more do you do than others? Don’t even the tax collectors
do the same?
nodes.label: Matthew 5:47

nodes.text: Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.
nodes.label: Matthew 5:48

nodes.text: “Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:1

nodes.text: Therefore when you do merciful deeds, don’t sound a trumpet before yourself, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may get glory from men. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:2

nodes.text: But when you do merciful deeds, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand does,
nodes.label: Matthew 6:3

nodes.text: so that your merciful deeds may be in secret, then your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:4

nodes.text: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:5

nodes.text: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:6

nodes.text: In praying, don’t use vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:7

nodes.text: Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need, before you ask him.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:8

nodes.text: Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:9

nodes.text: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:10

nodes.text: Give us today our daily bread.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:11

nodes.text: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:12

nodes.text: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’
nodes.label: Matthew 6:13

variants.reading: the doxology is absent (the prayer ends at 'deliver us from the evil one')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' records 'Text omitted' for the doxology in א (Sinaiticus), B (Vaticanus), D (Bezae), Z, 0170, f1, the Latin and bo cop traditions and fathers incl. Tertullian and Origen. Codex Washingtonianus (W) stands with the manuscripts that include the doxology (E G K L W Δ Θ Π Σ f13 ... Byz), the reading the WEB prints.

nodes.text: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:14

nodes.text: But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:15

nodes.text: “Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:16

nodes.text: But you, when you fast, anoint your head, and wash your face;
nodes.label: Matthew 6:17

nodes.text: so that you are not seen by men to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:18

nodes.text: “Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;
nodes.label: Matthew 6:19

nodes.text: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal;
nodes.label: Matthew 6:20

nodes.text: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:21

nodes.text: “The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:22

nodes.text: But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
nodes.label: Matthew 6:23

nodes.text: “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:24

nodes.text: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
nodes.label: Matthew 6:25

nodes.text: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
nodes.label: Matthew 6:26

nodes.text:
“Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment
to his lifespan?
nodes.label: Matthew 6:27

nodes.text: Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,
nodes.label: Matthew 6:28

nodes.text: yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:29

nodes.text: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
nodes.label: Matthew 6:30

nodes.text: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
nodes.label: Matthew 6:31

nodes.text: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:32

nodes.text: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:33

nodes.text: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
nodes.label: Matthew 6:34

nodes.text: “Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:1

nodes.text: For with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:2

nodes.text: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
nodes.label: Matthew 7:3

nodes.text: Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye;’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye?
nodes.label: Matthew 7:4

nodes.text: You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:5

nodes.text: “Don’t give that which is holy to the dogs, neither throw your pearls before the pigs, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:6

nodes.text: “Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:7

nodes.text: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:8

nodes.text: Or who is there among you, who, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?
nodes.label: Matthew 7:9

nodes.text: Or if he asks for a fish, who will give him a serpent?
nodes.label: Matthew 7:10

nodes.text: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
nodes.label: Matthew 7:11

nodes.text: Therefore whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:12

nodes.text: “Enter in by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter in by it.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:13

nodes.text:
How
narrow is the gate, and restricted is the way that leads to life! Few are those who find it.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:14

nodes.text: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:15

nodes.text: By their fruits you will know them. Do you gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
nodes.label: Matthew 7:16

nodes.text: Even so, every good tree produces good fruit; but the corrupt tree produces evil fruit.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:17

nodes.text: A good tree can’t produce evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree produce good fruit.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:18

nodes.text: Every tree that doesn’t grow good fruit is cut down, and thrown into the fire.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:19

nodes.text: Therefore by their fruits you will know them.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:20

nodes.text: Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven; but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:21

nodes.text: Many will tell me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in your name, in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many mighty works?’
nodes.label: Matthew 7:22

nodes.text: Then I will tell them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity.’
nodes.label: Matthew 7:23

nodes.text: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine, and does them, I will liken him to a wise man, who built his house on a rock.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:24

nodes.text: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall, for it was founded on the rock.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:25

nodes.text: Everyone who hears these words of mine, and doesn’t do them will be like a foolish man, who built his house on the sand.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:26

nodes.text: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it fell—and great was its fall.”
nodes.label: Matthew 7:27

nodes.text: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching,
nodes.label: Matthew 7:28

nodes.text: for he taught them with authority, and not like the scribes.
nodes.label: Matthew 7:29
Matt 8:1
nodes.text: When he came down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.

nodes.label: Matt 8:2
nodes.text: Behold, a leper came to him and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:3
nodes.text:
Jesus stretched out his hand, and touched him, saying,
“I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

nodes.label: Matt 8:4
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“See that you tell nobody, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:5
nodes.text: When he came into Capernaum, a centurion came to him, asking him,

nodes.label: Matt 8:6
nodes.text: and saying, “Lord, my servant lies in the house paralyzed, grievously tormented.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:7
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“I will come and heal him.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:8
nodes.text: The centurion answered, “Lord, I’m not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

nodes.label: Matt 8:9
nodes.text: For I am also a man under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and tell another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and tell my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:10
nodes.text:
When Jesus heard it, he marveled, and said to those who followed,
“Most certainly I tell you, I haven’t found so great a faith, not even in Israel.

nodes.label: Matt 8:11
nodes.text: I tell you that many will come from the east and the west, and will sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven,

nodes.label: Matt 8:12
nodes.text: but the children of the Kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:13
nodes.text:
Jesus said to the centurion,
“Go your way. Let it be done for you as you have believed.” His servant was healed in that hour.

nodes.label: Matt 8:14
nodes.text: When Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his wife’s mother lying sick with a fever.

nodes.label: Matt 8:15
nodes.text: He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and served him.

nodes.label: Matt 8:16
nodes.text: When evening came, they brought to him many possessed with demons. He cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were sick;

nodes.label: Matt 8:17
nodes.text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “He took our infirmities, and bore our diseases.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:18
nodes.text: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes around him, he gave the order to depart to the other side.

nodes.label: Matt 8:19
nodes.text: A scribe came, and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:20
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:21
nodes.text: Another of his disciples said to him, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:22
nodes.text:
But Jesus said to him,
“Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:23
nodes.text: When he got into a boat, his disciples followed him.

nodes.label: Matt 8:24
nodes.text: Behold, a violent storm came up on the sea, so much that the boat was covered with the waves, but he was asleep.

nodes.label: Matt 8:25
nodes.text: They came to him, and woke him up, saying, “Save us, Lord! We are dying!”

nodes.label: Matt 8:26
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?”
 Then he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.

nodes.label: Matt 8:27
nodes.text: The men marveled, saying, “What kind of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

nodes.label: Matt 8:28
nodes.text:
When he came to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes,
 two people possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that nobody could pass that way.

variants.reading: Gadarenes (Γαδαρηνων)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists Γαδαρηνων (Gadarenes) in B (Vaticanus), also C, M, Θ, Σ, 174, 1010, ℓ 253 and versional fathers - the reading of most modern translations.

variants.reading: Gerasenes (Γερασηνων)
variants.note: The article's named witnesses (minuscule 892c, Claromontanus Δ, the Latin tradition, Origen) are not manuscript nodes of this graph, so attested_by is left empty rather than inventing ids.

variants.reading: Gazarenes (Γαζαρηνων)
variants.note: The article lists Γαζαρηνων (Gazarenes) in א* - the original hand of Sinaiticus; its corrector (א2) reads Gergesenes, the WEB reading of this passage.

nodes.label: Matt 8:29
nodes.text: Behold, they cried out, saying, “What do we have to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?”

nodes.label: Matt 8:30
nodes.text: Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding far away from them.

nodes.label: Matt 8:31
nodes.text: The demons begged him, saying, “If you cast us out, permit us to go away into the herd of pigs.”

nodes.label: Matt 8:32
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Go!”
They came out, and went into the herd of pigs: and behold, the whole herd of pigs rushed down the cliff into the sea, and died in the water.

nodes.label: Matt 8:33
nodes.text: Those who fed them fled, and went away into the city, and told everything, including what happened to those who were possessed with demons.

nodes.label: Matt 8:34
nodes.text: Behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged that he would depart from their borders.

nodes.label: Matt 9:1
nodes.text: He entered into a boat, and crossed over, and came into his own city.

nodes.label: Matt 9:2
nodes.text:
Behold, they brought to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic,
“Son, cheer up! Your sins are forgiven you.”

nodes.label: Matt 9:3
nodes.text: Behold, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man blasphemes.”

nodes.label: Matt 9:4
nodes.text:
Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said,
“Why do you think evil in your hearts?

nodes.label: Matt 9:5
nodes.text: For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Get up, and walk?’

nodes.label: Matt 9:6
nodes.text:
But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins-” (then he said to the paralytic),
“Get up, and take up your mat, and go to your house.”

nodes.label: Matt 9:7
nodes.text: He arose and departed to his house.

nodes.label: Matt 9:8
nodes.text: But when the multitudes saw it, they marveled and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.

nodes.label: Matt 9:9
nodes.text:
As Jesus passed by from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax collection office. He said to him,
“Follow me.” He got up and followed him.

nodes.label: Matt 9:10
nodes.text: As he sat in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and sat down with Jesus and his disciples.

nodes.label: Matt 9:11
nodes.text: When the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

nodes.label: Matt 9:12
nodes.text:
When Jesus heard it, he said to them,
“Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.

nodes.label: Matt 9:13
nodes.text:
But you go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’
for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

nodes.label: Matt 9:14
nodes.text: Then John’s disciples came to him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples don’t fast?”

nodes.label: Matt 9:15
nodes.text:
Jesus said to them,
“Can the friends of the bridegroom mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast.

nodes.label: Matt 9:16
nodes.text: No one puts a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for the patch would tear away from the garment, and a worse hole is made.

nodes.label: Matt 9:17
nodes.text: Neither do people put new wine into old wine skins, or else the skins would burst, and the wine be spilled, and the skins ruined. No, they put new wine into fresh wine skins, and both are preserved.”

nodes.label: Matt 9:18
nodes.text: While he told these things to them, behold, a ruler came and worshiped him, saying, “My daughter has just died, but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.”

nodes.label: Matt 9:19
nodes.text: Jesus got up and followed him, as did his disciples.

nodes.label: Matt 9:20
nodes.text: Behold, a woman who had an issue of blood for twelve years came behind him, and touched the fringe of his garment;

nodes.label: Matt 9:21
nodes.text: for she said within herself, “If I just touch his garment, I will be made well.”

nodes.label: Matt 9:22
nodes.text:
But Jesus, turning around and seeing her, said,
“Daughter, cheer up! Your faith has made you well.” And the woman was made well from that hour.

nodes.label: Matt 9:23
nodes.text: When Jesus came into the ruler’s house, and saw the flute players, and the crowd in noisy disorder,

nodes.label: Matt 9:24
nodes.text:
he said to them,
“Make room, because the girl isn’t dead, but sleeping.”
They were ridiculing him.

nodes.label: Matt 9:25
nodes.text: But when the crowd was put out, he entered in, took her by the hand, and the girl arose.

nodes.label: Matt 9:26
nodes.text: The report of this went out into all that land.

nodes.label: Matt 9:27
nodes.text: As Jesus passed by from there, two blind men followed him, calling out and saying, “Have mercy on us, son of David!”

nodes.label: Matt 9:28
nodes.text:
When he had come into the house, the blind men came to him. Jesus said to them,
“Do you believe that I am able to do this?”
They told him, “Yes, Lord.”

nodes.label: Matt 9:29
nodes.text:
Then he touched their eyes, saying,
“According to your faith be it done to you.”

nodes.label: Matt 9:30
nodes.text:
Their eyes were opened. Jesus strictly commanded them, saying,
“See that no one knows about this.”

nodes.label: Matt 9:31
nodes.text: But they went out and spread abroad his fame in all that land.

nodes.label: Matt 9:32
nodes.text: As they went out, behold, a mute man who was demon possessed was brought to him.

nodes.label: Matt 9:33
nodes.text: When the demon was cast out, the mute man spoke. The multitudes marveled, saying, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”

nodes.label: Matt 9:34
nodes.text: But the Pharisees said, “By the prince of the demons, he casts out demons.”

nodes.label: Matt 9:35
nodes.text: Jesus went about all the cities and the villages, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

nodes.label: Matt 9:36
nodes.text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd.

nodes.label: Matt 9:37
nodes.text:
Then he said to his disciples,
“The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the laborers are few.

nodes.label: Matt 9:38
nodes.text: Pray therefore that the Lord of the harvest will send out laborers into his harvest.”

nodes.label: Matt 10:1
nodes.text: He called to himself his twelve disciples, and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal every disease and every sickness.

nodes.label: Matt 10:2
nodes.text: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee; John, his brother;

nodes.label: Matt 10:3
nodes.text: Philip; Bartholomew; Thomas; Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus; Lebbaeus, who was also called Thaddaeus;

variants.reading: Thaddaeus (Θαδδαιος) alone
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists Θαδδαιος (Thaddaeus) in א (Sinaiticus) and B (Vaticanus), with later minuscules and versions - the name without Lebbaeus.

variants.reading: Lebbaeus (Λεββαιος) alone
variants.note: The article lists Λεββαιος (Lebbaeus) in D (Codex Bezae) and Origen's Latin text; neither is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty. The WEB text of this passage, 'Lebbaeus, who was also called Thaddaeus', is the majority (Byzantine) reading, which the article shows in C2, E-K, N, W, Δ, Θ, Π, Σ, f1 and Byz - Codex Washingtonianus (W) among them.

nodes.label: Matt 10:4
nodes.text: Simon the Canaanite; and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

nodes.label: Matt 10:5
nodes.text:
Jesus sent these twelve out, and commanded them, saying,
“Don’t go among the Gentiles, and don’t enter into any city of the Samaritans.

nodes.label: Matt 10:6
nodes.text: Rather, go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

nodes.label: Matt 10:7
nodes.text: As you go, preach, saying, ‘The Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!’

nodes.label: Matt 10:8
nodes.text:
Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers,
and cast out demons. Freely you received, so freely give.

nodes.label: Matt 10:9
nodes.text: Don’t take any gold, silver, or brass in your money belts.

nodes.label: Matt 10:10
nodes.text: Take no bag for your journey, neither two coats, nor shoes, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his food.

nodes.label: Matt 10:11
nodes.text: Into whatever city or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy; and stay there until you go on.

nodes.label: Matt 10:12
nodes.text: As you enter into the household, greet it.

nodes.label: Matt 10:13
nodes.text: If the household is worthy, let your peace come on it, but if it isn’t worthy, let your peace return to you.

nodes.label: Matt 10:14
nodes.text: Whoever doesn’t receive you, nor hear your words, as you go out of that house or that city, shake the dust off your feet.

nodes.label: Matt 10:15
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city.

nodes.label: Matt 10:16
nodes.text: “Behold, I send you out as sheep among wolves. Therefore be wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.

nodes.label: Matt 10:17
nodes.text: But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to councils, and in their synagogues they will scourge you.

nodes.label: Matt 10:18
nodes.text: Yes, and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the nations.

nodes.label: Matt 10:19
nodes.text: But when they deliver you up, don’t be anxious how or what you will say, for it will be given you in that hour what you will say.

nodes.label: Matt 10:20
nodes.text: For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.

nodes.label: Matt 10:21
nodes.text: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.

nodes.label: Matt 10:22
nodes.text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.

nodes.label: Matt 10:23
nodes.text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee into the next, for most certainly I tell you, you will not have gone through the cities of Israel, until the Son of Man has come.

nodes.label: Matt 10:24
nodes.text: “A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his lord.

nodes.label: Matt 10:25
nodes.text:
It is enough for the disciple that he be like his teacher, and the servant like his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul,
how much more those of his household!

nodes.label: Matt 10:26
nodes.text: Therefore don’t be afraid of them, for there is nothing covered that will not be revealed; and hidden that will not be known.

nodes.label: Matt 10:27
nodes.text: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear whispered in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.

nodes.label: Matt 10:28
nodes.text: Don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul. Rather, fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.

nodes.label: Matt 10:29
nodes.text:
“Aren’t two sparrows sold for an assarion coin?
Not one of them falls on the ground apart from your Father’s will,

nodes.label: Matt 10:30
nodes.text: but the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

nodes.label: Matt 10:31
nodes.text: Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.

nodes.label: Matt 10:32
nodes.text: Everyone therefore who confesses me before men, him I will also confess before my Father who is in heaven.

nodes.label: Matt 10:33
nodes.text: But whoever denies me before men, him I will also deny before my Father who is in heaven.

nodes.label: Matt 10:34
nodes.text: “Don’t think that I came to send peace on the earth. I didn’t come to send peace, but a sword.

nodes.label: Matt 10:35
nodes.text: For I came to set a man at odds against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

nodes.label: Matt 10:36
nodes.text: A man’s foes will be those of his own household.

nodes.label: Matt 10:37
nodes.text: He who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he who loves son or daughter more than me isn’t worthy of me.

nodes.label: Matt 10:38
nodes.text: He who doesn’t take his cross and follow after me, isn’t worthy of me.

nodes.label: Matt 10:39
nodes.text: He who seeks his life will lose it; and he who loses his life for my sake will find it.

nodes.label: Matt 10:40
nodes.text: He who receives you receives me, and he who receives me receives him who sent me.

nodes.label: Matt 10:41
nodes.text: He who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward. He who receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.

nodes.label: Matt 10:42
nodes.text: Whoever gives one of these little ones just a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, most certainly I tell you he will in no way lose his reward.”

nodes.label: Matt 11:1
nodes.text: When Jesus had finished directing his twelve disciples, he departed from there to teach and preach in their cities.

nodes.label: Matt 11:2
nodes.text: Now when John heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples

nodes.label: Matt 11:3
nodes.text: and said to him, “Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?”

nodes.label: Matt 11:4
nodes.text:
Jesus answered them,
“Go and tell John the things which you hear and see:

nodes.label: Matt 11:5
nodes.text:
the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear,
the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.

nodes.label: Matt 11:6
nodes.text: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”

nodes.label: Matt 11:7
nodes.text:
As these went their way, Jesus began to say to the multitudes concerning John,
“What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?

nodes.label: Matt 11:8
nodes.text: But what did you go out to see? A man in soft clothing? Behold, those who wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.

nodes.label: Matt 11:9
nodes.text: But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.

nodes.label: Matt 11:10
nodes.text: For this is he, of whom it is written, ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’

nodes.label: Matt 11:11
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, among those who are born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptizer; yet he who is least in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than he.

nodes.label: Matt 11:12
nodes.text: From the days of John the Baptizer until now, the Kingdom of Heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.

nodes.label: Matt 11:13
nodes.text: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.

nodes.label: Matt 11:14
nodes.text: If you are willing to receive it, this is Elijah, who is to come.

nodes.label: Matt 11:15
nodes.text: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.

nodes.label: Matt 11:16
nodes.text: “But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces, who call to their companions

nodes.label: Matt 11:17
nodes.text: and say, ‘We played the flute for you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned for you, and you didn’t lament.’

nodes.label: Matt 11:18
nodes.text: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon.’

nodes.label: Matt 11:19
nodes.text: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Behold, a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is justified by her children.”

nodes.label: Matt 11:20
nodes.text: Then he began to denounce the cities in which most of his mighty works had been done, because they didn’t repent.

nodes.label: Matt 11:21
nodes.text: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

nodes.label: Matt 11:22
nodes.text: But I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.

nodes.label: Matt 11:23
nodes.text:
You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, you will go down to Hades.

For if the mighty works had been done in Sodom which were done in you, it would have remained until today.

nodes.label: Matt 11:24
nodes.text: But I tell you that it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom, on the day of judgment, than for you.”

nodes.label: Matt 11:25
nodes.text:
At that time, Jesus answered,
“I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to infants.

nodes.label: Matt 11:26
nodes.text: Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.

nodes.label: Matt 11:27
nodes.text: All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows the Son, except the Father; neither does anyone know the Father, except the Son, and he to whom the Son desires to reveal him.

nodes.label: Matt 11:28
nodes.text: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

nodes.label: Matt 11:29
nodes.text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.

nodes.label: Matt 11:30
nodes.text: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”

nodes.label: Matt 12:1
nodes.text: At that time, Jesus went on the Sabbath day through the grain fields. His disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.

nodes.label: Matt 12:2
nodes.text: But the Pharisees, when they saw it, said to him, “Behold, your disciples do what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.”

nodes.label: Matt 12:3
nodes.text:
But he said to them,
“Haven’t you read what David did, when he was hungry, and those who were with him;

nodes.label: Matt 12:4
nodes.text: how he entered into God’s house, and ate the show bread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for those who were with him, but only for the priests?

nodes.label: Matt 12:5
nodes.text: Or have you not read in the law, that on the Sabbath day, the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath, and are guiltless?

nodes.label: Matt 12:6
nodes.text: But I tell you that one greater than the temple is here.

nodes.label: Matt 12:7
nodes.text:
But if you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’
you wouldn’t have condemned the guiltless.

nodes.label: Matt 12:8
nodes.text: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”

nodes.label: Matt 12:9
nodes.text: He departed there, and went into their synagogue.

nodes.label: Matt 12:10
nodes.text: And behold there was a man with a withered hand. They asked him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath day?” that they might accuse him.

nodes.label: Matt 12:11
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“What man is there among you, who has one sheep, and if this one falls into a pit on the Sabbath day, won’t he grab on to it, and lift it out?

nodes.label: Matt 12:12
nodes.text: Of how much more value then is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath day.”

nodes.label: Matt 12:13
nodes.text:
Then he told the man,
“Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out; and it was restored whole, just like the other.

nodes.label: Matt 12:14
nodes.text: But the Pharisees went out, and conspired against him, how they might destroy him.

nodes.label: Matt 12:15
nodes.text: Jesus, perceiving that, withdrew from there. Great multitudes followed him; and he healed them all,

nodes.label: Matt 12:16
nodes.text: and commanded them that they should not make him known:

nodes.label: Matt 12:17
nodes.text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,

nodes.label: Matt 12:18
nodes.text:
“Behold, my servant whom I have chosen;
my beloved in whom my soul is well pleased:
I will put my Spirit on him.
He will proclaim justice to the nations.

nodes.label: Matt 12:19
nodes.text:
He will not strive, nor shout;
neither will anyone hear his voice in the streets.

nodes.label: Matt 12:20
nodes.text:
He won’t break a bruised reed.
He won’t quench a smoking flax,
until he leads justice to victory.

nodes.label: Matt 12:21
nodes.text: In his name, the nations will hope.”

nodes.label: Matt 12:22
nodes.text: Then one possessed by a demon, blind and mute, was brought to him and he healed him, so that the blind and mute man both spoke and saw.

nodes.label: Matt 12:23
nodes.text: All the multitudes were amazed, and said, “Can this be the son of David?”

nodes.label: Matt 12:24
nodes.text: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, “This man does not cast out demons, except by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”

nodes.label: Matt 12:25
nodes.text:
Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them,
“Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.

nodes.label: Matt 12:26
nodes.text: If Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?

nodes.label: Matt 12:27
nodes.text: If I by Beelzebul cast out demons, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.

nodes.label: Matt 12:28
nodes.text: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you.

nodes.label: Matt 12:29
nodes.text: Or how can one enter into the house of the strong man, and plunder his goods, unless he first bind the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.

nodes.label: Matt 12:30
nodes.text: “He who is not with me is against me, and he who doesn’t gather with me, scatters.

nodes.label: Matt 12:31
nodes.text: Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven men.

nodes.label: Matt 12:32
nodes.text: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this age, nor in that which is to come.

nodes.label: Matt 12:33
nodes.text: “Either make the tree good, and its fruit good, or make the tree corrupt, and its fruit corrupt; for the tree is known by its fruit.

nodes.label: Matt 12:34
nodes.text: You offspring of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak good things? For out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks.

nodes.label: Matt 12:35
nodes.text:
The good man out of his good treasure brings out good things, and the evil man out of his evil treasure
brings out evil things.

nodes.label: Matt 12:36
nodes.text: I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment.

nodes.label: Matt 12:37
nodes.text: For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

nodes.label: Matt 12:38
nodes.text: Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees answered, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”

nodes.label: Matt 12:39
nodes.text:
But he answered them,
“An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, but no sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet.

nodes.label: Matt 12:40
nodes.text: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the whale, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

nodes.label: Matt 12:41
nodes.text: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, someone greater than Jonah is here.

nodes.label: Matt 12:42
nodes.text: The queen of the south will rise up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, someone greater than Solomon is here.

nodes.label: Matt 12:43
nodes.text: When an unclean spirit has gone out of a man, he passes through waterless places, seeking rest, and doesn’t find it.

nodes.label: Matt 12:44
nodes.text: Then he says, ‘I will return into my house from which I came out,’ and when he has come back, he finds it empty, swept, and put in order.

nodes.label: Matt 12:45
nodes.text: Then he goes, and takes with himself seven other spirits more evil than he is, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first. Even so will it be also to this evil generation.”

nodes.label: Matt 12:46
nodes.text: While he was yet speaking to the multitudes, behold, his mother and his brothers stood outside, seeking to speak to him.

nodes.label: Matt 12:47
nodes.text: One said to him, “Behold, your mother and your brothers stand outside, seeking to speak to you.”

nodes.label: Matt 12:48
nodes.text:
But he answered him who spoke to him,
“Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?”

nodes.label: Matt 12:49
nodes.text:
He stretched out his hand towards his disciples, and said,
“Behold, my mother and my brothers!

nodes.label: Matt 12:50
nodes.text: For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.”

nodes.label: Matt 13:1
nodes.text: On that day Jesus went out of the house, and sat by the seaside.

nodes.label: Matt 13:2
nodes.text: Great multitudes gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat, and sat, and all the multitude stood on the beach.

nodes.label: Matt 13:3
nodes.text:
He spoke to them many things in parables, saying,
“Behold, a farmer went out to sow.

nodes.label: Matt 13:4
nodes.text: As he sowed, some seeds fell by the roadside, and the birds came and devoured them.

nodes.label: Matt 13:5
nodes.text: Others fell on rocky ground, where they didn’t have much soil, and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of earth.

nodes.label: Matt 13:6
nodes.text: When the sun had risen, they were scorched. Because they had no root, they withered away.

nodes.label: Matt 13:7
nodes.text: Others fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked them.

nodes.label: Matt 13:8
nodes.text: Others fell on good soil, and yielded fruit: some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.

nodes.label: Matt 13:9
nodes.text: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

nodes.label: Matt 13:10
nodes.text: The disciples came, and said to him, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”

nodes.label: Matt 13:11
nodes.text:
He answered them,
“To you it is given to know the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven, but it is not given to them.

nodes.label: Matt 13:12
nodes.text: For whoever has, to him will be given, and he will have abundance, but whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he has.

nodes.label: Matt 13:13
nodes.text: Therefore I speak to them in parables, because seeing they don’t see, and hearing, they don’t hear, neither do they understand.

nodes.label: Matt 13:14
nodes.text:
In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says,

‘By hearing you will hear,
and will in no way understand;
Seeing you will see,
and will in no way perceive:

nodes.label: Matt 13:15
Matt 13:16
nodes.text: “But blessed are your eyes, for they see; and your ears, for they hear.

nodes.label: Matt 13:17
nodes.text: For most certainly I tell you that many prophets and righteous men desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see them; and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear them.

nodes.label: Matt 13:18
nodes.text: “Hear, then, the parable of the farmer.

nodes.label: Matt 13:19
nodes.text: When anyone hears the word of the Kingdom, and doesn’t understand it, the evil one comes, and snatches away that which has been sown in his heart. This is what was sown by the roadside.

nodes.label: Matt 13:20
nodes.text: What was sown on the rocky places, this is he who hears the word, and immediately with joy receives it;

nodes.label: Matt 13:21
nodes.text: yet he has no root in himself, but endures for a while. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he stumbles.

nodes.label: Matt 13:22
nodes.text: What was sown among the thorns, this is he who hears the word, but the cares of this age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.

nodes.label: Matt 13:23
nodes.text: What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word, and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit, and produces, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.”

nodes.label: Matt 13:24
nodes.text:
He set another parable before them, saying,
“The Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field,

nodes.label: Matt 13:25
nodes.text:
but while people slept, his enemy came and sowed darnel weeds
also among the wheat, and went away.

nodes.label: Matt 13:26
nodes.text: But when the blade sprang up and produced fruit, then the darnel weeds appeared also.

nodes.label: Matt 13:27
nodes.text: The servants of the householder came and said to him, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where did these darnel weeds come from?’

nodes.label: Matt 13:28
nodes.text:
“He said to them, ‘An enemy has done this.’
“The servants asked him, ‘Do you want us to go and gather them up?’

nodes.label: Matt 13:29
nodes.text: “But he said, ‘No, lest perhaps while you gather up the darnel weeds, you root up the wheat with them.

nodes.label: Matt 13:30
nodes.text: Let both grow together until the harvest, and in the harvest time I will tell the reapers, “First, gather up the darnel weeds, and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the wheat into my barn.”’”

nodes.label: Matt 13:31
nodes.text:
He set another parable before them, saying,
“The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field;

nodes.label: Matt 13:32
nodes.text: which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs, and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.”

nodes.label: Matt 13:33
nodes.text:
He spoke another parable to them.
“The Kingdom of Heaven is like yeast, which a woman took, and hid in three measures
of meal, until it was all leavened.”

nodes.label: Matt 13:34
nodes.text: Jesus spoke all these things in parables to the multitudes; and without a parable, he didn’t speak to them,

nodes.label: Matt 13:35
Matt 13:36
nodes.text: Then Jesus sent the multitudes away, and went into the house. His disciples came to him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the darnel weeds of the field.”

nodes.label: Matt 13:37
nodes.text:
He answered them,
“He who sows the good seed is the Son of Man,

nodes.label: Matt 13:38
nodes.text: the field is the world; and the good seed, these are the children of the Kingdom; and the darnel weeds are the children of the evil one.

nodes.label: Matt 13:39
nodes.text: The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.

nodes.label: Matt 13:40
nodes.text: As therefore the darnel weeds are gathered up and burned with fire; so will it be at the end of this age.

nodes.label: Matt 13:41
nodes.text: The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather out of his Kingdom all things that cause stumbling, and those who do iniquity,

nodes.label: Matt 13:42
nodes.text: and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

nodes.label: Matt 13:43
nodes.text: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the Kingdom of their Father. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.

nodes.label: Matt 13:44
nodes.text: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like treasure hidden in the field, which a man found, and hid. In his joy, he goes and sells all that he has, and buys that field.

nodes.label: Matt 13:45
nodes.text: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who is a merchant seeking fine pearls,

nodes.label: Matt 13:46
nodes.text: who having found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had, and bought it.

nodes.label: Matt 13:47
nodes.text: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a dragnet, that was cast into the sea, and gathered some fish of every kind,

nodes.label: Matt 13:48
nodes.text: which, when it was filled, they drew up on the beach. They sat down, and gathered the good into containers, but the bad they threw away.

nodes.label: Matt 13:49
nodes.text: So will it be in the end of the world. The angels will come and separate the wicked from among the righteous,

nodes.label: Matt 13:50
nodes.text: and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.”

nodes.label: Matt 13:51
nodes.text:
Jesus said to them,
“Have you understood all these things?”

They answered him, “Yes, Lord.”

nodes.label: Matt 13:52
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“Therefore every scribe who has been made a disciple in the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who is a householder, who brings out of his treasure new and old things.”

nodes.label: Matt 13:53
nodes.text: When Jesus had finished these parables, he departed from there.

nodes.label: Matt 13:54
nodes.text: Coming into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished, and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom, and these mighty works?

nodes.label: Matt 13:55
nodes.text: Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother called Mary, and his brothers, James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?

nodes.label: Matt 13:56
nodes.text: Aren’t all of his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all of these things?”

nodes.label: Matt 13:57
nodes.text:
They were offended by him.
But Jesus said to them,
“A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and in his own house.”

nodes.label: Matt 13:58
nodes.text: He didn’t do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

nodes.label: Matt 14:1
nodes.text: At that time, Herod the tetrarch heard the report concerning Jesus,

nodes.label: Matt 14:2
nodes.text: and said to his servants, “This is John the Baptizer. He is risen from the dead. That is why these powers work in him.”

nodes.label: Matt 14:3
nodes.text: For Herod had laid hold of John, and bound him, and put him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife.

nodes.label: Matt 14:4
nodes.text: For John said to him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”

nodes.label: Matt 14:5
nodes.text: When he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.

nodes.label: Matt 14:6
nodes.text: But when Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced among them and pleased Herod.

nodes.label: Matt 14:7
nodes.text: Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatever she should ask.

nodes.label: Matt 14:8
nodes.text: She, being prompted by her mother, said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptizer.”

nodes.label: Matt 14:9
nodes.text: The king was grieved, but for the sake of his oaths, and of those who sat at the table with him, he commanded it to be given,

nodes.label: Matt 14:10
nodes.text: and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.

nodes.label: Matt 14:11
nodes.text: His head was brought on a platter, and given to the young lady: and she brought it to her mother.

nodes.label: Matt 14:12
nodes.text: His disciples came, and took the body, and buried it; and they went and told Jesus.

nodes.label: Matt 14:13
nodes.text: Now when Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there in a boat, to a deserted place apart. When the multitudes heard it, they followed him on foot from the cities.

nodes.label: Matt 14:14
nodes.text: Jesus went out, and he saw a great multitude. He had compassion on them, and healed their sick.

nodes.label: Matt 14:15
nodes.text: When evening had come, his disciples came to him, saying, “This place is deserted, and the hour is already late. Send the multitudes away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves food.”

nodes.label: Matt 14:16
nodes.text:
But Jesus said to them,
“They don’t need to go away. You give them something to eat.”

nodes.label: Matt 14:17
nodes.text: They told him, “We only have here five loaves and two fish.”

nodes.label: Matt 14:18
nodes.text:
He said,
“Bring them here to me.”

nodes.label: Matt 14:19
nodes.text: He commanded the multitudes to sit down on the grass; and he took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, broke and gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples gave to the multitudes.

nodes.label: Matt 14:20
nodes.text: They all ate, and were filled. They took up twelve baskets full of that which remained left over from the broken pieces.

nodes.label: Matt 14:21
nodes.text: Those who ate were about five thousand men, besides women and children.

nodes.label: Matt 14:22
nodes.text: Immediately Jesus made the disciples get into the boat, and to go ahead of him to the other side, while he sent the multitudes away.

nodes.label: Matt 14:23
nodes.text: After he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into the mountain by himself to pray. When evening had come, he was there alone.

nodes.label: Matt 14:24
nodes.text: But the boat was now in the middle of the sea, distressed by the waves, for the wind was contrary.

nodes.label: Matt 14:25
nodes.text: In the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came to them, walking on the sea.

nodes.label: Matt 14:26
nodes.text: When the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, “It’s a ghost!” and they cried out for fear.

nodes.label: Matt 14:27
nodes.text:
But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying,
“Cheer up! It is I!

Don’t be afraid.”

nodes.label: Matt 14:28
nodes.text: Peter answered him and said, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters.”

nodes.label: Matt 14:29
nodes.text:
He said,
“Come!”
Peter stepped down from the boat, and walked on the waters to come to Jesus.

nodes.label: Matt 14:30
nodes.text: But when he saw that the wind was strong, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, “Lord, save me!”

nodes.label: Matt 14:31
nodes.text:
Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and said to him,
“You of little faith, why did you doubt?”

nodes.label: Matt 14:32
nodes.text: When they got up into the boat, the wind ceased.

nodes.label: Matt 14:33
nodes.text: Those who were in the boat came and worshiped him, saying, “You are truly the Son of God!”

nodes.label: Matt 14:34
nodes.text: When they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret.

nodes.label: Matt 14:35
nodes.text: When the people of that place recognized him, they sent into all that surrounding region, and brought to him all who were sick;

nodes.label: Matt 14:36
nodes.text: and they begged him that they might just touch the fringe of his garment. As many as touched it were made whole.

nodes.label: Matt 15:1
nodes.text: Then Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from Jerusalem, saying,

nodes.label: Matt 15:2
nodes.text: “Why do your disciples disobey the tradition of the elders? For they don’t wash their hands when they eat bread.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:3
nodes.text:
He answered them,
“Why do you also disobey the commandment of God because of your tradition?

nodes.label: Matt 15:4
nodes.text:
For God commanded, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’
and, ‘He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’

nodes.label: Matt 15:5
nodes.text: But you say, ‘Whoever may tell his father or his mother, “Whatever help you might otherwise have gotten from me is a gift devoted to God,”

nodes.label: Matt 15:6
nodes.text: he shall not honor his father or mother.’ You have made the commandment of God void because of your tradition.

nodes.label: Matt 15:7
nodes.text: You hypocrites! Well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,

nodes.label: Matt 15:8
Matt 15:9
nodes.text:
And in vain do they worship me,
teaching as doctrine rules made by men.’”

nodes.label: Matt 15:10
nodes.text:
He summoned the multitude, and said to them,
“Hear, and understand.

nodes.label: Matt 15:11
nodes.text: That which enters into the mouth doesn’t defile the man; but that which proceeds out of the mouth, this defiles the man.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:12
nodes.text: Then the disciples came, and said to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended, when they heard this saying?”

nodes.label: Matt 15:13
nodes.text:
But he answered,
“Every plant which my heavenly Father didn’t plant will be uprooted.

nodes.label: Matt 15:14
nodes.text: Leave them alone. They are blind guides of the blind. If the blind guide the blind, both will fall into a pit.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:15
nodes.text: Peter answered him, “Explain the parable to us.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:16
nodes.text:
So Jesus said,
“Do you also still not understand?

nodes.label: Matt 15:17
nodes.text: Don’t you understand that whatever goes into the mouth passes into the belly, and then out of the body?

nodes.label: Matt 15:18
nodes.text: But the things which proceed out of the mouth come out of the heart, and they defile the man.

nodes.label: Matt 15:19
nodes.text: For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual sins, thefts, false testimony, and blasphemies.

nodes.label: Matt 15:20
nodes.text: These are the things which defile the man; but to eat with unwashed hands doesn’t defile the man.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:21
nodes.text: Jesus went out from there, and withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon.

nodes.label: Matt 15:22
nodes.text: Behold, a Canaanite woman came out from those borders, and cried, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, you son of David! My daughter is severely possessed by a demon!”

nodes.label: Matt 15:23
nodes.text:
But he answered her not a word.
His disciples came and begged him, saying, “Send her away; for she cries after us.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:24
nodes.text:
But he answered,
“I wasn’t sent to anyone but the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:25
nodes.text: But she came and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, help me.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:26
nodes.text:
But he answered,
“It is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:27
nodes.text: But she said, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:28
nodes.text:
Then Jesus answered her,
“Woman, great is your faith! Be it done to you even as you desire.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.

nodes.label: Matt 15:29
nodes.text: Jesus departed from there, and came near to the sea of Galilee; and he went up into the mountain, and sat there.

nodes.label: Matt 15:30
nodes.text: Great multitudes came to him, having with them the lame, blind, mute, maimed, and many others, and they put them down at his feet. He healed them,

nodes.label: Matt 15:31
nodes.text: so that the multitude wondered when they saw the mute speaking, the injured healed, the lame walking, and the blind seeing—and they glorified the God of Israel.

nodes.label: Matt 15:32
nodes.text:
Jesus summoned his disciples and said,
“I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days and have nothing to eat. I don’t want to send them away fasting, or they might faint on the way.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:33
nodes.text: The disciples said to him, “Where should we get so many loaves in a deserted place as to satisfy so great a multitude?”

nodes.label: Matt 15:34
nodes.text:
Jesus said to them,
“How many loaves do you have?”
They said, “Seven, and a few small fish.”

nodes.label: Matt 15:35
nodes.text: He commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground;

nodes.label: Matt 15:36
nodes.text: and he took the seven loaves and the fish. He gave thanks and broke them, and gave to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.

nodes.label: Matt 15:37
nodes.text: They all ate, and were filled. They took up seven baskets full of the broken pieces that were left over.

nodes.label: Matt 15:38
nodes.text: Those who ate were four thousand men, besides women and children.

nodes.label: Matt 15:39
nodes.text: Then he sent away the multitudes, got into the boat, and came into the borders of Magdala.

variants.reading: Magadan (some Greek manuscripts, followed by the Revised Version)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Magdala' article states that 'some Greek manuscripts give the name of the place as Magadan, and more recent translations (such as the Revised Version) follow this (Matthew 15:39)'. The article names no witness that is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty rather than inventing ids. The article also records Mark's parallel reading 'Dalmanutha', which a handful of manuscripts assimilate to Magdala or Magadan.

nodes.label: Matt 16:1
nodes.text: The Pharisees and Sadducees came, and testing him, asked him to show them a sign from heaven.

nodes.label: Matt 16:2
nodes.text:
But he answered them,
“When it is evening, you say, ‘It will be fair weather, for the sky is red.’

variants.reading: Verses 16:2b-3 omitted entirely
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists 'Text omitted — א B V X Y Γ ...' for Matthew 16:2-3: the whole weather-saying is absent from Sinaiticus (א) and Vaticanus (B) and a series of later uncials and minuscules.

variants.reading: The weather saying present (the WEB text)
variants.note: The article lists the saying in C, (D), F, G, H, (K), L, (N), O, (W), Δ, Θ, f1 and many minuscules and versions - witnesses that are not manuscript nodes of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

nodes.label: Matt 16:3
nodes.text: In the morning, ‘It will be foul weather today, for the sky is red and threatening.’ Hypocrites! You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but you can’t discern the signs of the times!

nodes.label: Matt 16:4
nodes.text:
An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and there will be no sign given to it, except the sign of the prophet Jonah.”
He left them, and departed.

nodes.label: Matt 16:5
nodes.text: The disciples came to the other side and had forgotten to take bread.

nodes.label: Matt 16:6
nodes.text:
Jesus said to them,
“Take heed and beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

nodes.label: Matt 16:7
nodes.text: They reasoned among themselves, saying, “We brought no bread.”

nodes.label: Matt 16:8
nodes.text:
Jesus, perceiving it, said,
“Why do you reason among yourselves, you of little faith, ‘because you have brought no bread?’

nodes.label: Matt 16:9
nodes.text: Don’t you yet perceive, neither remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?

nodes.label: Matt 16:10
nodes.text: Nor the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you took up?

nodes.label: Matt 16:11
nodes.text: How is it that you don’t perceive that I didn’t speak to you concerning bread? But beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

nodes.label: Matt 16:12
nodes.text: Then they understood that he didn’t tell them to beware of the yeast of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

nodes.label: Matt 16:13
nodes.text:
Now when Jesus came into the parts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying,
“Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?”

nodes.label: Matt 16:14
nodes.text: They said, “Some say John the Baptizer, some, Elijah, and others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.”

nodes.label: Matt 16:15
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“But who do you say that I am?”

nodes.label: Matt 16:16
nodes.text: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

nodes.label: Matt 16:17
nodes.text:
Jesus answered him,
“Blessed are you, Simon Bar Jonah, for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven.

nodes.label: Matt 16:18
nodes.text:
I also tell you that you are Peter,
and on this rock

I will build my assembly, and the gates of Hades
will not prevail against it.

nodes.label: Matt 16:19
nodes.text: I will give to you the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; and whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven.”

variants.reading: κλειδας (keys, plural)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists κλειδας ('keys') in א* B* L W, against κλεις ('key', singular) in א2 Bc C D f1 f13 and the majority text. The WEB reads the plural 'keys'.

variants.reading: κλεις (key, singular)
variants.note: Listed in the article for א2, Bc, C, D, f1, f13 and the majority text; these witnesses are not manuscript nodes of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

nodes.label: Matt 16:20
nodes.text: Then he commanded the disciples that they should tell no one that he was Jesus the Christ.

nodes.label: Matt 16:21
nodes.text: From that time, Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.

nodes.label: Matt 16:22
nodes.text: Peter took him aside, and began to rebuke him, saying, “Far be it from you, Lord! This will never be done to you.”

nodes.label: Matt 16:23
nodes.text:
But he turned, and said to Peter,
“Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, for you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.”

nodes.label: Matt 16:24
nodes.text:
Then Jesus said to his disciples,
“If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

nodes.label: Matt 16:25
nodes.text: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, and whoever will lose his life for my sake will find it.

nodes.label: Matt 16:26
nodes.text: For what will it profit a man, if he gains the whole world, and forfeits his life? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?

nodes.label: Matt 16:27
nodes.text: For the Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will render to everyone according to his deeds.

nodes.label: Matt 16:28
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste of death, until they see the Son of Man coming in his Kingdom.”
After six days, Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John his brother, and brought them up into a high mountain by themselves.
nodes.label: Matthew 17:1

nodes.text: He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and his garments became as white as the light.
nodes.label: Matthew 17:2

nodes.text: Behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them talking with him.
nodes.label: Matthew 17:3

nodes.text: Peter answered, and said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you want, let’s make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:4

nodes.text: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. Behold, a voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:5

nodes.text: When the disciples heard it, they fell on their faces, and were very afraid.
nodes.label: Matthew 17:6

nodes.text: Jesus came and touched them and said, “Get up, and don’t be afraid.”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:7

nodes.text: Lifting up their eyes, they saw no one, except Jesus alone.
nodes.label: Matthew 17:8

nodes.text: As they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, “Don’t tell anyone what you saw, until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:9

nodes.text: His disciples asked him, saying, “Then why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:10

nodes.text: Jesus answered them, “Elijah indeed comes first, and will restore all things,
nodes.label: Matthew 17:11

nodes.text: but I tell you that Elijah has come already, and they didn’t recognize him, but did to him whatever they wanted to. Even so the Son of Man will also suffer by them.”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:12

nodes.text: Then the disciples understood that he spoke to them of John the Baptizer.
nodes.label: Matthew 17:13

nodes.text: When they came to the multitude, a man came to him, kneeling down to him, and saying,
nodes.label: Matthew 17:14

nodes.text: “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is epileptic, and suffers grievously; for he often falls into the fire, and often into the water.
nodes.label: Matthew 17:15

nodes.text: So I brought him to your disciples, and they could not cure him.”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:16

nodes.text: Jesus answered, “Faithless and perverse generation! How long will I be with you? How long will I bear with you? Bring him here to me.”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:17

nodes.text: Jesus rebuked him, the demon went out of him, and the boy was cured from that hour.
nodes.label: Matthew 17:18

nodes.text: Then the disciples came to Jesus privately, and said, “Why weren’t we able to cast it out?”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:19

nodes.text: He said to them, “Because of your unbelief. For most certainly I tell you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will tell this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.
nodes.label: Matthew 17:20

nodes.text: But this kind doesn’t go out except by prayer and fasting.”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:21

variants.reading: the verse is absent (the saying ends at v 20, without the 'prayer and fasting' clause)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' records for Matthew 17:21 'verse omitted' in aleph* (Sinaiticus), B (Vaticanus), Theta, 0281 and further Greek manuscripts, the Latin, Syriac, Coptic, Ethiopic and Georgian versions and Eusebius. The WEB prints the verse; this graph carries the omission as the variant.

nodes.text: While they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered up into the hands of men,
nodes.label: Matthew 17:22

nodes.text: and they will kill him, and the third day he will be raised up.” They were exceedingly sorry.
nodes.label: Matthew 17:23

nodes.text: When they had come to Capernaum, those who collected the didrachma coins came to Peter, and said, “Doesn’t your teacher pay the didrachma?”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:24

nodes.text: He said, “Yes.” When he came into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive toll or tribute? From their children, or from strangers?”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:25

nodes.text: Peter said to him, “From strangers.” Jesus said to him, “Therefore the children are exempt.
nodes.label: Matthew 17:26

nodes.text: But, lest we cause them to stumble, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take up the first fish that comes up. When you have opened its mouth, you will find a stater coin. Take that, and give it to them for me and you.”
nodes.label: Matthew 17:27
Matt 18:1
nodes.text: In that hour the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Who then is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven?”

nodes.label: Matt 18:2
nodes.text: Jesus called a little child to himself, and set him in the middle of them,

nodes.label: Matt 18:3
nodes.text:
and said,
“Most certainly I tell you, unless you turn, and become as little children, you will in no way enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.

nodes.label: Matt 18:4
nodes.text: Whoever therefore humbles himself as this little child, the same is the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven.

nodes.label: Matt 18:5
nodes.text: Whoever receives one such little child in my name receives me,

nodes.label: Matt 18:6
nodes.text: but whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him that a huge millstone should be hung around his neck, and that he should be sunk in the depths of the sea.

nodes.label: Matt 18:7
nodes.text: “Woe to the world because of occasions of stumbling! For it must be that the occasions come, but woe to that person through whom the occasion comes!

nodes.label: Matt 18:8
nodes.text: If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from you. It is better for you to enter into life maimed or crippled, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into the eternal fire.

nodes.label: Matt 18:9
nodes.text:
If your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna
of fire.

nodes.label: Matt 18:10
nodes.text: See that you don’t despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that in heaven their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.

variants.reading: εἰς τοὺς οὐρανοὺς ('in heaven') omitted
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists 'text omitted — א* א? f1 f13 ... Clement Origen' for Matthew 18:10 'in heaven', against the reading in B (33) 892 Basil. The WEB reads 'in heaven'.

variants.reading: 'in heaven' present (the WEB text)
variants.note: Listed for B (33) 892 Basil; the other witnesses are not manuscript nodes of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

nodes.label: Matt 18:11
nodes.text: For the Son of Man came to save that which was lost.

variants.reading: Verse 18:11 omitted entirely
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists 'Verse omitted — א B L* ... Origen' for Matthew 18:11: the saying is absent from Sinaiticus (א) and Vaticanus (B).

variants.reading: The verse present, shortened ('For the Son of Man has come to save the lost')
variants.note: Listed in the article for D E F H K and many later witnesses and the Latin tradition; not manuscript nodes of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

nodes.label: Matt 18:12
nodes.text: “What do you think? If a man has one hundred sheep, and one of them goes astray, doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine, go to the mountains, and seek that which has gone astray?

nodes.label: Matt 18:13
nodes.text: If he finds it, most certainly I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine which have not gone astray.

nodes.label: Matt 18:14
nodes.text: Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

nodes.label: Matt 18:15
nodes.text: “If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.

variants.reading: εἰς σὲ ('against you') omitted: 'if he sins'
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists 'if he sins — א B 0281 f1 ...' for Matthew 18:15, omitting 'against you', against the fuller reading in D E F G H K and the majority. The WEB reads 'sins against you'.

variants.reading: 'against you' present (the WEB text)
