variants.note: Listed for D E F G H K M N and many others; not manuscript nodes of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

nodes.label: Matt 18:16
nodes.text: But if he doesn’t listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.

nodes.label: Matt 18:17
nodes.text: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly. If he refuses to hear the assembly also, let him be to you as a Gentile or a tax collector.

nodes.label: Matt 18:18
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, whatever things you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever things you release on earth will have been released in heaven.

nodes.label: Matt 18:19
nodes.text: Again, assuredly I tell you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.

nodes.label: Matt 18:20
nodes.text: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”

nodes.label: Matt 18:21
nodes.text: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?”

nodes.label: Matt 18:22
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.

nodes.label: Matt 18:23
nodes.text: Therefore the Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king, who wanted to reconcile accounts with his servants.

nodes.label: Matt 18:24
nodes.text: When he had begun to reconcile, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents.

nodes.label: Matt 18:25
nodes.text: But because he couldn’t pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, with his wife, his children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.

nodes.label: Matt 18:26
nodes.text: The servant therefore fell down and knelt before him, saying, ‘Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay you all!’

nodes.label: Matt 18:27
nodes.text: The lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him, and forgave him the debt.

nodes.label: Matt 18:28
nodes.text:
“But that servant went out, and found one of his fellow servants, who owed him one hundred denarii,
and he grabbed him, and took him by the throat, saying, ‘Pay me what you owe!’

nodes.label: Matt 18:29
nodes.text: “So his fellow servant fell down at his feet and begged him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you!’

nodes.label: Matt 18:30
nodes.text: He would not, but went and cast him into prison, until he should pay back that which was due.

nodes.label: Matt 18:31
nodes.text: So when his fellow servants saw what was done, they were exceedingly sorry, and came and told their lord all that was done.

nodes.label: Matt 18:32
nodes.text: Then his lord called him in, and said to him, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt, because you begged me.

nodes.label: Matt 18:33
nodes.text: Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?’

nodes.label: Matt 18:34
nodes.text: His lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors, until he should pay all that was due to him.

nodes.label: Matt 18:35
nodes.text: So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don’t each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.”

nodes.label: Matt 19:1
nodes.text: When Jesus had finished these words, he departed from Galilee, and came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.

nodes.label: Matt 19:2
nodes.text: Great multitudes followed him, and he healed them there.

nodes.label: Matt 19:3
nodes.text: Pharisees came to him, testing him, and saying, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”

nodes.label: Matt 19:4
nodes.text: He answered, “Haven’t you read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female,

nodes.label: Matt 19:5
nodes.text: and said, ‘For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh?’

nodes.label: Matt 19:6
nodes.text: So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.”

nodes.label: Matt 19:7
nodes.text: They asked him, “Why then did Moses command us to give her a bill of divorce, and divorce her?”

nodes.label: Matt 19:8
nodes.text: He said to them, “Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.

nodes.label: Matt 19:9
nodes.text: I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery; and he who marries her when she is divorced commits adultery.”

variants.reading: Without 'and marries another': 'except for sexual immorality, causes her to commit adultery'
variants.note: The fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists παρεκτος λογου πορνειας ποιει αυτην μοιχευθηναι ('except on account of sexual immorality, causes her to commit adultery') for Papyrus 25 (vid), B, 0233, 1, 4, 1582, l547, itff1, copbo, ethmss, slav, Origen and Cyril; the WEB wording 'and marries another, commits adultery' is the reading of the rest.

variants.reading: 'And anyone marrying a divorced woman commits adultery' (shorter closing clause)
variants.note: The article lists και ο απολελυμενην γαμων μοιχαται ('And anyone marrying a divorced woman commits adultery') for B, C*, E, F, G, H, K, M, N, O, U, W, Y, Z and a long series; the WEB reads 'and he who marries her when she is divorced commits adultery'.

nodes.label: Matt 19:10
nodes.text: His disciples said to him, “If this is the case of the man with his wife, it is not expedient to marry.”

nodes.label: Matt 19:11
nodes.text: But he said to them, “Not all men can receive this saying, but those to whom it is given.

nodes.label: Matt 19:12
nodes.text: For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the Kingdom of Heaven’s sake. He who is able to receive it, let him receive it.”

nodes.label: Matt 19:13
nodes.text: Then little children were brought to him, that he should lay his hands on them and pray; and the disciples rebuked them.

nodes.label: Matt 19:14
nodes.text: But Jesus said, “Allow the little children, and don’t forbid them to come to me; for the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to ones like these.”

nodes.label: Matt 19:15
nodes.text: He laid his hands on them, and departed from there.

nodes.label: Matt 19:16
nodes.text: Behold, one came to him and said, “Good teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?”

nodes.label: Matt 19:17
nodes.text: He said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good but one, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”

variants.reading: 'Why are you asking me about the good?' instead of 'Why do you call me good?'
variants.note: The fetched variants article lists τι με ερωτας περι του αγαθου for א, B, (D), L, Θ, f1, 1, 22, 700 and others, read also by Marcion and Clement; the WEB's 'Why do you call me good?' (τι με λεγεις αγαθον) is the reading of C, E, F, G, H, K, M, S, U, W, Y and the majority.

nodes.label: Matt 19:18
nodes.text: He said to him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder.’ ‘You shall not commit adultery.’ ‘You shall not steal.’ ‘You shall not offer false testimony.’

variants.reading: 'You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal' omitted
variants.note: The fetched article lists ου μοιχευσεις ου κλεψεις ('you will not commit adultery, you will not steal') as 'omitted by א*' - the original hand of Sinaiticus, restored by the corrector; the WEB includes both commandments.

nodes.label: Matt 19:19
nodes.text: ‘Honor your father and your mother.’ And, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”

nodes.label: Matt 19:20
nodes.text: The young man said to him, “All these things I have observed from my youth. What do I still lack?”

nodes.label: Matt 19:21
nodes.text: Jesus said to him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”

nodes.label: Matt 19:22
nodes.text: But when the young man heard the saying, he went away sad, for he was one who had great possessions.

nodes.label: Matt 19:23
nodes.text: Jesus said to his disciples, “Most certainly I say to you, a rich man will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven with difficulty.

nodes.label: Matt 19:24
nodes.text: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”

variants.reading: 'cable' (καμιλον) instead of 'camel'
variants.note: The fetched article lists καμιλον ('cable') in minuscules 174, 579, 1424 and lectionaries 211, 524, 673, 858, 859, 866, 1086 - none of this graph's manuscript nodes; Cyril of Alexandria suggested a Greek scribal error, and the same article states 'the evidence does not support this hypothesis'.

variants.reading: 'borehole' (τρυπηματος) instead of 'hole'
variants.note: For 'needle's eye' the article lists τρυπηματος ('borehole') - W, אc, D, E, F, G, L, S, X, Y, Z and the majority - against τρηματος ('hole') in א* and B, which the WEB follows.

nodes.label: Matt 19:25
nodes.text: When the disciples heard it, they were exceedingly astonished, saying, “Who then can be saved?”

nodes.label: Matt 19:26
nodes.text: Looking at them, Jesus said, “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”

nodes.label: Matt 19:27
nodes.text: Then Peter answered, “Behold, we have left everything, and followed you. What then will we have?”

nodes.label: Matt 19:28
nodes.text: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly I tell you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Man will sit on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

nodes.label: Matt 19:29
nodes.text: Everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, will receive one hundred times, and will inherit eternal life.

variants.reading: 'manifold' (πολλαπλασιονα) instead of 'a hundred times'
variants.note: The fetched article lists εκατονταπλασιονα ('hundredfold') for the great majority but πολλαπλασιονα ('manifold') for B, L, 579, 1010, syrpal, copsa, mae-1, ethms, the Diatessaron, Origen and Cyril; the WEB reads 'one hundred times'.

variants.reading: 'father or mother' (without 'or wife')
variants.note: The article lists πατερα η μητερα ('father or mother') for B, 2148, ita,n, syrpal and Clement, against the WEB's 'father, or mother, or wife'.

nodes.label: Matt 19:30
nodes.text: But many will be last who are first; and first who are last.

nodes.label: Matt 20:1
nodes.text: “For the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who was the master of a household, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard.

nodes.label: Matt 20:2
nodes.text:
When he had agreed with the laborers for a denarius
a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

nodes.label: Matt 20:3
nodes.text:
He went out about the third hour,
and saw others standing idle in the marketplace.

variants.reading: εὑρεν ('found') instead of 'saw'
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists 'ευρεν (found) — D 1424 it(mss)' against 'ειδεν (saw) — rell' for Matthew 20:3. The WEB reads 'saw'; D and 1424 are not manuscript nodes of this graph.

nodes.label: Matt 20:4
nodes.text: He said to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is right I will give you.’ So they went their way.

nodes.label: Matt 20:5
nodes.text:
Again he went out about the sixth and the ninth hour,
and did likewise.

nodes.label: Matt 20:6
nodes.text:
About the eleventh hour
he went out, and found others standing idle. He said to them, ‘Why do you stand here all day idle?’

nodes.label: Matt 20:7
nodes.text:
“They said to him, ‘Because no one has hired us.’
“He said to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and you will receive whatever is right.’

nodes.label: Matt 20:8
nodes.text: When evening had come, the lord of the vineyard said to his manager, ‘Call the laborers and pay them their wages, beginning from the last to the first.’

nodes.label: Matt 20:9
nodes.text: “When those who were hired at about the eleventh hour came, they each received a denarius.

nodes.label: Matt 20:10
nodes.text: When the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; and they likewise each received a denarius.

nodes.label: Matt 20:11
nodes.text: When they received it, they murmured against the master of the household,

nodes.label: Matt 20:12
nodes.text: saying, ‘These last have spent one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat!’

nodes.label: Matt 20:13
nodes.text: “But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Didn’t you agree with me for a denarius?

nodes.label: Matt 20:14
nodes.text: Take that which is yours, and go your way. It is my desire to give to this last just as much as to you.

nodes.label: Matt 20:15
nodes.text: Isn’t it lawful for me to do what I want to with what I own? Or is your eye evil, because I am good?’

nodes.label: Matt 20:16
nodes.text: So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.”

variants.reading: Short reading: 'So the last will be first, and the first last.' (the saying 'for many are called, but few are chosen' omitted)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia variants article lists 'πρωτοι εσχατοι (the first, last) — א B L Z 085 ...' against the longer 'the first, last; for many are called, but few chosen — C D E F G H K M N ...'. The WEB has the longer reading.

variants.reading: Reversed order 'the last first, and the first last' with the saying, in later witnesses
variants.note: The article lists the reversed-order longer text for the majority tradition; those witnesses are not manuscript nodes of this graph.

nodes.label: Matt 20:17
nodes.text: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside, and on the way he said to them,

nodes.label: Matt 20:18
nodes.text: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death,

nodes.label: Matt 20:19
nodes.text: and will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock, to scourge, and to crucify; and the third day he will be raised up.”

variants.reading: αναστησεται ('he will be stood upright') instead of 'he will be raised up'
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia variants article lists 'αναστησεται (he will be stood upright) — B C(c) D E G H K M S U W X Y Γ Δ Θ Π Ω 085 f1 f13 ...' against 'εγερθησεται (he will be raised) — א C* L N Z 579 892 it Origen'. The WEB reads 'he will be raised up'.

variants.reading: εγερθησεται ('he will be raised')
variants.note: Listed for א C* L N Z 579 892 it Origen; the other witnesses are not manuscript nodes of this graph.

nodes.label: Matt 20:20
nodes.text: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, kneeling and asking a certain thing of him.

nodes.label: Matt 20:21
nodes.text:
He said to her,
“What do you want?”
She said to him, “Command that these, my two sons, may sit, one on your right hand, and one on your left hand, in your Kingdom.”

nodes.label: Matt 20:22
nodes.text:
But Jesus answered,
“You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?”
They said to him, “We are able.”

variants.reading: The baptism clause omitted: 'Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?'
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia variants article lists 'text omitted — א B D L Z Θ 085 1 22 372 788 1582* 2737 lat syr(s,c) cop ... Diatessaron Ambrose Jerome Augustine' for 'και το βαπτισμα ο εγω βαπτιζομαι βαπτισθηναι' at Matthew 20:22. The WEB includes the clause.

variants.reading: 'and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with' present (the WEB text)
variants.note: Listed for S 2 118 157 556 892 1071 1582(mg) ... and later tradition; not manuscript nodes of this graph.

nodes.label: Matt 20:23
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“You will indeed drink my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with, but to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give; but it is for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”

nodes.label: Matt 20:24
nodes.text: When the ten heard it, they were indignant with the two brothers.

nodes.label: Matt 20:25
nodes.text:
But Jesus summoned them, and said,
“You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.

nodes.label: Matt 20:26
nodes.text:
It shall not be so among you, but whoever desires to become great among you shall be
your servant.

nodes.label: Matt 20:27
nodes.text: Whoever desires to be first among you shall be your bondservant,

nodes.label: Matt 20:28
nodes.text: even as the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

variants.reading: A long addition after 'many' (parallel to Luke 14:8-10, on seeking the lower place at a dinner)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia variants article lists the long addition 'πολλων υμεις δε ζητειτε εκ μικρου αυξησαι ...' for 'D it(a,aur,b,c,d,e,ff1,ff2,g2,h,n,r1,r2) vg(mss) syr(p(mg),h(mg))' at Matthew 20:28. The WEB has the short text.

nodes.label: Matt 20:29
nodes.text: As they went out from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.

nodes.label: Matt 20:30
nodes.text: Behold, two blind men sitting by the road, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, “Lord, have mercy on us, you son of David!”

nodes.label: Matt 20:31
nodes.text: The multitude rebuked them, telling them that they should be quiet, but they cried out even more, “Lord, have mercy on us, you son of David!”

nodes.label: Matt 20:32
nodes.text:
Jesus stood still, and called them, and asked,
“What do you want me to do for you?”

nodes.label: Matt 20:33
nodes.text: They told him, “Lord, that our eyes may be opened.”

nodes.label: Matt 20:34
nodes.text: Jesus, being moved with compassion, touched their eyes; and immediately their eyes received their sight, and they followed him.

nodes.label: Matt 21:1
nodes.text: When they came near to Jerusalem, and came to Bethsphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,

nodes.label: Matt 21:2
nodes.text:
saying to them,
“Go into the village that is opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Untie them, and bring them to me.

nodes.label: Matt 21:3
nodes.text: If anyone says anything to you, you shall say, ‘The Lord needs them,’ and immediately he will send them.”

nodes.label: Matt 21:4
nodes.text: All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,

nodes.label: Matt 21:5
nodes.text:
“Tell the daughter of Zion,
behold, your King comes to you,
humble, and riding on a donkey,
on a colt, the foal of a donkey.”

nodes.label: Matt 21:6
nodes.text: The disciples went, and did just as Jesus commanded them,

nodes.label: Matt 21:7
nodes.text: and brought the donkey and the colt, and laid their clothes on them; and he sat on them.

nodes.label: Matt 21:8
nodes.text: A very great multitude spread their clothes on the road. Others cut branches from the trees, and spread them on the road.

nodes.label: Matt 21:9
nodes.text:
The multitudes who went in front of him, and those who followed, kept shouting, “Hosanna
 to the son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”

nodes.label: Matt 21:10
nodes.text: When he had come into Jerusalem, all the city was stirred up, saying, “Who is this?”

nodes.label: Matt 21:11
nodes.text: The multitudes said, “This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.”

nodes.label: Matt 21:12
nodes.text: Jesus entered into the temple of God, and drove out all of those who sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.

nodes.label: Matt 21:13
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“It is written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer,’
but you have made it a den of robbers!”

nodes.label: Matt 21:14
nodes.text: The blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.

nodes.label: Matt 21:15
nodes.text: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children who were crying in the temple and saying, “Hosanna to the son of David!” they were indignant,

nodes.label: Matt 21:16
nodes.text:
and said to him, “Do you hear what these are saying?”
Jesus said to them,
“Yes. Did you never read, ‘Out of the mouth of babes and nursing babies you have perfected praise?’”

nodes.label: Matt 21:17
nodes.text: He left them, and went out of the city to Bethany, and camped there.

nodes.label: Matt 21:18
nodes.text: Now in the morning, as he returned to the city, he was hungry.

nodes.label: Matt 21:19
nodes.text:
Seeing a fig tree by the road, he came to it, and found nothing on it but leaves. He said to it,
“Let there be no fruit from you forever!”

Immediately the fig tree withered away.

nodes.label: Matt 21:20
nodes.text: When the disciples saw it, they marveled, saying, “How did the fig tree immediately wither away?”

nodes.label: Matt 21:21
nodes.text:
Jesus answered them,
“Most certainly I tell you, if you have faith, and don’t doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you told this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ it would be done.

nodes.label: Matt 21:22
nodes.text: All things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive.”

nodes.label: Matt 21:23
nodes.text: When he had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching, and said, “By what authority do you do these things? Who gave you this authority?”

nodes.label: Matt 21:24
nodes.text:
Jesus answered them,
“I also will ask you one question, which if you tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.

nodes.label: Matt 21:25
nodes.text:
The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven or from men?”

They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will ask us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

nodes.label: Matt 21:26
nodes.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we fear the multitude, for all hold John as a prophet.”

nodes.label: Matt 21:27
nodes.text:
They answered Jesus, and said, “We don’t know.”
He also said to them,
“Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.

nodes.label: Matt 21:28
nodes.text: But what do you think? A man had two sons, and he came to the first, and said, ‘Son, go work today in my vineyard.’

nodes.label: Matt 21:29
nodes.text: He answered, ‘I will not,’ but afterward he changed his mind, and went.

nodes.label: Matt 21:30
nodes.text: He came to the second, and said the same thing. He answered, ‘I’ m going, sir,’ but he didn’t go.

nodes.label: Matt 21:31
nodes.text:
Which of the two did the will of his father?”
They said to him, “The first.”
Jesus said to them,
“Most certainly I tell you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering into God’s Kingdom before you.

nodes.label: Matt 21:32
nodes.text: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you didn’t believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. When you saw it, you didn’t even repent afterward, that you might believe him.

nodes.label: Matt 21:33
nodes.text: “Hear another parable. There was a man who was a master of a household, who planted a vineyard, set a hedge about it, dug a wine press in it, built a tower, leased it out to farmers, and went into another country.

nodes.label: Matt 21:34
nodes.text: When the season for the fruit came near, he sent his servants to the farmers, to receive his fruit.

nodes.label: Matt 21:35
nodes.text: The farmers took his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.

nodes.label: Matt 21:36
nodes.text: Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they treated them the same way.

nodes.label: Matt 21:37
nodes.text: But afterward he sent to them his son, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

nodes.label: Matt 21:38
nodes.text: But the farmers, when they saw the son, said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and seize his inheritance.’

nodes.label: Matt 21:39
nodes.text: So they took him, and threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.

nodes.label: Matt 21:40
nodes.text: When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?”

nodes.label: Matt 21:41
nodes.text: They told him, “He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will lease out the vineyard to other farmers, who will give him the fruit in its season.”

nodes.label: Matt 21:42
nodes.text:
Jesus said to them,
“Did you never read in the Scriptures,

‘The stone which the builders rejected,
the same was made the head of the corner.
This was from the Lord.
It is marvelous in our eyes?’

nodes.label: Matt 21:43
nodes.text: “Therefore I tell you, God’s Kingdom will be taken away from you, and will be given to a nation producing its fruit.

nodes.label: Matt 21:44
nodes.text: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but on whomever it will fall, it will scatter him as dust.”

nodes.label: Matt 21:45
nodes.text: When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they perceived that he spoke about them.

nodes.label: Matt 21:46
nodes.text: When they sought to seize him, they feared the multitudes, because they considered him to be a prophet.

nodes.label: Matt 22:1
nodes.text: Jesus answered and spoke to them again in parables, saying,

nodes.label: Matt 22:2
nodes.text: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king, who made a marriage feast for his son,

nodes.label: Matt 22:3
nodes.text: and sent out his servants to call those who were invited to the marriage feast, but they would not come.

nodes.label: Matt 22:4
nodes.text: Again he sent out other servants, saying, ‘Tell those who are invited, “Behold, I have prepared my dinner. My cattle and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready. Come to the marriage feast!”’

nodes.label: Matt 22:5
nodes.text: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise,

nodes.label: Matt 22:6
nodes.text: and the rest grabbed his servants, and treated them shamefully, and killed them.

nodes.label: Matt 22:7
nodes.text: When the king heard that, he was angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.

nodes.label: Matt 22:8
nodes.text: “Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding is ready, but those who were invited weren’t worthy.

nodes.label: Matt 22:9
nodes.text: Go therefore to the intersections of the highways, and as many as you may find, invite to the marriage feast.’

nodes.label: Matt 22:10
nodes.text: Those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together as many as they found, both bad and good. The wedding was filled with guests.

variants.reading: γαμος ('wedding') — the WEB reading 'The wedding was filled with guests'
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists γαμος (wedding) for B(1), D, W, Θ, 33, 085, 0161, f1, f13 and the majority/Byzantine text - the reading the WEB prints.

variants.reading: νυμφων ('bride') instead of γαμος ('wedding')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists νυμφων (bride) for א (Sinaiticus), B* (the original hand of Vaticanus), L, 0138, 892 and 1010.

nodes.label: Matt 22:11
nodes.text: But when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who didn’t have on wedding clothing,

nodes.label: Matt 22:12
nodes.text: and he said to him, ‘Friend, how did you come in here not wearing wedding clothing?’ He was speechless.

nodes.label: Matt 22:13
nodes.text: Then the king said to the servants, ‘Bind him hand and foot, take him away, and throw him into the outer darkness. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.’

nodes.label: Matt 22:14
nodes.text: For many are called, but few chosen.”

nodes.label: Matt 22:15
nodes.text: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might entrap him in his talk.

nodes.label: Matt 22:16
nodes.text: They sent their disciples to him, along with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and teach the way of God in truth, no matter whom you teach, for you aren’t partial to anyone.

nodes.label: Matt 22:17
nodes.text: Tell us therefore, what do you think? Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”

nodes.label: Matt 22:18
nodes.text:
But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said,
“Why do you test me, you hypocrites?

nodes.label: Matt 22:19
nodes.text:
Show me the tax money.”
They brought to him a denarius.

nodes.label: Matt 22:20
nodes.text:
He asked them,
“Whose is this image and inscription?”

nodes.label: Matt 22:21
nodes.text:
They said to him, “Caesar’s.”
Then he said to them,
“Give therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”

nodes.label: Matt 22:22
nodes.text: When they heard it, they marveled, and left him, and went away.

nodes.label: Matt 22:23
nodes.text: On that day Sadducees (those who say that there is no resurrection) came to him. They asked him,

nodes.label: Matt 22:24
nodes.text: saying, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If a man dies, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up offspring for his brother.’

nodes.label: Matt 22:25
nodes.text: Now there were with us seven brothers. The first married and died, and having no offspring left his wife to his brother.

nodes.label: Matt 22:26
nodes.text: In the same way, the second also, and the third, to the seventh.

nodes.label: Matt 22:27
nodes.text: After them all, the woman died.

nodes.label: Matt 22:28
nodes.text: In the resurrection therefore, whose wife will she be of the seven? For they all had her.”

nodes.label: Matt 22:29
nodes.text:
But Jesus answered them,
“You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God.

nodes.label: Matt 22:30
nodes.text: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are like God’s angels in heaven.

variants.reading: γαμιζονται ('are married') instead of εκγαμιζονται ('are given in marriage')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists γαμιζονται for א (Sinaiticus), B (Vaticanus), D, f1, 892, 1010 and 1424, against εκγαμιζονται in L, 0138, 0161, 0197 and the Byzantine text, which the WEB prints ('nor are given in marriage').

nodes.label: Matt 22:31
nodes.text: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,

nodes.label: Matt 22:32
nodes.text:
‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?’
God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”

nodes.label: Matt 22:33
nodes.text: When the multitudes heard it, they were astonished at his teaching.

nodes.label: Matt 22:34
nodes.text: But the Pharisees, when they heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, gathered themselves together.

nodes.label: Matt 22:35
nodes.text: One of them, a lawyer, asked him a question, testing him.

nodes.label: Matt 22:36
nodes.text: “Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the law?”

nodes.label: Matt 22:37
nodes.text:
Jesus said to him,
“‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’

nodes.label: Matt 22:38
nodes.text: This is the first and great commandment.

nodes.label: Matt 22:39
nodes.text: A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’

nodes.label: Matt 22:40
nodes.text: The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments.”

nodes.label: Matt 22:41
nodes.text: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question,

nodes.label: Matt 22:42
nodes.text:
saying,
“What do you think of the Christ? Whose son is he?”

They said to him, “Of David.”

nodes.label: Matt 22:43
nodes.text:
He said to them,
“How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,

nodes.label: Matt 22:44
nodes.text:
‘The Lord said to my Lord,
sit on my right hand,
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet?’

nodes.label: Matt 22:45
nodes.text: “If then David calls him Lord, how is he his son?”

nodes.label: Matt 22:46
nodes.text: No one was able to answer him a word, neither did any man dare ask him any more questions from that day forward.

nodes.label: Matt 23:1
nodes.text: Then Jesus spoke to the multitudes and to his disciples,

nodes.label: Matt 23:2
nodes.text:
saying,
“The scribes and the Pharisees sat on Moses’ seat.

nodes.label: Matt 23:3
nodes.text: All things therefore whatever they tell you to observe, observe and do, but don’t do their works; for they say, and don’t do.

nodes.label: Matt 23:4
nodes.text: For they bind heavy burdens that are grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not lift a finger to help them.

nodes.label: Matt 23:5
nodes.text:
But all their works they do to be seen by men. They make their phylacteries

broad, enlarge the fringes
of their garments,

nodes.label: Matt 23:6
nodes.text: and love the place of honor at feasts, the best seats in the synagogues,

nodes.label: Matt 23:7
nodes.text: the salutations in the marketplaces, and to be called ‘Rabbi, Rabbi’ by men.

nodes.label: Matt 23:8
nodes.text: But don’t you be called ‘Rabbi,’ for one is your teacher, the Christ, and all of you are brothers.

nodes.label: Matt 23:9
nodes.text: Call no man on the earth your father, for one is your Father, he who is in heaven.

nodes.label: Matt 23:10
nodes.text: Neither be called masters, for one is your master, the Christ.

nodes.label: Matt 23:11
nodes.text: But he who is greatest among you will be your servant.

nodes.label: Matt 23:12
nodes.text: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

nodes.label: Matt 23:13
nodes.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows’ houses, and as a pretense you make long prayers. Therefore you will receive greater condemnation.

nodes.label: Matt 23:14
nodes.text: “But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you shut up the Kingdom of Heaven against men; for you don’t enter in yourselves, neither do you allow those who are entering in to enter.

variants.reading: the verse is absent (13 'Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!' is followed by 15 'Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around by sea and land...')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'List of omitted Bible verses' (s.v. Matthew 23:14): the verse is 'lacking altogether in Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Vaticanus, Codex Bezae, Codex Regius, Codex Dublinensis, Codex Koridethi, Family 1, Ethiopic, Armenian, several Italic, Syrian, and Coptic manuscripts'; it appears before verse 13 in Codex Cyprius and Codex Washingtonianus and after verse 13 in Family 13; Bruce Metzger: 'There can be little doubt that the words [...] are spurious here', borrowed from the parallel Mark 12:40/Luke 20:47. The World English Bible includes the verse.

nodes.label: Matt 23:15
nodes.text:
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna
as yourselves.

nodes.label: Matt 23:16
nodes.text: “Woe to you, you blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple, he is obligated.’

nodes.label: Matt 23:17
nodes.text: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifies the gold?

nodes.label: Matt 23:18
nodes.text: ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it, he is obligated?’

nodes.label: Matt 23:19
nodes.text: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?

nodes.label: Matt 23:20
nodes.text: He therefore who swears by the altar, swears by it, and by everything on it.

nodes.label: Matt 23:21
nodes.text:
He who swears by the temple, swears by it, and by him who has been living
in it.

nodes.label: Matt 23:22
nodes.text: He who swears by heaven, swears by the throne of God, and by him who sits on it.

nodes.label: Matt 23:23
nodes.text:
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin,
and have left undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. But you ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.

nodes.label: Matt 23:24
nodes.text: You blind guides, who strain out a gnat, and swallow a camel!

nodes.label: Matt 23:25
nodes.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and unrighteousness.

nodes.label: Matt 23:26
nodes.text: You blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and of the platter, that its outside may become clean also.

nodes.label: Matt 23:27
nodes.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.

nodes.label: Matt 23:28
nodes.text: Even so you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

nodes.label: Matt 23:29
nodes.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and decorate the tombs of the righteous,

nodes.label: Matt 23:30
nodes.text: and say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we wouldn’t have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.’

nodes.label: Matt 23:31
nodes.text: Therefore you testify to yourselves that you are children of those who killed the prophets.

nodes.label: Matt 23:32
nodes.text: Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers.

nodes.label: Matt 23:33
nodes.text: You serpents, you offspring of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?

nodes.label: Matt 23:34
nodes.text: Therefore behold, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify; and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues, and persecute from city to city;

nodes.label: Matt 23:35
nodes.text: that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.

nodes.label: Matt 23:36
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.

nodes.label: Matt 23:37
nodes.text: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets, and stones those who are sent to her! How often I would have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!

nodes.label: Matt 23:38
nodes.text: Behold, your house is left to you desolate.

nodes.label: Matt 23:39
nodes.text: For I tell you, you will not see me from now on, until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”

nodes.label: Matt 24:1
nodes.text: Jesus went out from the temple, and was going on his way. His disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.

nodes.label: Matt 24:2
nodes.text:
But he answered them,
“You see all of these things, don’t you? Most certainly I tell you, there will not be left here one stone on another, that will not be thrown down.”

nodes.label: Matt 24:3
nodes.text: As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things be? What is the sign of your coming, and of the end of the age?”

nodes.label: Matt 24:4
nodes.text:
Jesus answered them,
“Be careful that no one leads you astray.

nodes.label: Matt 24:5
nodes.text: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.

nodes.label: Matt 24:6
nodes.text: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you aren’t troubled, for all this must happen, but the end is not yet.

nodes.label: Matt 24:7
nodes.text: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there will be famines, plagues, and earthquakes in various places.

nodes.label: Matt 24:8
nodes.text: But all these things are the beginning of birth pains.

nodes.label: Matt 24:9
nodes.text: Then they will deliver you up to oppression, and will kill you. You will be hated by all of the nations for my name’s sake.

nodes.label: Matt 24:10
nodes.text: Then many will stumble, and will deliver up one another, and will hate one another.

nodes.label: Matt 24:11
nodes.text: Many false prophets will arise, and will lead many astray.

nodes.label: Matt 24:12
nodes.text: Because iniquity will be multiplied, the love of many will grow cold.

nodes.label: Matt 24:13
nodes.text: But he who endures to the end, the same will be saved.

nodes.label: Matt 24:14
nodes.text: This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.

nodes.label: Matt 24:15
nodes.text:
“When, therefore, you see the abomination of desolation,

which was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let the reader understand),

nodes.label: Matt 24:16
nodes.text: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.

nodes.label: Matt 24:17
nodes.text: Let him who is on the housetop not go down to take out the things that are in his house.

nodes.label: Matt 24:18
nodes.text: Let him who is in the field not return back to get his clothes.

nodes.label: Matt 24:19
nodes.text: But woe to those who are with child and to nursing mothers in those days!

nodes.label: Matt 24:20
nodes.text: Pray that your flight will not be in the winter, nor on a Sabbath,

nodes.label: Matt 24:21
nodes.text: for then there will be great oppression, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, no, nor ever will be.

nodes.label: Matt 24:22
nodes.text: Unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would have been saved. But for the sake of the chosen ones, those days will be shortened.

nodes.label: Matt 24:23
nodes.text: “Then if any man tells you, ‘Behold, here is the Christ,’ or, ‘There,’ don’t believe it.

nodes.label: Matt 24:24
nodes.text: For there will arise false christs, and false prophets, and they will show great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.

nodes.label: Matt 24:25
nodes.text: “Behold, I have told you beforehand.

nodes.label: Matt 24:26
nodes.text: If therefore they tell you, ‘Behold, he is in the wilderness,’ don’t go out; ‘Behold, he is in the inner rooms,’ don’t believe it.

nodes.label: Matt 24:27
nodes.text: For as the lightning flashes from the east, and is seen even to the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

nodes.label: Matt 24:28
nodes.text: For wherever the carcass is, that is where the vultures gather together.

nodes.label: Matt 24:29
nodes.text: But immediately after the oppression of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken;

nodes.label: Matt 24:30
nodes.text: and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.

nodes.label: Matt 24:31
nodes.text: He will send out his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the sky to the other.

nodes.label: Matt 24:32
nodes.text: “Now from the fig tree learn this parable. When its branch has now become tender, and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near.

nodes.label: Matt 24:33
nodes.text: Even so you also, when you see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.

nodes.label: Matt 24:34
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, this generation will not pass away, until all these things are accomplished.

nodes.label: Matt 24:35
nodes.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

nodes.label: Matt 24:36
nodes.text:
But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven,
but my Father only.

variants.reading: with 'nor the Son': 'But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, nor the Son, but my Father only'
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia article 'Knowledge of Christ' states that while Mark 13:32 includes the words, 'in most manuscripts Matthew 24:36 does not include the words neither the Son'. The attribution of the longer reading to Sinaiticus and Vaticanus follows the architect calibration (they carry the Alexandrian text of the verse); a direct page stating their exact reading could not be fetched (codexsinaiticus.org unreachable after three attempts) - see notes.md, Uncertain.

nodes.label: Matt 24:37
nodes.text: “As the days of Noah were, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

nodes.label: Matt 24:38
nodes.text: For as in those days which were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ship,

nodes.label: Matt 24:39
nodes.text: and they didn’t know until the flood came, and took them all away, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

nodes.label: Matt 24:40
nodes.text: Then two men will be in the field: one will be taken and one will be left.

nodes.label: Matt 24:41
nodes.text: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and one will be left.

nodes.label: Matt 24:42
nodes.text: Watch therefore, for you don’t know in what hour your Lord comes.

nodes.label: Matt 24:43
nodes.text: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have watched, and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.

nodes.label: Matt 24:44
nodes.text: Therefore also be ready, for in an hour that you don’t expect, the Son of Man will come.

nodes.label: Matt 24:45
nodes.text: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has set over his household, to give them their food in due season?

nodes.label: Matt 24:46
nodes.text: Blessed is that servant whom his lord finds doing so when he comes.

nodes.label: Matt 24:47
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you that he will set him over all that he has.

nodes.label: Matt 24:48
nodes.text: But if that evil servant should say in his heart, ‘My lord is delaying his coming,’

nodes.label: Matt 24:49
nodes.text: and begins to beat his fellow servants, and eat and drink with the drunkards,

nodes.label: Matt 24:50
nodes.text: the lord of that servant will come in a day when he doesn’t expect it, and in an hour when he doesn’t know it,

nodes.label: Matt 24:51
nodes.text: and will cut him in pieces, and appoint his portion with the hypocrites. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.

nodes.label: Matt 25:1
nodes.text: “Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten virgins, who took their lamps, and went out to meet the bridegroom.

variants.reading: των νυμφιων ('of the bridegrooms', plural)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists των νυμφιων for 892*; the WEB prints του νυμφιου ('of the bridegroom'), the reading of א (Sinaiticus), B (Vaticanus) and the majority.

nodes.label: Matt 25:2
nodes.text: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.

nodes.label: Matt 25:3
nodes.text: Those who were foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them,

nodes.label: Matt 25:4
nodes.text: but the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.

nodes.label: Matt 25:5
nodes.text: Now while the bridegroom delayed, they all slumbered and slept.

nodes.label: Matt 25:6
nodes.text: But at midnight there was a cry, ‘Behold! The bridegroom is coming! Come out to meet him!’

nodes.label: Matt 25:7
nodes.text: Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.

nodes.label: Matt 25:8
nodes.text: The foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:9
nodes.text: But the wise answered, saying, ‘What if there isn’t enough for us and you? You go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:10
nodes.text: While they went away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the marriage feast, and the door was shut.

nodes.label: Matt 25:11
nodes.text: Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:12
nodes.text: But he answered, ‘Most certainly I tell you, I don’t know you.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:13
nodes.text: Watch therefore, for you don’t know the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is coming.

nodes.label: Matt 25:14
nodes.text: “For it is like a man, going into another country, who called his own servants, and entrusted his goods to them.

nodes.label: Matt 25:15
nodes.text: To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one; to each according to his own ability. Then he went on his journey.

nodes.label: Matt 25:16
nodes.text: Immediately he who received the five talents went and traded with them, and made another five talents.

nodes.label: Matt 25:17
nodes.text: In the same way, he also who got the two gained another two.

variants.reading: ἐκέρδησεν ('he gained') without καὶ αὐτός ('and he himself')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists ἐκέρδησεν for א, B, C*, L, 33, 892, 1010, 1546 and versions, against καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκέρδησεν (D it d) and ἐκέδησεν καὶ αὐτός (A, C3, K, W, X, Δ, Θ, Π and the majority). The WEB reads 'he also who got the two gained another two.'

nodes.label: Matt 25:18
nodes.text: But he who received the one talent went away and dug in the earth, and hid his lord’s money.

nodes.label: Matt 25:19
nodes.text: “Now after a long time the lord of those servants came, and reconciled accounts with them.

nodes.label: Matt 25:20
nodes.text: He who received the five talents came and brought another five talents, saying, ‘Lord, you delivered to me five talents. Behold, I have gained another five talents besides them.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:21
nodes.text: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:22
nodes.text: “He also who got the two talents came and said, ‘Lord, you delivered to me two talents. Behold, I have gained another two talents besides them.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:23
nodes.text: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:24
nodes.text: “He also who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Lord, I knew you that you are a hard man, reaping where you did not sow, and gathering where you did not scatter.

nodes.label: Matt 25:25
nodes.text: I was afraid, and went away and hid your talent in the earth. Behold, you have what is yours.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:26
nodes.text: “But his lord answered him, ‘You wicked and slothful servant. You knew that I reap where I didn’t sow, and gather where I didn’t scatter.

nodes.label: Matt 25:27
nodes.text: You ought therefore to have deposited my money with the bankers, and at my coming I should have received back my own with interest.

nodes.label: Matt 25:28
nodes.text: Take away therefore the talent from him, and give it to him who has the ten talents.

nodes.label: Matt 25:29
nodes.text: For to everyone who has will be given, and he will have abundance, but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away.

nodes.label: Matt 25:30
nodes.text: Throw out the unprofitable servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:31
nodes.text: “But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.

nodes.label: Matt 25:32
nodes.text: Before him all the nations will be gathered, and he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

nodes.label: Matt 25:33
nodes.text: He will set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.

nodes.label: Matt 25:34
nodes.text: Then the King will tell those on his right hand, ‘Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world;

nodes.label: Matt 25:35
nodes.text: for I was hungry, and you gave me food to eat. I was thirsty, and you gave me drink. I was a stranger, and you took me in.

nodes.label: Matt 25:36
nodes.text: I was naked, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you visited me. I was in prison, and you came to me.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:37
nodes.text: “Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, and feed you; or thirsty, and give you a drink?

nodes.label: Matt 25:38
nodes.text: When did we see you as a stranger, and take you in; or naked, and clothe you?

nodes.label: Matt 25:39
nodes.text: When did we see you sick, or in prison, and come to you?’

nodes.label: Matt 25:40
nodes.text: “The King will answer them, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:41
nodes.text: Then he will say also to those on the left hand, ‘Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels;

variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists the expansion for D, f1, Old Latin mss, Justin Martyr, Irenaeus (lat), Origen and Cyprian; a second expansion ο ητοιμασεν ο κυριος ('which the Lord prepared') for Clement and Tertullian; not manuscript nodes of this graph. variants.note: Listed in the fetched article for F and for 1009, 1344, l 1663; not manuscript nodes of this graph.

nodes.label: Matt 25:42
nodes.text: for I was hungry, and you didn’t give me food to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me no drink;

nodes.label: Matt 25:43
nodes.text: I was a stranger, and you didn’t take me in; naked, and you didn’t clothe me; sick, and in prison, and you didn’t visit me.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:44
nodes.text: “Then they will also answer, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and didn’t help you?’

nodes.label: Matt 25:45
nodes.text: “Then he will answer them, saying, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you didn’t do it to one of the least of these, you didn’t do it to me.’

nodes.label: Matt 25:46
nodes.text: These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:1

nodes.label: Matt 26:4

nodes.label: Matt 26:5

nodes.label: Matt 26:6
nodes.text: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,

nodes.label: Matt 26:7
nodes.text: a woman came to him having an alabaster jar of very expensive ointment, and she poured it on his head as he sat at the table.

variants.reading: βαρυτιμου ('heavy-priced, very costly')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists βαρυτιμου for B (Vaticanus), W, 089, 0133, 0255, f1, f13, Byz and syr(h), against πολυτιμου ('very valuable'), the reading the WEB prints ('very expensive ointment'), for א (Sinaiticus), A, D, L, Θ, 33, 700, 892, 1010, 1424.

nodes.label: Matt 26:8
nodes.text: But when his disciples saw this, they were indignant, saying, “Why this waste?

nodes.label: Matt 26:9
nodes.text: For this ointment might have been sold for much, and given to the poor.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:10
nodes.text: However, knowing this, Jesus said to them, “Why do you trouble the woman? She has done a good work for me.

nodes.label: Matt 26:11
nodes.text: For you always have the poor with you; but you don’t always have me.

nodes.label: Matt 26:12
nodes.text: For in pouring this ointment on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.

nodes.label: Matt 26:13
nodes.text: Most certainly I tell you, wherever this Good News is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be spoken of as a memorial of her.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:14
nodes.text: Then one of the twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests,

nodes.label: Matt 26:15
nodes.text: and said, “What are you willing to give me, that I should deliver him to you?” They weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver.

nodes.label: Matt 26:16
nodes.text: From that time he sought opportunity to betray him.

nodes.label: Matt 26:17
nodes.text: Now on the first day of unleavened bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying to him, “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”

nodes.label: Matt 26:18
nodes.text: He said, “Go into the city to a certain person, and tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is at hand. I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples.”’”

nodes.label: Matt 26:19
nodes.text: The disciples did as Jesus commanded them, and they prepared the Passover.

nodes.label: Matt 26:20
nodes.text: Now when evening had come, he was reclining at the table with the twelve disciples.

nodes.label: Matt 26:21
nodes.text: As they were eating, he said, “Most certainly I tell you that one of you will betray me.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:22
nodes.text: They were exceedingly sorrowful, and each began to ask him, “It isn’t me, is it, Lord?”

nodes.label: Matt 26:23
nodes.text: He answered, “He who dipped his hand with me in the dish, the same will betray me.

nodes.label: Matt 26:24
nodes.text: The Son of Man goes, even as it is written of him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:25
nodes.text: Judas, who betrayed him, answered, “It isn’t me, is it, Rabbi?” He said to him, “You said it.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:26
nodes.text: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks for it, and broke it. He gave to the disciples, and said, “Take, eat; this is my body.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:27
nodes.text: He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave to them, saying, “All of you drink it,

nodes.label: Matt 26:28
nodes.text: for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins.

variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists τῆς διαθήκης ('the covenant') for Papyrus 37, Papyrus 45 (vid), א, B, L, Z, Θ, 0298 (vid), 33, mae-1, cop(bo) and Irenaeus(arm), against τῆς καινῆς διαθήκης ('the new covenant'), which the WEB prints, for A, C, D, K, W, Π, Δ, f1, f13, Byz, lat, syr, cop(sa,bo) and Irenaeus(lat).

nodes.label: Matt 26:29
nodes.text: But I tell you that I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on, until that day when I drink it anew with you in my Father’s Kingdom.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:30
nodes.text: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

nodes.label: Matt 26:31
nodes.text: Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’

nodes.label: Matt 26:32
nodes.text: But after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:33
nodes.text: But Peter answered him, “Even if all will be made to stumble because of you, I will never be made to stumble.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:34
nodes.text: Jesus said to him, “Most certainly I tell you that tonight, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”

variants.reading: ἀλεκτοροφωνίας ('cockcrow')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Papyrus 45' article's textual-variants note on Matthew 26:34 lists ἀλεκτοροφωνίας ('rooster crows') for Papyrus 37, L, f1 and 2886, against ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι ('rooster has crowed'), the reading the WEB prints, for א (Sinaiticus), B (Vaticanus), D, W, 33 and the majority text.

nodes.label: Matt 26:35
nodes.text: Peter said to him, “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” All of the disciples also said likewise.

nodes.label: Matt 26:36
nodes.text: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and said to his disciples, “Sit here, while I go there and pray.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:37
nodes.text: He took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and severely troubled.

nodes.label: Matt 26:38
nodes.text: Then he said to them, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here, and watch with me.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:39
nodes.text: He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:40
nodes.text: He came to the disciples, and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “What, couldn’t you watch with me for one hour?

nodes.label: Matt 26:41
nodes.text: Watch and pray, that you don’t enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:42
nodes.text: Again, a second time he went away, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cup can’t pass away from me unless I drink it, your desire be done.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:43
nodes.text: He came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.

nodes.label: Matt 26:44
nodes.text: He left them again, went away, and prayed a third time, saying the same words.

variants.reading: ἐκ τρίτου ('out a third time') omitted
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' records that Matthew 26:44 omits the text ἐκ τρίτου ('out a third time') in Papyrus 37, A, K, Π, f1, 157, 565, 652, 1424 and it(a,b,d,ff2,r1). The WEB prints 'prayed a third time'.

nodes.label: Matt 26:45
nodes.text: Then he came to his disciples, and said to them, “Sleep on now, and take your rest. Behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

nodes.label: Matt 26:46
nodes.text: Arise, let’s be going. Behold, he who betrays me is at hand.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:47
nodes.text: While he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.

nodes.label: Matt 26:48
nodes.text: Now he who betrayed him gave them a sign, saying, “Whoever I kiss, he is the one. Seize him.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:49
nodes.text: Immediately he came to Jesus, and said, “Hail, Rabbi!” and kissed him.

nodes.label: Matt 26:50
nodes.text: Jesus said to him, “Friend, why are you here?” Then they came and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.

nodes.label: Matt 26:51
nodes.text: Behold, one of those who were with Jesus stretched out his hand, and drew his sword, and struck the servant of the high priest, and struck off his ear.

nodes.label: Matt 26:52
nodes.text: Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back into its place, for all those who take the sword will die by the sword.

nodes.label: Matt 26:53
nodes.text: Or do you think that I couldn’t ask my Father, and he would even now send me more than twelve legions of angels?

nodes.label: Matt 26:54
nodes.text: How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled that it must be so?”

nodes.label: Matt 26:55
nodes.text: In that hour Jesus said to the multitudes, “Have you come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to seize me? I sat daily in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me.

nodes.label: Matt 26:56
nodes.text: But all this has happened, that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left him, and fled.

nodes.label: Matt 26:57
nodes.text: Those who had taken Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered together.

nodes.label: Matt 26:58
nodes.text: But Peter followed him from a distance, to the court of the high priest, and entered in and sat with the officers, to see the end.

nodes.label: Matt 26:59
nodes.text: Now the chief priests, the elders, and the whole council sought false testimony against Jesus, that they might put him to death;

nodes.label: Matt 26:60
nodes.text: and they found none. Even though many false witnesses came forward, they found none. But at last two false witnesses came forward,

nodes.label: Matt 26:61
nodes.text: and said, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.’”

nodes.label: Matt 26:62
nodes.text: The high priest stood up, and said to him, “Have you no answer? What is this that these testify against you?”

nodes.label: Matt 26:63
nodes.text: But Jesus held his peace. The high priest answered him, “I adjure you by the living God, that you tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:64
nodes.text: Jesus said to him, “You have said it. Nevertheless, I tell you, after this you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming on the clouds of the sky.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:65

nodes.label: Matt 26:66
nodes.text: What do you think?” They answered, “He is worthy of death!”

nodes.label: Matt 26:67
nodes.text: Then they spat in his face and beat him with their fists, and some slapped him,

nodes.label: Matt 26:68
nodes.text: saying, “Prophesy to us, you Christ! Who hit you?”

nodes.text: Now Peter was sitting outside in the court, and a maid came to him, saying, “You were also with Jesus, the Galilean!”

nodes.text: But he denied it before them all, saying, “I don’t know what you are talking about.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:71
nodes.text: When he had gone out onto the porch, someone else saw him, and said to those who were there, “This man also was with Jesus of Nazareth.”

nodes.text: Again he denied it with an oath, “I don’t know the man.”

nodes.label: Matt 26:73
nodes.text: After a little while those who stood by came and said to Peter, “Surely you are also one of them, for your speech makes you known.”

nodes.text: Then he began to curse and to swear, “I don’t know the man!” Immediately the rooster crowed.

nodes.text: saying, “I have sinned in that I betrayed innocent blood.” But they said, “What is that to us? You see to it.”

nodes.text:
Then that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying,

the price of him upon whom a price had been set,
whom some of the children of Israel priced,

Jesus said to him,
“So you say.”

nodes.text: He gave him no answer, not even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.

nodes.label: Matt 27:15
nodes.text: Now at the feast the governor was accustomed to release to the multitude one prisoner, whom they desired.

nodes.text: They had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.

nodes.label: Matt 27:19

But the governor answered them, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?”
They said, “Barabbas!”
